<!-- https://walletfeed.app/ -->
# WalletFeed

Spending for Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings

Ask about your spending in your own words, and Apple Intelligence on your iPhone answers with a chart and a summary. WalletFeed needs no account and has no servers of its own. Your transactions go only where you send them.

Coming soon to the App Store

## Apple Intelligence

- Ask Spending: Ask “dining this month vs last” to see a chart, the categories, the matching transactions and a summary.
- Monthly Summary: A short summary of your month, written from figures WalletFeed calculates.
- Search: Type “dining over $50 last month” to see those transactions and their total.
- Recurring charge names: “NETFLIX.COM 866-579” appears as Netflix, with the kind of service.

WalletFeed calculates every chart, total and list. Apple Intelligence runs on your iPhone and sees only what each feature needs. Requires an iPhone that supports Apple Intelligence, with Apple Intelligence turned on.

## Privacy

- No account: There’s nothing to sign up for, and WalletFeed doesn’t know who you are.
- No tracking: WalletFeed has no analytics, advertising or third-party code.
- No WalletFeed servers: WalletFeed reads transactions from Wallet on your iPhone when it needs them and doesn’t keep a copy.
- On your iPhone: Apple Intelligence features run on the device, and nothing is sent to a server.
- Destinations you add: With Pro, transactions go straight from your iPhone to the services you choose. Keys and sign-ins stay in the Keychain on your iPhone.

Read the [privacy policy](https://walletfeed.app/privacy/).

## Spending

- Spending: This month by day, category and merchant, compared with the same point last month.
- Transactions: Transactions from the Wallet accounts you share, grouped by month.
- Recurring Charges: Subscriptions and other charges that repeat, found in your history.
- Recurring Charge Alerts: A notification when a charge starts repeating or its price changes.
- Monthly Installments: Apple Card Monthly Installments charges, in their own section of Spending.
- Spending widget: This month’s spending and the same point last month, on your Home Screen or Lock Screen.
- Search and export: Search all your transactions, and export a CSV file when you need one.
- Siri and Shortcuts: Ask Siri to show your spending or search your transactions.

## WalletFeed Pro

WalletFeed Pro is optional. It sends new and changed transactions from your iPhone to the destinations you add.

- Budgeting apps: BankSync, Lunch Money, PocketSmith, Firefly III, Sure and Toshl Finance. BankSync also offers Sign In with BankSync.
- Sheets and databases: Google Sheets, Airtable, Notion, Coda, Supabase and Linear
- Automations: Zapier, Make and signed [webhooks](https://walletfeed.app/docs/webhooks/)
- Files: One CSV file, or a CSV, OFX or QIF file a month, in iCloud Drive or another folder
- AWS: Amazon S3, SQS, Kinesis Data Streams, DynamoDB and EventBridge

- Background Sync: Your destinations update within the hour, even when WalletFeed is closed.
- Send History: By default, a new destination also receives your earlier transactions, at a pace the service accepts. Zapier, Make and Linear start 30 days back.
- Shortcuts: Sync after each card tap, or get recent transactions in a shortcut.

## Pricing

- Yearly: $4.99/year, 1 week free
- Monthly: $0.99/month, 1 week free
- Lifetime: $19.99, One payment

The spending features are free, including the Apple Intelligence ones. WalletFeed Pro adds destinations, Background Sync, Send History and the Shortcuts actions that send or get transactions. It works with Family Sharing. WalletFeed runs on iPhone with iOS 26 or later, in the US.

- [**Apple Card to Lunch Money**Send transactions to your Lunch Money budget.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/)
- [**Apple Card to PocketSmith**Send transactions to a PocketSmith account.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/)
- [**Apple Card to Notion**Add each purchase to a Notion database.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/)
- [**Apple Card to a CSV file**Keep a CSV file that WalletFeed updates.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-csv/)
- [**All guides**Budgeting apps, spreadsheets, files, automations and AWS.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/)

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/privacy/ -->
# Privacy policy

Last updated October 29, 2026

WalletFeed needs no account and has no servers of its own. It reads your transactions from Wallet on your iPhone, holds them in memory only while it uses them, and doesn't keep a copy.

## Developer

WalletFeed is made by Phillip Harrison, an independent developer. Send questions about this policy to [support@walletfeed.app](mailto:support@walletfeed.app).

WalletFeed has no servers, so the developer holds no data about you to access, export or delete. If you email support, your message is used only to reply to you and is deleted once your question is resolved.

## Wallet data

WalletFeed reads transactions and account names from the Wallet accounts you choose to share through Apple's FinanceKit: Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings. iOS asks for your permission first.

You can change what you share at any time in the Settings app.

## Data on your iPhone

WalletFeed keeps only this on your iPhone:

- Sync positions (FinanceKit history tokens), so each destination receives only new changes.
- Your settings and each destination's settings, such as its name and filter.
- Destination credentials, such as API keys, webhook URLs and secrets, and folder access, in the Keychain. They stay on this iPhone and don't sync to iCloud Keychain.
- Sync status without transaction details: when each destination last synced, how many changes were sent, how far back its history has been sent, and a short error description if it failed. WalletFeed's widget can show this status.
- When WalletFeed's Shortcuts actions last ran, so Settings can show whether your automations work.
- For the Spending widget, two totals: your spending this month and at the same point last month, with their currency and the time they were updated. iOS keeps a copy of what the widget shows.
- If you turn on Recurring Charge Alerts, the IDs of transactions WalletFeed has already alerted on, so no alert comes twice. No amounts or merchants are kept for alerts.

WalletFeed doesn't keep a copy of your transactions. A Files destination saves them in the folder you choose.

## Destinations and exports

WalletFeed sends transactions only where you tell it to:

- A Files destination saves transactions in a folder you choose, such as one in iCloud Drive or On My iPhone, as one CSV file or as one CSV, OFX or QIF file per month.
- Services you connect, such as Lunch Money, Notion or AWS, receive transactions over HTTPS directly from your iPhone. WalletFeed connects with the key you paste, which stays in the Keychain on this iPhone.
- Google Sheets uses Google sign-in instead of a key, and the sign-in stays in the Keychain on this iPhone. WalletFeed asks Google only for access to files it creates, so it can open only its own spreadsheet in your Google Drive, where it adds and updates your transactions. It doesn't read, keep or share anything else from your Google Account. WalletFeed's use of information received from Google APIs adheres to the [Google API Services User Data Policy](https://developers.google.com/terms/api-services-user-data-policy), including the Limited Use requirements.
- BankSync can use Sign In with BankSync instead of a key. The sign-in stays in the Keychain on this iPhone, and WalletFeed can open only its own Apple Card table in your workspace.
- Webhooks, Zapier and Make receive each change at the address you paste. Webhook requests are signed with a secret made on your iPhone, which you share with your server.
- When you export a CSV, the file goes only where you send it from the share sheet.
- If you use WalletFeed's actions in Shortcuts, your shortcut receives the transactions they return.

Before a new destination receives anything, WalletFeed shows what it will get: which details of each transaction, from which accounts and from what date. Nothing is sent unless you agree.

Once data reaches a destination, that service's own terms and privacy policy apply. Removing a destination stops new data from going there, but WalletFeed can't delete what it already sent.

## Apple Intelligence and Siri

When Apple Intelligence is available, WalletFeed uses Apple's on-device model to write your monthly summary and a summary of each request on Spending, interpret searches and requests, name recurring charges and turn a rule you describe into a filter. It all runs on your iPhone, and nothing is sent to a server.

WalletFeed calculates every chart, total and list itself. The model writes the summaries in its own words from figures WalletFeed works out, such as your totals, the change from last month, categories, merchants and largest purchases, and for a request, the words you typed. It can get a figure wrong, so rely on the page's figures. To read a search, request or rule, the model gets only the words you type or say, and to name recurring charges, only their merchant names. Examples you tap on Spending are read by WalletFeed without the model. Nothing the model writes is saved, except the filter a rule creates.

Summarize Spending in Settings turns off both summaries. A request you send on Spending still goes to the model to be read.

When you ask Siri to show your spending or search WalletFeed, Siri opens the app and receives none of your transactions or spending. The Get Recent Card Transactions action is different: it returns transactions to the shortcut or Siri request that runs it.

## Analytics and tracking

WalletFeed has no analytics, advertising or third-party SDKs, and doesn't track you across apps or websites. If you share analytics with app developers in iOS Settings, Apple may share crash reports with the developer.

Sign In with BankSync goes through WalletFeed's referral link, so WalletFeed may earn a commission if you then pay for a BankSync plan.

## Purchases and notifications

Apple handles purchases and payments. WalletFeed checks on your iPhone which plan you have and whether it's active, and never sees your payment details.

If you turn on Remind If Sync Stops, WalletFeed schedules a local notification on your iPhone. It contains no transaction details.

If you turn on Recurring Charge Alerts, WalletFeed works out on your iPhone when a charge starts repeating or changes price, and posts a local notification with the charge's name and amounts. Notification Center keeps it until you clear it.

## Security

- WalletFeed covers its screen when you leave the app, so transactions don't appear in the app switcher.
- Transactions and spending are hidden while your screen is recorded or mirrored.
- The Spending widget's amounts are marked as private, so iOS can hide them while your iPhone is locked.
- You can require Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode to open WalletFeed.
- WalletFeed doesn't cache network responses on disk.

## Your choices

- Delete a destination in Destinations, or remove all of them in Settings. WalletFeed then deletes their credentials, sync positions and sync status from your iPhone.
- Stop sharing Wallet accounts in the Settings app. WalletFeed then clears the Spending widget's totals the next time it runs.
- Turn off Recurring Charge Alerts in Settings, or remove the Spending widget from your Home Screen or Lock Screen.
- Deleting WalletFeed removes its settings and sync status. Keychain items can remain after an app is deleted; if you install WalletFeed again, it erases them when it first opens.

## Children

WalletFeed is a personal finance app for adults and isn't directed at children under 13.

## This website

This site has no cookies, analytics or trackers. It's hosted on GitHub Pages, which may log visits under [GitHub's privacy statement](https://docs.github.com/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement).

## Changes

When this policy changes, this page and the app's privacy statement change together, with a new date.

## WalletFeed Pro

Apple sells WalletFeed Pro and processes every payment under the App Store’s terms. A subscription renews automatically unless you cancel it at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. To cancel or change your plan, open Settings on your iPhone, tap your name, then tap Subscriptions.

## Services you connect

When you add a destination, WalletFeed sends transactions from your iPhone directly to the service you choose. That service’s terms and privacy policy apply to the data it receives. You are responsible for the accounts, keys and sign-ins you connect, and for what you do with the data in those services. Removing a destination stops new data from going there, but WalletFeed can’t delete data that it already sent.

## Information, not advice

WalletFeed shows information from the Wallet accounts you share. It doesn’t give financial, tax or legal advice. Summaries from Apple Intelligence can contain errors, so use the figures that WalletFeed calculates.

## Trademarks

# Support

Send an e-mail to [support@walletfeed.app](mailto:support@walletfeed.app?subject=WalletFeed). In the e-mail, give the model of your iPhone and the version of iOS on it. For a problem with a destination, also give the service or the file format, for example Notion or CSV. Do not send API keys, tokens or data about your transactions.

To correct a problem, find it on this page or in [Troubleshooting](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/).

## If WalletFeed does not show your cards

WalletFeed is available only in the US. WalletFeed can read Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings accounts. It reads only the accounts that you select on the iOS screen for Wallet access.

Until you tap **Share** or **Don't Share** on this iOS screen, **Settings** › **Wallet** shows **Choose Accounts**. To select your accounts, do these steps:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Wallet** section, tap **Choose Accounts**.
3. On the iOS screen, select the accounts and the start date of each account.
4. Tap **Share**.

After you tap **Share** or **Don't Share**, iOS does not show this screen again. Then **Settings** › **Wallet** shows **Open Settings**. To change the accounts, do these steps:

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts and the start date of each account.
4. Open WalletFeed.

Refer to [Select the Wallet accounts that WalletFeed reads](https://walletfeed.app/docs/wallet-accounts/).

## If WalletFeed does not show Ask Spending

These functions are available only on an iPhone that can use Apple Intelligence, and only when Apple Intelligence is active:

- Ask Spending
- The Monthly Summary
- Search with Apple Intelligence
- The names in **Recurring Charges**
- A filter that you type as a sentence

If your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence, do these steps:

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Apple Intelligence & Siri**.
3. Activate Apple Intelligence.

Without Apple Intelligence, you can use **Spending** and **Search**. **Search** then finds the words that you type.

When WalletFeed can use Apple Intelligence, **Settings** shows **Summarize Spending** in the **Privacy & Security** section. If you deactivate **Summarize Spending**, Apple Intelligence does not make the Monthly Summary or the summaries in Ask Spending. Refer to [Ask Spending with Apple Intelligence](https://walletfeed.app/docs/ask-spending/).

## If a destination shows “Authentication failed”

The service did not let WalletFeed use the key, the token, the URL or the sign-in of the destination. Some causes are an expired key and a key that you deleted in the service.

1. In the service, make a new key, token or URL.
2. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap the destination.
4. Tap **Replace Key**, **Replace Token** or **Replace URL**.
5. Paste the new key, token or URL.
6. Tap **Replace**.

For Google Sheets, and for BankSync with **Sign In with BankSync**, the destination screen shows **Sign In Again**. For a webhook, the destination screen shows **URL** and **Authorization**.

It is not necessary to delete the destination. After you correct the problem, WalletFeed sends the changes that the destination did not receive. Refer to [Troubleshooting](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/#if-a-destination-shows-authentication-failed).

## If a destination receives changes only while WalletFeed is open

While WalletFeed is open, a destination receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. Then WalletFeed updates the Spending widget and **Recurring Charge Alerts**. If you have WalletFeed Pro and **Background Sync** is active, WalletFeed also sends the change to your destinations.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Sync** section, activate **Background Sync**.

**Settings** shows the **Sync** section only with WalletFeed Pro. After your iPhone starts again, destinations do not receive changes until you type your passcode one time.

To send each purchase seconds after you tap your iPhone to make the purchase, make an **After Each Card Tap** automation. The steps are in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Automations**. Refer to [Background Sync](https://walletfeed.app/docs/background-sync/).

## If a file changes only when you open WalletFeed

If WalletFeed cannot open the folder of a CSV, OFX or QIF file in the background, WalletFeed does not update the file. WalletFeed updates the file when you open WalletFeed, when a Shortcuts automation starts a WalletFeed action, or while your iPhone charges. Refer to [Troubleshooting](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/#if-a-file-changes-only-when-you-open-walletfeed).

## If a destination does not have your previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions, from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

A new Zapier, Make or Linear destination receives no more than 30 days of previous transactions. In Zapier, each transaction starts your Zap. In Make, each transaction starts your scenario. In Linear, each transaction can become an issue.

WalletFeed sends the history from the last transaction back to the first transaction. WalletFeed obeys the limits of each service. The destination screen shows **Sending History** and the number of transactions that WalletFeed sent. WalletFeed also sends the history in the background.

To send more previous transactions to a destination, do these steps:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Select a time, for example **90 Days**.
5. For Zapier, Make or Linear, tap **Send** in the message.

To stop the history, tap **Send History** › **Stop Sending**. The destination keeps the transactions that it received before you stopped the history. Refer to [Send previous transactions](https://walletfeed.app/docs/send-history/).

## Connect WalletFeed to BankSync

With **Sign In with BankSync**, an API key is not necessary. You can use **Sign In with BankSync** on the Free plan of BankSync.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Budgeting** section, tap **BankSync**.
4. Tap **Sign In with BankSync**.
5. On the BankSync page, get access to your BankSync account.
6. Give WalletFeed access to your BankSync workspace. Only the owner or an admin of the workspace can give this access.
7. Tap **Add**.

After you give access, BankSync makes an “Apple Card” table. WalletFeed can get access only to that table.

If BankSync does not make the table in approximately 30 seconds, WalletFeed shows “You're signed in, but BankSync hasn't created or shared the Apple Card table.”

The message also gives the table limit of your plan, for example “The Free plan allows one table.” To correct the problem, do these steps:

1. Tap **Open BankSync**.
2. Delete a table that you do not use, or change your plan to a plan that has more tables.
3. In WalletFeed, tap **Try Again**.

To use an API key, tap **Use an API Key Instead**. The Free plan and the Starter plan of BankSync do not include API keys. Refer to [Send Apple Card transactions to BankSync](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/).

**Note:** **Sign In with BankSync** uses the referral URL of WalletFeed. Thus, the BankSync form in WalletFeed shows “WalletFeed may earn a commission if you pay for BankSync.”

## If a destination shows a pending charge

Most destinations receive a charge while it is pending. When the charge posts, WalletFeed updates the charge in the destination. WalletFeed removes declined and expired charges from the destination.

OFX and QIF files include a charge only after it posts. To send a charge to a destination only after the charge posts, deactivate **Include Pending** in the filter of the destination.

Zapier, Make, a webhook, Amazon SQS, Kinesis Data Streams and EventBridge receive a message for each change. Your server or automation must then update its data. Refer to [Send charges only after they post](https://walletfeed.app/docs/choose-what-to-send/#send-charges-only-after-they-post).

## Send only some transactions to a destination

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Activate **Filter**.
4. Set the items of the filter, for example **Minimum**, **Accounts** or **Categories**.

With Apple Intelligence, you can also type the filter as a sentence, for example “Travel over $50, not Uber”. Refer to [Filter the transactions for a destination](https://walletfeed.app/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

## Change or cancel your plan

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Subscription** section, tap **Change Plan** or **Manage Subscription**.

WalletFeed shows **Change Plan** and **Manage Subscription** only for the **Monthly** plan and the **Yearly** plan. A Lifetime purchase has no subscription.

You can also change or cancel the subscription in the Settings app:

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap your name.
3. Tap **Subscriptions**.
4. Tap **WalletFeed**.

**Restore Purchases** is on the **WalletFeed Pro** screen. Refer to [WalletFeed Pro](https://walletfeed.app/docs/walletfeed-pro/).

## Delete your data

WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. Thus, there is no account data or server data to delete.

To delete a destination, do these steps:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Delete**.
4. In the message, tap **Delete**.

WalletFeed removes the destination, its key or sign-in, and its status from your iPhone. The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay in the service. To delete all destinations, tap **Settings** › **Remove All Destinations** › **Remove All**.

Refer to [Privacy and security](https://walletfeed.app/docs/privacy-and-security/) and the [privacy policy](https://walletfeed.app/privacy/).

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/webhooks/ -->
# Webhook format

A Webhook destination sends JSON to your HTTPS URL when transactions change. Your iPhone sends each request directly to the URL. Each request has a [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com) signature, so you can use a Standard Webhooks library to examine it.

## Request

- A `POST` request to the URL of the destination, with `Content-Type: application/json` and `User-Agent: WalletFeed-Webhooks/1`.
- The `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` and `webhook-signature` headers. The ID is `msg_` and 32 hexadecimal characters. The timestamp is the Unix time in seconds. To examine the signature, refer to [Signature](https://walletfeed.app/docs/webhooks/#verify).
- An `Authorization` header, if you typed a value in Authorization in WalletFeed. WalletFeed sends the value exactly as you typed it, for example `Bearer`, a space and a token.
- A maximum of 100 transactions, or 100 IDs to delete, in each request.
- A status code from 200 to 299 tells WalletFeed that you received the request. If WalletFeed cannot connect, or gets a different status code or no response in 30 seconds, it keeps the changes. It sends them again each time that it sends data, until you accept them.
- For history, WalletFeed waits between tries, from 1 minute to 1 day. It obeys `Retry-After` in a 429 or 503 response.

## Body

```
{
  "type": "transactions.changed",
  "timestamp": "2026-10-27T17:41:21Z",
  "data": {
    "upserted": [
      {
        "id": "8B3F0C2E-6D7A-4E8F-9C1B-2A4D5E6F7A8B",
        "accountID": "4F1E2D3C-…",
        "accountName": "Apple Card",
        "accountType": "liability",
        "date": "2026-10-27T15:02:11Z",
        "amount": 6.75,
        "currencyCode": "USD",
        "direction": "debit",
        "description": "Blue Bottle Coffee",
        "originalDescription": "BLUE BOTTLE COFFEE OAKLAND CA",
        "merchantName": "Blue Bottle Coffee",
        "merchantCategoryCode": 5814,
        "category": "dining",
        "status": "pending",
        "type": "pointOfSale"
      }
    ],
    "deletedIDs": []
  }
}
```

The top-level `type` is `transactions.changed`, also for history. `timestamp` is the date and time when WalletFeed sent the request, the same as `webhook-timestamp`.

Send Test in WalletFeed sends the same format with `"type": "walletfeed.test"` and one sample transaction. The sample has the ID `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`. Only the sample has the transaction type `purchase`.

WalletFeed sends deletions in a different request from new and changed transactions. Thus, in each request, one of the two lists is empty. A deletion has only the ID:

```
{
  "type": "transactions.changed",
  "timestamp": "2026-10-28T09:12:40Z",
  "data": {
    "upserted": [],
    "deletedIDs": ["8B3F0C2E-6D7A-4E8F-9C1B-2A4D5E6F7A8B"]
  }
}
```

## Changes

- Upsert each transaction on `id`. WalletFeed sends a transaction again when it changes. For example, a pending charge comes again with the same `id` when it posts. Then its `status` changes from `pending` or `authorized` to `booked`, and `amount` is the posted amount.
- Delete the transactions that have their IDs in `deletedIDs`. The IDs come from declined and expired charges, and from transactions that Wallet removed. If Wallet gives a posted charge a new ID, the previous ID comes in `deletedIDs`.
- `deletedIDs` can also contain IDs that you did not receive. This occurs for a charge that Wallet declined before WalletFeed sent it. It also occurs for a transaction that the filter or start date of the destination did not include. If you do not have a transaction with that ID, do nothing.
- WalletFeed sends the history of the destination (previous transactions) in `transactions.changed` requests too, newest first. History has no deletions and no declined charges. Upsert on `id` for history too, because Send History can send a transaction again.
- WalletFeed can send the same changes two times or more. After an error, it can also send again the requests that you accepted before the error.
- WalletFeed makes `webhook-id` from the contents of `data`. Two requests with the same `data` have the same `webhook-id`, so you can use it to find repeated requests. But when WalletFeed sends changes again, a request can also contain newer changes. Then the request has a different `webhook-id`.

## Fields

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | The Wallet transaction ID (a UUID). It stays the same when the transaction changes. |
| `accountID`, `accountName` | The ID and name of the Wallet account, for example Apple Card. |
| `accountType` | `liability` (Apple Card) or `asset` (Apple Cash, Savings). |
| `date`, `postedDate` | ISO 8601 in UTC. A transaction has `postedDate` after the charge posts, if Wallet gives the date. |
| `amount` | A positive number. `direction` gives the sign. |
| `direction` | `debit` (purchases, fees) or `credit` (refunds, payments, deposits). |
| `currencyCode` | ISO 4217, for example `USD`. A purchase in a different currency also has `foreignAmount` and `foreignCurrencyCode`. |
| `description`, `originalDescription` | The clean description from Wallet, and the description from the card network. |
| `merchantName`, `merchantCategoryCode` | Only if Wallet has them. The category code is the MCC from the card network. |
| `category` | The WalletFeed category from the MCC (`other` without an MCC): `groceries`, `dining`, `transport`, `fuel`, `travel`, `shopping`, `entertainment`, `subscriptions`, `utilities`, `health`, `services`, `cash` or `other`. |
| `status` | The Wallet status: `authorized`, `pending`, `booked` or `memo`. WalletFeed sends a declined or expired charge (`rejected`) as a deletion. |
| `type` | The [FinanceKit transaction type](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/financekit/transactiontype): `adjustment`, `atm`, `billPayment`, `check`, `deposit`, `directDebit`, `directDeposit`, `dividend`, `fee`, `interest`, `loan`, `pointOfSale`, `refund`, `standingOrder`, `transfer`, `unknown` or `withdrawal`. Send Test uses `purchase`. |

If Wallet has no value for a field, the transaction does not include that field.

## Signature

To get the signing secret, tap Share Signing Secret in WalletFeed. It is on the Webhook screen when you add the destination, and in the destination. The secret is `whsec_` and base64 text. With a Standard Webhooks library:

```
// Node: npm install standardwebhooks
import { Webhook } from "standardwebhooks";
const payload = new Webhook(process.env.WALLETFEED_SECRET).verify(rawBody, request.headers);
```

```
# Python: pip install standardwebhooks
from standardwebhooks.webhooks import Webhook
payload = Webhook(os.environ["WALLETFEED_SECRET"]).verify(raw_body, request.headers)
```

Without a library:

1. Decode the base64 text after `whsec_`. The result is the key.
2. Calculate the HMAC-SHA256 of `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{raw body}` with the key.
3. Encode the result in base64.
4. Compare it with the text after `v1,` in `webhook-signature`. Use a constant-time comparison.
5. Do not accept the request if `webhook-timestamp` is more than 5 minutes before or after the current time.

Use the raw body exactly as you received it. Do the check before you parse the JSON.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/ask-spending/ -->
# Ask Spending with Apple Intelligence

In Ask Spending, you type text about your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions, for example `Dining this month vs last`. Apple Intelligence on your iPhone reads your text. WalletFeed calculates the result and shows it as a chart and a list. Then Apple Intelligence writes a summary of the result.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone that can use Apple Intelligence, with iOS 26 or a newer version
- Apple Intelligence, active on the iPhone
- WalletFeed, with [access to your Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/).

WalletFeed is available only in the US. [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/) is not necessary for Ask Spending.

If Apple Intelligence is not available, [**Spending**](/docs/spending/) shows the total and the chart for this month, without the **Ask about your spending** field.

## Use Ask Spending

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. At the bottom of the screen, tap **Spending**.
3. At the top of the screen, tap the **Ask about your spending** field.
4. Type your text, for example `Groceries over $50`.

   You cannot type more than 200 characters.

5. Tap **Go** on the keyboard.

   The field shows a progress indicator. Then WalletFeed shows the result below the field.

   ![The result for "Dining this month vs last", with 9 transactions, a total of $188.70 and a line chart of this month and last month.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/ask-spending/walletfeed-ask-spending.webp)

6. If the chart shows days, weeks or months, put your finger on the chart.

   Above the chart, WalletFeed shows the day, week or month and the total at that point.

7. To show the total for a different day, week or month, move your finger on the chart.

## Use an example

When no result is on the screen, WalletFeed shows an example below the field. The example starts with "Try". At intervals of 4 seconds, a different example replaces it. WalletFeed shows only the examples that give a result for your transactions from this month and the two months before this month.

1. Tap the example below the field.

   ![The Spending screen with the empty "Ask about your spending" field and the example "Dining this month vs last" below it.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/ask-spending/walletfeed-spending.webp)

   The field then shows the example, and the keyboard opens.

2. To get a different result, change the text in the field.
3. Tap **Go** on the keyboard.

If you do not change the example, WalletFeed reads it without Apple Intelligence.

> **Note:** When the keyboard is open, when the field contains text, or when VoiceOver is active, the example does not change. With VoiceOver, the other examples are VoiceOver actions on the example button. When **Reduce Motion** is active, the example changes at intervals of 8 seconds.

## Write text that WalletFeed can read

Your text can contain the items in this table. It can also start with `how much did I spend`.

| Item | Examples |
|---|---|
| A period of time | `today`, `this week`, `last 30 days`, `September`, `last year` |
| A period to compare with | `vs last month`, `vs last year` |
| A category | `dining`, `groceries`, `travel` |
| A merchant name, or a part of it | `coffee` |
| A dollar limit for each transaction | `over $50`, `under $20`, `at least $50` |
| Refunds, money in or recurring charges | `refunds`, `money in`, `subscriptions` |
| A chart type | `by day`, `by week`, `by category`, `by merchant`, `trend`, `bars` |
| The largest transactions first | `biggest purchases`, `largest purchases` |

WalletFeed uses these rules for periods:

- If your text has no period of time, WalletFeed uses this month.
- `last month` is the calendar month before this month, and `past month` is the last 30 days. Weeks and years have the same rule. For example, `past year` is the last 12 months.
- For a month name, for example `September`, WalletFeed uses the September before this month. If this month is September, WalletFeed uses this month.
- WalletFeed compares a period only with the previous period, or with the same period of the previous year.
- If the period includes today, WalletFeed uses the other period only to the same day and time. For example, on October 20, `Dining this month vs last` compares October 1 to 20 with September 1 to 20.

If your text contains one of these items, WalletFeed shows "Couldn't read this." below the field:

- A word that removes transactions, for example `except`, `not` or `without`
- Two dollar limits, for example `between $10 and $50`
- Two types of transactions, for example `refunds and deposits`
- Two categories or two merchants to compare, for example `dining vs groceries`
- A period that WalletFeed cannot use, for example `yesterday`, `since March`, `this quarter` or `on Fridays`
- Text about balances or budgets.

## Read the result

At the top, the result shows the items that WalletFeed found in your text, with the Apple Intelligence icon. An example is "Dining · This month · vs last month".

Below these items, the result shows the number of transactions and their total. If you compare two periods, the result also shows the change, for example "↑ 38% VS SEP". If the other period has a total of zero or less, the result does not show the change.

The chart shows the totals by day, week, month, category or merchant. If you compare two periods by day, week or month, each point is the total from the first day of its period. If your text contains `trend` or `bars`, the chart shows the total for each day, week or month.

A summary is below the chart. If the summary has the Apple Intelligence icon, Apple Intelligence wrote it. A summary from Apple Intelligence can contain an incorrect number. A light bulb icon shows that WalletFeed wrote the summary from the facts that it calculates.

The **Categories** section shows the five largest categories, and **Other** for the remaining categories. The category totals include refunds. If you add the category totals, you get the total at the top of the result. If the refunds in a category are more than its purchases, the category total has a plus sign (+).

The **Merchants** section shows the five merchants that have the largest totals. WalletFeed shows this section only if the result has two or more merchants and the chart does not show merchants. For recurring charges, the result does not have this section.

At the bottom, the result shows the transactions in a section for each month, with the newest transaction first. If your text is about the largest transactions, the **Largest** section shows them, with the largest first.

If your text is about recurring charges, the result shows the [**Recurring Charges**](/docs/recurring-charges/) section above **Categories**. If your text also has no period of time and does not compare two periods, the result shows the number of these charges. In this result, the total is for one month of these charges, and the text "a month" comes after the total.

If WalletFeed finds no transactions for your text, the result shows "0 TRANSACTIONS" and $0.00.

## Change the text

When you change the text, WalletFeed removes the result and shows the total and the chart for this month again.

1. Tap **Clear** (the x button) in the field.
2. Tap the **Ask about your spending** field.
3. Type the new text.
4. Tap **Go** on the keyboard.

## Update the result

WalletFeed reads Wallet each time you open WalletFeed again, and when you swipe down at the top of **Spending**. Then WalletFeed calculates the result again from the transactions that it reads. Apple Intelligence does not read your text again.

1. At the top of **Spending**, swipe down.

## Set Summarize Spending to off

If you set **Summarize Spending** to off, Apple Intelligence does not write the summary of each result or the Monthly Summary. Thus, WalletFeed shows a light bulb icon and two facts that it calculates. Apple Intelligence continues to read the text that you type.

**Settings** shows **Summarize Spending** only when Apple Intelligence is available on your iPhone.

1. At the top of **Spending**, tap **Settings** (the gear button).
2. Scroll to **Privacy & Security**.
3. Set **Summarize Spending** to off.

   ![Settings with the Privacy & Security section, where Summarize Spending is on.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/ask-spending/walletfeed-settings-2.webp)

4. Tap **Done**.

## Privacy

Apple Intelligence operates on your iPhone. Ask Spending does not send data to a server. To read your text, Apple Intelligence gets only your text. To write a summary, it gets your text and the data that WalletFeed calculates. This data includes your totals, the change between two periods, the categories, the merchants and the largest purchases.

WalletFeed does not keep your text, the results or the summaries. For more information, refer to the [WalletFeed privacy policy](/privacy/).

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows "Couldn't read this."

WalletFeed cannot get a result from your text. Your text stays in the field, and WalletFeed shows an example below the field.

1. Change your text to use the items in [Write text that WalletFeed can read](#write-text-that-walletfeed-can-read).
2. Tap **Go** on the keyboard.

You can also tap the example below the field.

### If WalletFeed shows "Couldn't read Wallet. Pull down to try again."

WalletFeed did not get the transactions for the result from Wallet.

1. At the top of **Spending**, swipe down.

   Then WalletFeed reads Wallet and your text again.

### If Spending does not show "Ask about your spending"

**Spending** shows the field only if Apple Intelligence is available on your iPhone. Apple Intelligence is not available on all iPhone models, or in all languages and regions.

1. Make sure that your iPhone model is on the list in [Get started with the next generation of Apple Intelligence](https://support.apple.com/en-us/121115).
2. Open the Settings app.
3. Tap **Apple Intelligence & Siri**.
4. Set **Apple Intelligence** to on (or tap **Turn on Apple Intelligence**).

When Apple Intelligence is available, **Spending** shows the field.

### If the result shows "0 TRANSACTIONS"

WalletFeed read your text. But WalletFeed found no transactions for your text.

1. Make sure that the top of the result shows the correct period and category.
2. If the period or the category is not correct, change your text.
3. Tap **Go** on the keyboard.

### If the summary has an incorrect number

Apple Intelligence writes the summary from the numbers that WalletFeed calculates. WalletFeed does not examine the summary.

1. Use the total, the chart and the list, because WalletFeed calculates them.
2. To get the summary from WalletFeed, [set Summarize Spending to off](#set-summarize-spending-to-off).

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/background-sync/ -->
# Background Sync

**Background Sync** sends your new and changed Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions to your destinations while WalletFeed is not open. To send transactions to [destinations](/docs/destinations/), you must have [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/). WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.

## Times that destinations receive changes

A destination receives a new or changed transaction at these times:

| Condition | A destination receives the change |
| --- | --- |
| WalletFeed is open. | In seconds. |
| WalletFeed is not open, and **Background Sync** is on. | Approximately 1 hour or less after the change in Wallet. |
| You tap your iPhone to make a purchase, and you have an **After Each Card Tap** automation. | Seconds after you tap your iPhone. |
| Your **Every Day** automation starts. | At the time that you set in Shortcuts. |
| You tap **Sync Now** in **Settings** › **Sync**. | In seconds. |
| You charge your iPhone. | At a time that iOS selects. |

While WalletFeed is not open, iOS also starts WalletFeed after a change in Wallet to update the Spending widget and Recurring Charge Alerts. WalletFeed makes these updates without WalletFeed Pro and while **Background Sync** is off.

After your iPhone starts again, WalletFeed does not send changes to your destinations until you type your passcode.

If **Background Sync** cannot open the folder of a CSV, OFX or QIF file, it does not update the file. WalletFeed updates the file when you open WalletFeed, when an automation starts, or while you charge your iPhone.

A new destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. A new Zapier, Make or Linear destination receives a maximum of 30 days of previous transactions. Refer to [Send History](/docs/send-history/).

## Make sure that **Background Sync** is on

**Background Sync** is on until you set it to off. **Settings** shows the **Sync** section only with WalletFeed Pro.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Sync** section, if **Background Sync** is off, set it to on.

   ![WalletFeed Settings, with Background Sync on in the Sync section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/background-sync/walletfeed-settings.webp)

3. Tap **Done**.

## Add an **After Each Card Tap** automation

An **After Each Card Tap** automation sends each purchase seconds after you tap your iPhone to make the purchase. While **Background Sync** is on, this automation is not necessary. Without the automation, **Background Sync** sends the purchase in approximately 1 hour or less.

iOS does not let apps make automations. Thus, you add the automation in the Shortcuts app, and WalletFeed gives you the steps.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Sync** section, tap **Automations**.

   ![The Automations screen, with the steps for After Each Card Tap and Every Day.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/background-sync/walletfeed-automations.webp)

3. In the **After Each Card Tap** section, do the steps for your iPhone.

> **Note:** The sections that follow give the steps that WalletFeed shows. These steps are different on iOS 26 and on iOS 27. On iOS 27, they are also different with Apple Intelligence.

### Paste the text in Shortcuts

If step 1 in the **After Each Card Tap** section is **Copy Description**, do these steps. WalletFeed shows them on iOS 27 with Apple Intelligence. It also shows them after you tap **Describe It Instead**.

1. Tap **Copy Description**.

   **Copy Description** changes to **Copied**. WalletFeed copies the text `When I tap my Apple Card or Apple Cash card, run Sync New Purchase from WalletFeed without asking.`

2. Tap **Open Shortcuts**.
3. In Shortcuts, tap **+**.
4. Paste the text.
5. Make sure that the automation uses your cards.
6. Make sure that the automation starts without a message from Shortcuts.
7. Tap **Done**.

> **Note:** If Shortcuts does not make the automation from the text, **Set It Up Yourself** in WalletFeed gives a different procedure. This procedure is also in [Make the automation on iOS 27](#make-the-automation-on-ios-27).

### Make the automation on iOS 26

If step 2 in the **After Each Card Tap** section tells you to tap **Automation**, do these steps. WalletFeed shows them on iOS 26.

1. Tap **Open Shortcuts**.
2. In Shortcuts, tap **Automation**.
3. Tap **+** or **New Automation**.
4. Tap **Transaction**.
5. Select your cards.
6. Select **Run Immediately**.
7. Tap **Next**.
8. Tap **New Blank Automation** › **Add Action**.
9. Type WalletFeed in the search field.
10. Tap **Sync New Purchase**.
11. Tap **Done**.

### Make the automation on iOS 27

If step 2 in the **After Each Card Tap** section tells you to tap **Add Action**, do these steps. WalletFeed shows them on iOS 27 when Apple Intelligence is not available. It also shows them after you tap **Set It Up Yourself**.

1. Tap **Open Shortcuts**.
2. In Shortcuts, tap **Add Action**.
3. Type WalletFeed in the search field.
4. Tap **Sync New Purchase**.
5. In the action list, tap **Automation** › **Transaction**.
6. Select your cards.
7. Tap the arrow adjacent to the trigger.
8. Set **Confirm Before Run** to off.
9. Tap the information button **ⓘ** › **Privacy**.
10. Set **Allow Running When Locked** to on.
11. Tap **Done**.

## Add an **Every Day** automation

An **Every Day** automation sends changes one time each day, at a time that you select. It sends the changes that an **After Each Card Tap** automation does not send, for example purchases on the internet and changes to pending transactions.

**Automations** shows **Every Day** only when **Background Sync** is off or **Sample Data** is on. While **Background Sync** is on, an **Every Day** automation is not necessary. If you have an **Every Day** automation, it stays in Shortcuts and sends changes.

The steps for **Every Day** are the same as the steps in [Add an After Each Card Tap automation](#add-an-after-each-card-tap-automation), but these parts are different:

| Part | **After Each Card Tap** | **Every Day** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The text that you copy | `When I tap my Apple Card or Apple Cash card, run Sync New Purchase from WalletFeed without asking.` | `Every day at 9 PM, run Sync Transactions from WalletFeed without asking.` |
| The trigger in Shortcuts | **Transaction**, then your cards | **Time of Day**, then a time |
| The WalletFeed action | **Sync New Purchase** | **Sync Transactions** |
| Step 5 in [Paste the text in Shortcuts](#paste-the-text-in-shortcuts) | Make sure that the automation uses your cards. | Make sure that the time is correct. |

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Sync** section, tap **Automations**.
3. In the **Every Day** section, do the steps for your iPhone.

## **Last Run** and the **Automations** value

iOS does not tell apps about the automations that you have. Thus, for each automation, **Last Run** shows the last time that its WalletFeed action started. If Siri or a shortcut starts **Sync Transactions**, the **Last Run** of **Every Day** also changes. Until the WalletFeed action of an automation starts for the first time, its **Last Run** shows **Never**.

Each automation has a time limit. The time limit is 14 days for **After Each Card Tap** and 3 days for **Every Day**. In **Settings** › **Sync**, **Automations** shows one of these values:

| Value | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| **On** | Each automation on the **Automations** screen started in its time limit. |
| **1 of 2** | One of the two automations started in its time limit. |
| **Off** | **Background Sync** is on, **Sample Data** is off, and **After Each Card Tap** did not start in its time limit. |
| **Set Up** | **Background Sync** is off or **Sample Data** is on, and no automation started in its time limit. |

For the messages that the automations show, refer to [Siri and Shortcuts](/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/).

## Get the **Sync Stopped** notification

If **Remind If Sync Stops** is on and WalletFeed does not send to all your destinations correctly for 3 days, you get the **Sync Stopped** notification. Each time that WalletFeed sends to all your destinations correctly, the 3 days start again. The text of the notification is "WalletFeed hasn't synced in 3 days. Open it to catch up." The notification does not show information about your transactions.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Sync** section, set **Remind If Sync Stops** to on.
3. If iOS shows a message about notifications, tap **Allow**.

   If you do not let WalletFeed send notifications, **Remind If Sync Stops** stays off.

4. Tap **Done**.

## Send changes with **Sync Now**

When you tap **Sync Now**, WalletFeed sends the changes to your destinations.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Sync** section, tap **Sync Now**.

   ![WalletFeed Settings, with Initial History set to All and Sync Now with the time 1 minute ago.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/background-sync/walletfeed-settings-2.webp)

   While WalletFeed sends the changes, **Sync Now** shows a progress indicator. Then it shows a time, for example "1 minute ago".

3. Tap **Done**.

## Stop **Background Sync**

If you set **Background Sync** to off, iOS starts WalletFeed after a change in Wallet. But WalletFeed then updates only the Spending widget and Recurring Charge Alerts.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Sync** section, set **Background Sync** to off.
3. Tap **Done**.

While **Background Sync** is off, your destinations receive changes:

- When you open WalletFeed
- When you tap **Sync Now**
- When an automation from **Automations** starts
- While you charge your iPhone
- At times that iOS selects.

The **Automations** screen also shows **Every Day** while **Background Sync** is off. Refer to [Add an Every Day automation](#add-an-every-day-automation).

## If there is a problem

### If a destination does not receive a change after 1 hour

It is possible that **Background Sync** is off, that your iPhone started again, or that the destination has a problem.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.

   While WalletFeed is open, it sends changes in seconds.

2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Sync** section, if **Background Sync** is off, set it to on.
4. Tap **Sync Now**.
5. Tap **Done**.
6. Tap **Destinations** at the bottom of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen, with the n8n destination that shows Authentication failed.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/background-sync/walletfeed-destinations-failure.webp)

7. If a destination shows a problem, for example "Authentication failed", refer to [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting/).

### If **Settings** does not show the **Sync** section

**Settings** shows the **Sync** section only with WalletFeed Pro.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Subscription** section, tap **WalletFeed Pro**.
3. Select a plan.
4. Tap **Start Free Trial**, **Subscribe** or **Buy Lifetime**.

For the plans, refer to [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).

### If you get the **Sync Stopped** notification

In the last 3 days, WalletFeed did not send to all your destinations correctly.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations** at the bottom of the screen.
3. If a destination shows a problem, refer to [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting/).
4. If no destination shows a problem, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
5. In the **Sync** section, tap **Sync Now**.

### If **Last Run** shows **Never**

The **Last Run** of **After Each Card Tap** changes only after **Sync New Purchase** starts. An **After Each Card Tap** automation starts it only when you tap your iPhone to make a purchase.

1. After you make a purchase with your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Sync** section, tap **Automations**.
4. In the **After Each Card Tap** section, if **Last Run** shows **Never**, do the steps in [Add an After Each Card Tap automation](#add-an-after-each-card-tap-automation) again.

> **Note:** On iOS 27, **Set It Up Yourself** and **Describe It Instead** give a different procedure to make the same automation.

### If **Remind If Sync Stops** does not stay on

iOS does not let WalletFeed send notifications.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Notifications** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Set **Allow Notifications** to on.
4. Open WalletFeed.
5. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
6. In the **Sync** section, set **Remind If Sync Stops** to on.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/choose-what-to-send/ -->
# Filter the transactions for a destination

A filter selects the Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions that a destination receives from WalletFeed. If a destination has no filter, it receives all the transactions of the [Wallet accounts that WalletFeed reads](/docs/wallet-accounts/).

You can set a filter for each destination. For example, you can send your Apple Card transactions to one file and your Apple Cash transactions to a different file. After you add a destination, you set its filter on the screen of the destination.

To add a destination, you must have [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/). WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase. [Destinations](/docs/destinations/) tells you how to add a destination.

## Set a filter for a destination

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations** at the bottom of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with four destinations: Lunch Money, Budget 2026, Monthly CSV and n8n.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/choose-what-to-send/walletfeed-destinations.webp)

3. Tap the destination.

   ![The screen of the Lunch Money destination, with the Filter switch in the off position.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/choose-what-to-send/walletfeed-destination-detail.webp)

4. Set the **Filter** switch to on.

   Below the switch, WalletFeed shows the filter controls: **Include**, **Minimum**, **Include Pending**, **Accounts**, **Categories** and **Exclude**.

A destination receives a transaction only if all the filter controls include it. Until you change a control, the filter includes all transactions.

WalletFeed saves the filter each time that you change a control. When you change the filter, WalletFeed does not remove the transactions that the destination received.

## Send only purchases or only credits

1. On the screen of the destination, tap **Include**.
2. Tap **Purchases** or **Credits**.

   If you tap **Purchases**, the destination receives purchases and fees. If you tap **Credits**, the destination receives credits, for example refunds and payments.

To send all transactions again, select **All** in **Include**.

## Set a minimum amount

1. On the screen of the destination, tap **None** in the **Minimum** row.
2. Type the amount, for example 50.

   The destination receives only transactions of $50 or more.

WalletFeed uses the minimum for purchases and for credits. For example, a destination with a minimum of 50 does not receive a refund of $20.

To remove the minimum, delete the number in the **Minimum** row.

## Send charges only after they post

A pending charge can change before it posts.

1. On the screen of the destination, set the **Include Pending** switch to off.

   The destination receives each charge only after the charge posts.

OFX and QIF files include a charge only after it posts. The **Include Pending** switch does not change this.

## Select the accounts

1. On the screen of the destination, tap **Accounts**.

   The **Accounts** screen shows the Wallet accounts that WalletFeed reads.

2. Tap each account to send its transactions to the destination.

   The **Accounts** screen shows a checkmark on the row of each account that you select.

3. Tap the back button at the top of the screen.

   The **Accounts** row shows the number of accounts that you selected.

To send the transactions of all the accounts again, tap **All** at the top of the **Accounts** screen.

## Select the categories

WalletFeed sets the category of each transaction from its merchant category code (MCC). The categories are **Groceries**, **Dining**, **Transport**, **Fuel**, **Travel**, **Shopping**, **Entertainment**, **Subscriptions**, **Utilities**, **Health**, **Services**, **Cash & Transfers** and **Other**.

1. On the screen of the destination, tap **Categories**.
2. Tap each category to send its transactions to the destination.

   The **Categories** screen shows a checkmark on the row of each category that you select.

3. Tap the back button at the top of the screen.

   The **Categories** row shows the number of categories that you selected.

To send the transactions of all the categories again, tap **All** at the top of the **Categories** screen.

## Send no transactions from some merchants

1. On the screen of the destination, tap **Merchants** in the **Exclude** row.
2. Type the merchant names, with a comma between the names, for example `Uber, Starbucks`.

   The destination does not receive transactions from these merchants.

If the merchant name or the description of a transaction contains one of the names that you typed, the destination does not receive the transaction. You can type part of a name. For example, if you type `uber`, the destination does not receive transactions from Uber or Uber Eats. Uppercase and lowercase letters give the same result.

## Make a filter with Apple Intelligence

With Apple Intelligence, you can make a filter from a sentence. WalletFeed shows the text field for Apple Intelligence only if your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence and Apple Intelligence is active.

1. On the screen of the destination, set the **Filter** switch to on.
2. Tap the text field below **Filter**.

   Until you type, the field shows the example "Travel over $50, not Uber".

3. Type a sentence about the transactions to send to the destination, for example `Dining over $20, not Starbucks`.
4. Tap the Apple Intelligence icon at the end of the field.

   Apple Intelligence sets the filter controls from your sentence.

5. Examine the controls below the field.
6. If the value of a control is not correct, change the value.

When Apple Intelligence sets the controls, it does not keep the values that you set previously. But the accounts that you selected do not change. The **Minimum** and **Exclude** controls get only the amounts and merchant names that are in your sentence.

Apple Intelligence makes the filter on your iPhone from your sentence. It does not get your transactions.

## Send previous transactions with the filter

With [Send History](/docs/send-history/), you can send previous transactions to the destination.

1. On the screen of the destination, tap **Send History**.
2. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.
3. If WalletFeed shows a message, tap **Send**.

   The destination receives the transactions from that period that the filter includes.

## Filter the history of a new destination

Before a new destination receives transactions, WalletFeed shows a message. The message tells you the accounts and the start date of the transactions that the destination will receive. A new destination has no filter. Thus, the message shows all the Wallet accounts that WalletFeed reads.

When you tap **Send** (**Save** for a Files destination), the destination starts to receive transactions from the start date in **Initial History**. Until you change **Initial History**, it is **All**. A new Zapier, Make or Linear destination receives a maximum of 30 days of previous transactions.

To set the filter before a new destination receives previous transactions, set **Initial History** to **Today** before you add the destination.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations** at the bottom of the screen.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Sync** section, tap **Initial History**.

   ![The Settings screen, with All in the Initial History row of the Sync section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/choose-what-to-send/walletfeed-settings.webp)

4. Tap **Today**.
5. Tap **Done**.
6. Add the destination. Refer to [Destinations](/docs/destinations/).
7. In the message from WalletFeed, tap **Send** (**Save** for a Files destination).
8. Set the filter. Refer to [Set a filter for a destination](#set-a-filter-for-a-destination).
9. Tap **Send History**.
10. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.
11. If WalletFeed shows a message, tap **Send**.

    The destination receives the previous transactions that the filter includes.

**Initial History** stays at **Today** for the destinations that you add after this procedure.

## Remove the filter

1. On the screen of the destination, set the **Filter** switch to off.

   The destination receives all transactions again. WalletFeed removes the values of all the filter controls.

If you set the **Filter** switch to on again, you must set each control again.

To send the previous transactions that the filter did not include, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/).

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows "Couldn't create a rule. Try describing it another way."

Apple Intelligence cannot make a filter from your sentence.

1. Change the sentence in the text field.
2. Tap the Apple Intelligence icon again.
3. If WalletFeed shows the message again, set the controls below the field yourself.

### If WalletFeed does not show the text field for Apple Intelligence

The **Filter** switch is off, your iPhone cannot use Apple Intelligence, or Apple Intelligence is not active. You can set the filter without Apple Intelligence.

1. On the screen of the destination, set the **Filter** switch to on.
2. If WalletFeed does not show the field, make sure that your iPhone model is on the list in [Get started with the next generation of Apple Intelligence](https://support.apple.com/en-us/121115).
3. Open the Settings app.
4. Tap **Apple Intelligence & Siri**.
5. Activate Apple Intelligence.
6. Open WalletFeed again.
7. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.

### If a destination does not receive a transaction

One or more filter controls do not include the transaction. If the transaction is a pending charge and the **Include Pending** switch is off, the destination receives the charge after it posts.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Examine the filter controls, for example **Minimum** and **Accounts**.
3. Change the control that does not include the transaction.
4. Tap **Send History**.
5. Tap a period that includes the date of the transaction.
6. If WalletFeed shows a message, tap **Send**.

If the filter includes the transaction, find the cause in the guide for the destination. Refer to [Destination types](/docs/destinations/#destination-types).

### If a destination has transactions that the filter does not include

WalletFeed sent these transactions before you set the filter. When you change the filter, WalletFeed does not remove them.

1. Open the service or the file that receives the transactions, for example your spreadsheet or your budget app.
2. Remove the transactions that the filter does not include.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/destinations/ -->
# Destinations

A destination is an app, a spreadsheet, a file or a server that receives your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from WalletFeed. After you add a destination, WalletFeed sends new transactions and changes to transactions from your iPhone to the destination.

To send transactions to a destination, you must have [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/). WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase. Without WalletFeed Pro, you can look at the list of destination types.

## Destination types

Each destination type has a guide with all the steps. **Add Destination** shows the destination types in these sections:

| Section | Destinations |
|---|---|
| **Budgeting** | [BankSync](/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/), [Lunch Money](/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/), [PocketSmith](/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/), [Firefly III](/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/), [Sure](/guides/apple-card-to-sure/), [Toshl Finance](/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/) |
| **Sheets & Databases** | [Google Sheets](/guides/apple-card-to-google-sheets/), [Airtable](/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/), [Notion](/guides/apple-card-to-notion/), [Coda](/guides/apple-card-to-coda/), [Supabase](/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/), [Linear](/guides/apple-card-to-linear/) |
| **Automations** | [Zapier](/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/), [Make](/guides/apple-card-to-make/) |
| **Files** | [CSV File](/guides/apple-card-to-csv/), [OFX File](/guides/apple-card-to-ofx/), [QIF File](/guides/apple-card-to-qif/) |
| **Developers** | [AWS](/guides/apple-card-to-aws/) (Amazon S3, Amazon SQS, Kinesis Data Streams, DynamoDB and EventBridge), [Webhook](/guides/apple-card-to-webhook/) |

**Add Destination** shows one row for **Files** and one row for **AWS**. In the setup form, you select the file format in **Format**, or the AWS service in **Service**.

OFX and QIF files do not include pending charges.

The rows for Firefly III and Sure show **Self-hosted**. You install these apps on a server.

You can add more than one destination of the same type. For example, you can send the transactions of each Wallet account to a different CSV file.

To find a destination, type its name in the search field at the top of **Add Destination**. To open **Add Destination**, tap **+** in **Destinations**.

The search also finds a file format from the name of an app that uses the format. For example, "GnuCash" finds **OFX File** and **QIF File**.

![The Add Destination search with PocketSmith in the search field and PocketSmith as the result.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/destinations/walletfeed-add-destination-search.webp)

## Add a destination

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations** at the bottom of the screen.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The empty Destinations screen with the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/destinations/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. Tap the destination type, for example **Lunch Money**.

   ![The Add Destination screen with the search field, and the Budgeting and Sheets & Databases sections.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/destinations/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, the **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens. After you get WalletFeed Pro or tap **Restore Purchases**, the setup form opens.

5. Do the steps in the setup form.

   ![The Lunch Money setup form with the Access Token field, three steps and the Open Developers link.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/destinations/walletfeed-setup-lunch-money.webp)

   The form shows the steps below its fields. The [guide for each destination type](#destination-types) gives all the steps.

6. Tap **Add** at the top of the screen.

   Result: WalletFeed shows a message, for example **Send Transactions to Lunch Money?**

   The message tells you which data the destination receives and from which Wallet accounts. It also gives the start date. If the destination receives all previous transactions, the message shows "including earlier ones".

7. Tap **Send** (or **Save** for a Files destination).

   Result: WalletFeed closes **Add Destination** and starts to send transactions to the destination.

If you tap **Cancel** in the message, WalletFeed removes the destination and does not send transactions to it. The setup form stays open. You can change the text in the fields and tap **Add** again. If you close **Add Destination** before you tap **Send** or **Save**, WalletFeed also removes the destination.

A new destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. A new Zapier, Make or Linear destination receives a maximum of 30 days of previous transactions. After you add the destination, you can send more previous transactions with [Send History](/docs/send-history/).

> **Note:** WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. Thus, WalletFeed sends your transactions from your iPhone to the service that you select. The key or token for each destination stays in the Keychain on your iPhone.

The service keeps the data that it receives. After a service receives your transactions, the terms of that service are applicable to them.

## Destination status

**Destinations** shows each destination with its status below its name.

![The Destinations screen with three destinations, and Authentication failed with an orange exclamation mark on the n8n webhook.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/destinations/walletfeed-destinations-failure.webp)

These are the usual statuses:

| Status | Information |
|---|---|
| A time, for example "2 minutes ago" | The time of the last update to the destination. |
| "Sending history · 46%" | WalletFeed sends previous transactions to the destination. |
| "History paused · 46%" | WalletFeed does not send previous transactions at this time. Refer to [Send History](/docs/send-history/). |
| "Off" | **Enabled** is off. WalletFeed does not send transactions to the destination. |
| A failure, for example "Authentication failed" | The last update had a failure. Some failure messages also tell you what to do. The row shows an orange exclamation mark. Refer to [If there is a problem](#if-there-is-a-problem). |

## Updates to destinations

While WalletFeed is open, a destination receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then sends the change.

To update all destinations, swipe down on the list in **Destinations**. You can also tap **Settings** › **Sync** › **Sync Now**.

## Change a destination

To open a destination, tap it in **Destinations**.

![The Lunch Money destination with Name, Enabled, Last Sync, Replace Token, Filter, Send History, Send Test and Delete.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/destinations/walletfeed-destination-detail.webp)

The destination screen has these rows, from top to bottom:

| Rows | Function |
|---|---|
| **Name**, **Enabled** and **Last Sync** | You can change the name, and stop or start the destination. **Last Sync** shows the time and result of the last update. |
| **Replace Key**, **Replace Token**, **Replace URL**, **Sign In Again** or **Change Folder** | You can replace the key, token, URL or folder, or connect the account again. The rows are different for each destination type. |
| **Filter** | The filter selects the transactions that the destination receives. Refer to [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/). |
| **Send History** | WalletFeed sends previous transactions to the destination. Refer to [Send History](/docs/send-history/). |
| **Send Test** | WalletFeed sends a test transaction to the destination. |
| **Delete** | WalletFeed removes the destination. |

If WalletFeed sent transactions in the last update, **Last Sync** also shows the number of transactions, for example "1 minute ago · 2 sent". If the last update had a failure, the screen shows the failure below **Last Sync**.

## Change the name of a destination

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap the name in the **Name** row.
3. Type the new name.

   Result: **Destinations** shows the new name.

## Stop and start a destination

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Set **Enabled** to off.

   Result: In **Destinations**, the destination shows "Off". WalletFeed does not send transactions to it while **Enabled** is off.

To send transactions to the destination again, set **Enabled** to on.

## Send a test

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Send Test**.

   Result: WalletFeed sends one test transaction to the destination. If the destination receives it, the **Send Test** row shows a green checkmark. If the destination does not receive it, the screen shows the failure below **Send Test**.

The test transaction has the merchant name WalletFeed and the amount 4.20 USD. For a Files destination, WalletFeed writes a test file in the folder, for example `WalletFeed Test.csv`. You can delete the test transaction or the test file.

## Replace a key or connect again

If you make a new key in the service, you can replace the key in WalletFeed. It is not necessary to remove the destination and add it again.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap the row for the key, for example **Replace Key**, **Replace Token** or **Replace URL** (for Zapier and Make).
3. Paste the new key or URL in the field.
4. Tap **Replace**.

   Result: WalletFeed validates the new key with the service. If the key is correct, WalletFeed keeps the key and shows a checkmark. If the key is not correct, WalletFeed shows the failure below the row.

For some destinations, do different steps after step 1:

- If the destination screen shows **Sign In Again**, tap **Sign In Again**. Then obey the instructions on the page that opens.
- For a Files destination, tap **Change Folder**. Then select the folder.
- For a Webhook destination, tap **URL** or **Authorization**. Type the new text. Then tap **Save**.

## Remove a destination

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.

   Result: WalletFeed shows a message with the name of the destination, for example **Delete Lunch Money?**

3. Tap **Delete**.

   Result: WalletFeed removes the destination and its key from your iPhone.

The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay in the service. If you made a key in the service for WalletFeed, you can delete that key in the service.

In **Destinations**, you can also swipe left on a destination and tap **Delete**. Then WalletFeed removes the destination without a message.

## Remove all destinations

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. Scroll to the **Data** section.
3. Tap **Remove All Destinations**.

   ![The Settings screen with Export CSV and Remove All Destinations in the Data section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/destinations/walletfeed-settings-4.webp)

   Result: WalletFeed shows the message **Remove All Destinations?**

4. Tap **Remove All**.

   Result: WalletFeed removes all your destinations. The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay in each service.

## If there is a problem

### If a destination shows "Authentication failed"

The service does not let WalletFeed use the key or token of the destination. This occurs, for example, if you deleted the key in the service.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.

   ![The n8n destination with Authentication failed below Last Sync, and the URL and Authorization rows.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/destinations/walletfeed-destination-failure.webp)

2. If the destination uses a key, make a new key in the service.

   The [guide for the destination type](#destination-types) gives the steps.

3. In WalletFeed, do the steps in [Replace a key or connect again](#replace-a-key-or-connect-again).

### If a destination shows "Can't connect"

WalletFeed cannot connect to the service.

1. Make sure that your iPhone has an internet connection.
2. If the destination is on your server, make sure that the server operates.
3. In **Destinations**, swipe down on the list.

   Result: WalletFeed tries to update the destinations again.

### If a destination shows "Server error"

The service has a problem. When WalletFeed updates the destination again, it sends the same changes.

1. After some minutes, swipe down on the list in **Destinations**.

### If a destination shows "Off"

WalletFeed does not send transactions to the destination because **Enabled** is off.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Set **Enabled** to on.

### If Destinations shows "Sync Requires Pro"

Without WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed does not send transactions to your destinations. Your destinations stay in the list.

1. In **Destinations**, tap **Upgrade**.

   Result: The **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens.

2. Select a plan, or tap **Restore Purchases**.

### If a destination receives changes only while WalletFeed is open

**Background Sync** is off.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Sync** section, set **Background Sync** to on.

For more information, refer to [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/).

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/export-csv/ -->
# Make a CSV file with Export CSV

In WalletFeed, **Export CSV** makes a CSV file of your Apple Card transactions from a period that you select. You can save the file in Files or send it to a different app. [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/) is not necessary for **Export CSV**.

## Save your transactions in a CSV file

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.

   ![The Transactions screen with the gear button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/export-csv/walletfeed-transactions.webp)

3. In the **Data** section, tap **Export CSV**.

   ![The Settings screen with Export CSV in the Data section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/export-csv/walletfeed-settings-3.webp)

4. Tap **Range**.
5. Select a period.

   ![The Export CSV screen shows This Month in Range, 29 in Transactions and the Export button.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/export-csv/walletfeed-export-csv.webp)

   **Transactions** shows the number of transactions in the period.

6. Tap **Export**.

   The iOS menu opens with the name of the file, for example `Apple Card This Month.csv`.

7. Tap **Save to Files**.
8. Select a folder.
9. Tap **Save**.

At step 7, you can also select AirDrop, Mail or a different app in the menu. The file goes only to the app or person that you select.

## Periods in Range
