When you open **Export CSV**, **Range** shows **This Month**. You can select one of these periods:

| Period | Transactions in the file |
| --- | --- |
| **This Month** | The transactions from the first day of this month. |
| **Last Month** | All the transactions of the month before this month. |
| **Last 90 Days** | The transactions from the last 90 days. |
| **This Year** | The transactions from January 1 of this year. |
| **All** | All the transactions that WalletFeed can read in Wallet. |

## The file

The name of the file has the period in it, for example `Apple Card Last Month.csv` or `Apple Card All.csv`. Each file name starts with `Apple Card`. But a file can also have Apple Cash or Savings transactions.

The file has the transactions from each Wallet account that WalletFeed can read. The **Account** column shows the account of each transaction. [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/) tells you how to change the accounts that WalletFeed can read.

The first row has the names of the columns. Each row after it has one transaction. The rows are in date sequence. The newest transaction is first. The file also has pending transactions.

The file does not change after WalletFeed makes it. For new transactions, or for a pending charge after it posts, you must make a new file.

WalletFeed makes the file on your iPhone and does not keep it. You can open the file in [Numbers](/guides/apple-card-to-numbers/) or [Excel](/guides/apple-card-to-excel/).

## Columns in the file

The file has these columns, from left to right:

| Column | Data |
| --- | --- |
| **Date** | The date of the transaction in the time zone of your iPhone, for example 2026-10-28. |
| **Posted Date** | The date when the transaction posted. This cell is empty until the transaction posts. |
| **Merchant** | The name of the merchant. If Wallet has no merchant name, this cell has the text from **Description**. |
| **Description** | The text of the transaction in Wallet. |
| **Original Description** | The text of the transaction on the card statement. |
| **Amount** | The value, for example -23.40. The value of a `debit` is less than zero. The value of a `credit` is more than zero. |
| **Currency** | The currency code, for example USD. |
| **Direction** | `debit` or `credit`. For example, purchases and fees are `debit`, and payments and refunds are `credit`. |
| **Status** | The status in Wallet, for example `pending` or `authorized` before the charge posts, `booked` after it posts, or `rejected` for a declined charge. |
| **Type** | The type of transaction in Wallet, for example `pointOfSale` for a purchase, `refund`, `transfer` or `fee`. |
| **Category** | The WalletFeed category, for example Groceries, Travel or Cash & Transfers. |
| **MCC** | The merchant category code, for example 5411. If Wallet has no code, this cell is empty. |
| **Account** | The name of the Wallet account, for example Apple Card. |
| **Foreign Amount** | For a transaction in a different currency, the value in this currency. |
| **Foreign Currency** | The code of the currency in **Foreign Amount**. |
| **WalletFeed ID** | The ID of the transaction. A transaction has the same ID in each file from **Export CSV**. |

Each value in **Amount** and **Foreign Amount** has two digits after the decimal point and no commas, for example 1250.00. The file is UTF-8 text in the RFC 4180 CSV format.

If the first character in **Merchant**, **Description**, **Original Description** or **Account** is `=`, `+`, `-` or `@`, WalletFeed puts an apostrophe (`'`) before this character. Thus, a spreadsheet does not use the text as a formula.

## Get a file that WalletFeed updates

With [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), WalletFeed can save your transactions in a [CSV file in a folder](/guides/apple-card-to-csv/). This file has the same columns. WalletFeed then updates the file when your transactions change. [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) gives the times of these updates.

WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.

## If there is a problem

### If you cannot tap **Export**

You cannot tap **Export** while WalletFeed reads your transactions, or when the period has no transactions.

1. Wait until **Transactions** shows a number.
2. If the number is 0, select a different period in **Range**.

### If each period has 0 transactions

WalletFeed cannot read the transactions of your Wallet accounts.

If **Settings** › **Wallet** in WalletFeed shows **Choose Accounts**, do these steps:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings**.
2. In the **Wallet** section, tap **Choose Accounts**.

   The Wallet access screen opens.

3. Select the accounts that WalletFeed reads.
4. Tap **Share**.

If **Settings** › **Wallet** in WalletFeed shows **Open Settings**, do these steps:

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts that WalletFeed reads.
4. Open WalletFeed.

[Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/) gives all the steps.

### If the file has sample transactions

When **Sample Data** is on, WalletFeed shows two months of sample transactions. The file then has only sample transactions.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings**.
2. In the **Data** section, set **Sample Data** to off.
3. Tap **Export CSV**.
4. Select the period in **Range**.
5. Tap **Export**.

### If the file does not have a new transaction

The file does not change after WalletFeed makes it.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings**.
2. In the **Data** section, tap **Export CSV**.
3. Select the period in **Range**.
4. Tap **Export**.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/get-started/ -->
# First steps with WalletFeed

WalletFeed shows the transactions from your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings accounts on your iPhone. To start, you open WalletFeed and select the Wallet accounts that it can read.

## Before you start

WalletFeed is available only in the US. You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- An Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account in Wallet on the iPhone
- WalletFeed on the iPhone (from the App Store).

If you do not have an Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account, refer to [Use WalletFeed with sample transactions](#use-walletfeed-with-sample-transactions).

## Open WalletFeed for the first time

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.

   The **Welcome to WalletFeed** screen opens. This screen tells you about **Ask Spending**, **Destinations**, **On-Device Privacy** and **Background Sync**. If Apple Intelligence is not available on your iPhone, the first item is **Spending and Search**.

   ![The Welcome to WalletFeed screen with the Continue button at the bottom.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/get-started/walletfeed-welcome.webp)

2. Tap **Continue**.

   **Transactions** opens, and iOS shows a message with the buttons **Don't Allow** and **Select Accounts**.

## Select the Wallet accounts for WalletFeed

After you give WalletFeed access to your accounts or tap **Don't Allow**, iOS does not show the message with **Select Accounts** again. Then you can change the accounts for WalletFeed only in the Settings app.

1. Tap **Select Accounts**.

   The list of Wallet accounts opens.

2. Select the accounts for WalletFeed (for example, your Apple Card).

   You can also select a start date for each account. WalletFeed can read only the transactions that occur on or after that date.

3. Tap the **Share with** button.

   **Transactions** shows the transactions from the accounts that you selected.

If you tap **Don't Allow**, **Transactions** shows **Wallet Access Off**. To let WalletFeed read Wallet after that, refer to [If Transactions shows "Wallet Access Off"](#if-transactions-shows-wallet-access-off).

If you tap **Cancel** in the list of Wallet accounts, **Transactions** shows **No Cards**. To select the accounts again, refer to [If Transactions shows "No Cards"](#if-transactions-shows-no-cards).

> **Note:** WalletFeed reads your transactions from Wallet on your iPhone, but it does not keep these transactions. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers.

## Look at your transactions

**Transactions** shows your transactions below the name of each month. The newest transactions are at the top.

![The Transactions screen with the October transactions and the tabs at the bottom of the screen.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/get-started/walletfeed-transactions.webp)

Each row shows the merchant and the amount. The day is below the amount. Below the merchant, a row can also show "Pending". If a transaction is not from the account that has the most transactions, its row also shows the account name (for example, Apple Cash).

At the end of the list, WalletFeed shows the date of the first transaction that it can read. To let WalletFeed read the transactions from before that date, refer to [Change the accounts that WalletFeed reads](/docs/wallet-accounts/#change-the-accounts-that-walletfeed-reads).

## Use the other tabs

The tabs and the search button at the bottom of the screen open the other parts of WalletFeed:

- The [**Spending**](/docs/spending/) tab shows the total amount of your purchases this month, for each day, category and merchant.
- The [**Destinations**](/docs/destinations/) tab shows the destinations that receive your transactions from WalletFeed (for example, a budget app or a spreadsheet).
- The search button opens [**Search**](/docs/search/). Search finds the transactions that have the merchant or the amount that you type.

You can use Spending, [Ask Spending](/docs/ask-spending/), Search, [Recurring Charges](/docs/recurring-charges/), the [Spending widget](/docs/spending-widget/) and [CSV export](/docs/export-csv/) without [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/). To send transactions to a destination, you must have WalletFeed Pro. WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.

## Use WalletFeed with sample transactions

If you do not have an Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account, you can use WalletFeed with sample transactions. WalletFeed shows **Sample Data** in **Settings** only if you have no destinations or if **Sample Data** is on.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. Scroll to the **Data** section.
3. Set **Sample Data** to on.
4. Tap **Done**.

   **Transactions** shows two months of sample transactions. It does not show the transactions from your Wallet.

When you set **Sample Data** to off, WalletFeed shows the transactions from your Wallet again.

## Correct problems with Wallet accounts

### If Transactions shows "Wallet Access Off"

WalletFeed cannot read your Wallet accounts. This problem occurs after you tap **Don't Allow**, or after you remove the Wallet access for WalletFeed in the Settings app.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts for WalletFeed.
4. Open WalletFeed again.

   **Transactions** shows your transactions.

### If Transactions shows "No Cards"

You did not give WalletFeed access to your Wallet accounts, and you did not tap **Don't Allow**. This problem occurs after you tap **Cancel** in the list of Wallet accounts.

1. In **Transactions**, tap **Choose Accounts**.
2. Do the steps in [Select the Wallet accounts for WalletFeed](#select-the-wallet-accounts-for-walletfeed).

### If Transactions shows "No Transactions"

WalletFeed can read Wallet, but it finds no transactions in the accounts that you selected.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select more Wallet accounts for WalletFeed.
4. Open WalletFeed again.

### If Transactions shows "Wallet Unavailable"

On this iPhone, WalletFeed cannot read transactions from Wallet. Below **Wallet Unavailable**, WalletFeed shows "This iPhone can't share Wallet data." To use WalletFeed without Wallet data, refer to [Use WalletFeed with sample transactions](#use-walletfeed-with-sample-transactions).

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/ -->
# WalletFeed User Guide

How to use each part of WalletFeed on your iPhone.

- [First steps with WalletFeed](https://walletfeed.app/docs/get-started/index.md): Open WalletFeed on your iPhone for the first time and select the Wallet accounts that it can read. Then look at your Apple Card transactions.
- [Select the Wallet accounts that WalletFeed reads](https://walletfeed.app/docs/wallet-accounts/index.md): Give WalletFeed access to your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account on your iPhone. Change the accounts and their start dates in the Settings app.
- [Transactions](https://walletfeed.app/docs/transactions/index.md): WalletFeed shows your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions on your iPhone. The list shows pending charges and refunds in month sections.
- [Spending](https://walletfeed.app/docs/spending/index.md): Spending in WalletFeed shows the total of your Apple Card and Apple Cash purchases this month. It also shows the totals by day, category and merchant.
- [Ask Spending with Apple Intelligence](https://walletfeed.app/docs/ask-spending/index.md): In Ask Spending, you type text about your Apple Card transactions, for example "Dining this month vs last". WalletFeed shows a chart, a list and a summary.
- [Search](https://walletfeed.app/docs/search/index.md): Find your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions with Search in WalletFeed. Type a merchant name or an amount, or use Apple Intelligence.
- [Recurring Charges and alerts](https://walletfeed.app/docs/recurring-charges/index.md): WalletFeed finds the recurring charges on your Apple Card, such as subscriptions. It can send a notification for a new recurring charge or a price change.
- [Spending widget](https://walletfeed.app/docs/spending-widget/index.md): Put the WalletFeed Spending widget on your iPhone Home Screen or Lock Screen. It shows the This Month total and the Same Point Last Month total.
- [Make a CSV file with Export CSV](https://walletfeed.app/docs/export-csv/index.md): Make a CSV file of your Apple Card transactions on your iPhone with Export CSV in WalletFeed. You select a period, then you save or send the file.
- [Siri and Shortcuts](https://walletfeed.app/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/index.md): Use Siri and the Shortcuts app with WalletFeed on your iPhone to open Spending, find transactions and send Apple Card transactions to destinations.
- [WalletFeed Pro](https://walletfeed.app/docs/walletfeed-pro/index.md): WalletFeed Pro lets WalletFeed send your Apple Card transactions to destinations. This page gives the prices and tells you how to change or cancel a plan.
- [Destinations](https://walletfeed.app/docs/destinations/index.md): WalletFeed sends your Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to an app, a spreadsheet or a file. You can add, change, stop and remove destinations.
- [Filter the transactions for a destination](https://walletfeed.app/docs/choose-what-to-send/index.md): A WalletFeed filter selects the Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions that a destination receives, by account, category, merchant or amount.
- [Background Sync](https://walletfeed.app/docs/background-sync/index.md): Background Sync sends your Apple Card transactions to your destinations while WalletFeed is not open. Automations in Shortcuts can also send them.
- [Send previous transactions](https://walletfeed.app/docs/send-history/index.md): Send History sends your previous Apple Card transactions to a WalletFeed destination. Initial History sets the start date of new destinations.
- [Privacy and security](https://walletfeed.app/docs/privacy-and-security/index.md): This page about WalletFeed privacy and security tells you which data WalletFeed keeps and sends, and how to lock the app with Face ID.
- [Troubleshooting](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/index.md): The steps on this page correct problems with WalletFeed, for example missing cards, "Authentication failed", "Sync Stopped" and copies of transactions.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/privacy-and-security/ -->
# Privacy and security

WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. It reads your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from Wallet on your iPhone. It sends them directly from your iPhone to the [destinations](/docs/destinations/) that you add. For the full text, refer to the [WalletFeed privacy policy](/privacy/).

## Data that WalletFeed keeps

WalletFeed keeps your transactions in memory only while it uses them. It does not save a copy of them.

WalletFeed keeps some settings and status data:

- Your settings and the settings of each destination stay on your iPhone. These include the name and the [filter](/docs/choose-what-to-send/) of each destination.
- The keys, webhook addresses and sign-ins of your destinations stay in the Keychain on your iPhone. iOS encrypts the Keychain. These items do not go to iCloud Keychain or to your other devices.
- No person at WalletFeed can see or get your keys. Your iPhone sends each key only to its service.
- The status of each destination contains no transaction data. For example, the status gives the **Last Sync** time and the number of changes that WalletFeed sent.
- WalletFeed keeps two totals for the [Spending widget](/docs/spending-widget/), one for this month and one for the same days of last month. The widget shows these totals, and iOS keeps a copy of them.

## Data that WalletFeed sends

WalletFeed sends your transactions only to the destinations and apps that you select:

- A service that you connect (for example, Lunch Money or Notion) receives the transactions directly from your iPhone through HTTPS.
- A Files destination saves the transactions in a folder that you select (for example, a folder in iCloud Drive).
- A CSV file from [Export CSV](/docs/export-csv/) goes only to the app that you select in the iOS menu.
- When a [shortcut](/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/) or Siri uses **Get Recent Card Transactions**, WalletFeed gives your transactions to that shortcut or to Siri.

If you tell Siri to show Spending or to do a search in WalletFeed, Siri opens WalletFeed. Siri receives none of your transactions.

Before a new destination receives transactions, WalletFeed shows a message, for example "Send Transactions to Lunch Money?". The message tells you which data the destination will receive, from which accounts and from which date. For a service, the message also tells you "It keeps what it receives." WalletFeed does not send data until you tap **Send**. For a Files destination, the button is **Save**. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the destination.

After a service receives your data, the terms and the privacy policy of that service are applicable to the data. If you delete a destination, WalletFeed does not send more data to it. But WalletFeed cannot delete the data that the destination received.

## Apple Intelligence

If Apple Intelligence is available on your iPhone, WalletFeed uses it for these features:

- The [Monthly Summary](/docs/spending/) and the summary of each result in [Ask Spending](/docs/ask-spending/)
- Your searches, the text that you type in Ask Spending, and the rules that you write for a destination filter
- The names of your [recurring charges](/docs/recurring-charges/).

Apple Intelligence operates on your iPhone. For these features, WalletFeed does not send data to a server. To read your text, Apple Intelligence gets only the words that you type or speak. To give names to recurring charges, it gets only the merchant names.

WalletFeed calculates all the charts, totals and lists. Apple Intelligence can write an incorrect number in a summary. If a summary and the totals on the screen are different, the totals are correct.

WalletFeed does not keep the text that Apple Intelligence writes. It keeps only the filter that Apple Intelligence makes from a rule.

## Stop the Apple Intelligence summaries

**Settings** shows **Summarize Spending** only if Apple Intelligence is available on your iPhone. If it is not available, WalletFeed does not write these summaries.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Privacy & Security** section, set **Summarize Spending** to off.

   ![The Settings screen in WalletFeed, with Require Face ID, Summarize Spending and Privacy in the Privacy & Security section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/privacy-and-security/walletfeed-settings-2.webp)

4. Tap **Done**.

After you set **Summarize Spending** to off, Apple Intelligence does not write the Monthly Summary or the summary of each result in Ask Spending. But Apple Intelligence continues to read the text that you send in Ask Spending.

## Lock WalletFeed with Face ID

You can lock WalletFeed with Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode. The label in **Settings** changes with the type of iPhone:

- On an iPhone with Face ID, the label is **Require Face ID**.
- On an iPhone with Touch ID, the label is **Require Touch ID**.
- On an iPhone without Face ID or Touch ID, the label is **Require Passcode**.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Privacy & Security** section, set **Require Face ID** (or **Require Touch ID** or **Require Passcode**) to on.

   ![The Settings screen in WalletFeed, with the Require Face ID switch in the Privacy & Security section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/privacy-and-security/walletfeed-settings-2.webp)

4. Use Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode.

   If Face ID does not identify you, **Require Face ID** stays off.

5. Tap **Done**.

WalletFeed locks each time that you close it or go to a different app. When you open WalletFeed again, it starts Face ID one time.

If Face ID does not identify you, tap **Unlock** to try again.

If you set **Require Face ID** to off, WalletFeed does not lock.

## Screen protection

In these conditions, your iPhone does not show your transactions or amounts:

- When WalletFeed is not the active app, it puts a cover on its screen. Thus, the app switcher does not show your transactions.
- While you record the screen of your iPhone, or show it on a different screen, WalletFeed does not show your transactions or amounts.
- While your iPhone is locked, iOS can show the Spending widget without its amounts.

## Notifications

If you set **Recurring Charge Alerts** to on in **Settings**, WalletFeed finds new and changed recurring charges on your iPhone. Then WalletFeed shows a notification with the name and the amounts of the charge. Notification Center keeps the notification until you clear it.

A **Remind If Sync Stops** notification contains no transaction data.

## Analytics and purchases

WalletFeed has no analytics, advertisements or third-party SDKs (code from other companies). It does not monitor you in different apps or on websites.

If you let Apple give analytics data to app developers (in the Settings app), Apple can give crash reports to the developer of WalletFeed.

Apple processes the purchases of [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/). WalletFeed does not receive your payment information.

## Delete a destination

When you delete a destination, WalletFeed erases its settings, its key and its status from your iPhone.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations** at the bottom of the screen.
3. Tap the destination.
4. Tap **Delete**.

   ![The screen of a Lunch Money destination, with Delete at the bottom.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/privacy-and-security/walletfeed-destination-detail.webp)

5. In the message, tap **Delete** again.

The message tells you "Transactions already sent stay at the destination." WalletFeed cannot delete these transactions.

## Remove all destinations

**Settings** shows **Remove All Destinations** only if you have a destination.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Data** section, tap **Remove All Destinations**.

   ![The Settings screen in WalletFeed, with Export CSV and Remove All Destinations in the Data section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/privacy-and-security/walletfeed-settings-3.webp)

4. In the message, tap **Remove All**.

WalletFeed erases the settings, the keys and the status of all your destinations from your iPhone. The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay at each destination.

## Change the Wallet accounts that WalletFeed reads

To remove an account from WalletFeed, deselect it in the Settings app. Refer to [Change the accounts that WalletFeed reads](/docs/wallet-accounts/#change-the-accounts-that-walletfeed-reads).

If WalletFeed cannot get access to Wallet, it erases the totals of the Spending widget the next time that it operates.

## Data after you delete WalletFeed

When you delete WalletFeed, iOS removes the settings of WalletFeed and the status of your destinations. But the WalletFeed items in the Keychain can stay on your iPhone. If you install WalletFeed again, it erases these items when it opens for the first time.

## Read the privacy statement in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Privacy & Security** section, tap **Privacy**.

   ![The Privacy screen in WalletFeed, with the Wallet data and Data on your iPhone sections.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/privacy-and-security/walletfeed-privacy.webp)

In the **About** section of **Settings**, **Privacy Policy** opens the [privacy policy](/privacy/) on this website.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/recurring-charges/ -->
# Recurring Charges and alerts

WalletFeed finds the recurring charges on your Apple Card, such as subscriptions and bills, and shows them on the [Spending](/docs/spending/) screen. Recurring Charge Alerts can send you a notification when a new recurring charge starts, or when the price of a recurring charge changes.

[WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/) is not necessary for Recurring Charges or for Recurring Charge Alerts.

## Find your recurring charges

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Spending**.
3. Scroll to **Recurring Charges**.

   ![The Recurring Charges section of the Spending screen shows PG&E, Netflix and Spotify, with the price of each charge.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/recurring-charges/walletfeed-recurring.webp)

Each row in the list shows these items:

- An icon for the category of the charge
- The name of the charge
- The word **Monthly** or **Weekly**
- The price of the last charge.

With Apple Intelligence, the row can show the type of service before **Monthly** or **Weekly**, for example **Streaming · Monthly**.

The first charge in the list has the largest total for one month. For a **Weekly** charge, this total is approximately 4.3 times the price of the last charge.

If WalletFeed finds no recurring charges, **Spending** does not show the **Recurring Charges** section.

## Rules for a recurring charge

WalletFeed reads your transactions from this month and from the two months before it. WalletFeed puts the charges from one merchant in **Recurring Charges** in these conditions:

- All the charges have the same merchant name. For example, “Netflix.com” and “NETFLIX.COM” are the same merchant.
- The price of each charge is not more than 15% different from the price of the last charge.
- For **Monthly**, there are two or more charges. Each charge is 26 to 35 days after the charge before it.
- For **Weekly**, there are three or more charges. Each charge is 6 to 8 days after the charge before it.

For example, if a month between two charges has no charge from the merchant, **Recurring Charges** does not show the merchant.

These transactions are not in **Recurring Charges**:

- Refunds, transfers, bill payments and declined transactions
- Apple Card Monthly Installments (**Spending** shows them in the **Monthly Installments** section)
- Charges that occur each year (WalletFeed finds only **Monthly** and **Weekly** charges).

## Names from Apple Intelligence

For names from Apple Intelligence, you must have an iPhone that can use Apple Intelligence. Apple Intelligence must be active on that iPhone.

Wallet can show a merchant name such as “NETFLIX.COM 866-579”. With Apple Intelligence, WalletFeed shows a short name, such as Netflix. WalletFeed can also show a type of service, such as **Streaming**. When the list has names from Apple Intelligence, WalletFeed shows **Apple Intelligence suggested these names.** below the list.

WalletFeed uses a name only if the first word of the name is in the merchant name from Wallet. WalletFeed gets names for only the first 12 charges in the list. If a charge has no name from Apple Intelligence, the row shows the merchant name from Wallet.

## Activate Recurring Charge Alerts

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Notifications** section, set the **Recurring Charge Alerts** switch to on.

   ![The WalletFeed Settings screen with the Recurring Charge Alerts switch in the Notifications section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/recurring-charges/walletfeed-settings.webp)

4. If iOS shows a message about notifications, tap **Allow**.

   If you do not let WalletFeed send notifications, the switch stays off.

5. Tap **Done**.

When you set the **Recurring Charge Alerts** switch to on, WalletFeed sends no notifications for the charges that are in Wallet at that time. You get notifications only for new charges.

## Notifications for recurring charges

WalletFeed sends a notification for these changes:

| Change | Title of the notification | Text of the notification |
|---|---|---|
| A charge becomes a recurring charge | “Netflix repeats monthly” or “Netflix repeats weekly” | “$15.49 each month” or “$15.49 each week” |
| The price of a recurring charge increases | “Netflix costs more” | “$17.99, up from $15.49” |
| The price of a recurring charge decreases | “Netflix costs less” | “$15.49, down from $17.99” |

WalletFeed sends a notification about a price change only in these conditions:

- The charges from the merchant were in **Recurring Charges** before the new charge.
- The new charge is 26 to 35 days after the charge before it (6 to 8 days for a **Weekly** charge).
- The new price is more than 2% different from the price before it.

After a price change of more than 15%, WalletFeed can remove the charge from **Recurring Charges**. WalletFeed shows the charge again when each price in the three months that WalletFeed reads is not more than 15% different from the new price.

WalletFeed sends a notification only for a charge from the last 7 days. It sends only one notification for each charge. The notification uses the name from Apple Intelligence. If the charge has no name from Apple Intelligence, the notification uses the merchant name from Wallet.

When you open WalletFeed, it reads your transactions and sends the new notifications. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. **Background Sync** is not necessary for these notifications.

## Stop Recurring Charge Alerts

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Notifications** section, set the **Recurring Charge Alerts** switch to off.
4. Tap **Done**.

## Privacy

WalletFeed finds your recurring charges on your iPhone. Each time that it does this, it reads your transactions from Wallet. WalletFeed does not keep a copy of your transactions.

To give names to the charges, Apple Intelligence gets only the merchant names. Apple Intelligence makes the names on your iPhone. WalletFeed sends nothing to a server.

For Recurring Charge Alerts, WalletFeed keeps only transaction IDs. It keeps no prices and no merchant names.

A notification shows the name of the charge and its prices. Notification Center keeps the notification until you remove it. When notification previews are off, iOS does not show the text of the notification on the Lock Screen.

For more information, refer to the [WalletFeed privacy policy](/privacy/).

## If there is a problem

### If a new subscription is not in Recurring Charges

WalletFeed shows a **Monthly** charge only after the second charge from the merchant. It shows a **Weekly** charge only after the third charge.

1. When Wallet shows the next charge from the merchant, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Spending**.
3. If **Recurring Charges** does not show the charge, refer to [Rules for a recurring charge](#rules-for-a-recurring-charge).

### If the Recurring Charge Alerts switch does not stay on

iOS does not let WalletFeed send notifications.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Notifications** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Set the **Allow Notifications** switch to on.
4. Open WalletFeed.
5. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
6. In the **Notifications** section, set the **Recurring Charge Alerts** switch to on.

### If you get no notification

WalletFeed sends a notification only for a new recurring charge or a price change from the last 7 days.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. Make sure that the **Recurring Charge Alerts** switch is on.
4. If the switch is on, open the Settings app on your iPhone.
5. Tap **Notifications** › **WalletFeed**.
6. Make sure that the **Allow Notifications** switch is on.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/search/ -->
# Search

Search in WalletFeed finds your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions. You type a part of a merchant name, a description, a category or an amount. Search then shows each transaction that has your text. With Apple Intelligence, Search can also make filters from your text, for example from `Dining over $50 last month`. You can use Search without [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).

Search uses the transactions of the [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/) that WalletFeed can read. When you open Search, WalletFeed reads these transactions on your iPhone. WalletFeed does not store these transactions.

## Find a transaction

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap the search button at the bottom of the screen.

   ![The Transactions screen, with the tab bar and the search button at the bottom of the screen.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/search/walletfeed-transactions.webp)

   Search shows the search field and the keyboard.

3. Type a part of a merchant name, a category or an amount, for example `Uber`, `Dining` or `23.40`.

   Search shows the results while you type.

Search finds the same transactions for `uber`, `Uber` and `UBER`.

The results are in one section for each month. [Transactions](/docs/transactions/) has the same sections.

To type different text, tap the clear button in the search field. To close Search, tap the close button (X). Then WalletFeed shows the tab that you used before you opened Search.

## Find transactions in a category

When the search field is empty, Search shows **Categories**. This list has the categories of your transactions.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap the search button at the bottom of the screen.
3. If the search field has text, tap the clear button in the search field.
4. In **Categories**, tap a category, for example **Groceries**.

   Search puts the name of the category in the search field and shows the results.

## Find transactions with Apple Intelligence

Search with Apple Intelligence reads your text and makes filters from it. For example, `Dining over $50 last month` gives the filters **Dining · Over $50.00 · Last month**. Search with Apple Intelligence is available only if your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence and Apple Intelligence is active. On these iPhones, the empty search field shows **Dining over $50 last month** as an example.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap the search button at the bottom of the screen.
3. Type a category, a merchant name, an amount or a period, for example `Dining over $50 last month`.

   While you type, Search shows the transactions that have your text. If no transaction has your text, Search shows **Tap Search to use Apple Intelligence.**

4. Tap **Search** on the keyboard.

   While Apple Intelligence reads your text, Search shows the Apple Intelligence icon and a progress indicator above the results.

   ![The Search screen with the filters Groceries, Over $50.00 and Last 30 days, and a row with 4 transactions and a total amount of $277.57.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/search/walletfeed-search.webp)

At the top of the results, Search shows the filters that Apple Intelligence found in your text, for example **Groceries · Over $50.00 · Last 30 days**. Below the filters, a row shows the number of transactions and their total amount. If Search finds no transactions for the filters, the row shows **0 transactions** and $0.00.

Apple Intelligence can find these filters in your text:

- One or more categories, for example **Dining** or **Groceries**
- A merchant, for example `Uber`
- Only purchases (**Purchases**), or only money that you received (**Money in**)
- An amount with `over` or `under`, for example `over $50`
- One period (**Last 7 days**, **Last 30 days**, **This month** or **Last month**).

A word that is not a category name can also give a category. For example, `restaurants` gives **Dining**, and `gas` gives **Fuel**.

WalletFeed uses a merchant or an amount only if it is in your text. If Apple Intelligence gives a different merchant or amount, or cannot read your text, Search shows **Couldn't read this search. Showing text matches.** Then the list shows the transactions that have your text.

To find a merchant, WalletFeed uses only the letters and numbers in your text. Uppercase letters and accents do not change the result. WalletFeed also finds the merchant if your text adds "s" or "es" to the end of the name. For example, `Ubers` finds Uber, and `trader joes` finds Trader Joe's.

WalletFeed calculates the number of transactions and the total amount. Apple Intelligence does not calculate them.

For **Money in**, the total amount is the money that you received. For the other filters, WalletFeed adds the amounts of your purchases. Refunds decrease the total amount. Payments and transfers do not change it.

When you change the text, WalletFeed removes the filters.

To use Apple Intelligence again, tap **Search** on the keyboard.

> **Note:** Apple Intelligence reads your text on your iPhone and receives only this text. Your transactions do not go to Apple Intelligence.

## Open Search with Siri

1. On your iPhone, start Siri.
2. Tell Siri "Search WalletFeed" or "Find a transaction in WalletFeed".

   You hear "What are you looking for?"

3. Tell Siri the transactions to find, for example "dining over $50 last month".

   Search opens with your text in the search field. If Search with Apple Intelligence is available, Apple Intelligence then reads the text.

Siri does not receive your transactions or the total amount. Only WalletFeed shows them.

In the Shortcuts app, the name of this action is **Search Transactions**. For more information, refer to [Siri and Shortcuts](/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/).

## If there is a problem

### If Search shows **No Cards**

You did not tap **Share** or **Don't Share** on the **Share Wallet Data** screen.

1. Tap **Choose Accounts**.

   The **Share Wallet Data** screen opens.

2. Select the accounts that WalletFeed can read.

   ![The Share Wallet Data screen, with the switches for Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings set to on.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/search/walletfeed-wallet-access.webp)

3. Tap **Share**.

### If Search shows **Wallet Access Off**

You tapped **Don't Share**, or you stopped Wallet access for WalletFeed in the Settings app. After you tap **Share** or **Don't Share**, iOS does not show the **Share Wallet Data** screen again.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts that WalletFeed can read.
4. Open WalletFeed again.

### If Search shows **No Results for “…”**

No transaction has your text in its merchant name, description, category or amount.

1. Make sure that your text is correct.
2. Type shorter text, for example only the first part of the merchant name.
3. If Search shows **Tap Search to use Apple Intelligence.**, tap **Search** on the keyboard.

### If Apple Intelligence does not read your text

Apple Intelligence reads only text that has 2 to 200 characters. If the empty search field shows **Transactions**, Search with Apple Intelligence is not available on your iPhone.

1. Make sure that your text has 2 to 200 characters.
2. Tap **Search** on the keyboard.

If the empty search field shows **Transactions**, do these steps:

1. Make sure that your iPhone model is on the list in [Get started with the next generation of Apple Intelligence](https://support.apple.com/en-us/121115).
2. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
3. Tap **Apple Intelligence & Siri**.
4. Set **Apple Intelligence** to on, or tap **Turn on Apple Intelligence**.
5. Open WalletFeed again.

### If Search shows **Couldn't read this search. Showing text matches.**

In your text, Apple Intelligence did not find filters that WalletFeed can use. Search then shows the transactions that have your text.

1. Type shorter text that has a category, a merchant name, an amount or a period, for example `groceries this month`.
2. Tap **Search** on the keyboard.

### If a transaction is not in the results

Search finds only the transactions of the Wallet accounts that WalletFeed can read. Wallet gives WalletFeed the transactions of each account from the start date that you selected.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Change the accounts that WalletFeed can read, or their start dates.
4. Open WalletFeed again.
5. Type your text in the search field again.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/send-history/ -->
# Send previous transactions

A WalletFeed [destination](/docs/destinations/) can receive your previous Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions. In WalletFeed, **Initial History** sets the start date of each new destination. **Send History** sends previous transactions to one of your destinations.

Destinations and **Send History** are part of [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/). WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase. If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, **Send History** opens the **WalletFeed Pro** screen.

## Set the start date for new destinations

A new destination receives your transactions from the date that **Initial History** sets. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. If you change **Initial History**, only the destinations that you add after the change use the new period.

WalletFeed shows the **Sync** section only if you have WalletFeed Pro.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Sync** section, tap **Initial History**.

   ![The WalletFeed Settings screen with All for Initial History in the Sync section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/send-history/walletfeed-settings.webp)

3. Select a period.
4. Tap **Done**.

These are the periods of **Initial History**:

| Period | A new destination receives |
| --- | --- |
| **Today** | The transactions from the day that you add the destination. |
| **30 Days** | The transactions from the last 30 days. |
| **90 Days** | The transactions from the last 90 days. |
| **1 Year** | The transactions from the last 12 months. |
| **All** | All the transactions that WalletFeed can read. |

Each transaction starts a Zap in Zapier, uses a credit in Make and becomes an issue in Linear. Thus, a new Zapier, Make or Linear destination receives a maximum of 30 days of previous transactions. **Send History** can send previous transactions to these destinations.

WalletFeed can read only the Wallet accounts and the period that you select in iOS. You can change them in the Settings app, in **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.

## Send to a new destination

Before a new destination receives transactions, WalletFeed shows a message. The message tells you the data that the destination will receive, the Wallet accounts and the start date.

1. To add the destination, do the steps in [Add a destination](/docs/destinations/#add-a-destination).
2. Read the message, for example **Send Transactions to Lunch Money?**

   If **Initial History** is **All**, the message shows "including earlier ones" and no date. For Zapier, Make and Linear, the message shows the start date.

   For a CSV, OFX or QIF file, the title of the message is **Save Transactions to Files?**, and the button is **Save**.

3. Tap **Send** or **Save**.

WalletFeed then sends your transactions to the destination. It sends the newest transactions first.

If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the new destination and does not send transactions to it.

## Send previous transactions to a destination

You can also send the transactions of a period to a destination that you added, for example after you change its [filter](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations** at the bottom of the screen.
2. Tap the destination.

   ![The Destinations tab with Lunch Money, Budget 2026, Monthly CSV and n8n.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/send-history/walletfeed-destinations.webp)

3. Tap **Send History**.

   ![The Lunch Money destination screen, with Send History below Filter.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/send-history/walletfeed-destination-detail.webp)

4. Select **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.
5. If WalletFeed shows a message, for example **Send History to Zapier?**, tap **Send**.

   This message is only for Zapier, Make and Linear. The message tells you the result in the service:

   - "Each transaction runs your Zap."
   - "Each transaction runs your scenario."
   - "Each transaction can become an issue."

   On the Linear Free plan, a workspace can have no more than 250 issues.

WalletFeed then starts to send the history. Above **Send History**, the destination screen shows **Sending History** and a progress bar.

WalletFeed sends all the transactions of the period, and it starts with the newest transactions. It uses the filter of the destination and does not send declined transactions.

The first day of the period also becomes the start date of the destination. Then, WalletFeed sends changes only for the transactions from that date.

If a new transaction occurs while WalletFeed sends the history, WalletFeed sends the new transaction first.

If a Webhook, Zapier, Make, Amazon SQS, Kinesis Data Streams or EventBridge destination has a transaction, it receives a second copy. Other destinations keep one copy of each transaction.

## Monitor the history

While WalletFeed sends the history, the destination screen shows **Sending History** above **Send History**. The screen also shows numbers and a month, for example "2,340 of 5,120 · back to March 2023":

- The first number is the number of transactions that WalletFeed sent. This number also includes the transactions that the destination had and the transactions that the filter does not include.
- The second number is the number of transactions in the period.
- The month tells you that WalletFeed sent all the transactions after a date in that month.

The progress bar shows less than 100% until WalletFeed completes the history. In **Destinations**, the row of the destination shows "Sending history · 46%". When WalletFeed waits or cannot continue the history, the row shows "History paused · 46%".

The destination screen shows one of these items above **Send History**:

| Item | Information |
| --- | --- |
| **Sending History** and numbers | WalletFeed sends the history. |
| "Paused" | WalletFeed does not send the history at this time. For example, **Enabled** is off, or you do not have WalletFeed Pro. |
| "Too many requests.", "Can't connect." or "Server error (502).", then "Trying again in 10 min." | The service has a problem or a limit, or WalletFeed cannot connect to it. WalletFeed tries again at the time that the message shows. |
| An orange exclamation mark, a message and **Try Again** | WalletFeed cannot continue until you correct a problem. The steps are in [Correct a problem with the history](#correct-a-problem-with-the-history). |
| **History** with "All sent" | WalletFeed sent all the transactions. |
| **History** with "Sent from March 3, 2023" | WalletFeed sent all the transactions from that date. |
| **History** with "Stopped" | You tapped **Stop Sending**. |

## History in the background

While WalletFeed is open, it sends the history. When you go to a different app, iOS can let WalletFeed continue in the background. This can occur after you select a period in **Send History**, or after you tap **Send** or **Save** for a new destination.

iOS then shows a Live Activity, for example "Sending history to Lunch Money" with "2,340 of 5,120". If you tap **Cancel** in the Live Activity, or if you close WalletFeed in the app switcher, WalletFeed stops the history for a time. WalletFeed continues the history when you open WalletFeed again, or when iOS starts WalletFeed in the background. The procedure to stop the history is in [Stop the history](#stop-the-history).

iOS can also let WalletFeed send the history while your iPhone charges and you do not use it. For short periods, iOS can start WalletFeed to send the history.

WalletFeed sends the history to each service at a speed that the service accepts. Thus, if a slow service receives a large history, the history can continue for some days.

## Stop the history

WalletFeed shows **Stop Sending** only until it completes the history.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Send History**.
3. Tap **Stop Sending**.

   **History** shows "Stopped".

The destination keeps the transactions that it received. WalletFeed continues to send new transactions to the destination.

To send the history again, select a period in **Send History**.

## Send previous transactions after a filter change

A change to the filter of a destination changes only the transactions that WalletFeed sends after the change.

If the new filter includes more transactions, WalletFeed does not send the previous transactions that the new filter adds. If the new filter does not include some transactions, the destination keeps the transactions that it received before the change.

To send the previous transactions with the new filter, do the steps in [Send previous transactions to a destination](#send-previous-transactions-to-a-destination).

## Correct a problem with the history

### If the history shows "Authentication failed"

The service did not accept the key, token or sign-in of the destination, or the permissions of the key changed.

1. If the message includes "Replace the key.", make a new key in the service. For the steps, refer to the [guide for the destination type](/docs/destinations/#destination-types).
2. In WalletFeed, replace the key of the destination, or connect the destination again. For the steps, refer to [Replace a key or connect again](/docs/destinations/#replace-a-key-or-connect-again).
3. On the destination screen, tap **Try Again**.

WalletFeed also tries again after approximately 1 hour, and then after longer periods of no more than 24 hours. When the service accepts a new transaction from WalletFeed, the history also continues.

### If the history shows "Can't open the folder. Choose it again."

WalletFeed cannot open the folder of the CSV, OFX or QIF file.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Change Folder**.
3. Select the folder.

   The history starts again, and WalletFeed writes the transactions to that folder.

### If the history shows "Check the destination, then try again."

The service rejected the transactions. The message starts with the cause, for example "Rejected (HTTP 404)".

These are some problems that can stop the history:

- On the Airtable Free plan, a base can have no more than 1,000 records.
- If a Make scenario is not active, Make keeps the transactions in a queue. On the Make Free plan, the queue can have no more than 50 items.
- If a Zap is off, Zapier rejects the transactions. Zapier can start to reject them some hours after you set the Zap to off.

1. Correct the problem in the service.
2. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
3. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
4. Tap **Try Again**.

WalletFeed also tries again after approximately 1 hour, and then after longer periods of no more than 24 hours.

### If the history shows "Paused"

WalletFeed does not send the history at this time, for example because **Enabled** is off or you do not have WalletFeed Pro.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Make sure that **Enabled** is on.
3. Make sure that you have WalletFeed Pro. In **Settings**, the **Subscription** section shows your plan.
4. Keep WalletFeed open.

   When WalletFeed continues the history, numbers replace "Paused".

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/ -->
# Siri and Shortcuts

You can use Siri and the Shortcuts app with WalletFeed on your iPhone. Siri can open **Spending** or **Search** in WalletFeed. The WalletFeed actions in Shortcuts can send your Apple Card transactions to your [destinations](/docs/destinations/) or give them to a shortcut.

**Show Spending** and **Search Transactions** operate without WalletFeed Pro. For the actions that send or give your transactions, and for the **Sync Transactions** control, you must have [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/). WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.

## WalletFeed actions

WalletFeed gives these actions to Siri and the Shortcuts app:

| Action | Result | WalletFeed Pro |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Show Spending** | WalletFeed opens **Spending**. | Not necessary |
| **Search Transactions** | WalletFeed opens **Search** with the transactions that you tell Siri to find. | Not necessary |
| **Sync Transactions** | WalletFeed sends new and changed transactions to your destinations. WalletFeed does not open. | Necessary |
| **Sync New Purchase** | WalletFeed sends your last purchase after Wallet records it. WalletFeed does not open. This action is for a **Transaction** automation. | Necessary |
| **Get Recent Card Transactions** | WalletFeed gives your transactions from the last 7 days to the shortcut. You can change the number of days. | Necessary |

## Use Siri with WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, start Siri.
2. Tell Siri one of these instructions:

| Tell Siri | Result |
| --- | --- |
| "Show my spending in WalletFeed" or "Open my spending in WalletFeed" | WalletFeed opens **Spending**. |
| "Search WalletFeed" or "Find a transaction in WalletFeed" | You hear "What are you looking for?" You tell Siri the transactions to find. Then WalletFeed opens **Search**. |
| "Sync WalletFeed" or "Send my card transactions with WalletFeed" | WalletFeed sends new and changed transactions to your destinations. |
| "Get card transactions from WalletFeed" | Siri receives your transactions from the last 7 days. |

When you tell Siri "Sync WalletFeed", WalletFeed does not open. After WalletFeed sends the transactions, Siri gives a message, for example "Changes sent: 3." Refer to [Messages from WalletFeed actions](#messages-from-walletfeed-actions).

## Find transactions with Siri

1. On your iPhone, start Siri.
2. Tell Siri "Search WalletFeed".

   You hear "What are you looking for?"

3. Tell Siri the transactions to find, for example "dining over $50 last month".

   **Search** opens in WalletFeed and shows your instruction in the search field.

   ![The Search screen with the filters Groceries, Over $50.00 and Last 30 days, and 4 transactions with a total of $277.57.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/walletfeed-search.webp)

With Apple Intelligence, WalletFeed reads your instruction on your iPhone. Then **Search** shows the transactions and their total. Search with Apple Intelligence operates only on an iPhone that can use Apple Intelligence, and only when Apple Intelligence is active.

Without Apple Intelligence, **Search** shows the results that you get when you type your instruction in the search field. For more information, refer to [Search](/docs/search/).

## The **Sync Transactions** control

WalletFeed has a control with the name **Sync Transactions**. You can add it to Control Center, the Lock Screen or the Action button. The control shows **Sync**.

When you use the control, WalletFeed opens. With WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed then sends new and changed transactions to your destinations. While WalletFeed is open, your destinations receive changes in seconds.

## Use your transactions in a shortcut

**Get Recent Card Transactions** gives your transactions to the subsequent action in a shortcut. For example, a shortcut can send them to Notes or Mail.

1. On your iPhone, open the Shortcuts app.
2. To make a new shortcut, tap **+**.
3. To change a shortcut that you have, tap **•••** on the shortcut.
4. Tap **Search Actions**.
5. Type WalletFeed in the search field.
6. Tap **Get Recent Card Transactions**.

   The action shows "Get card transactions from the last 7 days".

7. To change the number of days, tap **7**.
8. Type the number of days.
9. Add the actions that use the transactions.

The action gives the transactions of the [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/) that you select for WalletFeed. WalletFeed reads them from Wallet when the action operates. WalletFeed does not keep a copy.

The action gives this information for each transaction:

| Name in Shortcuts | Data |
| --- | --- |
| **Merchant** | The name of the merchant. If Wallet has no merchant name, **Merchant** has the description of the transaction. |
| **Amount** | The value of the transaction, with its currency. This value is more than zero for debits and for credits. |
| **Date** | The date of the transaction. |
| **Category** | The WalletFeed category, for example **Groceries** or **Dining**. |
| **Status** | The status of the transaction in Wallet, for example `pending`, `authorized`, `booked` (posted) or `rejected` (declined). |
| **Credit** | **Credit** shows if the transaction is a credit, for example a refund or a payment. |

## Send transactions with an automation

An automation in the Shortcuts app can send your transactions while WalletFeed is not open. iOS does not let apps make automations. Thus, you make the automation in Shortcuts, with the steps that WalletFeed shows.

If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, **Settings** does not show the **Sync** section. Refer to [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Sync** section, tap **Automations**.

   ![The WalletFeed Settings screen with Background Sync and Automations in the Sync section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/walletfeed-settings.webp)

4. Do the steps in the **After Each Card Tap** section.

   ![The Automations screen with Last Run, Copy Description and Open Shortcuts in the After Each Card Tap section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/walletfeed-automations.webp)

5. If the screen also shows **Every Day**, do the steps in the **Every Day** section.

The steps on the screen are different on iOS 26 and iOS 27. On iOS 27, when Apple Intelligence is active, step 1 is **Copy Description**. You paste the copied text in Shortcuts. Then you make sure that the automation is correct.

On iOS 27, a different procedure is below the steps. It is in **Set It Up Yourself** when Apple Intelligence is active, or in **Describe It Instead** when Apple Intelligence is not active. For the steps of each procedure, refer to [Run a shortcut after each Apple Card purchase](/guides/apple-card-shortcuts/).

The **Automations** screen can show these automations:

| Automation | WalletFeed action | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **After Each Card Tap** | **Sync New Purchase**, in a **Transaction** automation | WalletFeed sends each purchase some seconds after you make it with your iPhone. |
| **Every Day** | **Sync Transactions**, in a **Time of Day** automation | WalletFeed sends the changes that **After Each Card Tap** does not send, for example purchases on the internet and posted charges. |

The **Automations** screen shows **Every Day** only if **Background Sync** is off or **Sample Data** is on. When **Background Sync** is on and WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. Thus, an **After Each Card Tap** automation is not necessary, but you can make one. Refer to [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/).

If you made an **Every Day** automation, it continues to operate when the **Automations** screen does not show **Every Day**.

After **Sync New Purchase** starts, it waits a maximum of 18 seconds for Wallet to record the purchase. If Wallet records the purchase after this time, WalletFeed sends the purchase when it sends changes again.

### **Last Run** and the **Automations** value

On the **Automations** screen, the section of each automation starts with **Last Run**. **Last Run** shows the last time that the action operated, for example "2 hr. ago". If the action did not operate, **Last Run** shows **Never**. For **Every Day**, **Last Run** also changes when you use **Sync Transactions** with Siri or in a different shortcut.

The **Automations** value in **Settings** shows if each automation operated in its period. The period of **After Each Card Tap** is the last 14 days, and the period of **Every Day** is the last 3 days. The value is one of these:

| Value | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| **On** | Each automation on the **Automations** screen operated in its period. |
| **1 of 2** | One of the two automations operated in its period. |
| **Set Up** | No automation operated in its period, and **Background Sync** is off or **Sample Data** is on. |
| **Off** | **Background Sync** is on, **Sample Data** is off, and **After Each Card Tap** did not operate in its period. |

iOS does not tell WalletFeed about your automations. You change or delete an automation in the Shortcuts app.

## Messages from WalletFeed actions

When **Sync Transactions** or **Sync New Purchase** stops, the action gives a message. Siri shows or speaks the message. In an automation, Shortcuts can show the message as a notification. The message is one of these:

| Message | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| "Changes sent: 3." | WalletFeed sent 3 changes. The number is the total for all your destinations. |
| "Nothing new to send." | **Sync Transactions** did not find a new change. |
| "Nothing new yet." | **Sync New Purchase** did not find a new change. |
| "Changes sent: 3. One destination needs attention." | WalletFeed cannot send to one destination. If more destinations have this problem, the message gives the number of destinations. |
| "Sync requires WalletFeed Pro." | WalletFeed Pro is not active on this iPhone. |
| "Open WalletFeed and allow Wallet access." | WalletFeed cannot read your Wallet accounts. |
| "Add a destination in WalletFeed first." | WalletFeed has no destination that is on. |

Without WalletFeed Pro, **Get Recent Card Transactions** shows "This action requires WalletFeed Pro."

## Your data in Siri and Shortcuts

When you use **Show Spending** or **Search Transactions** with Siri, Siri opens WalletFeed. Siri does not receive your transactions or the totals on **Spending**. For **Search Transactions**, Siri receives only your instruction.

**Get Recent Card Transactions** gives your transactions to the shortcut or to Siri. The subsequent actions in the shortcut can send the transactions to different apps.

On your iPhone, WalletFeed records the last time that **Sync Transactions** operated and the last time that **Sync New Purchase** operated. WalletFeed uses these times to show **Last Run** on the **Automations** screen and the **Automations** value in **Settings**.

## If there is a problem

### If **Last Run** shows **Never**

The automation did not start the WalletFeed action on this iPhone.

1. On your iPhone, open the Shortcuts app.
2. Tap **Automation**.

   On iOS 27, the Shortcuts app shows the shortcuts that have an automation trigger.

3. Find the automation.
4. If you cannot find the automation, do the steps in [Send transactions with an automation](#send-transactions-with-an-automation) again.
5. Open the automation.
6. Make sure that the automation starts **Sync New Purchase** or **Sync Transactions**.
7. On iOS 26, make sure that the automation uses **Run Immediately**.
8. On iOS 27, tap the arrow adjacent to the trigger at the top of the shortcut.
9. On iOS 27, make sure that **Confirm Before Run** is off.
10. On iOS 27, tap the information button **ⓘ** › **Privacy**.
11. On iOS 27, make sure that **Allow Running When Locked** is on.

### If the message is "Sync requires WalletFeed Pro."

WalletFeed Pro is not active on this iPhone. When **Get Recent Card Transactions** shows "This action requires WalletFeed Pro.", the cause is the same.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Subscription** section, tap the **WalletFeed Pro** row that shows **Upgrade**.
4. If you have a plan, tap **Restore Purchases** below the plans.
5. If you do not have a plan, get WalletFeed Pro. Refer to [Get WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/#get-walletfeed-pro).

### If the message is "Open WalletFeed and allow Wallet access."

WalletFeed cannot read your Wallet accounts.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Transactions**.
3. If WalletFeed shows **No Cards**, do the steps in [Select the accounts from WalletFeed](/docs/wallet-accounts/#select-the-accounts-from-walletfeed).
4. If WalletFeed shows **Wallet Access Off**, do the steps in [If WalletFeed shows Wallet Access Off](/docs/wallet-accounts/#if-walletfeed-shows-wallet-access-off).

### If the message is "Add a destination in WalletFeed first."

WalletFeed has no destination that is on.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. If there is no destination, do the steps in [Add a destination](/docs/destinations/#add-a-destination).
4. If a destination shows **Off**, tap the destination.
5. Set **Enabled** to on.

### If the message is "Changes sent: 3. One destination needs attention."

WalletFeed cannot send to one or more destinations.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Find the destination that shows a message below its name, for example "Authentication failed".

   ![The Destinations screen with the message Authentication failed and a warning symbol for the n8n destination.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/walletfeed-destinations-failure.webp)

4. Find the message in [If there is a problem](/docs/destinations/#if-there-is-a-problem) on the Destinations page.
5. Do the steps for that message.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/spending-widget/ -->
# Spending widget

The Spending widget shows the total of your purchases for this month on your Home Screen or Lock Screen. You can use the widget without [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/) and without a [destination](/docs/destinations/).

## Totals in the widget

The widget and the [**Spending**](/docs/spending/) tab show the same totals for all the [Wallet accounts that WalletFeed reads](/docs/wallet-accounts/). The **This Month** total is from the first day of this month to the last update. The **Same Point Last Month** total is for the month before this month, from its first day to the same day and time.

The totals include pending purchases. Refunds decrease the totals. Transfers, bill payments and declined transactions are not in the totals.

## Widget shapes

| Widget | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| Small, on the Home Screen | **This Month** and **Same Point Last Month** |
| Medium, on the Home Screen | **This Month**, **Same Point Last Month** and the change |
| On the Lock Screen | **Spending**, this month's total and the change |
| One line on the Lock Screen | This month's total, for example "$1,234.56 this month" |

The medium widget and the Lock Screen widget show the change from the **Same Point Last Month** total with an arrow, for example "↓ 14% vs Sep". The arrow points down when the **This Month** total is less than the **Same Point Last Month** total. It points up when the **This Month** total is the same as or more than the **Same Point Last Month** total. If the **Same Point Last Month** total is $0.00 or less, the widget does not show the change.

When you charge your iPhone on its side, iOS can show the widget in [StandBy](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/use-standby-iph878d77632/ios).

## Add the widget to your Home Screen

1. On your iPhone, go to the Home Screen page that will show the widget.
2. Touch and hold an area with no apps until the apps start to move.
3. Tap **Edit** at the top of the screen.
4. Tap **Add Widget**.
5. In the search field, type `WalletFeed`.
6. Tap **WalletFeed**. iOS shows the small **Spending** widget.

   Until WalletFeed has your totals, the widget shows example totals before you add it.

7. To add the medium widget, swipe left to it.
8. Tap **Add Widget**.
9. To move the widget, drag it to a different position.
10. Tap **Done**.

Apple gives more information in [Add, edit, and remove widgets on iPhone](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/add-edit-and-remove-widgets-iphb8f1bf206/ios).

## Add the widget to your Lock Screen

1. To show the Lock Screen, push the side button of your iPhone.
2. If iOS does not show the Lock Screen, push the side button again.
3. Touch and hold the Lock Screen.
4. If iOS shows the passcode screen, type your passcode.
5. If iOS does not show **Customize** at the bottom of the screen, do step 3 again.
6. Tap **Customize**.
7. Tap **Add Widgets**. If the Lock Screen does not show **Add Widgets**, tap the widgets on the Lock Screen.
8. In the list of apps, tap **WalletFeed**.
9. Tap the **Spending** widget.
10. To close the list of widgets, swipe down.
11. Tap **Done**.

Apple gives more information in [Create a custom iPhone Lock Screen](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/create-a-custom-lock-screen-iph4d0e6c351/ios).

## Updates to the widget

WalletFeed updates the widget when you open WalletFeed. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. WalletFeed then updates the widget.

WalletFeed Pro is not necessary for these updates. WalletFeed shows **Settings** › **Sync** only with WalletFeed Pro. If you set [**Background Sync**](/docs/background-sync/) to off there, WalletFeed continues to update the widget.

When a new month starts, the widget shows $0.00 for this month. The widget does not show the **Same Point Last Month** total or the change. After WalletFeed updates the widget, the widget shows the totals again.

> **Note:** When **Sample Data** is on in **Settings**, the widget shows the totals from **Sample Data**.

## Privacy

For the widget, WalletFeed keeps only this information on your iPhone:

- The two totals
- The currency of the totals
- The time of the last update.

iOS keeps a copy of the information that the widget shows. This copy has no transactions, merchants or categories.

On a locked iPhone, iOS can show the widget without the totals and the change.

If you stop WalletFeed's access to Wallet, WalletFeed removes the totals from the widget when you open WalletFeed again.

## If there is a problem

### If the widget tells you to open WalletFeed

The widget shows "Open WalletFeed to see your spending." before WalletFeed reads Wallet for the first time, and after WalletFeed's access to Wallet stops. The one-line widget shows "Open WalletFeed".

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. If WalletFeed shows **No Cards** or **Wallet Access Off**, give WalletFeed [access to Wallet](/docs/wallet-accounts/).

### If the widget total does not include a new purchase

When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet.

1. Open WalletFeed. WalletFeed updates the widget.

### If the widget shows no totals on a locked iPhone

On a locked iPhone, iOS can show the widget without the totals and the change.

1. Make sure that your iPhone is not locked.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/spending/ -->
# Spending

On your iPhone, Spending in WalletFeed shows the total of your Apple Card and Apple Cash purchases for this month. It also shows a bar for each day, your largest categories and merchants, and the charges that occur each month or each week. You can use Spending without [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).

## Open Spending

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. At the bottom of the screen, tap **Spending**.

   ![Spending with the October total of $1,317.68, a chart with a bar for each day, and the Monthly Summary.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/spending/walletfeed-spending.webp)

   Result: WalletFeed reads your transactions from Wallet. Then Spending shows the total and the chart for this month.

WalletFeed calculates the values for Spending on your iPhone and does not keep your transactions.

If Spending does not show a total, refer to [If there is a problem](#if-there-is-a-problem).

## The total for this month

The section for the month shows these items:

- The name of the month
- The change from the total at the same day and time of the month before this month (for example, "70% VS SEP" with an up arrow)
- The total for this month
- A chart with one bar for each day of the month
- The Monthly Summary, below the chart.

An up arrow shows that the total increased, and a down arrow shows that it decreased. On the chart, the line with the label "Avg" shows the average for one day (for example, "Avg $45").

The total includes pending purchases. Refunds decrease the total. Transfers, bill payments and declined transactions are not in the total.

WalletFeed compares this month with the same days and time of the month before this month. For example, on October 15 at 2:00 PM, WalletFeed compares the total for October with the total from September 1 to September 15 at 2:00 PM. Spending shows the change only if the total for these days of the month before this month is more than zero.

The average is the total for this month divided by the number of days from the first day of the month to this day.

## Show the total for one day

1. On the chart, put your finger on the bar for a day.

   Result: The top of the section shows the date and the total for that day. The other bars become dim.
2. To show the total for a different day, move your finger to the bar for that day.

## Monthly Summary

The Monthly Summary is below the chart. It gives facts about your purchases this month.

If Apple Intelligence is active on your iPhone and **Summarize Spending** is on, Apple Intelligence writes the Monthly Summary. Apple Intelligence uses facts that WalletFeed calculates (for example, the total and your largest purchase). A Monthly Summary from Apple Intelligence has the Apple Intelligence icon.

> **Note:** Apple Intelligence can write an incorrect value in the Monthly Summary. WalletFeed calculates all other values on Spending.

Apple Intelligence operates on your iPhone. WalletFeed does not send your transactions to a server for the Monthly Summary.

In each of these conditions, the Monthly Summary shows a light bulb icon and the first two facts that WalletFeed calculates:

- Apple Intelligence is not available on your iPhone.
- **Summarize Spending** is off in **Settings**.
- Apple Intelligence cannot write the Monthly Summary.

An example of the two facts is "You've spent $1,318 so far this month. That's 70% more than at this point last month."

## Stop the Monthly Summary from Apple Intelligence

**Settings** shows **Summarize Spending** only when Apple Intelligence is available on your iPhone.

1. At the top of Spending, tap **Settings** (the gear button).
2. Scroll to **Privacy & Security**.
3. Set the **Summarize Spending** switch to off.

   ![Settings with Summarize Spending set to on in the Privacy & Security section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/spending/walletfeed-settings-2.webp)

   Result: The Monthly Summary shows the two facts from WalletFeed.
4. Tap **Done**.

When **Summarize Spending** is off, [Ask Spending](/docs/ask-spending/) also shows two facts from WalletFeed.

To start the Monthly Summary from Apple Intelligence again, set the **Summarize Spending** switch to on.

## Categories and merchants

The **Categories** section shows the five categories with the largest totals this month. **Other** shows the total of all other categories. At the top of the section, a bar shows each category in a different color. The length of each color shows the part of the total for that category.

The **Merchants** section, at the bottom of Spending, shows the five merchants with the largest totals this month.

## Recurring Charges

The **Recurring Charges** section shows charges that occur again each month or each week (for example, subscriptions). Spending shows this section only when WalletFeed finds one or more of these charges. For each charge, the section shows the name, **Monthly** or **Weekly**, and the value of the last charge.

To find these charges, WalletFeed reads the transactions from this month and the two months before this month. Apple Intelligence can give each charge a type and a name that is easy to read. For example, "NETFLIX.COM 866-579" becomes "Netflix", and its type is "Streaming". When Apple Intelligence gives these names, the section shows "Apple Intelligence suggested these names."

![Recurring Charges with three monthly charges, and Merchants with five merchants.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/spending/walletfeed-recurring.webp)

For more information, refer to [Recurring Charges](/docs/recurring-charges/).

## Monthly Installments

If you have Apple Card Monthly Installments, the **Monthly Installments** section shows your installment charges. The section shows the charges from the month of the last installment charge. The largest charge is first. For each charge, the section shows the name, the date (for example, "Sep 30") and the value.

Each installment charge has the date of the last day of a month. Thus, until the last day of this month, the section shows the charges from the month before this month. **Recurring Charges** does not show installment charges.

Wallet does not give WalletFeed the remaining payments or the remaining balance. Thus, the section does not show them.

## Use Ask Spending

If Apple Intelligence is available on your iPhone, Spending shows **Ask about your spending** at the top of the screen.

1. Tap **Ask about your spending**.
2. Type the transactions that you want to see (for example, "Dining this month vs last").
3. Tap **Go** on the keyboard.

   ![Spending with "Dining this month vs last" in the field, a total of $188.70 and a chart with the lines "This month" and "Last month".](https://walletfeed.app/docs/spending/walletfeed-ask-spending.webp)

   Result: Spending shows the total, the chart, the categories and the transactions for the text that you typed.
4. To show the total for this month again, tap **Clear** (the x button).

For more information, refer to [Ask Spending](/docs/ask-spending/).

## Show new transactions

To show new transactions on Spending, swipe down on the screen.

## If there is a problem

### If Spending shows "No Cards"

You did not select Wallet accounts for WalletFeed.
