1. Tap **Choose Accounts**.

   Result: iOS shows the Wallet access screen.
2. Select the accounts that WalletFeed reads.
3. For each account, select the start date.
4. Tap **Share**.

For more information, refer to [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/).

### If Spending shows "Wallet Access Off"

You did not let WalletFeed read Wallet, or you stopped its access to Wallet in the Settings app.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts that WalletFeed reads.
4. Open WalletFeed again.

### If Spending shows "No Spending"

The Wallet accounts that WalletFeed can read have no purchases this month, or the total for this month is zero or less than zero. For the transactions in the total, refer to [The total for this month](#the-total-for-this-month).

If Spending does not include a Wallet account, refer to [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/).

### If Spending shows "Couldn't Read Wallet"

WalletFeed cannot read your transactions from Wallet.

To make WalletFeed read Wallet again, swipe down on the screen.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/transactions/ -->
# Transactions

The **Transactions** tab in WalletFeed shows your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions on your iPhone. WalletFeed reads the transactions from Wallet and does not keep them.

## Open your transactions

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Transactions** at the bottom of the screen.

   ![The Transactions tab with the October transactions and a pending charge at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/transactions/walletfeed-transactions.webp)

The list has a section for each month. The month of your last transaction is at the top. Each section starts with the last transaction of its month. If a month is before this year, the section also shows the year, for example "September 2025".

## Transaction rows

Each row shows these items:

- An icon for the category
- The merchant name
- The amount
- The date.

The icon shows the category, for example a car for **Transport**. WalletFeed uses the merchant category code (MCC) to find the category.

If Wallet gives no merchant name, the row shows the description of the transaction.

Some rows have a second line below the merchant name. This line shows **Pending** until the transaction posts. If most transactions in the list are from a different account, this line shows the account name of the transaction. For example, when most transactions are from Apple Card, Apple Cash rows show "Apple Cash".

The amount of a credit, for example a refund, is green and has a plus sign (+).

For a transaction in the last 7 days, the row shows **Today**, **Yesterday** or the name of the day, for example "Tuesday". For a date before these 7 days, the row shows the month and the day, for example "Oct 3". If the date is before this year, the row also shows the year.

The row does not show the category name, but VoiceOver speaks it with the other items in the row. Wallet does not give apps the name of the person who used the card. Thus, the row does not show this name.

## Apple Card Monthly Installments

If you use Apple Card Monthly Installments, the list shows the charge for each month with your other transactions. Apple adds these charges on the last day of the month. In [Spending](/docs/spending/), the **Monthly Installments** section also shows the charges from the last month that has installment charges. Wallet does not give apps other installment information, for example the name of the item, the number of installments or the balance.

## Show more transactions

WalletFeed reads 200 transactions first. When you scroll to the end of the list, WalletFeed reads 200 more transactions.

1. Scroll to the end of the list.
2. Continue to scroll until WalletFeed shows a message at the end of the list.

   The message gives the date of the row at the end of the list, for example "Showing transactions from March 4, 2025."

   If **Sample Data** is on, WalletFeed does not show the message.

For each account, Wallet gives WalletFeed the transactions from a start date. You select this date when you [give WalletFeed access to the account](/docs/wallet-accounts/).

## Change the accounts or the start dates

You select the accounts and their start dates on the Wallet access screen. After you tap **Share** or **Don't Share**, iOS does not show this screen again. Then you change the accounts and the start dates in the Settings app.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts that WalletFeed reads.
4. To get the transactions before the start date of an account, change the start date.
5. Open WalletFeed.

   When WalletFeed opens, it reads Wallet again.

## Update the list

WalletFeed reads your transactions again each time you open WalletFeed or the **Transactions** tab.

1. At the top of the list, swipe down.

   Then WalletFeed reads your transactions from Wallet again. If WalletFeed cannot read Wallet, the list does not change.

## Find a transaction

1. Tap the search button at the bottom of the screen.
2. Type a part of a merchant name, a category or an amount.

   Then [Search](/docs/search/) shows the results in the same rows and month sections as **Transactions**.

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows "No Cards"

You did not select Wallet accounts for WalletFeed.

1. Tap **Choose Accounts**.

   Then iOS shows the Wallet access screen.

2. Select the accounts that WalletFeed reads.
3. For each account, select the start date.
4. Tap **Share**.

### If WalletFeed shows "Wallet Access Off"

You did not let WalletFeed read Wallet, or you stopped its access to Wallet in the Settings app. After you tap **Don't Share**, iOS does not show the Wallet access screen again.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts that WalletFeed reads.
4. Open WalletFeed.

   When WalletFeed opens, it reads Wallet again.

### If WalletFeed shows "No Transactions"

The accounts that WalletFeed reads have no transactions from their start dates. If WalletFeed cannot read Wallet, it also shows this message.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select more accounts for WalletFeed.
4. If an account has transactions before its start date, select a start date before these transactions.
5. Open WalletFeed.

   When WalletFeed opens, it reads Wallet again.

### If WalletFeed shows "Wallet Unavailable"

This iPhone cannot give Wallet data to apps. Thus, WalletFeed cannot show transactions on this iPhone. WalletFeed is for iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. It is available only in the US.

### If a transaction is not in the list

WalletFeed shows only the Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions that Wallet gives to WalletFeed.

1. At the top of the list, swipe down.
2. Scroll until you find the transaction, or until WalletFeed shows a message at the end of the list.
3. In the Wallet app, find the account and the date of the transaction.
4. If WalletFeed does not read the account, or the date is before the start date, do the steps in [Change the accounts or the start dates](#change-the-accounts-or-the-start-dates).

### If the list shows transactions that you did not make

If **Sample Data** is on, WalletFeed shows two months of sample transactions and does not show your Wallet transactions.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Data** section, set **Sample Data** to off.
3. Tap **Done**.

If **Sample Data** is off or not in the **Data** section, the transactions can be from a co-owner of your Apple Card. The rows do not show the person who used the card.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/ -->
# Troubleshooting

WalletFeed shows a message when it cannot read Wallet or send transactions to a destination.

## Correct problems with Wallet and Apple Intelligence

### If WalletFeed does not show your cards

WalletFeed shows only the Wallet accounts that you let it read. It can read only Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings in the US.

Until you tap **Share** or **Don't Share** on the iOS screen **Share Wallet Data**, **Settings** › **Wallet** shows **Choose Accounts**. To let WalletFeed read your accounts, do these steps:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Wallet** section, tap **Choose Accounts**.

   ![WalletFeed Settings, with Choose Accounts in the Wallet section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/walletfeed-settings.webp)

   Result: iOS shows **Share Wallet Data**.

3. Set the switch to on for each account that you let WalletFeed read.

   ![The Share Wallet Data screen, with switches for Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings, and the Share button.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/walletfeed-wallet-access.webp)

4. Tap **Share**.

After you tap **Share** or **Don't Share**, iOS does not show **Share Wallet Data** again. Then **Settings** › **Wallet** shows **Open Settings**. To change the accounts that WalletFeed can read, do these steps:

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts that you let WalletFeed read.
4. Select the start date of each account.
5. Open WalletFeed.

For more information, refer to [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/).

### If WalletFeed does not show Ask Spending

WalletFeed shows Ask Spending only on an iPhone that can use Apple Intelligence, and only when Apple Intelligence is active.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Apple Intelligence & Siri**.
3. Activate Apple Intelligence.
4. Open WalletFeed.
5. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
6. In the **Privacy & Security** section, find **Summarize Spending**.

   ![WalletFeed Settings, with the Summarize Spending switch in the Privacy & Security section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/walletfeed-settings-2.webp)

   If WalletFeed shows **Summarize Spending**, WalletFeed can use Apple Intelligence. **Spending** then shows the field **Ask about your spending**.

   If WalletFeed does not show **Summarize Spending**, it cannot use Apple Intelligence at this time.

When **Summarize Spending** is off, **Spending** shows Ask Spending, but Apple Intelligence does not write the Monthly Summary. The Monthly Summary then shows two facts from WalletFeed.

Without Apple Intelligence, you can use **Spending** and **Search**. **Search** then finds the words that you type. For more information, refer to [Ask Spending](/docs/ask-spending/).

## Correct problems with destinations

### If a destination shows "Authentication failed"

The service did not let WalletFeed use the key, the token or the sign-in of the destination.

Some causes are:

- A deleted key
- An expired key
- A key that can only read data, for example a **Read Only** key in Sure.

If you do not select a different **Expiration** when you make a key in BankSync, BankSync stops the key after 90 days.

The destination screen has a button that corrects the problem:

| Destination | Button |
| --- | --- |
| A destination with an API key, for example Sure | **Replace Key** |
| A destination with a token, for example Lunch Money | **Replace Token** |
| A destination with a sign-in, for example Google Sheets | **Sign In Again** |
| Zapier or Make | **Replace URL** |
| Webhook | **URL** and **Authorization** |

To use a new key, token or URL, do these steps:

1. In the service, make a new key, token or URL (refer to the guide for the destination in [Destinations](/docs/destinations/)).
2. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.

   ![The Destinations screen, with "Authentication failed" below the n8n destination.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/walletfeed-destinations-failure.webp)

3. Tap the destination.

   ![The n8n destination screen, with "Authentication failed" below Last Sync, and the URL and Authorization rows.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/walletfeed-destination-failure.webp)

4. Tap **Replace Key**, **Replace Token** or **Replace URL**.
5. Paste the new key, token or URL.
6. Tap **Replace**.

For a webhook, do steps 1, 2 and 3. Then do these steps:

1. Tap **URL** or **Authorization**.
2. Type the new value.
3. Tap **Save**.

A destination with a sign-in can also show "Signed out. Sign in again in the destination's settings." To correct this problem, do these steps:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Sign In Again**.
4. Get access to the same account that you used for the destination.

It is not necessary to delete the destination. After you correct the problem, WalletFeed sends the changes that the destination did not receive.

If the destination screen shows **Sending History** and **Try Again**, tap **Try Again**.

### If Destinations shows "Sync Requires Pro"

You do not have WalletFeed Pro at this time. WalletFeed sends transactions to destinations only with WalletFeed Pro.

1. In **Destinations**, tap **Upgrade**.
2. If you have a plan, tap **Restore Purchases** below the plans.

   Result: If the App Store finds your plan, the **WalletFeed Pro** screen closes.

3. If you do not have a plan, select a plan.
4. Complete the purchase.

For the plans, refer to [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).

### If a destination shows "Off"

On the destination screen, **Enabled** is off. Thus, WalletFeed does not send transactions to the destination.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Set **Enabled** to on.

   ![The Lunch Money destination screen, with the Enabled switch on.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/walletfeed-destination-detail.webp)

### If destinations receive changes only while WalletFeed is open

**Background Sync** is off, or your iPhone started again and you did not type its passcode after that.

While WalletFeed is open, destinations receive changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet.

WalletFeed shows the **Sync** section in **Settings** only with WalletFeed Pro.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Sync** section, set **Background Sync** to on.

   ![WalletFeed Settings, with the Background Sync switch on in the Sync section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/walletfeed-background-sync.webp)

3. After your iPhone starts again, type its passcode one time.

For more information, refer to [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/).

To send each purchase seconds after you tap your iPhone to make the purchase, do these steps:

1. In **Settings** › **Sync**, tap **Automations**.

   ![The Automations screen, with the steps for After Each Card Tap.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/troubleshooting/walletfeed-automations.webp)

2. In **After Each Card Tap**, do the steps on the screen.

### If you get the notification "Sync Stopped"

For 3 days, WalletFeed did not send the changes to all your destinations correctly, and **Remind If Sync Stops** is on in **Settings** › **Sync**.

The notification tells you "WalletFeed hasn't synced in 3 days. Open it to catch up."

1. Open WalletFeed.

   Result: WalletFeed sends the changes to your destinations.

2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. If a destination shows a message, find the message on this page.

If you do not let WalletFeed send notifications, **Remind If Sync Stops** stays off.

### If a destination shows "Can't open the folder. Choose it again."

At this time, WalletFeed cannot open the folder that contains the CSV, OFX or QIF file.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Change Folder**.
4. Select the same folder again.
5. If WalletFeed shows "Couldn't open this folder.", select a different folder.

After you select the folder, WalletFeed saves all the transactions of the destination in the folder again.

### If a file changes only when you open WalletFeed

WalletFeed did not get access to the folder in the background. WalletFeed does not show a message for this problem.

1. Open WalletFeed.

   Result: WalletFeed changes the file while WalletFeed is open.

iOS can also start WalletFeed to change the file while your iPhone gets power from a charger. An automation from **Settings** › **Sync** › **Automations** also changes the file.

### If BankSync does not make the Apple Card table

BankSync did not make the table in approximately 30 seconds, for example because the workspace is at the table limit of its plan.

WalletFeed shows "You're signed in, but BankSync hasn't created or shared the Apple Card table." The message also gives the table limit of your plan, for example "The Free plan allows one table."

1. Tap **Open BankSync**.
2. In BankSync, delete a table that you do not use, or select a plan that has more tables.
3. In WalletFeed, tap **Try Again**.
4. If WalletFeed does not show the message again, tap **Add**.

If WalletFeed shows the message again, do these steps:

1. Tap **Sign In Again**.
2. In BankSync, give WalletFeed access to the workspace. Only the owner or an admin of the workspace can give this access.
3. In WalletFeed, tap **Add**.

API keys are available only on BankSync's Standard plan or a higher plan. With one of these plans, you can tap **Use an API Key Instead**. For more information, refer to [Send Apple Card transactions to BankSync](/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/).

> **Note:** The **Sign In with BankSync** button uses WalletFeed's referral URL. Below the button, WalletFeed shows "WalletFeed may earn a commission if you pay for BankSync."

## Prevent copies of transactions

### If Zapier, Make or a webhook receives a transaction two times

If WalletFeed stops before it sends all the changes, WalletFeed sends the same changes a second time after it starts again.

Zapier and Make do not find copies. Thus, a Zap or a scenario that adds a row for each change can add a transaction two times. **Send History** also sends previous transactions again.

1. Open the Zap or the scenario.
2. Before the step that adds a row, add a step that finds the row by its `id`.
3. If the step finds the row, update that row.
4. If the step does not find the row, add a new row.

A webhook server must update the row that has the same `id` as the transaction. The server can use the `webhook-id` header to find a request that WalletFeed sent two times. For more information, refer to [Webhook format](/docs/webhooks/).

### If your app shows each imported transaction two times

You imported the same QIF file two times, and a QIF file has no transaction ID.

1. In your app, delete the second copy of each transaction.
2. Import each QIF file only one time, after the end of its month.

An OFX file has an ID for each transaction. Actual, GnuCash and Moneydance use this ID and do not add a transaction two times. A CSV file has a **WalletFeed ID** column, but only some apps use it to find copies.

### If a destination shows a transaction two times

WalletFeed finds each transaction in the destination by its ID. If WalletFeed cannot find that ID, it adds the transaction again.

WalletFeed keeps the ID in these locations:

| Destination | Location of the ID |
| --- | --- |
| Google Sheets | Column A, **WalletFeed ID** |
| Airtable, Notion and Coda | The **WalletFeed ID** field, property or column |
| PocketSmith | The `wf:` note |
| Linear | The **WalletFeed ID** row and the WalletFeed attachment, in the team that you selected |

In Notion, WalletFeed also cannot find a row that you moved to the archive.

1. In the service, find the two copies of the transaction.
2. Delete the copy that has no ID or a changed ID.
3. Do not change or delete the ID of the other transactions.

## Send an e-mail to customer support

If the steps on this page do not correct the problem, send an e-mail to [support@walletfeed.app](mailto:support@walletfeed.app). In the e-mail, include these items:

- The model of your iPhone
- The version of iOS on your iPhone
- The destination that has the problem, for example Google Sheets.

Do not send API keys, tokens or information about your transactions. In WalletFeed, **Settings** › **Support** opens the support page.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/wallet-accounts/ -->
# Select the Wallet accounts that WalletFeed reads

WalletFeed reads the transactions of the Wallet accounts that you select on your iPhone. It can read your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings accounts. When you open WalletFeed for the first time, you select the accounts. After this, you change them in the Settings app.

## Select your accounts for the first time

When you open WalletFeed for the first time, it shows **Welcome to WalletFeed**.

1. Tap **Continue**.

   ![The Welcome to WalletFeed screen, with the text "Next, choose the Wallet accounts to share." above the Continue button.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/wallet-accounts/walletfeed-welcome.webp)

   **Transactions** opens, and iOS shows the Wallet access screen.

2. Select the accounts that WalletFeed reads.
3. For each account, select the start date.

   From this date, WalletFeed can read the transactions of the account.

4. Tap **Share**.

   **Transactions** shows the transactions of the accounts that you selected.

If you tap **Don't Share**, WalletFeed cannot read Wallet. Then **Transactions** shows **Wallet Access Off**. After this, you select the accounts in the Settings app. The steps are in [Change the accounts that WalletFeed reads](#change-the-accounts-that-walletfeed-reads).

## Select the accounts from WalletFeed

Until you tap **Share** or **Don't Share** on the Wallet access screen, WalletFeed shows **Choose Accounts** in **Settings** › **Wallet**. In **Transactions**, **Spending** and **Search**, WalletFeed also shows **Choose Accounts** below **No Cards**.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Wallet** section, tap **Choose Accounts**.

   ![The WalletFeed Settings screen, with Choose Accounts in the Wallet section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/wallet-accounts/walletfeed-settings.webp)

   Then, iOS shows the Wallet access screen.

3. Do steps 2 to 4 in [Select your accounts for the first time](#select-your-accounts-for-the-first-time).

## Change the accounts that WalletFeed reads

After you tap **Share** or **Don't Share**, iOS does not show the Wallet access screen again. You change the accounts and their start dates in the Settings app.

At the end of the **Transactions** list, a message starts with "Showing transactions from" and gives a date. If you select a start date before this date in step 4, WalletFeed can also read the transactions before this date.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts that WalletFeed reads.
4. For each account, select the start date.
5. Open WalletFeed.

   When WalletFeed opens, it reads the accounts again.

If you do not select an account in step 3, WalletFeed cannot read the transactions of this account. A destination keeps the transactions that it received before the change.

> **Note:** After you tap **Share** or **Don't Share**, **Settings** › **Wallet** in WalletFeed shows **Open Settings**. **Open Settings** opens the WalletFeed page in the Settings app.

## Accounts and destinations

With [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), WalletFeed sends transactions to [destinations](/docs/destinations/) (for example, Lunch Money or Google Sheets). A destination receives the transactions of the accounts that WalletFeed reads.

Before a new destination receives transactions, WalletFeed shows a message. The message tells you which data the destination receives, and which accounts the data is from. The message also gives the start date, or it contains "including earlier ones". After you tap **Send**, the destination starts to receive transactions. For a CSV, OFX or QIF file, the button is **Save**.

If you set **Filter** to on for a destination, you can select the accounts for this destination in **Accounts**. The steps are in [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

## Correct problems with Wallet access

### If WalletFeed shows Wallet Access Off

WalletFeed cannot read Wallet, because you tapped **Don't Share** or you stopped its access in the Settings app.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts that WalletFeed reads.
4. Open WalletFeed.

### If WalletFeed shows No Transactions

The accounts that WalletFeed can read have no transactions from their start dates. WalletFeed shows "To share more Wallet accounts, open Settings › Privacy & Security › Wallet."

1. Do steps 1 and 2 in [Change the accounts that WalletFeed reads](#change-the-accounts-that-walletfeed-reads).
2. Select the accounts that WalletFeed reads.
3. If an account has transactions before its start date, select a start date before these transactions.
4. Open WalletFeed.

### If WalletFeed does not show an account

WalletFeed reads only the Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings accounts that you selected.

1. If the account is an Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account, do the steps in [Change the accounts that WalletFeed reads](#change-the-accounts-that-walletfeed-reads).

### If WalletFeed shows Wallet Unavailable

WalletFeed cannot get the Wallet data on this iPhone. WalletFeed is for iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. It is available only in the US.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/docs/walletfeed-pro/ -->
# WalletFeed Pro

WalletFeed Pro lets WalletFeed send your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions to [destinations](/docs/destinations/), for example a budget app or a spreadsheet. WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.

You can use these functions without WalletFeed Pro:

- [Spending](/docs/spending/)
- [Ask Spending](/docs/ask-spending/)
- [Search](/docs/search/)
- [Recurring Charges](/docs/recurring-charges/)
- The [Spending widget](/docs/spending-widget/)
- [Export CSV](/docs/export-csv/).

## Functions of WalletFeed Pro

WalletFeed sends your transactions to each destination that you add. While WalletFeed is open, a destination receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then sends the change.

A new destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. A new Zapier, Make or Linear destination receives a maximum of 30 days of previous transactions. On the destination screen, [Send History](/docs/send-history/) sends the transactions from before that date.

WalletFeed Pro adds the **Sync** section to **Settings**.

## Plans and prices

The **WalletFeed Pro** screen shows these plans:

| Plan | Price | Free trial |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Yearly** | $4.99 a year ($0.42 a month) | 1 week |
| **Monthly** | $0.99 a month | 1 week |
| **Lifetime** | $19.99, one time | No free trial |

**Yearly** and **Monthly** are subscriptions. **Lifetime** is a one-time purchase.

You can get one free trial of WalletFeed Pro, for **Yearly** or for **Monthly**. After the free trial, the subscription continues at the price of the plan. If you cannot get a free trial, the button at the bottom of the screen shows **Subscribe** for **Yearly** and **Monthly**.

You can use Family Sharing with WalletFeed Pro.

## Get WalletFeed Pro

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.

   ![The Transactions screen with the gear button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/walletfeed-pro/walletfeed-transactions.webp)

3. In the **Subscription** section, tap the **WalletFeed Pro** row that shows **Upgrade**.

   **Settings** closes, and the **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens. It shows the plans and their prices. WalletFeed selects **Yearly**.

   ![The WalletFeed Pro screen with a checkmark on the Yearly plan, and the Start Free Trial button at the bottom.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/walletfeed-pro/walletfeed-pro.webp)

4. Tap a plan.

   The text below the button at the bottom of the screen gives the terms of the plan, for example "1 week free, then $4.99/year."

5. Tap the button at the bottom of the screen, for example **Start Free Trial** or **Buy Lifetime**.
6. Complete the purchase on the App Store screen.

   The **WalletFeed Pro** screen closes. When you open **Settings** again, the **Subscription** section shows your plan, for example **Yearly**.

## Get WalletFeed Pro when you add a destination

Without WalletFeed Pro, the **Add Destination** screen shows all the destinations. When you tap a destination, WalletFeed shows the **WalletFeed Pro** screen.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations** at the bottom of the screen.
2. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   The **Add Destination** screen opens.

   ![The Add Destination screen with the Budgeting section and the Sheets & Databases section.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/walletfeed-pro/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

3. Tap a destination, for example PocketSmith.

   The **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens. It shows the icon of the destination above the title.

   ![The WalletFeed Pro screen with the PocketSmith icon above the title.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/walletfeed-pro/walletfeed-store-destination.webp)

4. If you have a plan, tap **Restore Purchases** below the plans.

   If the App Store finds your plan, the form for the destination opens. Steps 5 to 7 are not necessary.

5. Tap a plan.
6. Tap the button at the bottom of the screen, for example **Start Free Trial**.
7. Complete the purchase on the App Store screen.

   The **WalletFeed Pro** screen changes to the form for the destination.

## Get WalletFeed Pro on a different iPhone

When WalletFeed starts, it gets your plan from the App Store. If you have a plan but **Settings** shows **Upgrade**, for example on a new iPhone, you can get WalletFeed Pro again with **Restore Purchases**.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Subscription** section, tap the **WalletFeed Pro** row that shows **Upgrade**.
3. Tap **Restore Purchases** below the plans.

   If the App Store finds your plan, the **WalletFeed Pro** screen closes. If the App Store finds no plan, WalletFeed shows "No purchases to restore."

   If an error occurs, WalletFeed shows "Couldn't restore purchases."

## Change your plan

You can change from **Yearly** to **Monthly**, or from **Monthly** to **Yearly**. You can also change from a subscription to **Lifetime**. If you have **Lifetime**, you cannot select a subscription.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Subscription** section, tap **Change Plan**.

   ![The Settings screen with Yearly in the WalletFeed Pro row, and Change Plan and Manage Subscription below it.](https://walletfeed.app/docs/walletfeed-pro/walletfeed-settings.webp)

   **Settings** closes, and the **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens. Your plan shows **Current**.

3. Tap a different plan.
4. Tap the button at the bottom of the screen, for example **Subscribe** or **Buy Lifetime**.
5. Complete the purchase on the App Store screen.

   The **WalletFeed Pro** screen closes.

If you have a subscription when you get **Lifetime**, the subscription continues until you cancel it. After you get **Lifetime**, WalletFeed does not show **Change Plan** or **Manage Subscription**. You can cancel the subscription in the Settings app (refer to [Cancel your subscription](#cancel-your-subscription)).

## Cancel your subscription

A subscription continues automatically at the end of each period, for example at the end of the free trial or of a month. If you cancel it 24 hours or more before the end of a period, it stops at the end of that period. WalletFeed Pro stays active until that time.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Subscription** section, tap **Manage Subscription**.

   The subscriptions screen of the App Store opens.

3. Cancel the subscription.

You can also cancel the subscription in the Settings app:

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap your name at the top of the screen.
3. Tap **Subscriptions**.
4. Tap WalletFeed.
5. Cancel the subscription.

## After WalletFeed Pro stops

When WalletFeed Pro stops, WalletFeed keeps your destinations, but it does not send transactions to them. These changes also occur:

- The **Destinations** screen shows **Sync Requires Pro** and an **Upgrade** button.
- If WalletFeed did not send all the transactions from **Initial History** or **Send History** to a destination, the destination screen shows "Paused" below **Sending History**.
- The **Settings** screen does not show the **Sync** section.

The transactions that WalletFeed sent to a destination stay there. The other functions of WalletFeed continue to operate.

## If there is a problem

### If the Destinations screen shows **Sync Requires Pro**

WalletFeed Pro is not active on this iPhone.

1. On the **Destinations** screen, tap **Upgrade**.
2. If you have a plan, tap **Restore Purchases** below the plans.

   If the App Store finds your plan, the **WalletFeed Pro** screen closes. Steps 3 to 5 are not necessary.

3. Tap a plan.
4. Tap the button at the bottom of the screen, for example **Subscribe**.
5. Complete the purchase on the App Store screen.

### If the WalletFeed Pro screen shows "Couldn't load prices."

WalletFeed cannot get the plans from the App Store.

1. Make sure that your iPhone has a connection to the internet.
2. Tap **Try Again**.

### If WalletFeed shows "Waiting for approval."

The purchase must get approval, for example through Ask to Buy in Family Sharing.

When the purchase gets approval, WalletFeed Pro starts on your iPhone.

### If WalletFeed shows "Couldn't complete the purchase."

The App Store did not complete the purchase.

1. Make sure that your iPhone has a connection to the internet.
2. Tap the button at the bottom of the **WalletFeed Pro** screen again.

### If WalletFeed shows "Couldn't restore purchases."

WalletFeed cannot get your purchases from the App Store.

1. Make sure that your iPhone has a connection to the internet.
2. Tap **Restore Purchases** again.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to your app or server

There is no web API for your Apple Card transactions. Apple lets an app on your iPhone read them with the FinanceKit API, but only after you give the app access.

WalletFeed is an iPhone app that reads your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions with FinanceKit. With WalletFeed Pro, it sends each change from your iPhone to your server, AWS, Supabase or BankSync.

## FinanceKit on iPhone

FinanceKit is the part of iOS that lets apps read data from Wallet. It is available only on iPhone. In the US, FinanceKit gives apps access to your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings accounts.

Before an app can read your data, iOS shows your Wallet accounts. You select the accounts that the app can read, and a start date for each account. You can change the accounts and the start dates in the Settings app, in **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet**.

Apple has no bank feed for your Apple Card transactions.

If you make an iPhone app, your app must have the FinanceKit entitlement from Apple. Apple gives this entitlement only to an iPhone app in the Finance category of the App Store in the US or the UK. Apple also tells developers that the app must "provide financial management tools". For more information, refer to [FinanceKit on the Apple Developer site](https://developer.apple.com/financekit/).

## Destinations for your app or server

WalletFeed can send your transactions to the destinations in this table.

| Destination | Data that it receives |
| --- | --- |
| **Webhook** | JSON in a `POST` request to your HTTPS URL, with not more than 100 transactions in each request |
| **Amazon S3** | One CSV or JSON Lines file for each month, in your bucket |
| **Amazon SQS** | One message for each change |
| **Kinesis Data Streams** | One record for each change |
| **DynamoDB** | One item for each transaction |
| **EventBridge** | One event for each change |
| **Supabase** | One row for each transaction, in a Postgres table in your Supabase project |
| **BankSync** | One row for each transaction, in a BankSync table that your AI agents can read |

In the **Add Destination** list, **Amazon S3**, **Amazon SQS**, **Kinesis Data Streams**, **DynamoDB** and **EventBridge** are all in **AWS**. You can add more than one destination.

These pages give all the steps for each destination:

- [Send Apple Card transactions to a webhook](/guides/apple-card-to-webhook/)
- [Send Apple Card transactions to AWS](/guides/apple-card-to-aws/)
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Supabase](/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/)
- [Send Apple Card transactions to BankSync](/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/).

## Before you start

You must have:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- WalletFeed on that iPhone
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase
- For a webhook, a server with an HTTPS URL that your iPhone can connect to from the internet
- For AWS, an AWS account in which you can make an IAM user and an access key
- For Supabase, a Supabase project
- For BankSync, a BankSync workspace in which you are the owner or an admin.

WalletFeed is available only in the US.

## Step 1: Give WalletFeed access to your Wallet accounts

If WalletFeed shows your transactions, go to [Step 2](#step-2-add-the-destination).

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. On the **Welcome to WalletFeed** screen, tap **Continue**. iOS shows your Wallet accounts.

   ![The Welcome to WalletFeed screen, with the Continue button at the bottom.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/walletfeed-welcome.webp)
3. Select the accounts that WalletFeed can read.
4. For each account, select the start date of the transactions that WalletFeed can read.
5. Tap **Share**. The **Transactions** tab shows the transactions of the accounts that you selected.

If WalletFeed shows **No Cards**, tap **Choose Accounts**. iOS shows your Wallet accounts. Then do steps 3 thru 5. For more information, refer to [Select the Wallet accounts that WalletFeed reads](/docs/wallet-accounts/).

## Step 2: Add the destination

1. Tap **Destinations** at the bottom of the screen.
2. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations, and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)
3. Find the destination in the **Add Destination** list, or type its name in the search field.

   ![The Add Destination list, with the Budgeting section and the first part of the Sheets & Databases section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

   The **Developers** section has **Webhook** and **AWS**. **Supabase** is in **Sheets & Databases**, and **BankSync** is in **Budgeting**.
4. Tap the destination.
5. If WalletFeed shows **WalletFeed Pro**, get WalletFeed Pro. Then WalletFeed shows the screen of the destination.

## Step 3: Connect the destination

Do the steps for your destination. WalletFeed keeps the keys, the secrets and the webhook URL in the Keychain on your iPhone.

### Webhook

1. To change the name of the destination, type a different name in **Name**.

   ![The Webhook screen in WalletFeed, with Name, the URL field, Authorization (Optional), Share Signing Secret, Send Test and the steps.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/walletfeed-setup-webhook.webp)
2. Type the HTTPS URL of your server in the field that shows `https://example.com/hook`.
3. If your server must get an `Authorization` header, type its value in **Authorization (Optional)**.
4. Tap **Share Signing Secret**. iOS shows a menu with **Copy**.
5. Tap **Copy**, or send the secret to your computer, for example with AirDrop.
6. Add the secret to your server.
7. Tap **Send Test**. Your server receives a request with `type` set to `walletfeed.test` and one test transaction.
8. Tap **Add**.

WalletFeed uses [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com) signatures. Your server uses the secret to make sure that WalletFeed sent each request. For the JSON fields and the signature, refer to [Webhook format](/docs/webhooks/).

### AWS

For DynamoDB, the table must have a String partition key with the name `id`, and no sort key.

WalletFeed accepts only the access key of an IAM user. It does not accept an access key that has a session token.

1. In **Service**, select **Amazon S3**, **Amazon SQS**, **Kinesis Data Streams**, **DynamoDB** or **EventBridge**.

   ![The AWS screen in WalletFeed, with Service set to Amazon S3, and the Access Key ID, Secret Access Key, Region, Endpoint, Bucket, Prefix and Format fields.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/walletfeed-setup-amazon-s3.webp)
2. If the AWS region of your service is not `us-east-1`, type the region in **Region**.
3. For Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2 or a different service that uses the S3 API, type its URL in **Endpoint**.
4. Type the value for your service in **Bucket**, **Queue URL**, **Stream**, **Table** or **Event Bus**.
5. Tap **Share IAM Policy**.
6. Send the policy to your computer, for example with AirDrop.
7. On your computer, open [IAM in the AWS console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/iam/home#/users).
8. Make an IAM user that has the policy from WalletFeed.
9. Make an access key for the user.
10. Send the access key ID and the secret access key to your iPhone, for example with AirDrop.
11. In WalletFeed, paste the access key ID in **Access Key ID**.
12. Paste the secret access key in **Secret Access Key**.
13. Tap **Add**. WalletFeed does a test before it adds the destination.

For the test, WalletFeed writes and deletes a test file in S3. For DynamoDB, WalletFeed makes sure that the table has the correct partition key. SQS, Kinesis Data Streams and EventBridge receive one test event.

### Supabase

1. In your Supabase project, click **Connect**.
2. In "Connect to your project", click **Server**.
3. If you use a computer, send the project URL and the key to your iPhone, for example with AirDrop.
4. Copy the publishable key from the `SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=` row. The key starts with `sb_publishable_`.
5. In WalletFeed, paste the key in **Publishable Key**.

   ![The Supabase screen in WalletFeed, with the Publishable Key field, the project URL field, Share SQL and the steps.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/walletfeed-setup-supabase.webp)
6. Copy the project URL from the `SUPABASE_URL=` row.
7. In WalletFeed, paste the project URL in the field below **Publishable Key**. When this field is empty, it shows `https://abcd.supabase.co`.
8. Tap **Share SQL**.
9. Tap **Copy**, or send the SQL to your computer, for example with AirDrop.
10. Paste the SQL in the **SQL Editor** of your Supabase project.
11. Click **Run**.
12. Click **Run query**.
13. In WalletFeed, tap **Add**.

The SQL makes the table `walletfeed_transactions`. It also adds a policy that lets only this destination read and write the table. WalletFeed does not accept a secret key, which starts with `sb_secret_`.

A new project has a publishable key with the name `default`. If the project has no publishable key, make a key in **Project Settings** › **API Keys** with **New publishable key**.

### BankSync

1. Tap **Sign In with BankSync**.

   ![The BankSync screen in WalletFeed, with Sign In with BankSync and Use an API Key Instead.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/walletfeed-setup-banksync.webp)
2. On the BankSync page, tap **Continue with Google**, or type your e-mail address in **Email**.

   ![The BankSync page with Continue with Google, an Email field and Continue with email.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/banksync-sign-in-with-banksync.webp)
3. If you typed your e-mail address, tap **Continue with email**.
4. If BankSync has no account for your e-mail address, do the steps on the BankSync page to make an account.
5. On the BankSync page, give WalletFeed access to your BankSync workspace. BankSync makes the **Apple Card** table, and WalletFeed shows **Signed In**.

   Only the owner or an admin of the workspace can give this access.
6. Tap **Add**.

The **Sign In with BankSync** button uses WalletFeed's referral URL. Below the button, WalletFeed shows the message "WalletFeed may earn a commission if you pay for BankSync."

On the Free plan, a workspace can have only one table. If the workspace has a different table, BankSync cannot make the **Apple Card** table. As a result, WalletFeed shows **Try Again** and **Open BankSync**.

You can also tap **Use an API Key Instead**. API keys are available only on BankSync's Standard plan or a higher plan. In BankSync, the keys are in **Settings** › **Developers** › **API Keys**. [Send Apple Card transactions to BankSync](/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/) gives the steps for an API key.

## Step 4: Start to send transactions

After you tap **Add**, WalletFeed shows a message before it sends data. The message tells you the data that the destination will receive. It also gives the accounts and the start date. For a webhook, the title of the message is "Send Transactions to Your Server?"

1. Read the message.
2. Tap **Send**. WalletFeed adds the destination and starts to send your transactions.

If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed does not add the destination.

## Transaction data

Each destination receives this data for a transaction:

- An ID that stays the same when the transaction changes
- The account name, for example Apple Card
- The date, the currency and the value of the transaction
- The description, the merchant name and the merchant category code (MCC), if Wallet has them
- The WalletFeed category, for example groceries or travel
- The status in Wallet, for example `pending` or `booked`
- For a charge in a different currency, the value in that currency.

This table gives the value of a charge at each destination. It also tells you the result when Wallet removes a transaction.

| Destination | Value of a charge | Removed transaction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Webhook** | A number more than zero, with `direction` set to `debit` | WalletFeed puts the ID of the transaction in `deletedIDs`. |
| **Amazon S3** | A number less than zero | WalletFeed writes the file of the month again, without the transaction. |
| **Amazon SQS**, **Kinesis Data Streams**, **EventBridge** | A number less than zero | WalletFeed sends an event with `event` set to `deleted` and only the `id`. |
| **DynamoDB** | A number less than zero | WalletFeed deletes the item. |
| **Supabase** | A number less than zero | WalletFeed deletes the row. |
| **BankSync** | A number less than zero | WalletFeed deletes the row, and BankSync moves the row to the BankSync trash. |

If you do not change **Prefix** or **Format**, the S3 file for October 2026 is `walletfeed/transactions/2026-10.csv`.

In EventBridge, the `source` of each event is `app.walletfeed`. The `detail-type` is `Transaction Created`, `Transaction Updated` or `Transaction Deleted`.

WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to your server or service. After a service receives your transactions, the terms of that service are applicable to them.

## New and changed transactions

- While WalletFeed is open, a destination receives changes in seconds.
- When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then sends the change. **Background Sync** is on until you set it to off.
- A pending charge has the status `pending` or `authorized`. When the status changes to `booked`, the destination receives the transaction again, with the same ID and the value of the `booked` transaction.
- WalletFeed removes declined charges, expired charges and the transactions that Wallet removes.
- A refund is a different transaction. Its type is `refund`.
- For a webhook, if your server does not send a status code from 200 to 299, WalletFeed sends the same changes again in the subsequent request.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. WalletFeed sends the newest transactions first.

To send previous transactions again, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

While WalletFeed sends the history, you can stop **Send History**:

1. Tap **Send History**.
2. Tap **Stop Sending**.

WalletFeed can send only the transactions that iOS lets it read. To let WalletFeed read more previous transactions, change the start date in the Settings app, in **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.

## Change or remove the destination

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.

Then do one of these steps:

- To send only some transactions, set **Filter** to on (refer to [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/)).
- To stop the destination for a time, set **Enabled** to off.
- To change the URL or the `Authorization` value of a webhook, tap **URL** or **Authorization**.
- To use a new AWS access key, Supabase key or BankSync API key, tap **Replace Key**.

To remove the destination:

1. Tap **Delete**. WalletFeed shows the message "Transactions already sent stay at the destination."
2. Tap **Delete** again.

To remove the transactions that WalletFeed sent, delete them on your server or in the service.

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows "Wallet Access Off"

WalletFeed cannot read Wallet, because you tapped **Don't Share** or you stopped its access in the Settings app.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts that WalletFeed can read.
4. Open WalletFeed.

### If WalletFeed does not show your Apple Card transactions

You did not select your Apple Card when iOS showed your Wallet accounts, or you are a participant in Apple Card Family. FinanceKit does not give participants access to the Apple Card account.

To select your Apple Card:

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select your Apple Card.
4. Open WalletFeed.

### If the destination shows "Authentication failed"

Your server or the service did not accept the key, the `Authorization` value or the access from **Sign In with BankSync**. The HTTP status code was 401 or 403.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.

   ![The Destinations list, with the destination n8n, which shows Authentication failed.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/walletfeed-destinations-failure.webp)
2. Tap the destination.

   ![The screen of the webhook destination n8n, with Authentication failed below Last Sync, and the URL and Authorization rows.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/walletfeed-destination-failure.webp)

For a webhook, do these steps:

1. Tap **Authorization**.
2. Type the correct value.
3. Tap **Save**.
4. Tap **Send Test**.

For AWS, do these steps:

1. Tap **Replace Key**.
2. Paste the access key ID in **Access Key ID**.
3. Paste the secret access key in **Secret Access Key**.
4. Tap **Replace**.
5. Tap **Send Test**.

For Supabase or a BankSync API key, do these steps:

1. Tap **Replace Key**.
2. Paste the correct key.
3. Tap **Replace**.
4. Tap **Send Test**.

For **Sign In with BankSync**, do these steps:

1. Tap **Sign In Again**.
2. Tap **Send Test**.

### If the destination shows "Can't connect"

WalletFeed did not get a response from your server or the service.

1. Make sure that your iPhone can connect to the internet.
2. For a webhook, make sure that your server operates and that it accepts HTTPS requests.
3. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
4. Tap the destination.
5. For a webhook, make sure that the URL in the **URL** row is correct.
6. Tap **Send Test**.

### If the AWS screen shows "Wrong region for this bucket."

The S3 bucket is in a different AWS region.

1. In **Region**, type the region of the bucket.
2. Tap **Add**.

### If the AWS screen shows "Key rejected"

AWS did not accept the access key, or the IAM policy of the user is not correct.

1. On your computer, open IAM.
2. Make sure that the user has the policy from **Share IAM Policy**.
3. In WalletFeed, paste the access key ID in **Access Key ID** again.
4. Paste the secret access key in **Secret Access Key** again.
5. Tap **Add**.

### If your software receives an event two times

SQS, Kinesis Data Streams and EventBridge can receive the same event again. This occurs when WalletFeed sends the same changes again. A FIFO queue in SQS removes the second copy of an event if the queue receives it 5 minutes or less after the first copy.

1. In the software that reads the events, identify each transaction by its `id`.
2. If an event has the same `event` and `status` as the last event for that `id`, discard the new event.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-shortcuts/ -->
# Run a shortcut after each Apple Card purchase

A Shortcuts automation on your iPhone can send your Apple Card purchases to your WalletFeed [destinations](/docs/destinations/) in seconds. The automation starts only when you tap your iPhone to make a purchase with your Apple Card or Apple Cash card.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- WalletFeed, with access to your Wallet accounts
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase
- One or more [destinations](/docs/destinations/) in WalletFeed, for example Google Sheets or Lunch Money
- Your Apple Card or Apple Cash card in Wallet on your iPhone
- The Shortcuts app on your iPhone.

WalletFeed is available only in the US. You must have WalletFeed Pro to send transactions to destinations.

## Step 1: Open Automations in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.

   Result: WalletFeed shows **Settings**.
3. If **Settings** does not show **Sync**, get [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).
4. In the **Sync** section, tap **Automations**.

   ![The WalletFeed Settings screen with Background Sync and Automations in the Sync section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-shortcuts/walletfeed-settings.webp)

   Result: WalletFeed shows **Automations**. **After Each Card Tap** is at the top of the screen.

## Step 2: Make the automation in Shortcuts

iOS does not let apps make automations. Thus, you make the automation one time in the Shortcuts app. In **After Each Card Tap**, WalletFeed shows the steps for your iPhone. These steps are different for iOS 26, iOS 27 and iOS 27 with Apple Intelligence.

Do only the procedure for your iPhone. To find this procedure, look at step 1 in WalletFeed.

### iOS 27 with Apple Intelligence

On iOS 27 with Apple Intelligence, Shortcuts can make a shortcut from text that you give it. WalletFeed gives you the text. In WalletFeed, step 1 is **Copy Description**.

1. In **After Each Card Tap**, tap **Copy Description**.

   ![The Automations screen with Copy Description and its text below After Each Card Tap.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-shortcuts/walletfeed-automations.webp)

   Result: WalletFeed copies the text below **Copy Description** and shows **Copied**. The text is "When I tap my Apple Card or Apple Cash card, run Sync New Purchase from WalletFeed without asking."
2. Tap **Open Shortcuts**.

   Result: The Shortcuts app opens.
3. Tap **+**.

   Result: Shortcuts shows a new shortcut. You can type the task that the shortcut must do.
4. Paste the text.
5. Make sure that the shortcut uses your Apple Card or Apple Cash card.
6. Tap the arrow adjacent to the trigger at the top of the shortcut.
7. Make sure that **Confirm Before Run** is off.
8. Tap the information button **ⓘ** › **Privacy**.
9. Make sure that **Allow Running When Locked** is on.
10. Tap **Done**.

If Shortcuts does not let you type the task or does not make the automation, do these steps:

1. Open WalletFeed again.
2. In **After Each Card Tap**, tap **Set It Up Yourself**.
3. Below **Set It Up Yourself**, tap **Open Shortcuts**.
4. Do steps 2 to 11 in [iOS 27 without Apple Intelligence](#ios-27-without-apple-intelligence).

### iOS 27 without Apple Intelligence

On iOS 27, an automation is a trigger at the top of a shortcut. In WalletFeed, step 1 is **Open Shortcuts**, and **Describe It Instead** is below the steps.

1. In **After Each Card Tap**, tap **Open Shortcuts**.

   Result: Shortcuts opens a new shortcut.
2. Tap **Add Action**.
3. Type WalletFeed in the search field.
4. Tap **Sync New Purchase**.
5. In the action list, tap **Automation** › **Transaction**.
6. Select your cards.
7. Tap the arrow adjacent to the trigger at the top of the shortcut.
8. Set **Confirm Before Run** to off.
9. Tap the information button **ⓘ** › **Privacy**.
10. Set **Allow Running When Locked** to on.
11. Tap **Done**.

### iOS 26

On iOS 26, automations have a tab in Shortcuts. Your other devices do not get these automations. In WalletFeed, step 1 is **Open Shortcuts**, and WalletFeed does not show **Describe It Instead**.

1. In **After Each Card Tap**, tap **Open Shortcuts**.

   Result: The Shortcuts app opens.
2. Tap **Automation**.
3. If you have no automations, tap **New Automation**.
4. If you have one or more automations, tap **+**.
5. Tap **Transaction**.
6. Select your cards.
7. Select **Run Immediately**.
8. Tap **Next**.
9. Tap **New Blank Automation** › **Add Action**.
10. Type WalletFeed in the search field.
11. Tap **Sync New Purchase**.
12. Tap **Done**.
13. If you use WalletFeed on a different iPhone, do this procedure again on that iPhone.

## Step 3: Make sure that the automation operates

After you tap your iPhone to make a purchase with your Apple Card or Apple Cash card, do these steps:

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Sync** section, look at the value adjacent to **Automations**.

   Result: **Automations** shows **On** or **1 of 2**. The table below gives each value.
4. Tap **Automations**.
5. In **After Each Card Tap**, look at **Last Run**.

   Result: **Last Run** shows the time of the last operation of **Sync New Purchase**, for example "2 hr. ago".
6. If **Last Run** shows **Never**, refer to [If Last Run shows Never after a purchase](#if-last-run-shows-never-after-a-purchase).

**Automations** in **Settings** shows if each automation operated in its period. The period is the last 14 days for **After Each Card Tap** and the last 3 days for **Every Day**.

| **Automations** shows | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| **On** | Each automation on the **Automations** screen operated in its period. |
| **1 of 2** | Only one of the two automations operated in its period. |
| **Set Up** | No automation operated in its period, and [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is off or **Sample Data** is on. |
| **Off** | **After Each Card Tap** did not operate in the last 14 days, **Background Sync** is on, and **Sample Data** is off. |

When **Background Sync** is on, the automation is not necessary. Without the automation, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet.

## Time to send each purchase

When you tap your iPhone to make a purchase with your Apple Card or Apple Cash card, the automation starts **Sync New Purchase**. This WalletFeed action operates in the background. It does not open WalletFeed.

At that time, Wallet does not have the purchase. First, WalletFeed sends the changes that your destinations did not receive. Then it waits for Wallet to record the purchase. When Wallet records the purchase, WalletFeed sends the purchase to your destinations.

WalletFeed waits for the purchase until 18 seconds after the action starts. If Wallet records the purchase after that time, WalletFeed sends the purchase when it sends other changes. While WalletFeed is open, it sends each change in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open and **Background Sync** is on, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. Refer to [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/).

The automation starts only when you tap your iPhone to make a purchase. Thus, online purchases and posted charges do not start the automation. Your Savings account has no card. As a result, Savings transactions also do not start the automation. WalletFeed sends these changes while WalletFeed is open, or when iOS starts WalletFeed.

The automation does not change the data that WalletFeed sends to your destinations. WalletFeed also uses the filter of each destination. Refer to [filters for destinations](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

After your iPhone starts again, WalletFeed cannot send to destinations until you type your passcode one time.

When the action stops, it gives a short message. Shortcuts can show the message as a notification.

| Message | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| "Changes sent: 2." | WalletFeed sent 2 changes. The number is the total for all your destinations. |
| "Nothing new yet." | WalletFeed did not find a new change to send. |
| "Changes sent: 1. One destination needs attention." | WalletFeed cannot send to one destination. If two or more destinations have a problem, the message gives the number of these destinations. |
| "Sync requires WalletFeed Pro." | WalletFeed Pro is not active on this iPhone. |
| "Open WalletFeed and allow Wallet access." | WalletFeed does not have access to your Wallet accounts. |
| "Add a destination in WalletFeed first." | WalletFeed has no destination that is on. |

To correct a problem, refer to [If there is a problem](#if-there-is-a-problem).

## Send other changes each day

If **Background Sync** is off or **Sample Data** is on, **Automations** also shows **Every Day**. An **Every Day** automation starts **Sync Transactions** at a time that you select. This action sends new transactions and other changes to your destinations, for example online purchases and posted charges.

For **Every Day**, the text that you paste is "Every day at 9 PM, run Sync Transactions from WalletFeed without asking."

To make the automation, do [Step 2](#step-2-make-the-automation-in-shortcuts) with these changes:

- Use the steps below **Every Day** in WalletFeed.
- If you paste the text, make sure that the time in Shortcuts is correct.
- Tap **Sync Transactions**, not **Sync New Purchase**.
- Tap **Time of Day**, not **Transaction**.
- Select a time, not your cards.

If **Background Sync** is on, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. Thus, WalletFeed does not show **Every Day**. An **Every Day** automation that you made continues to operate.

## Stop or change the automation

iOS does not tell WalletFeed about your automations. To change the cards or the time, open the automation in the Shortcuts app.

To stop the automation, delete it in the Shortcuts app. After you delete it, WalletFeed sends new purchases while WalletFeed is open, or when iOS starts WalletFeed. The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay at each destination.

## Other WalletFeed actions in Shortcuts

WalletFeed has more actions for the Shortcuts app. For example, **Get Recent Card Transactions** gives your transactions from the last 7 days to the subsequent action in a shortcut. You can change the number of days. Refer to [Siri and Shortcuts](/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/).

## If there is a problem

### If Last Run shows Never after a purchase

The automation did not start, or it did not start the WalletFeed action.

1. Open the Shortcuts app.
2. If you cannot find the automation, do [Step 2](#step-2-make-the-automation-in-shortcuts) again.
3. Make sure that the automation uses your Apple Card or Apple Cash card.
4. Make sure that the automation starts **Sync New Purchase**.
5. On iOS 26, make sure that the automation uses **Run Immediately**.
6. On iOS 27, make sure that **Confirm Before Run** is off.
7. On iOS 27, make sure that **Allow Running When Locked** is on.

### If the message is "Nothing new yet."

WalletFeed did not send the purchase before the action stopped. For example, Wallet recorded the purchase more than 18 seconds after the action started.

1. If a destination has a filter, make sure that the filter includes the purchase (refer to [filters for destinations](/docs/choose-what-to-send/)).
2. To send the purchase at this time, open WalletFeed.

> **Note:** If you do not open WalletFeed, WalletFeed sends the purchase when iOS starts WalletFeed. When WalletFeed is not open and **Background Sync** is on, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet.

### If the message is "Sync requires WalletFeed Pro."

WalletFeed Pro is not active on this iPhone.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. Tap **WalletFeed Pro**.
4. If your Apple Account has a WalletFeed Pro purchase, tap **Restore Purchases**.
5. If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, get it (refer to [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/)).

### If the message is "Open WalletFeed and allow Wallet access."

WalletFeed does not have access to your Wallet accounts.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts that WalletFeed can read (refer to [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/)).
4. Open WalletFeed.

### If the message is "Add a destination in WalletFeed first."

WalletFeed has no destination that is on.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. If a destination shows **Off**, do these steps:

   1. Tap the destination.
   2. Set **Enabled** to on.

4. If there is no destination, tap **+** to add a destination (refer to [Destinations](/docs/destinations/)).

### If the message includes "needs attention" or "need attention"

WalletFeed cannot send to one or more destinations.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Find the destination with the problem. Below its name, WalletFeed shows the cause, for example "Authentication failed".

   ![The Destinations screen with Authentication failed and a warning symbol for the n8n destination.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-shortcuts/walletfeed-destinations-failure.webp)
4. Tap the destination.
5. Do the steps for this cause in [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting/) or in the guide for the destination.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-by-category/ -->
# See Apple Card spending by category

WalletFeed shows your Apple Card spending by category on your iPhone. The [**Spending**](/docs/spending/) tab shows this month's total, a chart with a bar for each day, the categories and the merchants with the largest totals.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- Your Apple Card in Wallet on your iPhone
- WalletFeed, from the App Store
- An iPhone that can use Apple Intelligence, with Apple Intelligence active (necessary only for [Ask Spending](/docs/ask-spending/) and for [Search](/docs/search/) with Apple Intelligence).

WalletFeed is available only in the US. You can use **Spending** without [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).

## Step 1: Give WalletFeed access to your Apple Card

If WalletFeed shows your transactions, go to [Step 2](#step-2-read-the-total-for-this-month).

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. If WalletFeed shows **Welcome to WalletFeed**, tap **Continue**.

   ![The Welcome to WalletFeed screen with the Continue button at the bottom.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-by-category/walletfeed-welcome.webp)

3. If WalletFeed shows **No Cards**, tap **Choose Accounts**.
4. When iOS shows your Wallet accounts, set the switch for your Apple Card to on.

   ![The Share Wallet Data screen, with the switches for Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings in the on position.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-by-category/walletfeed-wallet-access.webp)

5. Tap **Share**.

WalletFeed can read only the accounts that you select. You can change the accounts in the Settings app, in **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.

## Step 2: Read the total for this month

1. Tap **Spending** at the bottom of the screen.

   ![The Spending screen with the October total of $1,317.68, a chart with a bar for each day and the top of Categories.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-by-category/walletfeed-spending.webp)

2. To read the total for one day, touch the chart and move your finger to that day.

   **Spending** shows the date and the total for that day.

The top part of **Spending** shows these items:

- The name of the month and the total of your purchases in this month
- An arrow and the change from the month before this month, for example "70% vs Sep"
- A chart with a bar for each day of the month
- The Monthly Summary, a short text below the chart.

WalletFeed compares the same days of the two months. For example, on October 20, it compares October 1 to 20 with September 1 to 20.

On the chart, the line with the label "Avg $45" shows the average for each day, from the first day of the month to today.

If your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence, Apple Intelligence writes the Monthly Summary from the results that WalletFeed calculates. Apple Intelligence can write a number that is not correct. The total, the chart and the lists come from WalletFeed. Without Apple Intelligence, WalletFeed writes the Monthly Summary. This summary usually gives the total and the change from the month before this month.

To get the Monthly Summary from WalletFeed on an iPhone with Apple Intelligence, do these steps:

1. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Privacy & Security** section, set **Summarize Spending** to off.

   ![The Privacy & Security section of Settings, with the Summarize Spending switch in the on position.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-by-category/walletfeed-settings-2.webp)

3. Tap **Done**.

The [Spending widget](/docs/spending-widget/) shows the total for this month and the total for the same days of the month before this month. You can put the widget on the Home Screen or the Lock Screen.

## Step 3: Find the categories and the merchants

1. On **Spending**, scroll to **Categories**.

   **Categories** shows a bar with one color for each category. Below the bar, each row shows a category and its total for this month.

2. Scroll to **Merchants**.

   **Merchants** shows the five merchants with the largest totals for this month.

   ![The Spending screen with Other at the bottom of Categories, then Recurring Charges and Merchants.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-by-category/walletfeed-recurring.webp)

In **Categories**, WalletFeed shows your five largest categories. If you have more than five categories, or transactions in **Other**, the last row is **Other**. This row shows the total of the remaining categories and the transactions in **Other**.

Between **Categories** and **Merchants**, **Spending** can also show [**Recurring Charges**](/docs/recurring-charges/) and **Monthly Installments**.

## Step 4: Use Ask Spending for a different month

If your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence, and Apple Intelligence is active, **Spending** has the field **Ask about your spending** at the top. The name of this feature is [Ask Spending](/docs/ask-spending/). Without Apple Intelligence, **Spending** shows only this month.

1. At the top of **Spending**, tap **Ask about your spending**.
2. Type your text, for example `Spending by category last month`.
3. Tap **Go** on the keyboard.

   The result has a chart with a bar for each category. Below the chart, WalletFeed shows **Categories**, **Merchants** and the transactions.

4. To type a different text, tap **Clear** (the x button).

   **Spending** shows this month again.

5. Tap **Ask about your spending**.
6. Type a category and a period, for example `Dining this month vs last`.
7. Tap **Go**.

   ![The result for Dining this month vs last, with 9 transactions, a total of $188.70 and a line chart for the two months.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-by-category/walletfeed-ask-spending.webp)

Above the result, WalletFeed shows how it read your text, for example "Dining · This month · vs last month". When WalletFeed shows no result, it shows an example below the field. If you tap the example, WalletFeed puts the text of the example in the field.

You can type a period, for example `today`, `this week`, `last 30 days`, `last month`, `last 3 months`, `this year` or the name of a month. To compare with the month before this month, you can add `vs last month`.

Apple Intelligence operates on your iPhone. When Apple Intelligence reads your text, it gets only that text. WalletFeed calculates the numbers in the result. Then Apple Intelligence writes the short text below the chart from these numbers.

## Find the transactions in a category

[Search](/docs/search/) finds the transactions in all the Wallet accounts that WalletFeed can read.

1. Tap the search button at the bottom of the screen.
2. In **Categories**, tap a category.

   Search puts the name of the category in the search field. Then Search shows the transactions in that category. Above the transactions of each month, Search shows the name of the month.

If your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence, you can also type a category and a period:

1. In the search field, type your text, for example `Groceries last month`.
2. Tap **Search** on the keyboard.

   Above the transactions, Search shows the number of transactions and their total.

   ![The Search screen with the result Groceries · Over $50.00 · Last 30 days, 4 transactions and a total of $277.57.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-by-category/walletfeed-search.webp)

## Categories and totals

WalletFeed sets the category of each transaction from its merchant category code (MCC). Wallet supplies the MCC with the transaction. If a transaction has no MCC, or an MCC that WalletFeed does not know, its category is **Other**.

WalletFeed uses these categories:

- **Groceries**
- **Dining**
- **Transport**
- **Fuel**
- **Travel**
- **Shopping**
- **Entertainment**
- **Subscriptions**
- **Utilities**
- **Health**
- **Services**
- **Cash & Transfers**
- **Other**.

WalletFeed calculates all the totals in **Spending** with these rules:

- Purchases and fees increase the totals. Refunds decrease the totals.
- Transfers and payments are not in the totals.
- Pending purchases are in the totals. Declined purchases are not in the totals.
- The totals include the purchases from all the Wallet accounts that WalletFeed can read, for example Apple Cash.

WalletFeed reads your transactions from Wallet on your iPhone when it shows **Spending**. WalletFeed does not keep a copy of your transactions.

## If there is a problem

### If Spending shows "Wallet Access Off"

WalletFeed does not have access to Wallet. After the first time that iOS shows your Wallet accounts, you can give access only in the Settings app.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select your Apple Card.
4. Open WalletFeed again.

### If Spending shows "No Spending"

WalletFeed found no purchases for this month in the Wallet accounts that it can read. On the first days of a month, WalletFeed can show this message.

If your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence, you can read the totals for the month before this month:

1. At the top of **Spending**, tap **Ask about your spending**.
2. Type `Spending by category last month`.
3. Tap **Go**.

To give WalletFeed access to more Wallet accounts, do these steps:

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select more Wallet accounts.
4. Open WalletFeed again.

### If Spending shows "Couldn't Read Wallet"

WalletFeed did not get your transactions from Wallet. For the same problem, Ask Spending shows "Couldn't read Wallet. Pull down to try again."

1. At the top of **Spending**, swipe down.

   Then WalletFeed reads Wallet again.

### If Spending does not show "Ask about your spending"

WalletFeed shows this field only on an iPhone that can use Apple Intelligence, with Apple Intelligence active.

1. Make sure that your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence.
2. In the Settings app on your iPhone, activate Apple Intelligence.

Without Apple Intelligence, **Spending** shows this month. Search shows the transactions in a category.

### If Ask Spending shows "Couldn't read this."

WalletFeed could not read your text, or WalletFeed cannot show that result. WalletFeed cannot show these results:

- A result that compares two categories or two merchants, for example `Dining vs Groceries`
- A result without the transactions of one category or one merchant, for example `not Uber` or `except Dining`
- A result with two limits for a purchase, for example `over $20 and under $50`.

To get a result, do these steps:

1. Tap **Clear** (the x button).
2. Tap **Ask about your spending**.
3. Type a shorter text with one category and one period, for example `Travel this year`.
4. Tap **Go**.

### If WalletFeed shows no transactions for a month before this month

Wallet gives WalletFeed the transactions of an account only from the start date that you selected for that account.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. For your Apple Card, select a start date before that month.
4. Open WalletFeed again.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-widget/ -->
# Add an Apple Card spending widget

The WalletFeed [Spending widget](/docs/spending-widget/) shows the total of your Apple Card and Apple Cash charges for this month on the Home Screen or the Lock Screen of your iPhone. It can also show the total for the month before this month, to the same day and time.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- Your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account in Wallet on your iPhone.
- WalletFeed, from the App Store.

[WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/) and destinations are not necessary for the widget.

## Step 1: Give WalletFeed access to Wallet

The widget shows totals only after WalletFeed gets [access to your Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/) and reads your transactions. If WalletFeed shows your transactions, WalletFeed has this access. Then you can go to [Step 2](#step-2-add-the-widget-to-the-home-screen).
