If WalletFeed shows **Wallet Access Off**, the steps are in [If WalletFeed shows “Wallet Access Off”](#if-walletfeed-shows-wallet-access-off).

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. If WalletFeed shows **Welcome to WalletFeed**, tap **Continue**.

   ![The Welcome to WalletFeed screen with the Continue button at the bottom.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-widget/walletfeed-welcome.webp)

3. If **Transactions** shows **No Cards**, tap **Choose Accounts**.
4. On the **Share Wallet Data** screen, select the accounts that WalletFeed can read.

   ![The Share Wallet Data screen with switches for Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings, and the Share button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-widget/walletfeed-wallet-access.webp)

5. For each account, select the start date.
6. Tap **Share**. WalletFeed then reads your transactions and calculates the totals for the widget.

## Step 2: Add the widget to the Home Screen

1. On your iPhone, go to the Home Screen page where you will put the widget.
2. Touch and hold an empty area of the screen until the apps move.
3. Tap **Edit** at the top of the screen.
4. Tap **Add Widget**.
5. In the search field, type `WalletFeed`.
6. Tap **WalletFeed**.
7. Swipe to the small or the medium **Spending** widget.
8. Tap **Add Widget**.
9. To move the widget, drag it to a different position.
10. Tap **Done**.

> **Note:** When you swipe in step 7, iOS also shows the **Sync Status** widget. This widget shows the status of your destinations. Destinations are part of WalletFeed Pro.

## Add the widget to the Lock Screen

On the Lock Screen, the **Spending** widget can be below the time or above it.

1. If your iPhone shows the Home Screen or an app, push the side button.
2. If iOS does not show the Lock Screen, push the side button.
3. Touch and hold the Lock Screen until iOS shows **Customize** at the bottom of the screen.
4. Tap **Customize**.
5. If iOS shows the Lock Screen and the Home Screen, tap the Lock Screen.
6. To put the rectangular widget below the time, tap **Add Widgets** or the widgets below the time.
7. To put the one-line widget above the time, tap the date above the time.
8. Tap **WalletFeed**.
9. Tap the **Spending** widget.
10. Tap **Done**.

## Totals in each widget

The **Spending** widgets show these totals:

| Widget | Position | Totals |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Small | Home Screen | The **This Month** total, with the **Same Point Last Month** total below it. |
| Medium | Home Screen | The **This Month** and **Same Point Last Month** totals, and the change between the two totals, for example “↓ 14% vs Sep”. |
| Rectangular | Lock Screen, below the time | The total for this month and the change from the **Same Point Last Month** total. |
| One-line | Lock Screen, above the time | The total for this month, for example “$1,234.56 this month”. |

If the **This Month** total is less than the **Same Point Last Month** total, the change has a “↓” arrow. If the **Same Point Last Month** total is 0 or less than 0, the widget does not show the change.

The widget shows the same totals as the [Spending](/docs/spending/) tab in WalletFeed. The totals include each account that you gave WalletFeed access to in [Step 1](#step-1-give-walletfeed-access-to-wallet). The total for this month starts on the first day of the month. The **Same Point Last Month** total is from the first day of the month before this month to the same day and time in that month. Purchases and other charges increase the totals, and refunds decrease them. Transfers, payments and rejected purchases do not change the totals.

When a new month starts, the widget shows 0 for this month. Until WalletFeed updates the widget, the widget does not show the **Same Point Last Month** total or the change.

To look at the same totals in a chart with a bar for each day:

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Spending**.

   ![The Spending tab with the total for October, the change from September and a chart with a bar for each day.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-widget/walletfeed-spending.webp)

## Widget updates

WalletFeed updates the widget when you open WalletFeed. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. WalletFeed then updates the widget.

WalletFeed Pro and [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) are not necessary for these updates.

## Data in the widget

For the widget, WalletFeed keeps only two totals on your iPhone, with their currency and the time of the update. The widget has no transactions, merchants or categories. iOS keeps a copy of the data that the widget shows.

On a locked iPhone, iOS can show the widget without the totals and the change.

## Change or remove the widget

To change the accounts in the totals:

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security**.
3. Tap **Wallet**.
4. Tap **WalletFeed**.
5. Select the accounts that WalletFeed can read.
6. Open WalletFeed. WalletFeed then updates the widget.

If you select no accounts in step 5, WalletFeed clears the totals from the widget in step 6.

To remove the widget from the Home Screen:

1. Touch and hold the widget.
2. Tap **Remove Widget**.
3. If iOS shows a message, tap **Remove**.

To change the small widget to the medium widget:

1. Remove the small widget.
2. Add the medium widget, as in [Step 2](#step-2-add-the-widget-to-the-home-screen).

To remove the rectangular widget from the Lock Screen:

1. If your iPhone shows the Home Screen or an app, push the side button.
2. If iOS does not show the Lock Screen, push the side button.
3. Touch and hold the Lock Screen until iOS shows **Customize** at the bottom of the screen.
4. Tap **Customize**.
5. If iOS shows the Lock Screen and the Home Screen, tap the Lock Screen.
6. Tap the widgets below the time.
7. Tap **−** on the **Spending** widget.
8. Tap **Done**.

## If there is a problem

### If the widget shows “Open WalletFeed to see your spending.”

WalletFeed did not read your transactions in Wallet, or WalletFeed does not have access to Wallet. The one-line widget shows only “Open WalletFeed”.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Transactions**.

If **Transactions** shows your transactions, WalletFeed updated the widget when WalletFeed opened. If **Transactions** shows **No Cards**, do these steps:

1. Tap **Choose Accounts**.
2. On the **Share Wallet Data** screen, select the accounts that WalletFeed can read.
3. For each account, select the start date.
4. Tap **Share**.

If **Transactions** shows **Wallet Access Off**, the steps are in [If WalletFeed shows “Wallet Access Off”](#if-walletfeed-shows-wallet-access-off).

### If WalletFeed shows “Wallet Access Off”

WalletFeed does not have access to Wallet. After you tap **Share** or **Don't Share**, iOS does not show the **Share Wallet Data** screen again.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security**.
3. Tap **Wallet**.
4. Tap **WalletFeed**.
5. Select the accounts that WalletFeed can read.
6. Open WalletFeed. WalletFeed then updates the widget.

### If the widget does not show a new purchase

WalletFeed did not update the widget after the purchase. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet.

1. Open WalletFeed. WalletFeed then updates the widget.
2. Go to the Home Screen.

### If the widget shows totals that are not from your accounts

The widget shows the totals of the sample transactions because **Sample Data** is on.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Data** section, set **Sample Data** to off. WalletFeed then clears the sample totals and calculates your totals from Wallet.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/ -->
# Import Apple Card transactions into Actual Budget

WalletFeed writes your Apple Card transactions for Actual Budget from your iPhone to iCloud Drive, in one OFX file for each month. Then, on a computer, you import the file into an Apple Card account in Actual Budget.

## Before you start

You must have:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- Apple Card in Wallet on that iPhone
- WalletFeed, with [access to your Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/)
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), which is necessary for destinations (a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase)
- iCloud Drive on your iPhone
- A computer with access to your iCloud Drive
- Actual Budget, open in a web browser on that computer.

WalletFeed is available only in the US.

On a Mac, iCloud Drive is in Finder. On Windows, you can use iCloud for Windows, or download the files from iCloud.com.

Actual Budget does not show the **Import** button on a phone screen. Thus, you import the files on a computer.

## Step 1: Add an OFX file in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the **Destinations** search field, type `Actual`.

   ![The Add Destination screen with the Destinations search field above the Budgeting list.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

5. Tap **OFX File**.

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, the **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens. After you get WalletFeed Pro, the **Files** screen opens.

6. Make sure that **Format** is **OFX**.

   ![The Files screen with OFX in Format, the Folder row, the name WalletFeed and three steps.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/walletfeed-setup-ofx-file.webp)

   Do not use **QIF** for Actual Budget. A QIF file has no transaction IDs. Thus, Actual Budget can show two charges with the same amount as one transaction.

7. Tap **Folder**.
8. Select a folder in iCloud Drive.

   The **Folder** row shows the name of the folder. You open this folder on your computer in Step 3.

9. To use a different name for the files, type the name in **Name**.

   Each file has the transactions of one month. The name of the file has the month, such as `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`.

10. Tap **Add**.
11. When WalletFeed shows **Save Transactions to Files?**, tap **Save**.

    The message shows the data that the folder receives. It also shows the Wallet accounts and the start date of this data. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the new destination.

WalletFeed adds the destination to **Destinations** with the name **WalletFeed**, or the name that you typed. Then WalletFeed writes a file for each month that has posted transactions.

If WalletFeed has access to Apple Cash or Savings, the files also contain their transactions. Actual Budget does not import these transactions from a file that also has Apple Card transactions. To import them, refer to [Import Apple Cash or Savings](#import-apple-cash-or-savings).

## Step 2: Make an Apple Card account in Actual Budget

You do this step one time.

1. On your computer, open Actual Budget in a web browser.
2. If Actual Budget shows **Sign in to this Actual instance**, get access to Actual Budget with the password of your server.
3. If Actual Budget shows **Files**, click the name of your budget.
4. If Actual Budget shows **Welcome to Actual**, click **Start budgeting**.

   ![The Actual Budget welcome page with the Start budgeting button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/actual-budget-start-budgeting.webp)

   Actual Budget makes a budget with the name **My Finances**. Do not click **Import my budget**, because it is not for OFX files.

5. At the bottom of the sidebar, click **Add account**.

   ![The Actual Budget sidebar with the Add account button at the bottom.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/actual-budget-add-account.webp)

6. Click **Create a local account**.

   ![The Add account window with the Create a local account button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/actual-budget-create-local-account.webp)

7. In **Name:**, type `Apple Card`.
8. Do not select **Off budget**.

   You cannot change **Off budget** after you make the account.

9. Make sure that **Balance:** is `0`.
10. Click **Create**.

    ![The Create Local Account window with the name Apple Card, an Off budget checkbox that is not selected, a balance of 0 and the Create button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/actual-budget-account-name-apple-card.webp)

Actual Budget opens the **Apple Card** account page. The sidebar shows **Apple Card** below **On budget**.

## Step 3: Import the file in Actual Budget

Do these steps each time that you import new transactions into Actual Budget.

1. On your computer, in the Actual Budget sidebar, click **Apple Card**.

   Actual Budget puts all the transactions from the file into the account that is open.

2. Click **Import**.

   ![The Apple Card account page in Actual Budget with no transactions and the Import button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/actual-budget-account-import-button.webp)

3. In the window that your browser shows, open the folder in iCloud Drive that you selected in Step 1.
4. Open the file of the month, such as `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`.

   You can open only one file at a time. Do not open `WalletFeed Test.ofx`, because it has only a sample transaction.

5. In **Import transactions (OFX)**, make sure that each new transaction has a blue **+** icon.
6. Click the import button, such as **Import 6 transactions**.

   ![The Import transactions (OFX) window with six new Apple Card transactions and the Import 6 transactions button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/actual-budget-import-preview.webp)

   The number in the button is the number of new transactions. It is not necessary to change the checkboxes below the list.

7. Make sure that the **Apple Card** page shows the transactions.

   ![The Apple Card account in Actual Budget with six imported transactions in the Payment and Deposit columns.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/actual-budget-imported-transactions.webp)

   At the top of the page, Actual Budget shows the number of transactions without a category, such as **6 uncategorized transactions**.

## Import the same month again

WalletFeed updates the file of the month when your transactions change. You can import the file again during the month or after the end of the month. Actual Budget uses the ID of each transaction to find the transactions that you imported. It adds only the new transactions.

1. In the Actual Budget sidebar, click **Apple Card**.
2. Click **Import**.
3. Open the file of the month again, such as `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`.
4. Make sure that only the new transactions have a blue **+** icon.

   ![The Import transactions (OFX) window with one new transaction, Shell, and six gray rows for the transactions that you imported.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/actual-budget-reimport-updated-month.webp)

   The transactions that you imported have gray rows, and Actual Budget does not select them.

5. Click the import button, such as **Import 1 transactions**.

   ![The Apple Card account in Actual Budget with seven different transactions.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/actual-budget-after-second-import.webp)

A transaction goes into the file of the month of the purchase. A purchase at the end of a month can post after the end of that month. When it posts, WalletFeed adds the transaction to the file of the month of the purchase. If you import the file of each month again some days after the end of the month, Actual Budget also gets these transactions.

## Import Apple Cash or Savings

Actual Budget does not import Apple Cash or Savings transactions from a file that also has Apple Card transactions. Thus, you use one destination and one Actual Budget account for each Wallet account.

To write only Apple Card transactions to the files of your first destination, do these steps:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap your OFX destination, such as **WalletFeed**.
3. Set **Filter** to on.
4. Tap **Accounts**.
5. Select Apple Card.
6. On your iPhone, open the Files app.
7. In the destination folder, delete the files of this destination, such as `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`.

   These files can contain the transactions of all your Wallet accounts, because WalletFeed wrote them before you set the filter.

8. Open WalletFeed again.
9. On the destination screen, tap **Send History** › **All**.

   Then WalletFeed writes the files again with only the Apple Card transactions.

To add a destination for Apple Cash or Savings, do these steps:

1. Add one more **OFX File** destination with a different **Name**, such as `Apple Cash` (refer to Step 1).
2. Do steps 1 thru 9 above again for the new destination, with Apple Cash or Savings in step 5.
3. In Actual Budget, make one more local account for that Wallet account, such as `Apple Cash` (refer to Step 2).
4. Import the files of the new destination into that account (refer to Step 3).

## Data that Actual Budget receives

Each OFX file has the posted transactions of one month. This table shows the column in Actual Budget for each Wallet field.

| Wallet | Actual Budget |
| --- | --- |
| Posted date | **Date**. This date can be after the date of the purchase in Wallet. |
| Merchant, or the description if Wallet has no merchant | **Payee**, with 32 characters at most |
| Description, card statement text and the value in a foreign currency | **Notes** |
| A purchase or a fee | **Payment**, without a minus sign |
| A refund, a payment or a deposit | **Deposit** |
| Transaction ID | Actual Budget does not show the ID. It uses the ID to find the transactions that you imported. |
| Category | The file has no category. **Category** shows **Categorize**. |

Purchases make the balance of the **Apple Card** account less than zero, such as -549.61.

When Actual Budget adds a new payee, it can change some uppercase letters in the name to lowercase letters. For example, "NETFLIX.COM 866-579" becomes "Netflix.Com 866-579".

If **Notes** shows the same text as **Payee**, you can clear **Import notes from file** in **Import transactions (OFX)**. Then **Notes** has no text, and Actual Budget does not show the description, the card statement text or the value in a foreign currency.

If WalletFeed has access to more than one Wallet account, each file has the transactions of all these accounts. Actual Budget imports only the Apple Card transactions from a file that has them. When a file has no Apple Card transactions, Actual Budget puts all its transactions into the account that is open.

WalletFeed writes the files only to the folder that you select. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers.

## Changes to the files

While WalletFeed is open, the file of the month receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then updates the file. If WalletFeed cannot open the folder at that time, WalletFeed changes the file when you open WalletFeed, or while your iPhone is on a charger.

Actual Budget gets the changes only when you import the file again.

WalletFeed writes only posted transactions to an OFX file. After a pending charge posts, WalletFeed writes the charge to the file. The charge has the same ID before and after it posts. A declined charge does not post. Thus, the file does not contain it. A refund is a different transaction, and Actual Budget shows it in **Deposit**.

If Wallet removes a transaction of this month or the previous month, WalletFeed removes it from the file. If you imported the transaction, it stays in Actual Budget. You can delete it in Actual Budget.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. WalletFeed writes a file for each month that has posted transactions. It is not necessary to import all the files.

To change **Initial History**, do these steps before you add the destination:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In **Sync**, tap **Initial History**.

   ![The Settings screen, with All in Initial History in the Sync section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/walletfeed-settings.webp)

3. Select **Today**, **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

To write the files of previous months again, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In **Destinations**, tap your OFX destination, such as **WalletFeed**.
2. Tap **Send History**.
3. Select **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

WalletFeed writes the file of each month in that period again. When you import a file again, Actual Budget adds only the transactions that it does not have.

## Change or remove the destination

In **Destinations**, tap your OFX destination. Then use this table:

| Change | On the destination screen |
| --- | --- |
| Stop the changes to the files for a time | Set **Enabled** to off. |
| Write only Apple Card transactions | Refer to [Import Apple Cash or Savings](#import-apple-cash-or-savings). |
| Write only some transactions | Set **Filter** to on. Then set **Include**, **Minimum**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**. |
| Use a different folder | Tap **Change Folder**. Then select the folder. WalletFeed writes all the files again in the new folder. |
| Make sure that WalletFeed can write to the folder | Tap **Send Test**. The folder gets `WalletFeed Test.ofx` with a sample transaction. Do not import this file. |
| Remove the destination | Tap **Delete**. Then tap **Delete** again. The files stay in the folder, and the transactions stay in Actual Budget. |

For more information about the filter, refer to [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

## If there is a problem

### If Actual Budget does not show “Import”

Actual Budget shows **Import** only on the page of an account, and not on a phone screen.

1. Open Actual Budget in a web browser on a computer.
2. In the sidebar, click **Apple Card**.

### If the button shows “Import 0 transactions”

Actual Budget has all the transactions in the file. This is not an error.

1. Click **×** to close the window.

   ![The Import transactions (OFX) window for a file that you imported, with six gray rows, the Import 0 transactions button and the × button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/actual-budget-reimport-same-file.webp)

### If Actual Budget shows a deleted transaction again

Actual Budget selects **Reimport deleted transactions** if you do not change it. Thus, Actual Budget shows deleted transactions as new when you import a month again.

1. In **Import transactions (OFX)**, clear **Reimport deleted transactions**.

   ![The Import transactions (OFX) window with Reimport deleted transactions not selected, seven gray rows that include the deleted Nopa transaction, and the Import 0 transactions button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/actual-budget-reimport-deleted-off.webp)

   You can also clear the checkbox of the deleted transaction.

2. If the import button shows **Import 0 transactions**, click **×**.
3. If the import button shows a different number, click it.

### If Apple Cash or Savings transactions are not in Actual Budget

Actual Budget does not import Apple Cash or Savings transactions from a file that also has Apple Card transactions.

1. Add a destination for each Wallet account (refer to [Import Apple Cash or Savings](#import-apple-cash-or-savings)).

### If Apple Cash or Savings transactions are in the Apple Card account

If a file has no Apple Card transactions, Actual Budget puts all its transactions into the account that is open.

1. Write only Apple Card transactions to the files of your OFX destination (refer to [Import Apple Cash or Savings](#import-apple-cash-or-savings)).
2. In Actual Budget, delete the transactions that are not from Apple Card.

### If the dates in Actual Budget are after the dates in Wallet

Actual Budget shows the posted date of the charge. Wallet shows the date of the purchase. This is not an error.

### If a pending charge is not in Actual Budget

WalletFeed writes a charge to the file only after it posts.

1. After the charge posts in Wallet, import the file of the month again.

### If the folder has no file for a month

WalletFeed writes a file only for a month that has posted transactions.

1. In WalletFeed, open the destination.
2. Tap **Send Test**.

   Then the folder gets `WalletFeed Test.ofx`. If the folder has this file, WalletFeed can write to the folder.

3. To write the files of all months, tap **Send History**.
4. Tap **All**.

### If WalletFeed shows “Couldn't open this folder.”

WalletFeed cannot get access to the folder that you selected. WalletFeed shows this message on the **Files** screen and on the destination screen.

1. Tap **Folder** on the **Files** screen, or **Change Folder** on the destination screen.
2. Select a different folder in iCloud Drive.

### If the destination shows “Can't open the folder. Choose it again.”

WalletFeed does not have access to the folder of the destination.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Change Folder**.
4. Select the folder again.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Airtable

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a table in Airtable. You make a personal access token in Airtable. Then you paste the token in WalletFeed.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed, with access to your Wallet accounts. Refer to [First steps with WalletFeed](/docs/get-started/).
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/). Destinations are part of WalletFeed Pro. WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.
- An Airtable account. You can make an account at [airtable.com](https://airtable.com/signup).
- A web browser for the Airtable steps. The screenshots show Airtable on a computer.

> **Note:** A new Airtable account starts with a 14-day trial of the Team plan. On the Airtable Free plan, the maximum number of records in a base is 1,000. For each workspace on this plan, the maximum number of API calls is 1,000 each month.

## Your token stays on your iPhone

- WalletFeed keeps the personal access token in the Keychain on your iPhone. iOS encrypts the Keychain.
- The personal access token does not go to iCloud Keychain or to your other devices.
- WalletFeed has no account and no servers. No person at WalletFeed can see or get the personal access token.
- Your iPhone sends the personal access token only to Airtable, in each request to Airtable.
- When you delete the destination, WalletFeed deletes the personal access token from your iPhone. You can also delete the token in Airtable.

## Step 1: Make a base in Airtable

A base is an Airtable database. If you have a base for your transactions, go to [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-personal-access-token-in-airtable).

1. On your computer, get access to your [Airtable](https://airtable.com) account.
2. On **Home**, click **+ Create** at the bottom of the sidebar.

   ![The Airtable Home page with the Create button at the bottom of the sidebar.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-home-create.webp)

3. Click **Build an app on your own**.

   ![The dialog "How do you want to start?" with the highlighted card "Build an app on your own".](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-build-on-your-own.webp)

   Airtable opens a new base with the name **Untitled Base**. In this dialog, Airtable uses "app" for a base. On the base and in the token form, Airtable uses "base".
4. If Airtable shows a message with a **Skip** or **Dismiss** button, click the button.
5. Click **Untitled Base**, at the top of the page.

   ![A new Airtable base with the highlighted name Untitled Base at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-new-base.webp)

6. In the **Base name** box, delete **Untitled Base**.
7. Type a name for the base, for example `WalletFeed`.

   ![The Airtable base panel with WalletFeed Docs as the new base name.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-rename-base.webp)

8. Press **Return** or **Enter**.
9. Click outside the panel.

> **Note:** A new base can show an Omni panel on the left side. The **«** button closes the Omni panel.

> **Note:** The new base also has a table with the name **Table 1**. WalletFeed does not change this table.

## Step 2: Make a personal access token in Airtable

1. On your computer, open [Airtable](https://airtable.com).
2. On **Home**, click your account picture in the top-right corner.
3. Click **Builder hub**.

   ![The Airtable account menu with the highlighted Builder hub item.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-account-menu.webp)

   Airtable opens **Builder hub** in a new browser tab, on the **Personal access tokens** page.
4. Click **Create token**.

   ![The Personal access tokens page with the highlighted Create token button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-personal-access-tokens.webp)

5. In **Name**, type `WalletFeed`.

   ![The new token form with WalletFeed in the Name box.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-token-name.webp)

   Airtable shows this name in the revision history of the records that WalletFeed writes. The form also tells you not to give the token to third-party apps. Refer to [The Airtable text about third-party apps](#the-airtable-text-about-third-party-apps).
6. Below **Scopes**, click **+ Add a scope**.
7. In **Find a scope**, type `data.records`.
8. Select `data.records:read` and `data.records:write`.

   ![The scope list for data.records with the selected read and write scopes.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-scopes-records.webp)

9. In **Find a scope**, replace the text with `schema.bases`.
10. Select `schema.bases:read` and `schema.bases:write`.

    ![The scope list for schema.bases with the selected read and write scopes.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-scopes-schema.webp)

11. To close the list, press **Esc**.
12. Make sure that the form shows the four scopes below **Scopes**.
13. Below **Access**, click **+ Add a base**.

    ![The token form with the four scopes and the highlighted Add a base link.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-scopes-added.webp)

14. Click your base, below the name of its workspace.

    ![The base list with the highlighted WalletFeed Docs base.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-add-base.webp)

    The token has access only to this base. If you click **All current and future bases in this workspace**, the token gets access to all the bases in the workspace.
15. Click **Create token**.

    ![The completed token form with the highlighted Create token button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-create-token.webp)

16. In the **Your token has been created** dialog, click the clipboard button on the right side of the token.

    ![The dialog "Your token has been created" with the highlighted clipboard button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-token-created.webp)

    Airtable shows the token only one time. You cannot click **Done** until you copy the token.
17. Click **Done**.
18. Until you paste the token in [Step 3](#step-3-add-airtable-in-walletfeed), do not copy different text.

> **Note:** If you use a Mac with the same Apple Account as your iPhone, you can paste the token on the iPhone with [Universal Clipboard](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102430).

### The Airtable text about third-party apps

In the token form and in the token dialog, Airtable shows the text "Only use this token for your own development. Don't share it with third-party services and applications." WalletFeed is a third-party app. These items give information about the token in WalletFeed:

- WalletFeed keeps the token on your iPhone. Refer to [Your token stays on your iPhone](#your-token-stays-on-your-iphone).
- Your transactions go from your iPhone to Airtable. They do not go through a WalletFeed server.
- The token has access only to the base or the workspace that you added in [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-personal-access-token-in-airtable). The token can do only the tasks that its four scopes let it do.
- If you delete the token in Airtable, WalletFeed has no access to your base. Refer to [Change or remove the destination](#change-or-remove-the-destination).

## Step 3: Add Airtable in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The empty Destinations screen with the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. Tap **Airtable**, in **Sheets & Databases**.

   ![The Add Destination list with Airtable in the Sheets & Databases group.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows the **WalletFeed Pro** screen first.
5. Tap **Personal Access Token**.

   ![The Airtable screen in WalletFeed with the Personal Access Token field and the steps for Airtable.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/walletfeed-setup-airtable.webp)

6. Paste the token.

   The form then shows **Base** and **Table**. **Base** shows the bases that the token can change.
7. In **Base**, select your base.
8. Do not change **Table**.

   **Table** shows **New Table**, and the form shows "Adds a WalletFeed Transactions table to the base." If the base has a **WalletFeed Transactions** table from a previous destination, **Table** shows that table.
9. Tap **Add**.

   The message **Send Transactions to Airtable?** gives the data that Airtable will receive, the accounts and the start date.
10. Tap **Send**.

    If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed sends nothing and removes the destination.

The new destination is in **Destinations**. Its name has two parts, for example **Airtable · WalletFeed**. The second part is the name of your base. WalletFeed starts to send your transactions.

## Step 4: Look at your transactions in Airtable

1. On your computer, open your base in Airtable.
2. Click the **WalletFeed Transactions** tab.

   ![The WalletFeed Transactions table in Airtable with six sample transactions.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-walletfeed-result.webp)

3. Move the pointer to the row of a transaction.
4. In the row, click the expand icon.

   ![The record of one transaction with its fields and a checkmark in the Pending box.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-result-record.webp)

   Airtable shows all the fields of the transaction.

To add a test record, do these steps on your iPhone:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap your Airtable destination.
3. Tap **Send Test**.

   The table gets a test record with WalletFeed in **Merchant** and -4.20 in **Amount**. You can delete this record in Airtable.

## Fields in Airtable

Each transaction is one record in the **WalletFeed Transactions** table. WalletFeed makes these fields:

| Airtable field | Data |
| --- | --- |
| **WalletFeed ID** | The ID of the transaction in Wallet. WalletFeed uses it to find and change the same record. |
| **Date** | The date of the transaction in your time zone, for example 2026-10-30. |
| **Merchant** | The name of the merchant. If Wallet has no merchant name, this field contains the description. |
| **Amount** | A number with two decimal places. A purchase or a fee is less than zero, and a refund or a payment is more than zero. |
| **Currency** | The currency code, for example `USD`. |
| **Category** | The WalletFeed category, for example Groceries or Fuel. |
| **Status** | The status in Wallet, for example `pending` or `booked`. |
| **Pending** | A checkbox. WalletFeed selects it while the status is `pending` or `authorized`. |
| **Account** | The name of the Wallet account, for example Apple Card. |
| **Description** | The description from Wallet. |
| **Type** | The type of transaction in Wallet, for example `pointOfSale` or `refund`. |
| **MCC** | The merchant category code, as a number. If Wallet has no code, this field is empty. |
| **Foreign Amount** | The value in the currency of the merchant, with the same sign as **Amount**. This field is empty for a purchase in US dollars. |
| **Foreign Currency** | The currency code of the merchant. This field is empty for a purchase in US dollars. |

WalletFeed does not change the fields that you add to the table. If you change a WalletFeed field in a record, WalletFeed replaces your change when that transaction changes again.

When you add Airtable in WalletFeed, you can select a different table in **Table**. The list in **Table** shows only the tables that have a field with the name **WalletFeed ID**. WalletFeed writes only to the WalletFeed fields that the table has. If you add a WalletFeed field to the table, WalletFeed writes to it after you tap **Send Test**.

## New and changed transactions

WalletFeed sends each change in Wallet to Airtable:

- While WalletFeed is open, Airtable receives changes in seconds.
- When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then sends the change. **Background Sync** is on until you set it to off.
- When your iPhone starts again, WalletFeed cannot send changes until you type your iPhone passcode.

When a transaction changes in Wallet, WalletFeed changes the table:

- WalletFeed adds a pending charge as a record and selects the **Pending** checkbox. When the status of the charge changes to `booked`, WalletFeed changes the same record and clears the checkbox.
- A refund is a new record, and its **Amount** is more than zero.
- If the status of a pending charge changes to `rejected`, WalletFeed removes the record of the charge. Wallet gives this status to a declined or expired charge.
- If Wallet removes a transaction, WalletFeed also removes its record.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

To send previous transactions after you add the destination, do these steps:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap your Airtable destination.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Select **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

To stop WalletFeed while it sends these transactions, tap **Send History** › **Stop Sending**. For more information, refer to [Send previous transactions](/docs/send-history/).

On the Airtable Free plan, you can decrease the number of records in the base. To do this, set **Initial History** to a shorter period before you add Airtable.

## Change or remove the destination

To open the destination, tap **Destinations** in WalletFeed. Then tap your Airtable destination. On the destination screen, you can make these changes:

- To send only some transactions, set **Filter** to on. You can set **Include**, **Minimum**, **Include Pending**, **Accounts**, **Categories** and **Exclude**. Refer to [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).
- To stop the destination for a period, set **Enabled** to off.
- To use a new token, tap **Replace Token**. Paste the new token. Then tap **Replace**. WalletFeed keeps the new token only if the new token lets WalletFeed read the table.
- To remove the destination, tap **Delete**. Then tap **Delete** again. WalletFeed removes the destination and its token from your iPhone.

If you remove the destination, the records that WalletFeed sent stay in Airtable. The terms of Airtable are applicable to these records.

To delete the token in Airtable, do these steps on your computer:

1. On **Home** in Airtable, click your account picture in the top-right corner.
2. Click **Builder hub**.

   Airtable opens the **Personal access tokens** page.
3. In the row of the token, click **…**.

   ![The token list with the WalletFeed token and its highlighted menu button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-token-list.webp)

4. Click **Delete token**.

   ![The token menu with the highlighted Delete token item.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-token-menu.webp)

5. Click **Delete**.

   ![The dialog "Are you sure you want to delete this token?" with the highlighted Delete button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/airtable-delete-token.webp)

   After this step, Airtable does not accept the token from WalletFeed.

## If there is a problem

### If you cannot click Done in the token dialog

Airtable does not let you click **Done** until you copy the token.

1. Click the clipboard button on the right side of the token.
2. Click **Done**.

### If you closed the token dialog before you copied the token

Airtable shows a token only one time. The **Token ID** in the token list is not the token.

1. Delete the token that you cannot use, with the procedure in [Change or remove the destination](#change-or-remove-the-destination).
2. Make a new token with the procedure in [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-personal-access-token-in-airtable).

### If WalletFeed shows "Token rejected (HTTP 401). Check it and try again."

Airtable did not accept the token.

1. Make sure that you pasted the full token from the **Your token has been created** dialog.
2. If you do not have the full token, make a new token with the procedure in [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-personal-access-token-in-airtable).
3. In WalletFeed, delete the text in **Personal Access Token**.
4. Paste the token.

### If WalletFeed shows "The token has no base you can edit. Add one to the token."

The token has no base, or you cannot change the bases that the token has.

1. In Airtable, make a new token with the procedure in [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-personal-access-token-in-airtable).
2. In WalletFeed, delete the text in **Personal Access Token**.
3. Paste the new token.

### If WalletFeed shows "The token can't reach this base. Add the base and every scope to it."

The token does not have the base or one of the four scopes. If you tap **Add** without the Creator permission for the base, WalletFeed can also show this message. WalletFeed can add the **WalletFeed Transactions** table only if you have this permission.

1. If you do not have the Creator permission for the base, make a base with the procedure in [Step 1](#step-1-make-a-base-in-airtable).
2. In Airtable, make a new token with the procedure in [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-personal-access-token-in-airtable).
3. In WalletFeed, delete the text in **Personal Access Token**.
4. Paste the new token.

### If WalletFeed shows "Airtable is limiting requests. Try again in 30 seconds."

Airtable accepts not more than five requests each second for one base. If a base gets more than five requests in one second, Airtable rejects requests for 30 seconds.

1. After 30 seconds, do the last step again in WalletFeed.

### If Destinations shows "Authentication failed"

Airtable does not accept the token. This occurs if you deleted the token, or if the token does not have the base or a scope.

![The Destinations list with Authentication failed below the name of a destination.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/walletfeed-destinations-failure.webp)

1. In Airtable, make a new token with the procedure in [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-personal-access-token-in-airtable).
2. In WalletFeed, tap the destination.
3. Tap **Replace Token**.
4. Paste the new token.
5. Tap **Replace**.

### If some transactions are not in the table

The cause can be a filter or the start date in **Initial History**.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap your Airtable destination.
3. Make sure that **Filter** is off, or that the filter includes these transactions.
4. To send previous transactions, tap **Send History**.
5. Select a period.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-aws/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to AWS

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to Amazon S3, Amazon SQS, Kinesis Data Streams, DynamoDB or EventBridge in your AWS account. You make a user in AWS with a policy from WalletFeed, then you paste an access key for that user into WalletFeed.

## Before you start

You must have:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- WalletFeed, with access to your [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/)
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase
- An AWS account that lets you make users and access keys in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
- A web browser, on a computer or on your iPhone.

WalletFeed is available only in the US.

WalletFeed can use only the commercial AWS Regions. It cannot use the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions or the China Regions.

## Your key stays on your iPhone

- WalletFeed keeps the access key in the Keychain on your iPhone. iOS encrypts the Keychain.
- The access key does not go to iCloud Keychain or to your other devices.
- WalletFeed has no account and no servers. No person at WalletFeed can see or get the access key.
- Your iPhone sends the access key only to AWS, in each request to AWS.
- When you delete the destination, WalletFeed deletes the access key from your iPhone. You can also delete the access key in AWS.

## Step 1: Make the AWS resource

WalletFeed sends your transactions to a bucket, a queue, a stream, a table or an event bus in your AWS account. Each of these is a resource in AWS.

Do the steps for the service that you will use. If you have the resource, go to [Step 2](#step-2-open-the-aws-screen-in-walletfeed).

### Amazon S3: make a bucket

1. On your computer, open the [Amazon S3 console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/s3/).
2. In the navigation bar, select the AWS Region for the bucket.
3. Click **General purpose buckets**.
4. Click **Create bucket**.
5. In **Bucket name**, type a name for the bucket.
6. Do not change the other values on the page. As a result, all four controls in **Block Public Access settings for this bucket** stay on.
7. Click **Create bucket**.
8. Record the bucket name and the code of the region, for example `us-east-1`.

For more information, refer to [Creating a general purpose bucket](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/create-bucket-overview.html) in the AWS documentation.

### Amazon SQS: make a queue

1. On your computer, open the [Amazon SQS console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/sqs/).
2. In the navigation bar, select the AWS Region for the queue.
3. Click **Create queue**.
4. For **Type**, keep **Standard**.
5. In **Name**, type a name for the queue.
6. Click **Create queue**. The **Details** page of the queue opens.
7. Copy the URL of the queue, for example `https://sqs.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/123456789012/MyQueue`.
8. Send the URL to your iPhone, for example with AirDrop.

You can also use a FIFO (first-in-first-out) queue. If the name of the queue has `.fifo` at the end, WalletFeed uses it as a FIFO queue.

For more information, refer to [Creating an Amazon SQS standard queue and sending a message](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/creating-sqs-standard-queues.html).

### Kinesis Data Streams: make a stream

1. On your computer, open the [Kinesis console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/kinesis).
2. In the navigation bar, select the AWS Region for the stream.
3. Click **Create data stream**.
4. Type a name for the stream.
5. Keep the **On-demand** capacity mode, or select **Provisioned**.
6. If you selected **Provisioned**, type the number of shards.
7. Click **Create Kinesis stream**.
8. Wait until the **Status** of the stream changes to **Active**.
9. Record the stream name and the code of the region.

For more information, refer to [Create a stream using the AWS Management Console](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/how-do-i-create-a-stream.html).

### DynamoDB: make a table

WalletFeed can write only to a table with the partition key `id` of the type String, and with no sort key.

1. On your computer, open the [DynamoDB console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/dynamodb/).
2. In the navigation bar, select the AWS Region for the table.
3. Click **Tables**.
4. Click **Create table**.
5. In **Table name**, type a name for the table.
6. In **Partition key**, type `id`.
7. Make sure that the type of the partition key is String.
8. Do not type a value in **Sort key**.
9. For **Table settings**, keep **Default settings**.
10. Click **Create table**.
11. Record the table name and the code of the region.

For more information, refer to [Create a table in DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/getting-started-step-1.html).

### EventBridge: make a rule on the event bus

WalletFeed sends events to the `default` event bus, or to a different event bus that you type in WalletFeed. A rule selects events with an event pattern. EventBridge sends an event to a target only when a rule on the event bus selects the event. Thus, you must make a rule that selects all the events from WalletFeed.

1. Make the resource that will receive the events, for example a queue (refer to [Amazon SQS: make a queue](#amazon-sqs-make-a-queue)).
2. On your computer, open the [EventBridge console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/events/).
3. In the navigation bar, select the AWS Region for the rule.
4. Click **Rules**.
5. Click **Create rule**.
6. Click **Advanced Builder**.
7. In **Name**, type a name for the rule.
8. For **Event bus**, select **AWS default event bus** (the `default` event bus), or the event bus that you will type in WalletFeed.
9. For **Rule type**, select **Rule with an event pattern**.
10. Click **Next**.
11. For **Event source**, select **AWS events or EventBridge partner events**.
12. In the **Creation method** section, for **Method**, select **Custom pattern (JSON editor)**.
13. Copy this pattern:

    ```json
    {"source": ["app.walletfeed"]}
    ```
14. Paste the pattern in **Event pattern**.
15. Click **Next**.
16. For **Target type**, select **AWS service**.
17. For **Select a target**, select the service that receives the events, for example Amazon SQS.
18. Select the resource of that service, for example your queue.
19. Click **Next**.
20. Click **Next** again.
21. Click **Create rule**.
22. Record the code of the region.

For more information, refer to [Creating rules using the Advanced Builder](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-create-rule-wizard.html).

## Step 2: Open the AWS screen in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations, and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-aws/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)
4. Scroll to the **Developers** section at the end of the list.
5. Tap **AWS** (the row that shows **S3, SQS, Kinesis, DynamoDB, EventBridge**).
6. If WalletFeed shows the **WalletFeed Pro** screen, get WalletFeed Pro on that screen. Then the AWS screen opens.
7. Tap **Service**.
8. Tap the service that you used in Step 1, for example **Amazon S3**.
9. If your resource is not in `us-east-1`, replace `us-east-1` in **Region** with the code of its region.
10. If you selected **Amazon S3**, type the bucket name in **Bucket**.

    ![The AWS screen for Amazon S3, with the fields Access Key ID, Secret Access Key, Region, Endpoint, Bucket, Prefix and Format.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-aws/walletfeed-setup-amazon-s3.webp)
11. If you selected **Amazon S3**, do not type a value in **Endpoint**.
12. If you selected **Amazon SQS**, paste the queue URL in **Queue URL**. WalletFeed uses the region in the queue URL.

    ![The AWS screen for Amazon SQS, with the Queue URL field and the Share IAM Policy button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-aws/walletfeed-setup-amazon-sqs.webp)
13. If you selected **Kinesis Data Streams**, type the stream name or the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) in **Stream**.

    ![The AWS screen for Kinesis Data Streams, with the Stream field and the Share IAM Policy button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-aws/walletfeed-setup-kinesis-data-streams.webp)
14. If you selected **DynamoDB**, type the table name or ARN in **Table**.

    ![The AWS screen for DynamoDB, with the Table field and the message "The partition key must be a string named id."](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-aws/walletfeed-setup-dynamodb.webp)
15. If you selected **EventBridge**, keep `default` in **Event Bus**, or type the name or ARN of your event bus.

    ![The AWS screen for EventBridge, with the value default in the Event Bus field.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-aws/walletfeed-setup-eventbridge.webp)

For Amazon S3, you can also change **Prefix** and **Format**. The format is **CSV** or **JSON Lines**. The prefix is the folder in the bucket. Its value is `walletfeed/` until you change it. The policy in Step 3 contains the prefix. Thus, you must set the prefix before you get the policy.

> **Note:** **Endpoint** is for a different storage service that uses the S3 API, for example Cloudflare R2 or Backblaze B2. The IAM steps on this page are only for AWS.

## Step 3: Make an IAM user with the policy

WalletFeed makes an IAM policy for the resource on the AWS screen. The policy lets the access key do only these actions on that resource:

| Service | Actions in the policy |
| --- | --- |
| Amazon S3 | `s3:PutObject` and `s3:DeleteObject` on the prefix in the bucket. WalletFeed deletes only its test file. |
| Amazon SQS | `sqs:SendMessage` on the queue |
| Kinesis Data Streams | `kinesis:PutRecords` on the stream |
| DynamoDB | `dynamodb:BatchWriteItem` and `dynamodb:DescribeTable` on the table |
| EventBridge | `events:PutEvents` on the event bus |

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Share IAM Policy**. iOS shows a menu to send or copy the policy.
2. If you use IAM on your computer, send the policy to your computer, for example with AirDrop.
3. If you use IAM on your iPhone, tap **Copy** in the menu.
4. Open the [IAM console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/iam/) (on your iPhone, you can also tap **Open IAM** on the AWS screen in WalletFeed).
5. Click **Users**.
6. Click **Create user**.
7. In **User name**, type a name for the user, for example `walletfeed`.
8. Click **Next**.
9. On the **Set Permissions** page, click **Next** (you add the policy after you make the user).
10. Click **Create user**.
11. Click **View user**.
12. Click the **Permissions** tab.
13. Click **Add permissions**.
14. Click **Create inline policy**.
15. In the **Policy editor**, select **JSON**.
16. Delete all the JSON in the editor.
17. If you sent the policy to your computer, copy the policy on your computer.
18. Paste the policy from WalletFeed in the editor.
19. Click **Next**.
20. In **Policy Name**, type a name for the policy, for example `walletfeed`.
21. Click **Create policy**.

> **Note:** AWS recommends temporary credentials for a person who uses AWS. For an app that cannot use an IAM role, the AWS documentation gives the steps to make an IAM user. WalletFeed accepts only the access key of an IAM user. It does not accept temporary credentials.

For more information, refer to [Create an IAM user for workloads that can't use IAM roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/getting-started-workloads.html).

## Step 4: Make an access key

1. On the page of the user, click the **Security credentials** tab.
2. In the **Access keys** section, click **Create access key**.
3. On the **Access key best practices & alternatives** page, select **Other**.
4. Click **Next**.
5. Type a description for the key, for example `WalletFeed on iPhone`, or keep the field empty.
6. Click **Create access key**.
7. Click **Show**. AWS shows the secret access key.
8. If you use IAM on your computer, send the access key ID and the secret access key to your iPhone.
9. Keep this page open until WalletFeed has the two values.

> **Note:** AWS shows the secret access key only one time. If you do not have it, you can make a new access key.

For more information, refer to [How an IAM administrator can manage IAM user access keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access-keys-admin-managed.html).

## Step 5: Paste the key and start to send

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed again.
2. If the AWS screen is not open, do Step 2 again.
3. Copy the access key ID.
4. In WalletFeed, paste the access key ID in **Access Key ID**. The first letters of the ID in the field are `AKIA`.
5. Copy the secret access key.
6. In WalletFeed, paste the secret access key in **Secret Access Key**.
7. Tap **Add**. WalletFeed uses the key to do a test of the resource.
8. If WalletFeed shows an error message below **Share IAM Policy**, refer to [If there is a problem](#if-there-is-a-problem).
9. Read the message, for example **Send Transactions to Amazon S3?**

   The message tells you the data that the service will receive, the accounts and the start date.
10. Tap **Send**. WalletFeed adds the destination and starts to send your transactions.

The test after you tap **Add** is different for each service:

- For Amazon S3, WalletFeed writes a test file in the prefix, for example `walletfeed/walletfeed-test.csv`. Then it deletes the file.
- For Amazon SQS, Kinesis Data Streams and EventBridge, WalletFeed sends one test event with the description `WalletFeed test transaction`.
- For DynamoDB, WalletFeed reads the keys of the table. It does not write an item.

If you tap **Cancel** in the message, WalletFeed does not add the destination. The AWS screen stays open.

The name of the new destination contains the name of the service and the name of the resource, for example **Amazon S3 · my-bucket**.

> **Note:** WalletFeed keeps the access key in the Keychain on your iPhone. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to your AWS account. After AWS receives your transactions, the terms of AWS are applicable to them.

## Data that AWS receives

| Service | Data |
| --- | --- |
| Amazon S3 | One file for each month, for example `walletfeed/transactions/2026-10.csv`, or `.jsonl` for JSON Lines. |
| Amazon SQS | One message for each change. The body of the message is the event. |
| Kinesis Data Streams | One record for each change. The data is the event, and the partition key is the `id` of the transaction. |
| DynamoDB | One item for each transaction, with the partition key `id`. A change replaces the item. |
| EventBridge | One event for each change, from the source `app.walletfeed`. The `detail` field is the WalletFeed event. |

In an EventBridge event, `detail-type` is `Transaction Created`, `Transaction Updated` or `Transaction Deleted`.

Each event is a JSON object with these fields:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `event` | `created` the first time, then `updated` after each change. `deleted` if a transaction becomes declined or expired, or Wallet removes it. |
| `id` | The WalletFeed ID of the transaction. |
| `date` | The day of the transaction, in the time zone of your iPhone. |
| `merchant` | The merchant name, or the description if Wallet has no merchant name. |
| `amount` | The value of the transaction. For purchases and fees, the value is less than zero. For payments and refunds, it is more than zero. |
| `currency` | The currency code, for example `USD`. |
| `category` | The WalletFeed category, for example `Groceries` or `Dining`. |
| `status` | The status in Wallet, for example `pending`, `authorized` or `booked`. |
| `pending` | `true` when the status is `pending` or `authorized`, and `false` at other times. |
| `account` | The account name, for example Apple Card. |
| `description` | The description of the transaction in Wallet. |
| `type` | The transaction type in Wallet, for example `pointOfSale` or `refund`. |
| `mcc` | The merchant category code. |
| `foreignAmount` | For a purchase in a different currency, the value in that currency. It has the same sign (plus or minus) as `amount`. |
| `foreignCurrency` | The code of that different currency. |

If Wallet does not give a value, the value is `null`, for example `foreignAmount` for a purchase in dollars. A `deleted` event has only `event` and `id`.

WalletFeed sends the test event on one line. The `date` is the day of the test. For Amazon SQS, Kinesis Data Streams and EventBridge, the test event has these values:

```json
{
  "account": "Sample Card",
  "amount": -4.2,
  "category": "Shopping",
  "currency": "USD",
  "date": "2026-10-30",
  "description": "WalletFeed test transaction",
  "event": "created",
  "foreignAmount": null,
  "foreignCurrency": null,
  "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
  "mcc": 5734,
  "merchant": "WalletFeed",
  "pending": true,
  "status": "pending",
  "type": "purchase"
}
```

In DynamoDB, each field is an attribute of the item. Strings are type S, numbers are type N, and `true` or `false` is type BOOL. WalletFeed does not write the fields that have no value.

In Amazon S3, a JSON Lines file has one line for each transaction. Each line is an object with the same fields, but with no `event`.

In Amazon S3, a CSV file has 16 columns. The first columns are Date, Posted Date, Merchant, Description, Original Description, Amount, Currency and Direction. The last columns are Status, Type, Category, MCC, Account, Foreign Amount, Foreign Currency and WalletFeed ID.

## New and changed transactions

While WalletFeed is open, AWS receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then sends the change. **Background Sync** is on until you set it to off.

When the status of a pending transaction changes to `booked`, WalletFeed sends the same transaction again. If a transaction becomes declined or expired, or if Wallet removes it, WalletFeed sends a `deleted` event. A refund is a different transaction, and its `amount` is more than zero.

In Amazon S3, when a month has a change, WalletFeed replaces the file of that month with a new file. The new file does not contain the deleted transactions. In DynamoDB, a change replaces the item, and a `deleted` event deletes the item. Thus, Amazon S3 and DynamoDB keep one copy of each transaction.

Amazon SQS, Kinesis Data Streams and EventBridge can receive the same event more than one time. You can use `id` to find the transaction in your data. If the `event` and `status` did not change, you can ignore the event. If WalletFeed sends a transaction to a FIFO queue again with no changes in 5 minutes or less, the queue ignores it.

If AWS does not accept some records, WalletFeed sends them again after 1 second. If AWS does not accept them again, the destination shows "AWS rejected" and the number of records. WalletFeed tries to send the records again when it sends more changes.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

To send transactions from a different period, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the AWS destination (the first part of its name is the name of the service, for example **Amazon S3 ·**).
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

Amazon SQS, Kinesis Data Streams and EventBridge receive each transaction again, as a `created` event. Amazon S3 and DynamoDB keep one copy of each transaction.

To stop **Send History**, tap **Send History** › **Stop Sending**.

## Change or remove the destination

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the AWS destination.

   ![The screen of a Lunch Money destination, with Name, Enabled, Last Sync, Replace Token, Filter, Send History, Send Test and Delete.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-aws/walletfeed-destination-detail.webp)

The screen of an AWS destination has the same controls, but it has no **Replace Token**. It shows the resource, for example **Bucket** or **Queue**. Below the resource, it shows **Region**, **Share IAM Policy** and **Replace Key**.

To send only some transactions:

1. Set **Filter** to on.
2. Select the transactions with **Accounts**, **Categories**, **Minimum** and the other controls.

For more information, refer to [Choose what to send](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

To stop the destination but keep it, set **Enabled** to off.

To use a different access key:

1. Tap **Replace Key**.
2. Paste the access key ID in **Access Key ID**.
3. Paste the secret access key in **Secret Access Key**.
4. Tap **Replace**.

When you tap **Replace**, WalletFeed does the same test that it does after you tap **Add**. WalletFeed keeps the new key only if the test is satisfactory. For Amazon SQS, Kinesis Data Streams and EventBridge, WalletFeed sends one test event.

You cannot change the region or the resource of a destination. You can have more than one AWS destination, for example a bucket and a queue.

To use a different resource:

1. Do Step 1 thru Step 5 again for the new resource.
2. Delete the destination that you do not use.

To remove the destination:

1. Tap **Delete**.
2. Tap **Delete** again.

WalletFeed tells you "Transactions already sent stay at the destination." The data stays in your AWS account until you delete it in AWS.

If no destination uses the access key, delete the key in IAM:

1. In the IAM console, click **Users**.
2. Click the name of the user.
3. Click the **Security credentials** tab.
4. In the **Access keys** section, click **Actions** for the key.
5. Click **Deactivate**.
6. In the dialog, click **Deactivate** again.
7. Click **Actions** for the key.
8. Click **Delete**.
9. In the dialog, type the access key ID.
10. Click **Delete**.

## If there is a problem

### If you cannot tap Add

WalletFeed lets you tap **Add** only when all the necessary fields have a value. **Region** must contain only letters, numbers and hyphens.

1. Make sure that **Access Key ID** and **Secret Access Key** are not empty.
2. Make sure that **Region** has a code, for example `us-east-1`, and not a name, for example US East.
3. For Amazon S3, make sure that **Bucket** is not empty.
4. If **Endpoint** has a value, make sure that its first part is not `http://`. WalletFeed accepts only HTTPS.
5. For Amazon SQS, paste all of the queue URL again. The first part of the URL is `https://sqs.`.
6. For Kinesis Data Streams or DynamoDB, make sure that **Stream** or **Table** is not empty.

### If WalletFeed shows "Key rejected"

AWS did not accept the key, or the IAM policy of the user does not let the key do the action. WalletFeed shows the HTTP code, for example "Key rejected (HTTP 403). Check the key and its IAM policy."

1. Copy the access key ID.
2. In WalletFeed, paste the access key ID in **Access Key ID**.
3. Copy the secret access key.
4. In WalletFeed, paste the secret access key in **Secret Access Key**.
5. In the IAM console, open the user.
6. On the **Permissions** tab, make sure that the user has the policy from **Share IAM Policy**.
7. If you changed the resource or the region after you got the policy, tap **Share IAM Policy** again.
8. If you got a new policy, replace the policy of the user with the new policy.
9. In WalletFeed, tap **Add**.

### If WalletFeed shows "Wrong region for this bucket."

The bucket is not in the region that **Region** shows.

1. In the Amazon S3 console, find the region of the bucket.
2. In WalletFeed, type the code of that region in **Region**.
3. Tap **Add**.

### If WalletFeed shows "Not found. Check the name and the region."

AWS did not find a bucket with the name in **Bucket**.

1. In WalletFeed, make sure that the name in **Bucket** is the same as the bucket name in AWS.
2. Make sure that **Region** has the code of the region of the bucket.
3. Tap **Add**.

### If WalletFeed shows a message about the partition key

If the DynamoDB table has a different partition key or a sort key, WalletFeed shows "The table's partition key must be a string named id."

1. Make a new DynamoDB table with the partition key `id` of the type String, and no sort key.
2. In WalletFeed, type the name of the new table in **Table**.
3. Tap **Share IAM Policy**.
4. Replace the policy of the user with the new policy.
5. Tap **Add**.

### If WalletFeed shows "Couldn't connect" with HTTP 400

WalletFeed shows "Couldn't connect: The server returned an error (HTTP 400)." AWS did not accept the data from WalletFeed. For example, the name of the queue, the stream, the table or the event bus is incorrect. The resource can also be in a different region.

1. In the AWS console, find the resource and its region.
2. In WalletFeed, type the name of the resource again, or paste the queue URL again.
3. In **Region**, type the code of the region of the resource.
4. Tap **Add**.

### If the destination shows "Authentication failed"

AWS did not accept the key the last time that WalletFeed sent changes. For example, a person deactivated or deleted the key, or removed the policy from the user.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.

   ![The Destinations list, with an n8n destination that shows Authentication failed.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-aws/walletfeed-destinations-failure.webp)
2. Tap the AWS destination.

   ![The screen of an n8n destination, with Authentication failed below Last Sync.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-aws/walletfeed-destination-failure.webp)
3. If the user has no policy from WalletFeed, add the policy to the user (refer to [Step 3](#step-3-make-an-iam-user-with-the-policy)).
4. If the user has no active access key, make a new access key (refer to [Step 4](#step-4-make-an-access-key)).
5. Tap **Replace Key**.
6. Paste the access key ID in **Access Key ID**.
7. Paste the secret access key in **Secret Access Key**.
8. Tap **Replace**.

### If the destination shows "AWS rejected" or "AWS throttled"

AWS did not accept some records, and it did not accept them again after 1 second. "AWS throttled" tells you that the resource received data too frequently. WalletFeed tries to send the records again when it sends more changes.

1. In WalletFeed, open the AWS destination.
2. Tap **Send Test**.
3. If **Send Test** shows HTTP 403, do the steps in [If the destination shows "Authentication failed"](#if-the-destination-shows-authentication-failed).
4. If the destination shows the error message again after WalletFeed sends more changes, examine the resource in the AWS console.

### If the EventBridge target receives no events

EventBridge sends an event to a target only when a rule on the event bus selects the event.

1. In the EventBridge console, make sure that the rule is on the same event bus as **Event Bus** in WalletFeed.
2. Make sure that the rule is in the same region as the destination.
3. Make sure that the event pattern of the rule is `{"source": ["app.walletfeed"]}`.
4. In WalletFeed, open the AWS destination.
5. Tap **Send Test**.

### If AWS does not receive new data

WalletFeed sends changes while it is open, or when iOS starts it in the background.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Make sure that **Background Sync** is on in **Settings** › **Sync**.
3. Open the AWS destination.
4. Make sure that the destination shows no error message below **Last Sync**.
5. Tap **Send Test**. AWS receives the test transaction with the description `WalletFeed test transaction`.

   For Amazon S3, WalletFeed writes the test file in the prefix, for example `walletfeed/walletfeed-test.csv`, and keeps the file. For DynamoDB, WalletFeed writes an item with the `id` `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`.
6. For Amazon S3 or DynamoDB, delete the test file or the test item in AWS.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to BankSync

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a table in BankSync. Then your AI agents can read the table through BankSync's MCP tools or its REST API.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed, with access to your Wallet accounts. Refer to [Select the Wallet accounts that WalletFeed reads](/docs/wallet-accounts/).
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), which is necessary for destinations. WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.
- A BankSync account. If you do not have a BankSync account, you can make the account in [Step 2](#step-2-connect-walletfeed-to-banksync).
- Access to your BankSync workspace as the owner or an admin.
- A workspace that can have one more table. On the Free plan, a workspace can have only one table.
- For an API key, BankSync's Standard plan or a higher plan.

## Your key stays on your iPhone

- WalletFeed keeps the API key or the sign-in in the Keychain on your iPhone. iOS encrypts the Keychain.
- The API key or the sign-in does not go to iCloud Keychain or to your other devices.
- WalletFeed has no account and no servers. No person at WalletFeed can see or get the API key or the sign-in.
- Your iPhone sends the API key or the sign-in only to BankSync, in each request to BankSync.
- When you delete the destination, WalletFeed deletes the API key or the sign-in from your iPhone. You can also delete the key, or remove WalletFeed, in BankSync.

## Step 1: Open BankSync in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the **Budgeting** section, tap **BankSync**.

   ![The Add Destination list with BankSync at the top of the Budgeting section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows the WalletFeed Pro screen before the BankSync form.

## Step 2: Connect WalletFeed to BankSync

You can use **Sign In with BankSync** on all BankSync plans, which include the Free plan. With **Sign In with BankSync**, WalletFeed can get access only to its **Apple Card** table. To use an API key, refer to [Connect with an API key](#connect-with-an-api-key).

The **Sign In with BankSync** button uses WalletFeed's referral URL. Thus, the form shows the text "WalletFeed may earn a commission if you pay for BankSync."

1. Tap **Sign In with BankSync**.

   ![The BankSync form in WalletFeed with Sign In with BankSync and Use an API Key Instead.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/walletfeed-setup-banksync.webp)

2. On the BankSync page, tap **Continue with Google**, or type your e-mail address in **Email**.

   ![The BankSync sign-in page with Continue with Google, an Email field and Continue with email.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/banksync-sign-in-with-banksync.webp)

3. If you typed an e-mail address, tap **Continue with email**.
4. If you have a BankSync account, complete the sign-in.
5. If you typed a new e-mail address, do these steps:

   1. Type a password in **Password**.
   2. Type the password again in **Confirm password**.
   3. Tap **Create account**.
   4. In your e-mail app, open the e-mail "Verify your email for BankSync".
   5. Tap the hyperlink in the e-mail.
   6. Open WalletFeed again.
   7. Tap **I've verified my email**.

      ![The BankSync Check your inbox screen with the I've verified my email button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/banksync-check-inbox.webp)

6. On the BankSync page about WalletFeed, give WalletFeed access to your workspace. Only the owner or an admin of the workspace can do this step.

   When you give access, BankSync adds WalletFeed to the workspace and makes the **Apple Card** table. WalletFeed waits a maximum of approximately 30 seconds for the table. Then the form shows **Signed In** and your workspace.

7. Tap **Add**.

## Step 3: Start to send transactions

After you tap **Add**, WalletFeed shows the message "Send Transactions to BankSync?". The message tells you the data that BankSync will receive, the Wallet accounts and the start date of the transactions.

1. Read the message.
2. Tap **Send**.

If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes BankSync from your destinations.

## Step 4: Find the table in BankSync

1. On a computer, open [app.banksync.io](https://app.banksync.io) in a web browser.
2. Get access to your BankSync account.
3. Click **Tables** at the top of the page.
4. If you used **Sign In with BankSync**, click the **Apple Card** table.
5. If you used an API key, click the table with the name from **Table** in WalletFeed.

   ![The BankSync Tables page with the Apple Card (WalletFeed) table.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/banksync-tables.webp)

6. To show only the columns that have data, do the steps in [If many columns in the table are empty](#if-many-columns-in-the-table-are-empty).

   ![Six sample transactions in the BankSync table, with the Date, Description, Amount, Category, Account Name, Pending and Wallet Status columns.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/banksync-result-walletfeed-columns.webp)

## Connect with an API key

You can also connect WalletFeed to BankSync with an API key. API keys are available only on BankSync's Standard plan or a higher plan. If you use an API key, WalletFeed makes the table. You can change the name of the table in WalletFeed.

The screenshots show BankSync in a web browser on a computer.

### Make an API key in BankSync

1. On a computer, open [app.banksync.io](https://app.banksync.io) in a web browser.
2. Get access to your BankSync account as the owner or an admin of the workspace.
3. Click the workspace name at the top left of the page.
4. Click **Settings**.

   ![The BankSync workspace menu with Settings selected.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/banksync-workspace-menu.webp)

5. In the sidebar, in the **WORKSPACE** group, click **Developers**.

   ![The BankSync Settings page with Developers in the sidebar.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/banksync-settings-developers.webp)

6. Click the **API Keys** tab.
7. Click **Create Key**.
8. In **Key Name**, type `WalletFeed`.
9. In **Expiration**, select **1 year** or **Never**.
