   When you click **Create Key**, BankSync selects **90 days**. After 90 days, WalletFeed cannot send transactions to BankSync with the expired key.

10. In **Permissions**, in the **tables** row, select **read** and **write**.
11. Click **Create API Key**.
12. Click the copy button (**Copy to clipboard**) adjacent to the `bsk_` key. BankSync shows the key only one time.
13. Click **Done**.

> **Note:** **Select all** gives the key full access to your workspace. WalletFeed uses only **read** and **write** in the **tables** row.

> **Note:** If you use a Mac with the same Apple Account as your iPhone, you can paste the key on your iPhone with [Universal Clipboard](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102430).

### Add the key in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open the BankSync form. Refer to [Step 1](#step-1-open-banksync-in-walletfeed).
2. Tap **Use an API Key Instead**.
3. Paste the key in **API Key**.
4. To use a different name for the table, type the name in **Table**.

   Until you change the name, **Table** contains **Apple Card (WalletFeed)**.

5. Tap **Add**.
6. In the message "Send Transactions to BankSync?", tap **Send**.
7. To find the table in BankSync, do the steps in [Step 4](#step-4-find-the-table-in-banksync).

## Data that BankSync receives

WalletFeed adds one row to the table for each transaction. Each row gets this data:

| Data | BankSync column |
| --- | --- |
| The transaction ID | **ID** |
| The posted date, or the purchase date while the charge is pending | **Date** |
| The purchase date | **Authorized Date** |
| The value, less than 0 for a purchase and more than 0 for a credit, for example a refund | **Amount** |
| The value of a purchase, or 0 | **Debit Amount** |
| The value of a credit, or 0 | **Credit Amount** |
| The currency, for example USD | **Currency** |
| The description that Wallet shows | **Description** |
| The card statement text | **Original Description** |
| The merchant name, if Wallet has one | **Merchant Name** |
| The WalletFeed category, for example Groceries or Travel | **Category** |
| The account name, for example Apple Card or Apple Cash | **Account Name** |
| Selected while the charge is pending | **Pending** |
| The Wallet status, for example `pending` or `booked` | **Wallet Status** |
| The merchant category code | **MCC** |
| For a purchase in a different currency, the value in that currency | **Foreign Amount** |
| For a purchase in a different currency, that currency | **Foreign Currency** |

BankSync's transactions table has more columns, for example **Card Last 4** and **Bank**. WalletFeed does not put data in them.

## Read the table with an AI agent

BankSync has a REST API and an MCP server. An AI agent that you connect to BankSync can read the Apple Card table with the BankSync table tools, for example `query_table_rows` and `aggregate_table_rows`. Thus, the agent can read your Apple Card transactions and the transactions from your other banks in BankSync.

BankSync includes API and MCP access on the Standard plan or a higher plan. On the Free plan, the **API Keys** tab shows "API & MCP aren't included on your plan".

1. To connect an AI agent, make an API key for the agent on the **API Keys** tab.

For more information, refer to [BankSync's guide to API keys](https://banksync.io/docs/api/api-keys).

## New and changed transactions

- While WalletFeed is open, BankSync receives changes in seconds.
- When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then sends the change.
- BankSync receives a pending charge with **Pending** selected. When the charge posts, WalletFeed changes the row of the charge. **Date** changes to the posted date, and **Pending** is not selected.
- A refund gets a new row with an **Amount** of more than 0.
- If a pending charge does not post, WalletFeed removes its row. BankSync moves the row to its trash.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. On the Free plan, a BankSync workspace can have a maximum of 5,000 rows.

After you add BankSync, you can send more previous transactions with **Send History**. Refer to [Send previous transactions](/docs/send-history/).

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap your BankSync destination.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

To stop **Send History** while WalletFeed sends the transactions, do these steps:

1. Tap **Send History**.
2. Tap **Stop Sending**.

## Change or remove the destination

The BankSync destination has the name "BankSync ·", then the name of your BankSync workspace.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap your BankSync destination.

On the destination screen, you can do these tasks:

| Task | Steps |
| --- | --- |
| Send only some transactions | Set **Filter** to on. Refer to [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/). |
| Stop the destination for a time | Set **Enabled** to off. |
| Change the name | Type a new name in **Name**. |
| Replace the API key | Tap **Replace Key**. Paste the new key. Tap **Replace**. |
| Get access again with **Sign In with BankSync** | Tap **Sign In Again**. |
| Remove the destination | Tap **Delete**. Then tap **Delete** again. |

When you remove the destination, the table and its rows stay in BankSync. WalletFeed tells you "Transactions already sent stay at the destination."

In **Settings** › **Developers** in BankSync, you can remove the access that WalletFeed has to your workspace. The **Connected Apps** tab shows the apps that have access to your workspace. The **API Keys** tab shows your API keys.

## If there is a problem

### If BankSync shows "Upgrade to create API keys"

The Free plan and the Starter plan do not include API keys.

![The BankSync API Keys page on the Free plan, with Upgrade to create API keys.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/banksync-api-keys-free-plan.webp)

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Sign In with BankSync Instead**.
2. Do the steps in [Step 2](#step-2-connect-walletfeed-to-banksync).

You can also change to the Standard plan or a higher plan in BankSync. Then you can use an API key.

### If WalletFeed shows "Key rejected"

BankSync did not accept the key. These are the possible causes:

- The key is incorrect or expired.
- The key does not have **read** and **write** in the **tables** row.
- The workspace is on the Free plan or the Starter plan. These plans do not include API keys.

1. Make a new key. Refer to [Make an API key in BankSync](#make-an-api-key-in-banksync).
2. If the BankSync form is open, do these steps:

   1. Paste the new key in **API Key**.
   2. Tap **Add**.

3. If **Destinations** shows your BankSync destination, do these steps on the destination screen:

   1. Tap **Replace Key**.
   2. Paste the new key.
   3. Tap **Replace**.

### If WalletFeed shows "hasn't created or shared the Apple Card table"

The workspace has the maximum number of tables for its plan, or BankSync did not make the table in approximately 30 seconds. WalletFeed tells you the limit of your plan, for example "The Free plan allows one table."

The table limit is 1 on Free, 2 on Starter, 5 on Standard, 25 on Professional and 100 on Business.

1. Tap **Open BankSync**.
2. Delete a table that you do not use, or change to a plan that has more tables.
3. In WalletFeed, tap **Try Again**.
4. If WalletFeed shows the message again, tap **Sign In Again**.

### If BankSync does not accept the sign-in

Only the owner or an admin of the workspace can give WalletFeed access to the workspace. WalletFeed shows "BankSync didn't accept the sign-in", or BankSync shows a message on its page.

1. Tap **Sign In with BankSync** again.
2. Get access to your BankSync account as the owner or an admin of the workspace.
3. If BankSync does not accept the sign-in again and your plan includes API keys, use an API key. Refer to [Connect with an API key](#connect-with-an-api-key).

### If the destination shows "Authentication failed"

BankSync did not accept the key or the sign-in. An expired API key can cause this message.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap your BankSync destination.
3. If the destination screen shows **Replace Key**, do these steps:

   1. Make a new key. Refer to [Make an API key in BankSync](#make-an-api-key-in-banksync).
   2. Tap **Replace Key**.
   3. Paste the new key.
   4. Tap **Replace**.

4. If the destination screen shows **Sign In Again**, tap **Sign In Again**.

WalletFeed can also show "Signed out. Sign in again in the destination's settings." Step 4 corrects this problem.

### If BankSync does not accept new rows

Your BankSync workspace has the maximum number of rows for your plan, for example 5,000 rows on the Free plan. The destination then shows the error from BankSync.

1. In BankSync, delete rows that you do not use, or change to a plan that has more rows.

### If BankSync shows only its logo

After you tap the hyperlink in the e-mail from BankSync, the BankSync page can show only the BankSync logo.

1. Load the page again.

### If BankSync has no Tables tab

BankSync's documentation tells you that Tables is in beta, and that BankSync activates Tables for each workspace.

1. In BankSync, click **Settings** › **Support**.
2. Tell BankSync customer support that your workspace has no **Tables** tab.

### If many columns in the table are empty

A BankSync transactions table has 24 columns, and WalletFeed puts data in 12 of them. The table also has 5 more columns for WalletFeed data, for example **Pending** and **Wallet Status**, at the right end of the table.

1. In the table, click **Fields**.
2. Remove the empty columns from the view.
3. Click **Save view**.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Coda

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a table in Coda. Coda changed its name to Superhuman Docs. You make the table and an API token in Superhuman Docs, and then you paste the token in WalletFeed.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed, and an Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account that WalletFeed can read.
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), which is necessary for [destinations](/docs/destinations/). It is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.
- A Superhuman Docs account. You can make an API token on the Free plan.
- A computer with a web browser, for the steps in Superhuman Docs.

## Your token stays on your iPhone

- WalletFeed keeps the API token in the Keychain on your iPhone. iOS encrypts the Keychain.
- The API token does not go to iCloud Keychain or to your other devices.
- WalletFeed has no account and no servers. No person at WalletFeed can see or get the API token.
- Your iPhone sends the API token only to Superhuman Docs, in each request to Superhuman Docs.
- When you delete the destination, WalletFeed deletes the API token from your iPhone. You can also delete the token in Superhuman Docs.

## Step 1: Make a doc and a table in Superhuman Docs

1. On your computer, open [Superhuman Docs](https://docs.superhuman.com/).
2. Get access to your Superhuman Docs account.
3. Click **+ New doc**.

   ![The Superhuman Docs home page, with the New doc button at the top of the sidebar.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-docs-home.webp)

4. If a message or the **Docs AI** panel opens, close it.
5. If the sidebar with the list of pages is not open, click the sidebar button at the top left.
6. Click the doc name, **Untitled doc**, at the top of the sidebar.

   ![A new doc in Superhuman Docs, with its name, Untitled doc, at the top of the sidebar.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-new-doc.webp)

7. Type a name for the doc, for example `WalletFeed`.
8. Press **Return**.
9. Click in the page, below **Add page title**. If you do not click in the page, Superhuman Docs adds the text that you type to the doc name.
10. Type `/table`.
11. In the menu, below **Tables**, click **Table**.

    ![The menu that opens when you type /table, with the Table item at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-insert-table.webp)

12. In the **New table** panel, click **Start blank**.

    ![The New table panel, with Start blank at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-start-blank.webp)

13. Double-click the table name, **Table**. This selects all of the name.
14. Type `WalletFeed Transactions`. In Step 4, WalletFeed selects the table that has this name.

    ![The table with its new name, WalletFeed Transactions.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-name-table.webp)

15. Press **Return**.
16. Keep the doc in **My Docs**.
17. Do not use **Share** on the doc.

> **Note:** On the Free plan, a doc that other persons can open has a limit of 1,000 table rows. If the doc has more rows than this limit for 14 days, Superhuman Docs stops all changes to the doc. A doc that only you can open does not have this limit.

## Step 2: Make the columns

WalletFeed writes only to the columns that have the names in this table. Only the **WalletFeed ID** column is necessary. Each name must have the same letters and spaces as in this table, but the letters can be uppercase or lowercase.

| Column name | Column type |
|---|---|
| WalletFeed ID | Text |
| Date | Date |
| Merchant | Text |
| Amount | Number |
| Currency | Text |
| Category | Text |
| Status | Text |
| Pending | Checkbox |
| Account | Text |
| Description | Text |
| Type | Text |
| MCC | Number |
| Foreign Amount | Number |
| Foreign Currency | Text |

A new table has four columns: **Name**, **Column 2**, **Column 3** and **Notes**. You change their names first, and then you add the other 10 columns.

1. Click the column name **Name**. This selects the column.
2. Click **Name** again.
3. Type `WalletFeed ID`.

   ![The first column, with its new name, WalletFeed ID.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-rename-first-column.webp)

4. Press **Return**.
5. Change the name of **Column 2** to `Date`, as in steps 1 to 4.
6. Put the pointer on **Date**. Superhuman Docs shows the type button (**T**) on the right side of the column name.
7. Click the type button.
8. Click **Column type** › **Date** › **Date**.

   ![The menu of the Date column, with Column type, Date and Date.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-column-type-date.webp)

9. Change the name of **Column 3** to `Merchant`, as in steps 1 to 4.
10. Change the name of **Notes** to `Amount`, as in steps 1 to 4.
11. Put the pointer on **Amount**.
12. Click the type button.
13. Click **Column type** › **Number** › **Number**. This step is necessary because the **Notes** column has the type **Canvas**.

    ![The menu of the Amount column, with Column type, Number and Number.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-column-type-number.webp)

14. Put the pointer on the column names. Superhuman Docs shows the **+** button at the right end of the column names.
15. If the table is wider than the window, scroll the table fully to the right.
16. Click **+**.

    ![The plus button at the end of the column names, which adds a column.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-add-column.webp)

17. In **Pick column type**, click **Text**.

    ![The Pick column type menu, with Text at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-pick-column-type.webp)

18. Type `Currency`. If you do not type a name, the column has the name **Text**, and WalletFeed does not write to it.

    ![A new column with the name Currency.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-name-new-column.webp)

19. Press **Return**.
20. For each column from `Category` to `Foreign Currency`, do steps 14 to 19 again, with its name and its column type. For a **Number** column, click **Number** › **Number** in step 17.
21. Put the pointer on the table.
22. Click **Options**.
23. Click **Columns**. The panel shows the 14 columns and their types.

    ![The Columns panel, with all 14 WalletFeed columns and their types.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-all-columns.webp)

You can delete the three empty rows of the new table. For each empty row, do these steps:

1. Right-click the row.
2. If the menu does not show **Delete row**, scroll to the bottom of the menu.
3. Click **Delete row**.

## Step 3: Make an API token in Superhuman Docs

1. On your computer, open the [Superhuman Docs home page](https://docs.superhuman.com/).
2. Click your name at the bottom of the sidebar.
3. Click **Account settings**.

   ![The account menu, with Account settings.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-account-menu.webp)

4. In the list on the left side, click **API connections**.

   ![The Account settings page, with API connections in the list on the left side.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-account-settings.webp)

5. In **API tokens**, click **Generate API token**.

   ![The API tokens section, with the Generate API token button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-api-connections.webp)

6. In **Name**, type `WalletFeed`.
7. Click **Permission**. It shows **Read only** until you change it.
8. Click **Read and write**. With a **Read only** token, Superhuman Docs does not accept the transactions from WalletFeed.

   ![The New API token dialog, with Read and write in the Permission list.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-token-permission.webp)

9. In **Scopes**, keep **Content** and **All** selected. With **Selected content**, WalletFeed cannot find your doc.

   ![The New API token dialog with the name WalletFeed, Read and write in Permission, Content and All in Scopes, and the Generate token button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-token-settings.webp)

10. Click **Generate token**.
11. In **API token generated**, click **Copy**. Superhuman Docs shows the token only one time.

    ![The API token generated dialog, with the Copy button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-token-created.webp)

12. If you closed the dialog before you clicked **Copy**, do steps 5 to 11 again.

> **Note:** If you use a Mac with the same Apple Account as your iPhone, you can paste the token on the iPhone with [Universal Clipboard](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102430).

> **Note:** On your iPhone, **Open Account Settings** on the Coda screen in WalletFeed opens **Account settings** › **API connections** in Superhuman Docs.

## Step 4: Add Coda in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The empty Destinations screen, with the plus button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. Below **Sheets & Databases**, tap **Coda**. If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed first shows the **WalletFeed Pro** screen.
5. Paste the token in **API Token**.

   ![The Coda screen in WalletFeed, with the API Token field and three steps for Coda.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/walletfeed-setup-coda.webp)

6. If **Doc** does not show your doc, select your doc in **Doc**.
7. If **Table** does not show **WalletFeed Transactions**, select **WalletFeed Transactions** in **Table**.
8. Tap **Add**.
9. If WalletFeed shows a message in red below the fields, refer to [If there is a problem](#if-there-is-a-problem).
10. Read the **Send Transactions to Coda?** message.

    The message tells you which data the destination will receive, from which accounts and from which date. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the destination.

11. Tap **Send**.

    ![A Superhuman Docs table with six sample transactions in the 14 WalletFeed columns.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-walletfeed-result.webp)

After some seconds, your table in Superhuman Docs shows your transactions. In **Destinations**, the new destination has the name of your doc after Coda, for example **Coda · WalletFeed**.

## Data in each column

WalletFeed writes these values to the columns:

| Column | Value |
|---|---|
| WalletFeed ID | The ID of the transaction in Wallet. WalletFeed uses it to find the row again. |
| Date | The date of the transaction, in the time zone of your iPhone. |
| Merchant | The merchant name, or the description if Wallet has no merchant name. |
| Amount | The value of the transaction. |
| Currency | The currency code, for example USD. |
| Category | The WalletFeed category, for example Dining or Groceries. |
| Status | The status in Wallet, for example `pending` or `booked`. |
| Pending | A selected checkbox while the charge is pending. |
| Account | The account name, for example Apple Card or Apple Cash. |
| Description | The description from Wallet. |
| Type | The transaction type from Wallet, for example `pointOfSale`. |
| MCC | The merchant category code. A **Number** column shows 5814 as 5,814. |
| Foreign Amount | The value in the currency of the merchant. |
| Foreign Currency | The currency code of the merchant. |

A value in **Amount** or **Foreign Amount** is less than zero for money that goes out of the account. It is more than zero for money that goes into the account. **Foreign Amount** and **Foreign Currency** are empty for a transaction in US dollars.

Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to Superhuman Docs. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. WalletFeed keeps the token in the Keychain on your iPhone. After Superhuman Docs receives your transactions, the terms of Superhuman Docs are applicable to them.

## New and changed transactions

While WalletFeed is open, the table receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then sends the change.

A pending charge has a selected checkbox in **Pending**. When the charge changes from pending to posted, WalletFeed updates the same row.

For a refund or a payment, WalletFeed adds a new row with a value more than zero in **Amount**. For a declined charge, WalletFeed deletes the row. When Wallet removes a transaction, WalletFeed also deletes the row of that transaction.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › [**Initial History**](/docs/send-history/). **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

To send history from the screen of the destination, do these steps:

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Coda destination.
2. Tap **Send History**.
3. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

While WalletFeed sends the history, it shows **Sending History**. WalletFeed does not add a second row for a transaction that is in the table.

## Change or remove the destination

In WalletFeed, you change the destination on its screen. To open this screen, you tap the Coda destination in **Destinations**.

To send only some transactions:

1. Set **Filter** to on.
2. Set **Include**, **Minimum**, **Include Pending**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**.

For more information, refer to [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

To stop the destination for some time, set **Enabled** to off.

To use a new token:

1. Tap **Replace Token**.
2. Paste the new token.
3. Tap **Replace**. WalletFeed makes sure that the token can read the table and write to it.

To use a column that you make after you add the destination:

1. In Superhuman Docs, give the column a name from the table in Step 2.
2. In WalletFeed, tap **Send Test**. WalletFeed reads the columns again and adds a test row with the merchant WalletFeed.

You can delete the test row in Superhuman Docs.

You can change the name of a column after you add the destination. After the change, WalletFeed writes to the same column.

To remove the destination:

1. Tap **Delete**.
2. Tap **Delete** again. The rows that WalletFeed sent stay in the table.

To stop the token in Superhuman Docs:

1. On your computer, open **Account settings** › **API connections** in Superhuman Docs.
2. On the **WalletFeed** token, click **⋮**.
3. Click **Revoke**.

   ![The token menu, with Revoke.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-token-revoke-menu.webp)

4. In **Revoke token?**, click **Revoke**. After this step, WalletFeed cannot send transactions to the table.

   ![The Revoke token dialog, with the Revoke button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-token-revoke-confirm.webp)

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows "Authentication failed"

Superhuman Docs does not let the token change your table. For example, the token has **Read only** in **Permission**, or you used **Revoke** on the token.

1. On your computer, open **Account settings** › **API connections** in Superhuman Docs. A **Read only** token shows **Read only - Content** below its name.

   ![A token in the API tokens list with the line Read only - Content.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/coda-T1-token-read-only.webp)

2. Make a new token with **Read and write**, as in [Step 3](#step-3-make-an-api-token-in-superhuman-docs).
3. On your iPhone, tap the Coda destination in **Destinations**.
4. Tap **Replace Token**.
5. Paste the new token in **API Token**.
6. Tap **Replace**.

### If WalletFeed shows "The token can't reach this doc. Use one without restrictions."

The token has **Selected content** in **Scopes**. With this token, WalletFeed cannot find your docs.

1. In Superhuman Docs, make a new token with **Content** and **All**, as in Step 3.
2. In WalletFeed, if the screen shows **Replace Token**, tap **Replace Token**.
3. Paste the new token in **API Token**.
4. Tap **Add** or **Replace**.

### If WalletFeed shows "Token rejected (HTTP 401). Check it and try again."

The token is not correct, or you used **Revoke** on it.

1. In Superhuman Docs, make a new token, as in Step 3.
2. Click **Copy** to copy the token. The dots in the dialog are not the token.
3. In WalletFeed, if the screen shows **Replace Token**, tap **Replace Token**.
4. Paste the new token in **API Token**.
5. Tap **Add** or **Replace**.

### If WalletFeed shows "No docs yet. Create one with a table, then come back."

WalletFeed cannot find a doc in your Superhuman Docs account.

1. In Superhuman Docs, make the doc and the table, as in Step 1 and Step 2.
2. In WalletFeed, tap the back button.
3. Tap **Coda** again.
4. Paste the token again.
5. Do steps 6 to 11 in [Step 4](#step-4-add-coda-in-walletfeed).

### If WalletFeed shows "This table needs a column named WalletFeed ID."

No column in the table has the name **WalletFeed ID** with the same letters and spaces.

1. In WalletFeed, make sure that **Table** shows **WalletFeed Transactions**.
2. In Superhuman Docs, change the name of the first column to `WalletFeed ID`.
3. In WalletFeed, tap **Add** again.

### If a column stays empty

The column name is not the same as a name in Step 2, or you added the column after you added the destination. WalletFeed also does not write to a column that has a formula.

1. In Superhuman Docs, correct the name of the column.
2. On your iPhone, tap the Coda destination in **Destinations**.
3. Tap **Send Test**. WalletFeed reads the columns again and adds a test row.

### If WalletFeed shows "Server error (503)"

Superhuman Docs did not add or change the rows in approximately 15 seconds. When WalletFeed sends data again, it also sends these rows.

1. To send the rows at this time, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of **Destinations**.
2. Tap **Sync Now**.

### If Amount shows -23.4 and not -23.40

A **Number** column does not show a zero at the end of a value.

1. In Superhuman Docs, put the pointer on **Amount**.
2. Click the type button on the right side of the column name.
3. Click **Column type** › **Number** › **Currency**.

### If Table shows a table that you deleted

Superhuman Docs can keep the table of a deleted page in its list of tables.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Table**.
2. Tap **WalletFeed Transactions**.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-csv/ -->
# Save Apple Card transactions to a CSV file automatically

WalletFeed writes your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a CSV file in a folder that you select. When your transactions change, WalletFeed updates the file automatically.

## Before you start

For a CSV file that WalletFeed updates, you must have:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- WalletFeed, with access to your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/)
- A folder for the file in iCloud Drive, in **On My iPhone** or in a different file app, for example Dropbox.

WalletFeed is available only in the US.

WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase. Without WalletFeed Pro, you can [make one CSV file](#make-one-csv-file-without-walletfeed-pro), but WalletFeed does not update that file.

## Step 1: Add a CSV file in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations** at the bottom of the screen.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-csv/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the search field, type `CSV`.

   ![The Add Destination screen with the Destinations search field above the Budgeting list.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-csv/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

5. Tap **CSV File**.

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, the **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens. After you get WalletFeed Pro on that screen, the **Files** screen opens.

6. Make sure that **Format** is **CSV**.
7. Make sure that **Save As** is **One File**.

   ![The Files screen shows CSV in Format, One File in Save As and WalletFeed Transactions in Name.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-csv/walletfeed-setup-csv-file.webp)

   With **One File**, WalletFeed writes all your transactions to one file. The newest transaction is at the top of the file. If you select **One File per Month** in **Save As**, WalletFeed writes one file for each month. Each file has its month in the name, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.csv`.

8. Tap **Folder**.
9. Select a folder, for example in iCloud Drive.

   **Folder** then shows the name of the folder.

10. To give the file a different name, change the text in **Name**.

    The name of the file then has `.csv` at the end. For example, if **Name** is `Budget` or `Budget.csv`, the file is `Budget.csv`.

11. Tap **Add** at the top of the screen.

    If you did not select a folder, you cannot tap **Add**.

12. When WalletFeed shows **Save Transactions to Files?**, tap **Save**.

    The message tells you the folder, the data that the folder receives, the accounts and the period. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the new destination.

WalletFeed then writes your transactions to the file. WalletFeed does not keep your transactions in the app.

## Step 2: Open the file

1. On your iPhone, open the Files app.
2. Open the folder that you selected in Step 1.
3. Tap the file, for example `WalletFeed Transactions.csv`.

   With **One File per Month**, each month has a file, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.csv`.

If the folder is in iCloud Drive, you can also open the file on a computer that has access to your iCloud Drive. For the steps to use the file in a spreadsheet, refer to [the Numbers guide](/guides/apple-card-to-numbers/) or [the Excel guide](/guides/apple-card-to-excel/).

## Make one CSV file without WalletFeed Pro

[Export CSV](/docs/export-csv/) makes one CSV file with the transactions from a period that you select. You can use **Export CSV** without WalletFeed Pro. The file does not change after you save it.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Data** section, tap **Export CSV**.

   ![The Settings screen with Export CSV in the Data section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-csv/walletfeed-settings-3.webp)

4. Tap **Range**.

   ![The Export CSV screen shows This Month in Range, 29 transactions and the Export button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-csv/walletfeed-export-csv.webp)

5. Select **This Month**, **Last Month**, **Last 90 Days**, **This Year** or **All**.

   **Transactions** shows the number of transactions in that period.

6. Tap **Export**.
7. Tap **Save to Files**.
8. Select a folder.
9. Tap **Save**.

The name of the file has the period in it, for example `Apple Card Last Month.csv`. If the file has Apple Cash or Savings transactions, the name also starts with `Apple Card`. The file has the same columns as the file that WalletFeed updates.

## Columns in the file

Each CSV file from WalletFeed is UTF-8 text in the RFC 4180 CSV format. The file has one row for each transaction, and these columns:

| Column | Data |
| --- | --- |
| **Date** | The date of the transaction in the time zone of your iPhone, for example 2026-10-28. |
| **Posted Date** | The date when the charge posted. This cell is empty until the charge posts. |
| **Merchant** | The merchant name. If Wallet has no merchant name, this cell has the description. |
| **Description** | The description of the transaction in Wallet. |
| **Original Description** | The text of the transaction from the card network. |
| **Amount** | The value, for example -23.40. The value is a negative number for purchases and fees, and a positive number for payments and refunds. |
| **Currency** | The currency code, for example USD. |
| **Direction** | `debit` for purchases and fees, or `credit` for payments and refunds. |
| **Status** | The status in Wallet: `authorized`, `pending`, `booked` (posted) or `memo`. A file from **Export CSV** can also have `rejected` (declined). |
| **Type** | The transaction type in Wallet, for example `pointOfSale`, `refund` or `transfer`. |
| **Category** | The WalletFeed category, for example **Groceries**, **Dining** or **Cash & Transfers**. |
| **MCC** | The merchant category code from the card network. |
| **Account** | The Wallet account, for example Apple Card. |
| **Foreign Amount** | For a purchase in a different currency, the value in that currency. |
| **Foreign Currency** | The code of that different currency. |
| **WalletFeed ID** | The ID of the transaction. WalletFeed uses it to find and update each row. |

WalletFeed finds each column by its name. Thus, WalletFeed can update `WalletFeed Transactions.csv` after you move its columns. When WalletFeed updates the file, it writes the columns in the sequence that the table shows.

> **Caution:** Do not add columns or rows to `WalletFeed Transactions.csv`. WalletFeed writes only the columns in the table. When WalletFeed updates the file, it removes all other columns and all rows that have no **WalletFeed ID**.

## Changes to the file

While WalletFeed is open, the file receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then updates the file.

If WalletFeed cannot open the folder at that time, the file does not change. WalletFeed then updates the file at these times:

- When you open WalletFeed
- When an automation from **Settings** › **Sync** › **Automations** starts WalletFeed
- While your iPhone is on a charger, at a time that iOS selects.

A pending charge is in the file with the status `pending` or `authorized`. When the charge posts, WalletFeed updates the same row. The status changes to `booked`, and the row stays in its position.

WalletFeed removes the rows of declined charges and the rows of transactions that Wallet removes. A refund is a different transaction. In its row, **Amount** is a positive number and **Direction** is `credit`.

With **One File per Month**, when a transaction in a month changes, WalletFeed writes all the transactions of that month to the file again. If a month has no transactions, WalletFeed does not write a file for that month.

## Send previous transactions

A new CSV file also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. You can select **Today**, **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

To add transactions from before that date, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination, for example **WalletFeed Transactions**.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Select **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

Because WalletFeed finds each row by its **WalletFeed ID**, the file has only one row for each transaction.

## Change or remove the destination

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination, for example **WalletFeed Transactions**.

If you change **Name** on the screen of the destination, the name of the file does not change.

### Send only some transactions to the file

1. On the screen of the destination, set **Filter** to on.
2. Set **Include**, **Minimum**, **Include Pending**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**.

### Use a different folder

1. On the screen of the destination, tap **Change Folder**.
2. Select the new folder.

   Then WalletFeed writes the transactions from the start date to a file in the new folder.

### Stop the changes to the file

1. On the screen of the destination, set **Enabled** to off.

### Remove the destination

1. On the screen of the destination, tap **Delete**.
2. Tap **Delete** again.

   The file stays in the folder. WalletFeed does not remove the transactions that it wrote to the file.

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows “Couldn't open this folder.”

WalletFeed cannot get access to the folder that you selected.

1. Tap **Folder** (or **Change Folder** on the screen of the destination).
2. Select a different folder.

### If WalletFeed shows “Can't open the folder. Choose it again.”

WalletFeed does not have access to the folder of the destination at this time.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Change Folder**.
4. Select the same folder again.

### If WalletFeed shows “The file has no WalletFeed ID column. Rename it to start a new one.”

WalletFeed does not change a file that has no **WalletFeed ID** column.

1. On your iPhone, open the Files app.
2. Open the folder of the destination.
3. Touch and hold `WalletFeed Transactions.csv`.
4. Tap **Rename**.
5. Type a different name, for example `WalletFeed Transactions 1`.
6. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
7. Tap the destination.
8. Tap **Send History**.
9. Tap **All**.

WalletFeed makes a new `WalletFeed Transactions.csv` with all your transactions.

### If the folder has no CSV file

WalletFeed did not write the file to the folder.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Send Test**.

   The folder then gets `WalletFeed Test.csv` with a test transaction. If the Files app shows this file in the folder, WalletFeed can write to the folder.

4. To get all your transactions in the file, tap **Send History**.
5. Tap **All**.

### If new transactions are not in the file

WalletFeed did not update the file, or the app that shows the file did not read the file again after the change.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button).
3. In the **Sync** section, tap **Sync Now**.
4. Open the file again, for example `WalletFeed Transactions.csv`.

### If a name or description starts with an apostrophe

WalletFeed puts an apostrophe (`'`) before text that starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@`. Thus, a spreadsheet app does not use the text as a formula.

### If you cannot tap **Export**

WalletFeed disables **Export** while it reads the transactions, or when the period has no transactions.

1. Wait until **Transactions** shows a number.
2. If the number is 0, tap **Range**.
3. Select a different period, for example **All**.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-excel/ -->
# Open Apple Card transactions in Excel

WalletFeed writes your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions to a CSV file that Excel opens on a Mac or a PC. On your iPhone, you can make a file with [**Export CSV**](/docs/export-csv/), or get [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/) and let WalletFeed update a file in iCloud Drive.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- WalletFeed on your iPhone
- Excel on a Mac or a PC
- iCloud Drive on your iPhone and on your computer
- WalletFeed Pro, for a file that WalletFeed updates.

You can also use a different folder in the Files app, for example a folder in Dropbox.

WalletFeed is available only in the US. WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.

## Step 1: Make a CSV file on your iPhone

Do one of these procedures.

### Make a file one time

WalletFeed Pro is not necessary for **Export CSV**.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. At the top of the screen, tap **Settings** (the gear button).
3. In the **Data** section, tap **Export CSV**.

   ![The Settings screen shows Export CSV below Data.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-excel/walletfeed-settings-3.webp)

4. Tap **Range**.
5. Select **This Month**, **Last Month**, **Last 90 Days**, **This Year** or **All**.

   **Transactions** shows the number of transactions in the range.

   ![The Export CSV screen shows the range This Month and 29 transactions.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-excel/walletfeed-export-csv.webp)

6. Tap **Export**.

   Then, iOS shows a menu.

7. Tap **Save to Files**.
8. Save the file in a folder in iCloud Drive.

   The name of the file includes the range, for example `Apple Card This Month.csv`.

> **Note:** In the menu that iOS shows after you tap **Export**, you can also tap a different app to send the file to your computer. WalletFeed keeps no copy of the file. The file goes only to the folder or the app that you select.

### Update a file in iCloud Drive (WalletFeed Pro)

With WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed writes your transactions to a CSV file in a folder that you select. When your transactions change, WalletFeed updates the file.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen has no destinations and shows the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-excel/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the search field, type `Excel`.
5. Tap **CSV File**.

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows the WalletFeed Pro screen first. After you start the free trial or get WalletFeed Pro, the **Files** screen opens.

6. Make sure that **Format** is **CSV**.
7. Make sure that **Save As** is **One File**.

   With **One File**, all your transactions are in one file. WalletFeed puts the newest transaction first.

   ![The Files screen shows CSV in Format and One File in Save As.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-excel/walletfeed-setup-csv-file.webp)

   > **Note:** With **One File per Month**, each month has a different file, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.csv`.

8. Tap **Folder**.
9. Select a folder in iCloud Drive.

   After you select a folder, you can tap **Add**.

10. To give the file a different name, type the name in **Name**.

    If you do not change the name, the name of the file is `WalletFeed Transactions.csv`.

11. Tap **Add**.

    The message **Save Transactions to Files?** opens. The message shows the data that the folder will receive, the accounts and the start date.

12. Tap **Save**.

    Then, WalletFeed writes your transactions to the file.

> **Note:** WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. WalletFeed keeps no copy of the file. The file is in the folder that you selected.

## Step 2: Open the file in Excel

1. On your Mac or PC, find the file, for example in iCloud Drive.
2. Open the file in Excel.

   Excel shows one row for each transaction.

3. If WalletFeed updates the file, save your changes in a copy that has a different name.

> **Note:** When WalletFeed updates the file, WalletFeed removes the columns that it does not write. WalletFeed also removes the rows that have no WalletFeed ID. With **One File per Month**, WalletFeed writes the file for a month again. As a result, your changes to that file do not stay.

## Columns in the file

The first row has the names of the columns. Each row after it is one transaction. The file has these columns:

| Column | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Date | The date of the transaction, for example 2026-10-30. |
| Posted Date | The date that the transaction posted. For a pending transaction, this cell has no date. |
| Merchant | The name of the merchant. If Wallet has no merchant name, this cell has the text from Description. |
| Description | The description of the transaction from Wallet. |
| Original Description | The text of the transaction from the card network. |
| Amount | The value, for example `-23.40`. It is less than zero for a charge and more than zero for a payment or a refund. |
| Currency | The currency code, for example USD. |
| Direction | `debit` if Amount is less than zero, or `credit` if Amount is more than zero. |
| Status | The status from Wallet, for example `pending`, or `booked` for a posted transaction. A file from **Export CSV** can also have `rejected` for a declined transaction. |
| Type | The type from Wallet, for example `pointOfSale` or `refund`. |
| Category | The WalletFeed category, for example Groceries. |
| MCC | The merchant category code, for example 5411. |
| Account | The name of the Wallet account, for example Apple Card. |
| Foreign Amount | For a transaction in a different currency, the value in that currency. |
| Foreign Currency | The code of the currency in Foreign Amount, for example EUR. |
| WalletFeed ID | The ID of the transaction. WalletFeed uses it to find the row of a transaction that changes. |

If the first character in a text cell is `=`, `+`, `-` or `@`, WalletFeed puts an apostrophe (`'`) before the text. As a result, Excel reads the cell as text and does not use it as a formula.

## Changes to the file

WalletFeed does not update a file from **Export CSV**. While WalletFeed is open, the file of a CSV File destination receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then updates the file.

If WalletFeed cannot open the folder at that time, the file receives the changes when one of these conditions occurs:

- You open WalletFeed.
- A Shortcuts automation starts WalletFeed.
- iOS starts WalletFeed while your iPhone charges.

A pending transaction is in the file with the status `pending` or `authorized`. When the transaction posts, WalletFeed changes the same row. WalletFeed removes declined transactions from the file. A refund is a new row that has a value more than zero in Amount.

With **One File per Month**, WalletFeed writes the file for a month again each time that a transaction in that month changes.

## Send previous transactions

A new CSV File destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. You can select **Today**, **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

To send previous transactions to a destination after you add it:

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap the destination, for example **WalletFeed Transactions**.
4. Tap **Send History**.
5. Select **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

WalletFeed does not make two rows for one transaction. With **One File**, it finds the row that has the WalletFeed ID of the transaction and changes that row. For more information, refer to [Send History](/docs/send-history/).

## Change or remove the destination

To change the destination, tap it in [**Destinations**](/docs/destinations/). You can make these changes:

- To write only some transactions to the file, set **Filter** to on. Then, select accounts in **Accounts** or categories in **Categories**, or type a value in **Minimum**.
- To use a different folder, tap **Change Folder**. Then, select the folder. WalletFeed writes your transactions from the start date to a file in that folder.
- To stop the updates to the file but keep the destination, set **Enabled** to off.
- To change the name of the destination, type a different name in **Name**. The name of the file does not change.

With **One File**, WalletFeed does not remove the rows that it wrote before you changed the filter. With **One File per Month**, WalletFeed uses the filter each time that it writes the file for a month again. Then, WalletFeed removes the transactions that the filter does not include.

To remove the destination:

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. In the message, tap **Delete** again.

The file and the transactions that WalletFeed wrote to it stay in the folder.

## If there is a problem

### If you cannot tap **Export**

You cannot tap **Export** while WalletFeed reads the transactions, or if the range has no transactions.

1. Wait until **Transactions** shows a number.
2. If the number is 0, tap **Range**.
3. Select a larger range, for example **All**.
4. Tap **Export**.

### If the destination shows "Can't open the folder. Choose it again."

WalletFeed cannot open the folder that you selected.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Change Folder**.
3. Select the folder again.

WalletFeed writes your transactions to the file again. It does not make two rows for one transaction.

### If the destination shows "The file has no WalletFeed ID column. Rename it to start a new one."

WalletFeed cannot find the rows that it wrote, because the file has no WalletFeed ID column. For example, this problem occurs if you remove the column in Excel.

1. On your computer, change the name of the file.
2. On your iPhone, in **Destinations**, tap the destination.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Select **All**.

WalletFeed makes a new file and writes your transactions to it.

### If the file on your computer does not show new transactions

WalletFeed did not update the file after the last change in Wallet.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. At the top of the screen, tap **Settings** (the gear button).
3. In the **Sync** section, tap **Sync Now**.

   Then, **Sync Now** shows the time of the last update.

4. If the file is open in Excel on your computer, close the file.
5. On your computer, open the file in Excel again.

### If Destinations shows "Sync Requires Pro"

You do not have WalletFeed Pro at this time. WalletFeed keeps the destination, but it does not update the file.

1. In **Destinations**, tap **Upgrade**.
2. Start the free trial, or get WalletFeed Pro.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Firefly III

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to one account on your Firefly III server. You make a personal access token in Firefly III. Then you paste the token in WalletFeed and type the address of your server.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings in Wallet on that iPhone, and WalletFeed with [access to your Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/).
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), which is necessary for destinations. WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.
- Your Firefly III server, and a user account on it.
- An `https://` address for the server, with a certificate that iOS accepts. Your iPhone must connect to this address from all locations, and not only from your home Wi-Fi.

WalletFeed cannot use an `http://` address. The Firefly III image for Docker uses `http://` on port 8080. To get an `https://` address with a certificate that iOS accepts, you can use one of these:

- Tailscale HTTPS, with a `.ts.net` address
- A reverse proxy with a certificate from Let's Encrypt
- Cloudflare Tunnel.

You can also make a root certificate and install it on your iPhone. If you use a root certificate, you must set the switch for that certificate to on in **Settings** › **General** › **About** › **Certificate Trust Settings**.

WalletFeed sends the time of each transaction as the time on your iPhone. This time has no time zone. Firefly III reads the time in the time zone of the server. If the server time is before the time on your iPhone, a new transaction can have a time after the server time. As a result, Firefly III does not include the transaction in **Current balance** for some hours.

To prevent this problem, you can set `TZ` in the configuration of the server to your time zone. If `TZ` has no value, Firefly III uses UTC.

## Your token stays on your iPhone

- WalletFeed keeps the personal access token in the Keychain on your iPhone. iOS encrypts the Keychain.
- The personal access token does not go to iCloud Keychain or to your other devices.
- WalletFeed has no account and no servers. No person at WalletFeed can see or get the personal access token.
- Your iPhone sends the personal access token only to your Firefly III server, in each request to your Firefly III server.
- When you delete the destination, WalletFeed deletes the personal access token from your iPhone. You can also delete the token in Firefly III.

## Step 1: Make a personal access token in Firefly III

You can do these steps on a computer, or in Safari on your iPhone. With Universal Clipboard, you can copy the token on a Mac and paste it on your iPhone.

> **Caution:** Do not send the token to yourself in a message or an e-mail. The token gives access to all of your Firefly III data.

1. On your computer, get access to your Firefly III account in a web browser.
2. Click the person icon at the top right of the page (the icon has no text).

   ![The Firefly III home page with the highlighted person icon at the top right.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/firefly-iii-user-icon.webp)

3. Click **Remote access and tokens**.

   ![The Firefly III account menu, with the highlighted Remote access and tokens item.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/firefly-iii-user-menu.webp)

4. In the **Personal Access Tokens** section, click **Create new token**.

   ![The Remote access and tokens page, with the highlighted Create new token button in the Personal Access Tokens section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/firefly-iii-remote-access-page.webp)

   Do not click **Create New Client** in the **OAuth Clients and Applications** section. WalletFeed does not use OAuth clients.

5. In the **Name** field, type `WalletFeed`.
6. Click **Create**.

   ![The Create token dialog, with WalletFeed in the Name field and the highlighted Create button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/firefly-iii-create-token.webp)

7. Click in the large text box that shows the token.
8. To select all the text in the box, press Command-A on a Mac, or Ctrl-A on a Windows computer.
9. To copy the text, press Command-C on a Mac, or Ctrl-C on a Windows computer.

   ![The Personal Access Token dialog, with the blurred new token in a large text box.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/firefly-iii-token-created.webp)

   > **Note:** Firefly III shows the token only one time. The token is very long, and the dialog has no copy button.

10. Click **Close**.

## Step 2: Add Firefly III in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen in WalletFeed with no destinations, and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the **Budgeting** section, tap **Firefly III**.

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed first shows the **WalletFeed Pro** screen. After you get WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows the Firefly III screen.

5. Paste the token in the **Personal Access Token** field.

   ![The Firefly III screen in WalletFeed, with the Personal Access Token field, the server address field and three steps.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/walletfeed-setup-firefly-iii.webp)

   > **Note:** The page that **Firefly III Docs** opens gives the path **Options** › **Profile** › **OAuth**. Firefly III 6.7.9 does not have this path. Step 1 on this page gives the path for Firefly III 6.7.9.

6. In the field that shows `https://firefly.example.com`, type the address that you use to open Firefly III in a web browser.

   After you type the address, WalletFeed makes sure that the token and the address are correct. If they are correct, WalletFeed shows **Account**. If they are not correct, WalletFeed shows an error message (refer to [If there is a problem](#if-there-is-a-problem)). WalletFeed removes a `/`, `/api` or `/api/v1` at the end of the address.

7. If you made an account for your card in Firefly III, select that account in **Account**.

   **Account** shows the active asset accounts and liabilities in Firefly III. If one of these accounts has the name Apple Card, WalletFeed selects it, and **New Apple Card** is not in the list.

   If Firefly III has no account with the name Apple Card, WalletFeed selects **New Apple Card**. With **New Apple Card**, WalletFeed makes an asset account with the name Apple Card in Firefly III. This account has the role **Credit card** and the currency US dollars.

8. Tap **Add**.
9. When WalletFeed shows **Send Transactions to Firefly III?**, tap **Send**.

   The message tells you which data Firefly III receives, from which Wallet accounts and from which date. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the destination and does not send data. If WalletFeed made the Apple Card account, this account stays in Firefly III.

WalletFeed adds **Firefly III · Apple Card** to **Destinations** and starts to send your transactions. WalletFeed keeps the token in the Keychain on your iPhone.

## Step 3: Find your transactions in Firefly III

1. On your computer, in the Firefly III sidebar, click **Accounts**.
2. Click **Asset accounts**.

   ![The Firefly III sidebar, with Accounts open and the highlighted Asset accounts item.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/firefly-iii-accounts-menu.webp)

3. Click **Apple Card** (the account with the role **Credit card**).

   ![The Asset accounts list, with the highlighted Apple Card account and its Credit card role.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/firefly-iii-apple-card-account.webp)

4. Look at the **Transactions** section on the **Apple Card** page.

   ![The Transactions section of the Apple Card account in Firefly III, with six transactions from WalletFeed and their amounts, dates, merchants and categories.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/firefly-iii-walletfeed-result.webp)

## Data that Firefly III receives

WalletFeed puts all of your transactions in one Firefly III account. These transactions come from each Wallet account that WalletFeed has access to. This table shows the Firefly III field for each Wallet field.

| Wallet | Firefly III |
| --- | --- |
| A purchase | A withdrawal from your account to an expense account |
| A refund or a different credit | A deposit to your account from a revenue account |
| Merchant | The name of the expense account or revenue account. If Wallet has no merchant, WalletFeed uses the description. |
| Amount | **Amount**, with two decimals |
| Date | **Date**, with the time on your iPhone |
| Posted date | Book date |
| Description | **Description**. If Wallet has no description, WalletFeed uses the merchant. |
| Category, but not Other | **Category**. If the category is new, Firefly III adds it. |
| Amount in a foreign currency | Foreign amount and foreign currency |
| Card statement text, merchant category code and foreign amount | **Notes** |
| The WalletFeed ID of the transaction | **External ID** |
| No Wallet field | The `walletfeed` tag. A pending charge also has the `pending` tag. |

![A withdrawal in Firefly III, with its category, external ID, notes, and the walletfeed and pending tags.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/firefly-iii-result-transaction-detail.webp)

WalletFeed sets the category and the notes only when it adds a transaction. When WalletFeed updates a transaction, it changes only the amounts, the dates and the `pending` tag. Your changes to the description, the category, the notes and your tags stay.

Firefly III receives a payment to your card as a deposit from a revenue account. In Firefly III, you can change this deposit to a transfer. A rule can also make this change, because Firefly III uses your rules on each new transaction.

If Firefly III does not have the foreign currency, WalletFeed sends the transaction again without the foreign amount. The notes also show the foreign amount.

Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to your Firefly III server. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers.

## New and changed transactions

While WalletFeed is open, Firefly III receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then sends the change.

WalletFeed sends a pending charge to Firefly III with the `pending` tag. When Wallet shows the charge as posted, WalletFeed updates the same transaction and removes the `pending` tag. If Wallet shows a charge as declined or expired, WalletFeed deletes the transaction in Firefly III.

> **Caution:** If you add splits to a WalletFeed transaction in Firefly III, WalletFeed does not update that transaction. Thus, the amounts, the dates and the `pending` tag do not change when Wallet changes the charge. If Wallet shows the charge as declined or expired, WalletFeed deletes the transaction and its splits.

If Firefly III does not accept a change, WalletFeed tries to send that change again when it subsequently sends changes.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. To change it, do these steps before you add Firefly III:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Sync** section, tap **Initial History**.

   ![In the Sync section of the Settings screen, Initial History shows All.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/walletfeed-settings.webp)

3. Select **Today**, **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

To send more previous transactions to your Firefly III destination, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In **Destinations**, tap your Firefly III destination (for example, **Firefly III · Apple Card**).
2. Tap **Send History**.
3. Select **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

WalletFeed does not add a transaction two times. Before WalletFeed adds a transaction, it makes sure that the **External ID** of the transaction is not in Firefly III.

If you delete a transaction in Firefly III, **Send History** does not add it again. If Wallet subsequently changes the amount of that transaction, WalletFeed adds the transaction again.

While WalletFeed sends the transactions, the destination shows **Sending History** and a progress bar.

To stop Send History, tap **Send History** › **Stop Sending**.

## Change or remove the destination

In **Destinations**, tap your Firefly III destination. Then use this table:

| Change | On the destination screen |
| --- | --- |
| Stop the destination for a time | Set **Enabled** to off. |
| Send only some transactions | Set **Filter** to on. Then set **Include**, **Minimum**, **Include Pending**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**. |
| Send transactions from only one Wallet account (for example, Apple Card) | Set **Filter** to on. Then select the account in **Accounts**. |
| Use a new token | Tap **Replace Token**. Paste the new token. Then tap **Replace**. WalletFeed makes sure that Firefly III accepts the token. |
| Make sure that WalletFeed can send | Tap **Send Test**. Firefly III receives a test withdrawal of $4.20 with the merchant WalletFeed. You can delete this withdrawal in Firefly III. |
| Remove the destination | Tap **Delete**. Then tap **Delete** again. The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay in Firefly III. |

For more information about the filter, refer to [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

### Replace the token after one year

You can use a personal access token for one year. In Firefly III, **Expires at** shows the last date that you can use the token.

![The Personal Access Tokens list, with the WalletFeed token and its Expires at date.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/firefly-iii-token-list.webp)

1. Make a new token (refer to [step 1](#step-1-make-a-personal-access-token-in-firefly-iii)).
2. In WalletFeed, on the destination screen, tap **Replace Token**.
3. Paste the new token.
4. Tap **Replace**.

### Delete the token in Firefly III

When you remove the destination, the token stays in Firefly III. To delete the token, do these steps:

1. In Firefly III, click the person icon.
2. Click **Remote access and tokens**.
3. In the **WalletFeed** row of **Personal Access Tokens**, click **Delete**.

   ![The Personal Access Tokens list, with the highlighted Delete button for the WalletFeed token.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/firefly-iii-delete-token.webp)

When you click **Delete**, Firefly III deletes the token and does not show a message first. The row stays on the page until you load the page again.

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows "Use your server's HTTPS address."

The address does not use `https://`. For example, it starts with `http://`.

1. If your server has no `https://` address, get an `https://` address for it (refer to [Before you start](#before-you-start)).
2. Type the `https://` address of your server.

### If WalletFeed shows "iOS doesn't trust your server's certificate."

iOS does not accept the certificate of your server. WalletFeed shows this message for a self-signed certificate.

1. Give your server a certificate that iOS accepts (refer to [Before you start](#before-you-start)).

### If WalletFeed shows "Can't reach your server."

Your iPhone cannot connect to the address. WalletFeed cannot use `localhost` or an address on your home network (for example, `192.168.1.20`).

1. Use an `https://` address that your iPhone can connect to from all locations.

### If WalletFeed shows "No Firefly III API at this address."

The address is not the address of your Firefly III server.

1. Type the address that you use to open Firefly III in a web browser.

### If WalletFeed shows "Token rejected (HTTP 401)"

Firefly III does not accept the token. Possible causes are a deleted token, an expired token or a token that you did not copy fully. The message can also show 403.

1. Make a new token (refer to [step 1](#step-1-make-a-personal-access-token-in-firefly-iii)).
2. Make sure that you copied all of the token.
3. Paste the new token in the **Personal Access Token** field.

### If you closed the token dialog before you copied the token

Firefly III shows a token only one time.

1. In **Personal Access Tokens**, click **Delete** in the row of the token that you did not copy.
2. Make a new token (refer to [step 1](#step-1-make-a-personal-access-token-in-firefly-iii)).

### If the destination shows "Authentication failed"

Firefly III does not accept the token. Possible causes are an expired token or a token that you deleted in Firefly III.

1. Make a new token (refer to [step 1](#step-1-make-a-personal-access-token-in-firefly-iii)).
2. In WalletFeed, on the destination screen, tap **Replace Token**.
3. Paste the new token.
4. Tap **Replace**.

### If the destination shows "Can't connect"

Your iPhone cannot connect to the server. This can occur when your iPhone is not on your home Wi-Fi. WalletFeed tries to connect again when it subsequently sends changes.

1. Make sure that your iPhone can open the `https://` address of the server from all locations.

### If a new transaction is not in Current balance

The server time is before the time on your iPhone. As a result, the transaction has a time after the server time.

1. Set `TZ` in the configuration of the server to your time zone.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-gnucash/ -->
# Import Apple Card transactions into GnuCash

You can import your Apple Card transactions into GnuCash with OFX files from WalletFeed. On your iPhone, WalletFeed writes one file for each month to a folder that you select. Then, you import each file in GnuCash on your computer.

## Before you start

You must have:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- WalletFeed, with [access to your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account](/docs/wallet-accounts/)
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase
- GnuCash on your computer
- iCloud Drive on your iPhone and on your computer, or a different location in the Files app that your computer can open, for example Dropbox.

WalletFeed is available only in the US.

## Step 1: Add an OFX file in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-gnucash/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the **Destinations** search field, type `GnuCash`.

   ![The Add Destination screen with the Destinations search field above the Budgeting list.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-gnucash/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

   The list shows **OFX File** and **QIF File**. An OFX file has a transaction ID for each transaction. Thus, GnuCash does not import a transaction two times. A QIF file has no transaction ID.

5. Tap **OFX File**.

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows the **WalletFeed Pro** screen. After you get WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows the **Files** screen.

6. Make sure that **Format** is **OFX**.

   ![The Files screen with OFX in Format, Choose… in Folder and WalletFeed in Name.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-gnucash/walletfeed-setup-ofx-file.webp)

7. Tap **Folder**.
8. Select a folder in iCloud Drive or in a different location.

   The **Folder** row shows the name of the folder. You can tap **Add** only after you select a folder.

9. To use a different name for the files, type the new name in **Name**.

   Each file name is that name with the month, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`.

10. Tap **Add**.
11. When WalletFeed shows **Save Transactions to Files?**, tap **Save**.

    The message gives the folder, the data that the folder receives, the accounts and the start date. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the new destination.

WalletFeed then writes one file for each month that has posted transactions, for example `WalletFeed 2026-09.ofx` and `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`.

> **Note:** WalletFeed writes the files only to the folder that you selected. WalletFeed does not keep a copy of the files.

## Step 2: Import the file in GnuCash

1. On your computer, open GnuCash.
2. Click **File** › **Import** › **Import OFX/QFX…**.
3. Open the folder that you selected in WalletFeed.
4. Select the file for a month, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`.

   To import the files of more than one month, you can select more than one file.

5. Click **Import**.
6. If GnuCash shows the **Generic import transaction matcher** window, go to step 10.

   When GnuCash imports a statement for a Wallet account for the first time, GnuCash shows the **Select Account** window. GnuCash does not show this window again for that Wallet account.

7. In the **Select Account** window, select the GnuCash account for the Wallet account (Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings).

   You can also add a GnuCash account with **New Account…**.

8. Click **OK**.

   Then, GnuCash stores the account that you selected for this Wallet account.

9. If GnuCash shows the **Select Account** window again, do steps 7 and 8 again.

   If the file has statements for more than one Wallet account, GnuCash shows the window for each of these accounts. Then, GnuCash shows the transactions from the file in the **Generic import transaction matcher** window.

10. To set the transfer account of a new transaction, double-click its row.

    The transfer account is the second account of the transaction, for example `Expenses:Groceries`.

11. Select the transfer account.
12. Click **OK**.
13. Do steps 10 thru 12 again for each new transaction that has no transfer account.
14. In the **Generic import transaction matcher** window, click **OK**.

    Then, GnuCash adds the transactions to the GnuCash accounts that you selected.

> **Note:** If a new transaction has no transfer account when you click **OK**, GnuCash puts the transaction in an Imbalance account.

When you import more files, GnuCash can set the transfer account of a new transaction from the accounts that you selected previously. For more information, refer to [Importing Transactions from Files](https://www.gnucash.org/docs/v5/C/gnucash-manual/trans-import.html) in the GnuCash manual.

## Data that GnuCash receives

Each OFX file has one statement for each Wallet account:

- A credit card statement for Apple Card
- A checking account statement for Apple Cash
- A savings account statement for Savings.

Each transaction in the file has this data:

| Data | In the OFX file |
| --- | --- |
| Date | The date of the transaction in Wallet. |
| Posted date | The date that the transaction posted. GnuCash uses this date as the date of the transaction. |
| Merchant | The merchant name, or the description if Wallet has no merchant name. WalletFeed writes only the first 32 characters. |
| Amount | The amount of the transaction. Purchases have a minus sign. Payments and refunds have no minus sign. |
| Currency | The currency of the statement, for example USD. |
| Memo | The description and the card network text, if they are different from the merchant name. The amount in a different currency, if there is one. |
| Type | The type of transaction, for example a purchase, a payment or a transfer. |
| Transaction ID | The ID of the transaction in Wallet. GnuCash uses this ID to find the transactions that it imported previously. |

The file does not include the WalletFeed category or the balance of the account. You set the transfer account of each transaction in GnuCash.

WalletFeed changes curly quotes, dashes and ellipses to ASCII characters. If the file cannot contain a character, WalletFeed writes a character that is almost the same, or `?`.

## New and changed transactions

While WalletFeed is open, the folder receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then updates the files.

If WalletFeed cannot open the folder at that time, WalletFeed writes the files when one of these occurs:

- You open WalletFeed.
- A Shortcuts automation starts WalletFeed.
- iOS starts WalletFeed while your iPhone gets power from a charger.

When a month has a change, WalletFeed writes the file of that month again. The file has all the transactions of the month. You can import the file of a month more than one time, for example the file of this month. GnuCash uses the transaction ID to find the transactions that it imported previously. GnuCash does not import these transactions again. If GnuCash previously imported all the transactions in a file, GnuCash shows a message that the file has no new transactions.

An OFX file includes a transaction only after the transaction posts. When a pending charge posts, WalletFeed adds the charge to the file with the same transaction ID. A charge that does not post, for example a declined charge, is not in the file.

A refund is a different transaction from the purchase. The amount of a refund has no minus sign.

If Wallet removes a transaction from this month or last month, WalletFeed removes the transaction from the file of that month. If GnuCash previously imported the transaction, the transaction stays in GnuCash until you delete it.

## Send previous transactions

A new OFX File destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

With [Send History](/docs/send-history/), WalletFeed writes the files again from a start date that you select:

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **WalletFeed**, or the name that you typed in **Name**.
4. Tap **Send History**.
5. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.
6. On your computer, import the files in GnuCash (refer to [Step 2](#step-2-import-the-file-in-gnucash)).

GnuCash does not import a transaction two times.

## Change or remove the destination

### Open the destination

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **WalletFeed**, or the name that you typed in **Name**.

If you change **Name** on this screen, the names of the files stay the same.

### Send only some transactions

1. Open the destination.
2. Set **Filter** to on.
3. Set **Include**, **Minimum**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**.

For more information, refer to [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

### Use a different folder

1. Open the destination.
2. Tap **Change Folder**.
3. Select the new folder.

After you change the folder, WalletFeed writes all the files again in the new folder. WalletFeed uses the same start date.

### Stop the destination, but keep it

1. Open the destination.
2. Set **Enabled** to off.

### Remove the destination

1. Open the destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. Tap **Delete** again.

The files stay in the folder. The transactions that you imported stay in GnuCash.

## If there is a problem

### If you cannot tap Add

You did not select a folder on the **Files** screen.

1. Tap **Folder**.
2. Select a folder in iCloud Drive or in a different location.

### If WalletFeed shows “Couldn't open this folder.”

WalletFeed cannot get access to the folder that you selected.
