1. Tap **Folder**, or **Change Folder** on the screen of the destination.
2. Select a different folder in iCloud Drive.

### If the destination shows “Can't open the folder. Choose it again.”

WalletFeed does not have access to the folder of the destination.

1. Open the destination.
2. Tap **Change Folder**.
3. Select the folder again.

WalletFeed writes the files again. GnuCash does not import a transaction two times.

### If the folder has no file for a month

WalletFeed writes a file for a month only when the month has posted transactions.

1. Open the destination.
2. Tap **Send Test**.

   Then, WalletFeed writes the file `WalletFeed Test.ofx` to the folder. The file has one test transaction. This file shows that WalletFeed can write to the folder.

3. Do not import `WalletFeed Test.ofx` in GnuCash.
4. Tap **Send History**.
5. Tap **All**.

### If GnuCash does not show new transactions

WalletFeed did not write the file after the last change in Wallet, or the new charges are pending.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. Tap **Sync Now**.

   ![The Settings screen with Background Sync, Initial History and Sync Now in the Sync section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-gnucash/walletfeed-settings.webp)

4. On your computer, import the file of the month again in GnuCash (refer to [Step 2](#step-2-import-the-file-in-gnucash)).

If the new charges are pending, WalletFeed adds them to the file after they post.

### If Destinations shows “Sync Requires Pro”

You do not have WalletFeed Pro at this time. WalletFeed keeps the destination, but WalletFeed does not write the files.

1. In **Destinations**, tap **Upgrade**.
2. Select a plan.
3. Tap **Start Free Trial**, **Subscribe** or **Buy Lifetime**.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-google-sheets/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Google Sheets

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to Google Sheets. After you connect your Google Account, WalletFeed makes a spreadsheet in your Google Drive and updates it when your transactions change.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version (WalletFeed is available only in the US)
- WalletFeed on your iPhone, with access to your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/) (a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase)
- A Google Account.

## Your sign-in stays on your iPhone

- WalletFeed keeps your Google sign-in in the Keychain on your iPhone. iOS encrypts the Keychain.
- Your Google sign-in does not go to iCloud Keychain or to your other devices.
- WalletFeed has no account and no servers. No person at WalletFeed can see or get your Google sign-in.
- Your iPhone sends your Google sign-in only to Google, in each request to Google.
- When you delete the destination, WalletFeed deletes your Google sign-in from your iPhone. You can also remove WalletFeed from your Google Account.

## Step 1: Add Google Sheets in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations** at the bottom of the screen.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with No Destinations and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-google-sheets/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In **Sheets & Databases**, tap **Google Sheets**.

   ![The Add Destination list with Google Sheets below Sheets & Databases.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-google-sheets/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

5. If WalletFeed shows **WalletFeed Pro**, get [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).

   Result: WalletFeed shows the **Google Sheets** screen.

## Step 2: Connect your Google Account

1. Tap **Sign In with Google**.

   ![The Google Sheets screen with the Sign In with Google button and the Spreadsheet field.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-google-sheets/walletfeed-setup-google-sheets.webp)

2. On the Google page, get access to your Google Account.
3. Give WalletFeed access to the files that it makes.

   Result: WalletFeed shows **Signed In**.

> **Note:** WalletFeed keeps the sign-in in the Keychain on your iPhone. With this sign-in, WalletFeed can open only the spreadsheets that it makes. The Google page shows this access as "See, edit, create, and delete only the specific Google Drive files you use with this app."

## Step 3: Make the spreadsheet

1. To give the spreadsheet a different name, type the name in the **Spreadsheet** field.

   The name is **WalletFeed Transactions** until you change it.

2. Tap **Add** at the top of the screen.

   Result: WalletFeed makes the spreadsheet in your Google Drive. Then WalletFeed shows the message **Send Transactions to Google Sheets?**

   The message shows the data that Google Sheets will receive, the Wallet accounts and the start date.

3. Tap **Send**.

   Result: WalletFeed starts to send your transactions to the spreadsheet.

If you tap **Cancel** in the message, WalletFeed sends no transactions and removes the destination. The spreadsheet stays in your Google Drive. It has only the header row.

## Step 4: Open the spreadsheet

1. In **Destinations**, tap the name of your spreadsheet, for example **WalletFeed Transactions**.
2. Tap **Open in Google Sheets**.

The spreadsheet has one tab, **Transactions**. Row 1 has the headers. Each row below row 1 has one transaction.

On a computer, you can also find the spreadsheet in your Google Drive.

## Columns in the spreadsheet

WalletFeed writes each row from column A to column N.

| Column | Header | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| A | **WalletFeed ID** | The ID of the transaction in WalletFeed |
| B | **Date** | The date of the transaction, in your time zone |
| C | **Merchant** | The merchant name. If Wallet has no merchant name, this column shows the data from **Description**. |
| D | **Amount** | Money out of the account is a negative number. Money into the account, for example a refund or a payment, is a positive number. |
| E | **Currency** | The currency code, for example USD |
| F | **Category** | The WalletFeed category, for example **Groceries** or **Dining** |
| G | **Status** | The status from Wallet, for example `booked` or `pending` |
| H | **Pending** | A checkbox that has a checkmark when the transaction is pending |
| I | **Account** | The name of the Wallet account, for example Apple Card |
| J | **Description** | The description of the transaction from Wallet |
| K | **Type** | The type of the transaction from Wallet, for example `pointOfSale` |
| L | **MCC** | The merchant category code, as a number |
| M | **Foreign Amount** | For a transaction in a different currency, the amount in that currency. Other transactions have no data in this column. |
| N | **Foreign Currency** | For a transaction in a different currency, the code of that currency. Other transactions have no data in this column. |

WalletFeed writes numbers in **Amount** and **Foreign Amount**. It writes dates in **Date**. You can use these numbers and dates in formulas.

You must not change column A, because WalletFeed uses the **WalletFeed ID** to find each row again. If you add columns, you must put them after column N.

You can change the name of the spreadsheet and the name of the **Transactions** tab. WalletFeed does not change the colors or fonts that you set.

Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to Google Sheets. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. After Google Sheets receives your transactions, the terms of Google are applicable to them.

## New and changed transactions

While WalletFeed is open, the spreadsheet receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then sends the change. **Background Sync** is on until you set it to off.

WalletFeed adds each new transaction as a new row at the end of the tab. If a transaction is pending, its row has a checkmark in **Pending**. When the status changes from `pending` to `booked`, WalletFeed updates the row of the transaction.

WalletFeed removes the rows of declined transactions and of transactions that Wallet removes. A refund is a new row with a positive number in **Amount**.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

To send transactions from before that start date, or to send them again, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In **Destinations**, tap your spreadsheet.
2. Tap **Send History**.
3. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

   Result: WalletFeed shows **Sending History** until it sends all the transactions.

If WalletFeed sends a transaction that is in the spreadsheet, it updates the row of the transaction and does not add a second row.

To stop before WalletFeed sends all the transactions, tap **Send History** › **Stop Sending**.

## Change or remove the destination

### Send only some transactions

1. In **Destinations**, tap your spreadsheet.
2. Set **Filter** to on (refer to [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/)).
3. Set the rule, for example in **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Minimum**.

If Apple Intelligence is active on your iPhone, you can also type a rule:

1. In the field below **Filter**, type the rule, for example "Travel over $50, not Uber".
2. Tap the Apple Intelligence icon at the end of the field.

### Stop and start the destination

1. In **Destinations**, tap your spreadsheet.
2. Set **Enabled** to off.

To start the destination again, set **Enabled** to on.

### Remove the destination

1. In **Destinations**, tap your spreadsheet.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. In the message, tap **Delete**.

   Result: WalletFeed sends no more transactions to the spreadsheet. WalletFeed also removes the Google sign-in for the spreadsheet from your iPhone.

When you remove the destination, the spreadsheet and the transactions in it stay in your Google Drive.

### Remove WalletFeed's access to your Google Account

To also remove the access that you gave WalletFeed in your Google Account, do these steps:

1. On a computer, open the [linked apps page](https://myaccount.google.com/linkedapps) of your Google Account.
2. Click **Access to your Google Account**.
3. Click **WalletFeed**.
4. Click **See details**.
5. Click **Remove access**.
6. Click **Confirm**.

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows "Signed out" or "Authentication failed"

Google does not let WalletFeed use your sign-in. This occurs, for example, if you removed WalletFeed's access in your Google Account, or if WalletFeed did not use the sign-in for 6 months.

1. In **Destinations**, tap your spreadsheet.
2. Tap **Sign In Again**.
3. On the Google page, get access to the Google Account that has the spreadsheet.
4. Give WalletFeed access to the files that it makes.

If you use a different Google Account, WalletFeed shows "This Google account can't open the spreadsheet. Use the one you set it up with."

### If WalletFeed shows "Google rejected the sign-in"

When WalletFeed tried to make the spreadsheet, Google did not let WalletFeed use the sign-in.

1. On the **Google Sheets** screen, tap **Use Another Account**.
2. On the Google page, get access to your Google Account.
3. Give WalletFeed access to the files that it makes.
4. Tap **Add** at the top of the screen.

### If the spreadsheet does not receive new transactions

When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If **Background Sync** is on, WalletFeed then sends the change.

1. Open WalletFeed.

   Result: WalletFeed sends the changes in seconds.

2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. Make sure that **Background Sync** is on.
4. Tap **Sync Now**.

### If Destinations shows "Sync Requires Pro"

Your WalletFeed Pro subscription stopped. WalletFeed Pro is necessary for all destinations.

1. Tap **Upgrade**.

   Result: WalletFeed shows the **WalletFeed Pro** screen.

2. If your Apple Account has a WalletFeed Pro purchase, tap **Restore Purchases**.
3. If your Apple Account has no WalletFeed Pro purchase, select a plan.
4. Complete the purchase.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Linear

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to Linear. In Linear, WalletFeed makes one issue for each transaction. You make a personal API key in Linear, and then you paste the key in WalletFeed.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed, with access to your [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/).
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase. You must have WalletFeed Pro to send transactions to Linear.
- A Linear account, from [Linear's sign-up page](https://linear.app/signup). You can use the Free plan of Linear.

> **Note:** On Linear's Free plan, a workspace can have a maximum of 250 issues. This limit does not include archived issues. Linear puts 4 issues in a new workspace. WalletFeed makes one issue for each transaction. With a filter, WalletFeed sends only some transactions (refer to [Step 3](#step-3-set-a-filter)).

## Your key stays on your iPhone

- WalletFeed keeps the API key in the Keychain on your iPhone. iOS encrypts the Keychain.
- The API key does not go to iCloud Keychain or to your other devices.
- WalletFeed has no account and no servers. No person at WalletFeed can see or get the API key.
- Your iPhone sends the API key only to Linear, in each request to Linear.
- When you delete the destination, WalletFeed deletes the API key from your iPhone. You can also revoke the key in Linear.

## Step 1: Make a personal API key in Linear

With a personal API key, WalletFeed can make issues in your Linear workspace.

1. On your iPhone, open [Linear's Security & access settings](https://linear.app/settings/account/security).

   > **Note:** On the Linear screen in WalletFeed, **Security & Access** opens the same page.

2. If Linear shows **Log in to Linear**, tap **Continue with email**.

   ![The Log in to Linear page, with the Continue with email button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/linear-login.webp)

   > **Note:** Linear does not use passwords. If your Linear account uses Google, **Continue with Google** also gives you access.

3. Type your e-mail address.

   ![The page in Linear for your e-mail address, with the Continue with email button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/linear-login-email.webp)

4. Tap **Continue with email**.
5. If Linear shows **Verifying it’s you**, tap the **Verify you are human** checkbox.

   ![The Linear page with the heading Verifying it’s you and the Verify you are human checkbox.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/linear-verify-human.webp)

6. On the **Check your email** page, tap **Enter code manually**.

   ![The Check your email page in Linear, with the Enter code manually button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/linear-check-email.webp)

7. Open the e-mail from Linear with the subject “Login for Linear”.

   The e-mail has a code of 10 letters and numbers.

   > **Note:** The hyperlink in the e-mail also gives you access to Linear.

8. In Linear, type the code in the field.

   ![The field for the login code in Linear, with the Continue with login code button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/linear-enter-code.webp)

9. Tap **Continue with login code**.

   Result: Linear shows **Security & access**.

10. If Linear does not show **Security & access**, open [Linear's Security & access settings](https://linear.app/settings/account/security) again.

    > **Note:** In Linear, **Security & access** is in the **Personal** group of **Settings**. The steps in WalletFeed show **Account** as the name of this group.

11. Scroll to **Personal API keys**, below **Sessions** and **Passkeys**.

    ![The Personal API keys section on an iPhone, with the New API key button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/linear-iphone-personal-api-keys.webp)

12. Tap **New API key**.

    Result: Linear shows **Create API key**.

13. In **Key name**, type `WalletFeed`.

    The name helps you find the WalletFeed key in the list of keys.

    ![The Create API key page on an iPhone, with the Key name field highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/linear-iphone-create-key.webp)

14. In **Permissions**, tap **Only select permissions…**.

    Linear selects **Full access** when the page opens. WalletFeed can also use a key with **Full access**, but WalletFeed uses only **Read** and **Write**.

15. Select **Read** and **Write**. Do not select **Admin**.

    Result: Linear also selects **Create and update issues** and **Create comments**.

    ![The Permissions section in Linear, with Only select permissions, Read and Write selected.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/linear-permissions.webp)

16. Optional: In **Team access**, tap **Only select teams…**.

    Linear selects **All teams you have access to** when the page opens. With **Only select teams…**, the key gets access to only the teams that you select.

17. If you tapped **Only select teams…**, tap **Select teams…**.
18. If Linear shows the list of teams, tap the team that will receive the issues.

    ![The list of teams below Only select teams, with the WalletFeed Docs team highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/linear-team-picker.webp)

19. Tap **Create**.

    Result: Linear shows the new key below **API key**, with the text “This API key is shown only once. Please copy it now.”

20. Tap the copy button to the right of the key.

    The copy button is an icon with no text. The key starts with `lin_api_`.

    ![The new API key in Linear, with the copy button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/linear-key-created.webp)

21. Keep the Linear page open until you paste the key in WalletFeed.

    Linear shows the key only one time. While the page is open, you can copy the key again.

## Step 2: Add Linear in WalletFeed

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Optional: If you have WalletFeed Pro and your workspace is on Linear's Free plan, set **Initial History** to **Today**. Then the new destination receives no transactions from before today.
   1. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
   2. In the **Sync** section, set **Initial History** to **Today**.

      ![WalletFeed Settings with the Sync section and Initial History set to All.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/walletfeed-settings.webp)

   3. Tap **Done**.
3. Tap **Destinations**.
4. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen in WalletFeed with the + button and no destinations.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

5. In **Sheets & Databases**, tap **Linear**. You can also type `Linear` in the search field.
6. If WalletFeed shows the **WalletFeed Pro** screen, get WalletFeed Pro on that screen. Then the **Linear** screen opens.
7. Paste the key in the **API Key** field. WalletFeed keeps the key in the Keychain on your iPhone.

   ![The Linear screen in WalletFeed with the API Key field, three steps and the Security & Access hyperlink.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/walletfeed-setup-linear.webp)

8. After WalletFeed reads the key, select a team in **Team**. This team receives the issues.
9. Optional: In **Project**, select a project. If you do not select a project, **Project** stays at **None**. A project must be in Linear before WalletFeed can show it.

   Below **Project**, WalletFeed shows “Each transaction becomes an issue to review.”

10. Tap **Add**.
11. Read the message **Send Transactions to Linear?** The message gives the fields that Linear receives, the accounts and the start date.
12. Tap **Send**. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed does not add the destination.

Then **Destinations** shows the new destination with the name of the team, for example “Linear · Finance”.

## Step 3: Set a filter

With a [filter](/docs/choose-what-to-send/), WalletFeed sends only some transactions to Linear. If your workspace is on Linear's Free plan, set a filter.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Linear destination.
2. Set **Filter** to on.

   ![The destination screen for Lunch Money in WalletFeed, with the Filter switch set to off.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/walletfeed-destination-detail.webp)

3. Optional: Set **Include** to **Purchases**. Then Linear receives no refunds or payments.
4. Optional: In **Minimum**, type an amount, for example `25`. Then Linear receives only transactions of $25 or more.
5. Optional: In **Accounts** or **Categories**, select only the accounts or the categories to send to Linear.
6. Optional: To send previous transactions with this filter, tap **Send History** (refer to [Send previous transactions](#send-previous-transactions)).

## Data that Linear receives

Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to Linear. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. After Linear receives your transactions, the terms of Linear are applicable to them.

WalletFeed puts each issue in the team that you selected. If you selected a project, WalletFeed also puts the issue in that project. If Triage is on for the team, a new issue goes to Triage. If Triage is off, the issue goes to the first Backlog status of the team.

To find the issues on a computer, do these steps:

1. On a computer, open [Linear](https://linear.app) in a web browser.
2. In the left column, find your team in **Your teams**.
3. If Linear does not show **Issues** below the name of your team, click the name of your team.
4. Below the name of your team, click **Issues**.
5. At the top of the list, click **All issues**.

   Result: If Triage is off, Linear shows the issues from WalletFeed in **Backlog**.

   ![The Issues page of the WalletFeed Docs team in Linear, with six transactions from WalletFeed in Backlog.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/linear-walletfeed-result.webp)

The title of each issue has the amount and the merchant, for example `$6.75 · Blue Bottle Coffee`. The description of the issue is a table with these rows:

| Row in the description | Value from Wallet |
| --- | --- |
| **Date** | The date of the transaction, for example 2026-10-29 |
| **Merchant** | The merchant name, or the description if Wallet has no merchant name |
| **Amount** | Less than zero for a charge, for example -84.12, and more than zero for a refund or a payment |
| **Currency** | The currency code, for example USD |
| **Category** | The WalletFeed category, for example Groceries |
| **Status** | The Wallet status, for example `pending`, or `booked` after the charge posts |
| **Pending** | Yes or No |
| **Account** | The Wallet account, for example Apple Card |
| **Description** | The description from Wallet |
| **Type** | The type of transaction, for example `pointOfSale` or `refund` |
| **MCC** | The merchant category code, for example 5411 |
| **Foreign Amount** and **Foreign Currency** | The amount and the currency of a charge in a different currency |
| **WalletFeed ID** | The transaction ID, in the last row |

WalletFeed does not write a row that has no value. In the description, an amount has no zeros at the end, for example -23.4 for $23.40.

Each issue also has an item with the name WalletFeed in its **Resources** section. WalletFeed uses this item and the **WalletFeed ID** row to find the issue again in the team that you selected.

![An issue from WalletFeed in Linear, with the table in the description and the WalletFeed item in Resources.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/linear-walletfeed-issue.webp)

> **Caution:** Do not remove the **WalletFeed ID** row or the WalletFeed item in **Resources**. If you remove the two, WalletFeed makes a second issue when it sends the transaction again.

## New and changed transactions

While WalletFeed is open, Linear receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then sends the change.

**Background Sync** is in **Settings** › **Sync**. It stays on until you set it to off. After your iPhone starts again, WalletFeed sends nothing to Linear until you type your iPhone passcode one time.

A pending charge becomes an issue with `· Pending` at the end of the title. When the charge posts, WalletFeed changes the title and the description of the same issue.

A refund and its charge become two different issues. The title of a refund or a payment has + before the amount, for example `+$49.00 · Apple Store`.

If a pending charge becomes a declined charge, or if Wallet removes a transaction, WalletFeed archives the issue. The archived issue stays in Linear.

### Changes that you make in Linear

When a transaction changes, WalletFeed writes the title and the description of its issue again. If you changed them in Linear, WalletFeed replaces your changes. WalletFeed does not change the status or the assignee of the issue.

## Send previous transactions

A new Linear destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. But a new Linear destination receives a maximum of 30 days of previous transactions.

To send transactions from a longer period, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Linear destination.
2. If your workspace is on Linear's Free plan, set a filter (refer to [Step 3](#step-3-set-a-filter)). Each previous transaction becomes one issue.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Select a period: **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.
5. Read the message **Send History to Linear?** The message shows “Each transaction can become an issue.”
6. Tap **Send**.

WalletFeed sends the newest transactions first. The destination screen shows the number of transactions that WalletFeed sent. **Send History** also uses the filter.

To stop **Send History**:

1. On the destination screen, tap **Send History**.
2. Tap **Stop Sending**. The issues that WalletFeed sent stay in Linear.

## Change or remove the destination

### Send only some transactions

To change the transactions that go to Linear, change the filter on the destination screen (refer to [Step 3](#step-3-set-a-filter)).

### Use a different team or project

The destination screen shows the **Team**, and the **Project** if you selected a project. You cannot change them. To use a different team or a different project:

1. Add Linear again with the new team or the new project (refer to [Step 2](#step-2-add-linear-in-walletfeed)).
2. Delete the previous Linear destination (refer to [Remove Linear from WalletFeed](#remove-linear-from-walletfeed)).

### Stop the destination for a time

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Linear destination.
2. Set **Enabled** to off.

To start the destination again, set **Enabled** to on.

### Replace the key

You can replace the key, for example after you revoke the key in Linear.

1. In Linear, make a new personal API key (refer to [Step 1](#step-1-make-a-personal-api-key-in-linear)).
2. In WalletFeed, tap the Linear destination in **Destinations**.
3. Tap **Replace Key**.
4. Paste the new key in the **API Key** field.
5. Tap **Replace**. Before WalletFeed keeps the new key, it makes sure that the key can get access to the team.

### Remove Linear from WalletFeed

1. In WalletFeed, tap the Linear destination in **Destinations**.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. In the message, tap **Delete**. The issues that WalletFeed sent stay in Linear.
4. Optional: Revoke the key in Linear (refer to [Revoke the key in Linear](#revoke-the-key-in-linear)).

### Revoke the key in Linear

After you revoke the key, WalletFeed cannot connect to Linear with it.

1. On your iPhone, open [Linear's Security & access settings](https://linear.app/settings/account/security).
2. Scroll to **Personal API keys**.
3. In the row of the WalletFeed key, tap **…**.

   If two keys have the name WalletFeed, the text “Created” in each row gives the date of the key.

4. Tap **Revoke API key**.

   ![The menu of the WalletFeed key, with Revoke API key highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/linear-revoke-menu.webp)

5. In the message **Revoke "WalletFeed"?**, tap **Revoke**.

   Result: Linear shows **"WalletFeed" key revoked**.

   ![The Security & access page in Linear, with the message that Linear revoked the WalletFeed key.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/linear-key-revoked.webp)

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows “Key rejected”

Linear did not accept the key because the key is not correct, or because a person revoked the key in Linear.

1. In Linear, make a new personal API key (refer to [Step 1](#step-1-make-a-personal-api-key-in-linear)).
2. If WalletFeed shows the message on the Linear screen, paste the new key in the **API Key** field.
3. If WalletFeed shows the message on the destination screen, replace the key (refer to [Replace the key](#replace-the-key)).

### If the destination shows “Authentication failed”

Linear did not accept the key, or the key cannot make or change issues in the team.

1. In Linear, make a new personal API key with **Full access**, or with **Read** and **Write**.
2. In WalletFeed, tap the Linear destination in **Destinations**.
3. Tap **Replace Key**.
4. Paste the new key in the **API Key** field.
5. Tap **Replace**.

### If WalletFeed shows “Give the key Read and Write access to the team”

Linear does not let the key get access to the team.

1. In Linear, make a new personal API key with **Full access**, or with **Read** and **Write**.
2. If you tap **Only select teams…**, select the team that you use with WalletFeed.
3. If WalletFeed shows the message on the Linear screen, paste the new key in the **API Key** field.
4. If WalletFeed shows the message on the destination screen, replace the key (refer to [Replace the key](#replace-the-key)).

### If WalletFeed shows “This key can't see any teams”

The key has access to no team in Linear.

1. In Linear, make a new personal API key with access to your team.
2. On the Linear screen in WalletFeed, paste the new key in the **API Key** field.

### If WalletFeed shows “Linear is limiting requests”

Linear has a limit for each user in each hour, and your account is at that limit.

1. Wait for 1 minute.
2. If WalletFeed shows the message on the Linear screen, tap **Try Again**.
3. If WalletFeed shows the message on the destination screen, replace the key again (refer to [Replace the key](#replace-the-key)).

### If new transactions do not become issues

On Linear's Free plan, a workspace can have a maximum of 250 issues. This limit does not include archived issues.

1. To decrease the number of issues in the limit, archive the issues that you do not use. For example, archive the 4 issues that Linear puts in a new workspace.
2. To send all your transactions to Linear, change your workspace to a different Linear plan, for example Basic. Basic has no limit on issues.
3. To send only some transactions, set a filter (refer to [Step 3](#step-3-set-a-filter)).

### If one transaction has two issues

If a person removes the **WalletFeed ID** row and the WalletFeed item in **Resources**, WalletFeed makes a new issue. If a person moves the issue to a different team, WalletFeed also makes a new issue.

1. In Linear, archive or delete the issue that has no **WalletFeed ID** row, or the issue in the different team. WalletFeed continues to change the other issue.
2. Keep the **WalletFeed ID** row and the WalletFeed item in **Resources** in each issue.

### If Linear receives changes only when WalletFeed is open

**Background Sync** is off, or your iPhone started again and you did not type its passcode.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Sync** section, set **Background Sync** to on.
3. Tap **Done**.
4. After your iPhone starts again, type its passcode one time.

### If Linear does not let you make an API key

An admin of your Linear workspace does not let members make API keys. Admins can always make API keys. On the Free plan, all users are admins.

1. Tell an admin of the workspace to set **API key creation** to **All members**. **API key creation** is in **Settings** › **Administration** › **API**.

   ![The API page in Linear, with All members highlighted in API key creation.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/linear-admin-api-key-creation.webp)

2. After the admin changes **API key creation**, make the key (refer to [Step 1](#step-1-make-a-personal-api-key-in-linear)).

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Lunch Money

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to Lunch Money. You make an access token in Lunch Money, then you paste the token in WalletFeed.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed on your iPhone, with access to your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account.
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/) (a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase). You must have WalletFeed Pro to send transactions to Lunch Money.
- A Lunch Money account and its password. Lunch Money has a 30-day free trial, and you can start the trial without a payment card. You can make an access token during the trial.

> **Note:** During the free trial, each Lunch Money page shows "Enter your billing information to avoid interruption in service!" This information is not necessary for an access token.

## Your access token stays on your iPhone

- WalletFeed keeps the access token in the Keychain on your iPhone. iOS encrypts the Keychain.
- The access token does not go to iCloud Keychain or to your other devices.
- WalletFeed has no account and no servers. No person at WalletFeed can see or get the access token.
- Your iPhone sends the access token only to Lunch Money, in each request to Lunch Money.
- When you delete the destination, WalletFeed deletes the access token from your iPhone. You can also delete the token in Lunch Money.

## Step 1: Open the Lunch Money form in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations, and the + icon at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. Below **Budgeting**, tap **Lunch Money**.

   ![The Add Destination screen with Lunch Money in the Budgeting list.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

5. If WalletFeed shows **WalletFeed Pro**, get [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).

   Result: After you get WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows the Lunch Money form.

## Step 2: Make an access token in Lunch Money

A Lunch Money access token gives access to all of the data in one budget. The token is for the budget that is open when you make the token. With the token, WalletFeed gets the list of your Lunch Money accounts and can make an Apple Card account. WalletFeed also adds, changes and deletes the transactions that it sends.

You can delete the token in Lunch Money (refer to [Delete the token in Lunch Money](#delete-the-token-in-lunch-money)). After you delete the token, WalletFeed cannot connect to Lunch Money with it.

To make the token on your iPhone, do these steps:

1. In the Lunch Money form, tap **Open Developers**.

   ![The Lunch Money form in WalletFeed, with the Access Token field and the Open Developers link.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/walletfeed-setup-lunch-money.webp)

   Result: Your web browser opens Lunch Money.

2. If Lunch Money shows "Welcome back!", get access to your Lunch Money account with your e-mail address and your password.

   ![The Lunch Money login page, with the LOGIN button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/lunch-money-login.webp)

   Result: Lunch Money shows **Home**. Lunch Money does not go back to the **Developers** page.

3. If Lunch Money does not show the **Developers** page, tap **☰** › **DEVELOPERS**.

   The menu icon (**☰**) is at the top right of the page. In the menu, **DEVELOPERS** is below **SETTINGS**.

   ![On an iPhone, the Lunch Money menu, with DEVELOPERS highlighted below SETTINGS.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/lunch-money-iphone-menu-developers.webp)

   Result: Lunch Money shows the **Developers** page.

4. Tap the green circle at the top of the page.

   The circle shows the first letter of the name of your budget. It is to the left of **☰**.

   ![On an iPhone, the top of the Lunch Money Developers page, with the green budget circle highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/lunch-money-iphone-green-circle.webp)

   Result: Lunch Money shows **Switch Accounts**. The open budget has "(Current)" after its name.

5. If you have more than one budget, tap the budget for your transactions.

   Above the list of budgets, Lunch Money shows **Create new budget account**. Do not tap it.

   ![On an iPhone, the Switch Accounts dialog in Lunch Money, with the open budget highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/lunch-money-iphone-switch-accounts.webp)

6. If you have only one budget, tap **CLOSE**.
7. Scroll to **NEW ACCESS TOKEN**.

   Lunch Money shows **NEW ACCESS TOKEN** below the form "Submit your contribution to Lunch Money". Do not use that form. That form sends a project to Lunch Money and does not make a token.

8. In **Label for access token (optional)**, type `WalletFeed`.

   The label helps you find the WalletFeed token in **ACTIVE ACCESS TOKENS**. It is not necessary to select an item in **What will you use this API key for? (optional)**.

   ![The new access token form in Lunch Money, with the label WalletFeed highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/lunch-money-token-label.webp)

9. Tap **REQUEST NEW ACCESS TOKEN**.

   ![On an iPhone, the new access token form below the SUBMIT button, with REQUEST NEW ACCESS TOKEN highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/lunch-money-iphone-request-token.webp)

   Result: Lunch Money shows the token in a box. Above the box, Lunch Money shows "This is your access token. Please save it now as this is the only time it will be shown to you!"

   > **Caution:** Do not tap **GOT IT!** before you tap **Copy**. After you tap **GOT IT!**, Lunch Money cannot show the token again.

10. In the box with the token, tap **Copy**.

    Lunch Money shows **Copy** in small text at the right end of the box.

    ![On an iPhone, the new access token in Lunch Money, with Copy highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/lunch-money-iphone-token-shown-copy.webp)

    Result: **Copy** changes to **Copied!**.

11. Tap **GOT IT!**.

    ![The Lunch Money token box after you copy the token, with the GOT IT! button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/lunch-money-token-copied-got-it.webp)

    Result: Lunch Money closes the box. **ACTIVE ACCESS TOKENS** shows the WalletFeed token.

## Step 3: Paste the token in WalletFeed

1. Open WalletFeed again.
2. If WalletFeed does not show the Lunch Money form, do [Step 1](#step-1-open-the-lunch-money-form-in-walletfeed) again.
3. Touch and hold **Access Token**.
4. Tap **Paste**.

   Result: WalletFeed connects to Lunch Money with the token. Then WalletFeed shows **Account**.

5. In **Account**, select the Lunch Money account for your transactions.

   If your budget has an account with the name Apple Card, WalletFeed selects that account. The list then does not show **New Apple Card Account**.

   If your budget has no account with that name, WalletFeed selects **New Apple Card Account**. With **New Apple Card Account**, WalletFeed makes a credit account with the name Apple Card. Its balance is $0.00.

   The list does not show closed accounts or accounts that cannot have transactions.

6. Tap **Add**.

   Result: WalletFeed shows **Send Transactions to Lunch Money?** The message tells you the data that Lunch Money receives, the Wallet accounts and the start date. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the new destination and does not send transactions.

7. Tap **Send**.

   Result: WalletFeed starts to send your transactions to Lunch Money. In **Destinations**, the name of the new destination starts with "Lunch Money".

   ![The Destinations screen with Lunch Money and three other destinations.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/walletfeed-destinations.webp)

## Data that Lunch Money receives

Lunch Money shows the transactions from WalletFeed on the **TRANSACTIONS** page, below **FINANCES**.

![The Lunch Money Transactions page with six sample transactions from WalletFeed in the Apple Card account.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/lunch-money-walletfeed-result.webp)

WalletFeed adds each transaction to the Lunch Money account that you selected. This account also receives the transactions from your other Wallet accounts, for example Apple Cash. To select the Wallet accounts, refer to [Send only some transactions](#send-only-some-transactions).

| From Wallet | In Lunch Money |
| --- | --- |
| The date of the transaction, in the time zone of your iPhone | **DATE** |
| The merchant name, or the description if there is no merchant name | **PAYEE** |
| The card statement text | Original payee name |
| The amount | **AMOUNT** |
| The currency | Currency |
| The ID of the transaction in Wallet | External ID |
| The Wallet status, the transaction type, the merchant category code and the WalletFeed category | Custom metadata |

Lunch Money shows a purchase with a minus sign, for example -$7.75. It shows a refund in green, for example $49.00. A payment to your card also goes to Lunch Money as money in.

WalletFeed uses the external ID to find the transaction again when the transaction changes. Apps that use the Lunch Money API can read the custom metadata.

WalletFeed does not set the Lunch Money category. Lunch Money uses your rules on each new transaction. Thus, a rule can set the category. Lunch Money shows each new transaction as unreviewed.

After WalletFeed adds a transaction, WalletFeed does not change the payee, category, notes, tags or review status. When the date, amount, currency or Wallet status changes in Wallet, WalletFeed makes the same change in Lunch Money.

If you change the date or the amount of a transaction in Lunch Money, WalletFeed can put the data from Wallet back. This occurs when WalletFeed sends the transaction again, for example with **Send History**.

If WalletFeed makes the Apple Card account, the account starts with a balance of $0.00. When WalletFeed adds or changes a transaction, the balance of the account does not change. But when WalletFeed deletes a transaction, Lunch Money changes the balance by the amount of that transaction. To correct the balance, refer to [If the balance in Lunch Money is not correct](#if-the-balance-in-lunch-money-is-not-correct).

Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to Lunch Money. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. After Lunch Money receives your transactions, the terms of Lunch Money are applicable to them.

## New and changed transactions

While WalletFeed is open, Lunch Money receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then sends the change.

Wallet shows a new charge as pending until the charge posts. Lunch Money does not show a pending status for transactions from WalletFeed. Thus, Lunch Money shows a pending charge as a usual transaction. WalletFeed sends the Wallet status in the custom metadata.

When the charge posts, WalletFeed uses the same transaction in Lunch Money. If the amount or the date changes, WalletFeed changes the transaction in Lunch Money. To send charges only after they post, you can set **Filter** to on and **Include Pending** to off (refer to [Send only some transactions](#send-only-some-transactions)).

Lunch Money receives a refund as a different transaction. If Wallet shows a charge as declined or expired, WalletFeed deletes the charge from Lunch Money. WalletFeed also deletes a transaction that Wallet removes. But WalletFeed does not delete a transaction that you divided or put in a group in Lunch Money.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. If you change **Initial History** before you add Lunch Money, the new destination receives transactions from the new start date.

To send previous transactions after you add Lunch Money, do these steps:

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Lunch Money destination.

   ![The Lunch Money destination in WalletFeed with Replace Token, Filter, Send History, Send Test and Delete.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/walletfeed-destination-detail.webp)

2. Tap **Send History**.
3. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

   Result: WalletFeed shows **Sending History** and the number of transactions that it sent.

4. To stop WalletFeed before it sends all of the transactions, tap **Send History** › **Stop Sending**.

WalletFeed sends previous transactions to Lunch Money in groups of 50. It waits 45 seconds between groups. Lunch Money does not receive the same transaction two times. If you changed the date or the amount of a transaction in Lunch Money, **Send History** puts the data from Wallet back.

For more information, refer to [Send previous transactions](/docs/send-history/).

## Change or remove the destination

You change the Lunch Money destination on its screen in **Destinations**. For more information about this screen, refer to [Destinations](/docs/destinations/).

### Send only some transactions

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Lunch Money destination.
2. Set **Filter** to on.
3. Set the filter controls (refer to the table).

| Control | Result |
| --- | --- |
| **Include** | WalletFeed sends all transactions, only purchases or only credits. |
| **Minimum** | WalletFeed sends only transactions of this amount or more. |
| **Include Pending** | If **Include Pending** is off, WalletFeed sends charges only after they post. |
| **Accounts** | WalletFeed sends only transactions from the Wallet accounts that you select. |
| **Categories** | WalletFeed sends only transactions in the categories that you select. |
| **Exclude** | WalletFeed does not send transactions from the merchants that you type. You must type a comma between two merchants. |

If Apple Intelligence is active, you can also type a rule in words:

1. In the field that shows "Travel over $50, not Uber", type the rule.
2. Tap the Apple Intelligence icon at the end of the field.

WalletFeed uses the filter only for the transactions that it sends after you set the filter. For more information, refer to [Filter the transactions for a destination](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

### Stop the destination for a time

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Lunch Money destination.
2. Set **Enabled** to off.

   Until you set **Enabled** to on again, WalletFeed does not send transactions to Lunch Money.

### Replace the token

If you deleted the token in Lunch Money, or if Lunch Money does not accept the token, do these steps:

1. Make a new access token for the same budget (refer to [Step 2](#step-2-make-an-access-token-in-lunch-money)).

   If the new token is for a different budget, WalletFeed cannot get access to the account.

2. Open WalletFeed again.
3. In **Destinations**, tap the Lunch Money destination.
4. Tap **Replace Token**.
5. Touch and hold **Access Token**.
6. Tap **Paste**.
7. Tap **Replace**.

   Result: Before WalletFeed puts the new token in the Keychain, WalletFeed connects to Lunch Money with the token. Then **Replace Token** shows a green checkmark.

### Remove Lunch Money from WalletFeed

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Lunch Money destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. Tap **Delete** again.

   Result: WalletFeed removes the destination and deletes the token from your iPhone. The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay in Lunch Money. Until you delete the token in Lunch Money, Lunch Money accepts the token.

### Delete the token in Lunch Money

1. On your iPhone, open [the Lunch Money Developers page](https://my.lunchmoney.app/developers).
2. If Lunch Money shows "Welcome back!", get access to your Lunch Money account with your e-mail address and your password.
3. If Lunch Money does not show the **Developers** page, tap **☰** › **DEVELOPERS**.
4. In **ACTIVE ACCESS TOKENS**, find the row for WalletFeed.

   Each row shows the label of the token and "Last activity". After WalletFeed uses the token, "Last activity" shows a date and a time.

   ![The list of active access tokens in Lunch Money, with the REVOKE button for WalletFeed highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/lunch-money-active-token-revoke.webp)

5. In the row for WalletFeed, tap **REVOKE**.

   Result: Lunch Money does not show a message before it deletes the token. Then Lunch Money shows "Successfully revoked token".

   ![On an iPhone, Lunch Money shows the message Successfully revoked token.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/lunch-money-iphone-token-revoked.webp)

After you delete the token, the Lunch Money destination in WalletFeed shows "Authentication failed" when WalletFeed tries to send transactions. To send transactions again, you must make a new token and [replace the token](#replace-the-token) in WalletFeed.

## If there is a problem

To make sure that WalletFeed can send transactions to Lunch Money, do these steps:

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Lunch Money destination.
2. Tap **Send Test**.

   Result: If Lunch Money receives the test transaction, WalletFeed shows a green checkmark.

> **Note:** **Send Test** adds a test transaction of $4.20 to the Lunch Money account. The payee of the test transaction is WalletFeed. If you tap **Send Test** again, WalletFeed does not add a second test transaction. You can delete the test transaction in Lunch Money.

### If WalletFeed shows "Token rejected (HTTP 401)"

Lunch Money does not accept the token, for example because you copied only a part of the token. WalletFeed then shows "Token rejected (HTTP 401). Request a new one in Lunch Money."

1. Make a new access token in Lunch Money (refer to [Step 2](#step-2-make-an-access-token-in-lunch-money)).
2. Open WalletFeed again.
3. Touch and hold **Access Token**.
4. Tap **Paste**.

### If the destination shows "Authentication failed"

Lunch Money does not accept the token of the destination, for example because a person deleted the token in Lunch Money.

1. Make a new access token in Lunch Money (refer to [Step 2](#step-2-make-an-access-token-in-lunch-money)).
2. Replace the token in WalletFeed (refer to [Replace the token](#replace-the-token)).

### If you did not copy the token

Lunch Money shows a token only one time.

1. In Lunch Money, open the **Developers** page again (refer to [Step 2](#step-2-make-an-access-token-in-lunch-money)).
2. In the row for the token that you did not copy, tap **REVOKE**.
3. Make a new access token (refer to [Step 2](#step-2-make-an-access-token-in-lunch-money)).

### If WalletFeed shows "The account is gone from Lunch Money" or "Rejected (HTTP 400)"

Lunch Money does not have the account for this destination, or the token is for a different budget. If you tap **Replace Token**, WalletFeed shows "The account is gone from Lunch Money. Add this destination again."

1. Remove the destination (refer to [Remove Lunch Money from WalletFeed](#remove-lunch-money-from-walletfeed)).
2. Add Lunch Money again (refer to [Step 1](#step-1-open-the-lunch-money-form-in-walletfeed)).

### If the transactions go to an incorrect budget

The token is for the budget that was open when you made the token.

1. Remove the destination (refer to [Remove Lunch Money from WalletFeed](#remove-lunch-money-from-walletfeed)).
2. Do [Step 1](#step-1-open-the-lunch-money-form-in-walletfeed), Step 2 and Step 3 again.

   In Step 2, tap the correct budget in **Switch Accounts** before you make the token.

The transactions in the incorrect budget stay there. You can delete them in Lunch Money.

### If Lunch Money does not receive new transactions

WalletFeed cannot send transactions to Lunch Money. For example, the destination is off, or **Background Sync** is off.

1. Open WalletFeed. While WalletFeed is open, it sends changes in seconds.
2. If **Destinations** shows **Sync Requires Pro**, tap **Upgrade**.
3. If the Lunch Money destination shows **Off**, set **Enabled** to on in the destination.
4. If **Filter** is on, make sure that the filter includes the new transactions.
5. Tap the gear icon at the top of **Destinations**.
6. Make sure that **Background Sync** is on.
7. Tap **Sync Now**.

After your iPhone starts again, WalletFeed cannot send transactions to destinations until you type your passcode one time.

### If the balance in Lunch Money is not correct

When WalletFeed deletes a transaction, Lunch Money changes the balance of the account. WalletFeed does not know the balance of your card.

1. On a computer, open [Lunch Money](https://my.lunchmoney.app) in a web browser.
2. Click **SETUP** at the top of the page.

   Result: Lunch Money shows **Accounts**.

3. Click the account that receives your transactions, for example **Apple Card**.

   ![The Lunch Money Accounts page, with the Apple Card credit account highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/lunch-money-accounts-apple-card.webp)

   Result: Lunch Money shows **Edit Account**.

4. In **CURRENT BALANCE**, type the correct balance.
5. Click **SAVE CHANGES**.

### If WalletFeed shows "Too many requests" or "Rejected (HTTP 429)"

Lunch Money accepts a maximum of 100 requests each minute.

1. Wait until WalletFeed tries again.

   Result: WalletFeed tries again at the time that it shows, or when it starts to send changes again.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Make

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a scenario in Make (the previous name of Make is Integromat). You add a Custom webhook in Make, then paste its URL in WalletFeed.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.
- A Make account. You can get an account on [Make's sign-up page](https://www.make.com/en/register). The Free plan has the **Webhooks** app.
- A computer with a web browser for the steps in Make. The screenshots show Make on a computer.

> **Note:** Make's Free plan has 1,000 credits each month. Each time that the webhook starts the scenario, the webhook uses 1 credit. Each module after the webhook uses more credits.

## Your URL stays on your iPhone

- WalletFeed keeps the webhook URL in the Keychain on your iPhone. iOS encrypts the Keychain.
- The webhook URL does not go to iCloud Keychain or to your other devices.
- WalletFeed has no account and no servers. No person at WalletFeed can see or get the webhook URL.
- Your iPhone sends the webhook URL only to Make, in each request to Make.
- When you delete the destination, WalletFeed deletes the webhook URL from your iPhone.

## Step 1: Add a Custom webhook in Make

The webhook gives you a URL. WalletFeed sends your transactions to this URL.

> **Caution:** Do not give the webhook URL to a different person. With the URL, a person can send data to your scenario.

1. On your computer, get access to your [Make](https://www.make.com) account.
2. Click **+ Create scenario**.

   ![The Make dashboard with the Create scenario button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/make-dashboard.webp)

3. If Make shows a **Scheduling** message, click **Got it**.
4. If Make shows the Maia panel, click **X** on the panel.

   Maia is not necessary for these steps.

5. In the scenario editor, click the large **+**.
6. In **Search all apps or modules**, type `Webhooks`.
7. Click the **Webhooks** app with the red icon.

   Make shows the app **Make** first. Below it, Make shows its webhook modules, for example **List webhooks**. The app **Make** is not correct for these steps.

   ![The Make app search with the Webhooks app highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/make-search-webhooks.webp)

8. In **Triggers**, click **Custom webhook**.

   **Custom mailhook** is above **Custom webhook**. **Custom mailhook** is not correct for these steps.

   ![The Webhooks app in Make with the Custom webhook trigger highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/make-custom-webhook.webp)

9. Below **Webhook**, click **Create a webhook**.
10. In **Webhook name**, replace the name with `WalletFeed`.
11. Do not click **+ Add API key**.

    If the webhook has an API key, Make accepts only the requests that contain the key. WalletFeed cannot send an API key.

12. Click **Save**.

    ![The Create a webhook dialog with WalletFeed as the name and the Save button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/make-name-webhook.webp)

13. Below **Webhook URL**, click the copy button at the end of the URL.

    Make does not show the full URL. If you select the text, you copy only a part of the URL.

    ![The webhook panel in Make with the copy button for the webhook URL highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/make-copy-webhook-url.webp)

14. Keep the scenario open.

    When you tap **Add** in WalletFeed, Make must show **Listening for data**.

> **Note:** If you use a Mac with the same Apple Account as your iPhone, you can paste the URL on your iPhone with [Universal Clipboard](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102430).

## Step 2: Add Make in WalletFeed

On Make's Free plan, while the scenario is not active, the queue of the webhook can contain a maximum of 50 transactions. A new Make destination receives a maximum of 30 days of previous transactions, and these can be more than 50.

If you use Make's Free plan, you can set **Initial History** to **Today** before you add Make. Then Make receives no previous transactions. To set **Initial History**, do these steps:

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Sync** section, set **Initial History** to **Today**.

   **Settings** shows the **Sync** section only with WalletFeed Pro.

4. Tap **Done**.

To add Make, do these steps:

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen in WalletFeed with the + button and no destinations.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In **Automations**, tap **Make**.

   You can also type `Make` in the search field.

5. If WalletFeed shows the **WalletFeed Pro** screen, get WalletFeed Pro on that screen. WalletFeed then opens the **Make** screen.
6. Paste the URL in the **Webhook Address** field.

   The URL stays in the Keychain on your iPhone.

   ![The Make screen in WalletFeed with the Webhook Address field and the Add button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/walletfeed-setup-make.webp)

7. Tap **Add**. WalletFeed sends a sample to Make.

   The sample is one transaction, with `merchant` WalletFeed and `amount` -4.2.

8. Read the message **Send Transactions to Make?**

   The message tells you the data that Make receives, the Wallet accounts of the transactions and the start date.

9. Tap **Send**. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed does not add the destination.

**Destinations** then shows the new destination with the name Make. WalletFeed sends the transactions from the start date to Make. Until the scenario is active, Make keeps these transactions in the queue of the webhook.

## Step 3: Save the scenario in Make

1. On your computer, make sure that Make shows **Detected data** with the fields of the sample.

   Make shows “15 values detected and ready to map”.

   ![Make shows the 15 fields that it found in WalletFeed's sample, with the Save button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/make-data-detected.webp)

2. Click **Save** in the webhook panel.
3. To change the scenario name, replace the name with `WalletFeed` at the top of the editor.
4. Click **Save** in the toolbar at the bottom of the editor.

   If a webhook is not in a scenario for more than 5 days, Make deactivates the webhook. Then WalletFeed cannot send transactions to it.

   ![The WalletFeed scenario in Make with the Save button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/make-save-scenario.webp)

## Step 4: Add modules and activate the scenario

1. In the scenario, add more modules after the webhook.

   These modules can use each field of a transaction, for example `amount` or `merchant`.

2. Click **Save** in the toolbar at the bottom of the editor.
3. To start the scenario one time, click **Run once**.

   If the queue of the webhook is empty, Make shows **Waiting for data...** until Make receives a request.

4. If Make shows **Use existing data**, click **Use existing data**.

   Make starts the scenario one time with data from the queue.

5. After the scenario starts, look at the fields in **Output**.
6. To activate the scenario, click the **Inactive** switch at the top of the editor.

   With **Immediately as data arrives**, the scenario starts each time that Make receives a request.

7. If Make shows a message about the data in the queue, click the button that processes the data.

   Then the scenario gets the transactions in the queue. If you delete the data, the scenario does not get these transactions.

## Data that Make receives

Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to Make. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. After Make receives your transactions, the terms of Make are applicable to them.

WalletFeed sends one HTTP request for each new or changed transaction. If a field has no value, Make shows the field as empty. The request has these 15 fields:

| Field in Make | Value from Wallet |
| --- | --- |
| `event` | `created` the first time that WalletFeed finds the transaction in Wallet, and `updated` after a change |
| `id` | The transaction ID from Wallet. The ID stays the same when the transaction changes. |
| `date` | The day of the purchase in your time zone, for example 2026-10-30 |
| `merchant` | The merchant name, or the description if Wallet has no merchant name |
| `amount` | A negative number for a purchase, for example -6.75, and a positive number for a refund or a payment |
| `currency` | The currency code, for example USD |
| `category` | The WalletFeed category, for example `Dining` |
| `status` | The Wallet status, for example `pending`, or `booked` after the charge posts |
| `pending` | `true` when `status` is `pending` or `authorized`, and `false` after the charge posts |
| `account` | The Wallet account, for example Apple Card |
| `description` | The description from Wallet |
| `type` | The type of transaction, for example `pointOfSale` or `refund` |
| `mcc` | The merchant category code, for example 5814 |
| `foreignAmount` | For a purchase in a different currency, the value in the currency of the merchant |
| `foreignCurrency` | The currency code of `foreignAmount` |

`foreignAmount` is also a negative number for a purchase and a positive number for a refund. If the bank does not accept a pending charge or Wallet removes a transaction, Make receives a request with only two fields. These fields are `id`, and `event` with the value `deleted`.

## New and changed transactions

While WalletFeed is open, Make receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then sends the change. **Background Sync** is on until you set it to off. After your iPhone starts again, WalletFeed does not send transactions until you type your iPhone passcode one time.

Make receives a pending charge again when the charge posts. Then `event` is `updated` and `status` is `booked`, with the same `id`. For a refund, `amount` is a positive number and `type` is `refund`.

Each request starts the scenario one time. Thus, an update also uses credits.

If WalletFeed stops while it sends changes, WalletFeed can send the same changes again. A scenario that adds rows must first try to find a row with the same `id`. If the scenario finds that row, it must change the row.

## Send previous transactions

A new Make destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. But Make receives a maximum of 30 days of previous transactions.

To send more transactions, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. On your computer, make sure that the scenario is active in Make.
2. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
3. In **Destinations**, tap the Make destination.
4. Tap **Send History**.
5. Tap a period: **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.
6. In the message **Send History to Make?**, tap **Send**.

   The message shows “Each transaction runs your scenario.”

WalletFeed sends the newest transactions first. While WalletFeed sends the transactions, the destination screen shows **Sending History** and a count, for example 20 of 50.

**Send History** uses the filter of the Make destination. Each transaction uses credits in Make. The Free plan has 1,000 credits each month.

To stop **Send History**, do these steps:

1. Tap **Send History**.
2. Tap **Stop Sending**.

The transactions that Make received stay in Make.

## Change or remove the destination

To change the transactions that go to Make, change the [filter](/docs/choose-what-to-send/) of the Make destination. To stop the destination for a period, set the **Enabled** switch to off.

In **Webhook**, the destination screen shows only the first part of the URL, for example `hook.us2.make.com`.

To find the URL of the webhook again, do these steps:

1. On your computer, in the Make sidebar, click **Webhooks**.
2. Click **WalletFeed**.
3. Below **Webhook URL**, click the copy button.

   ![The Detail page of the WalletFeed webhook in Make, with the copy button for the webhook URL highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/make-webhook-detail.webp)

To replace the URL, for example after you add a new webhook, do these steps:

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. In **Destinations**, tap the Make destination.
3. Tap **Replace URL**.
4. Paste the URL in the **Webhook Address** field.
5. Tap **Replace**.

   Before WalletFeed keeps the new URL, it sends a sample. If Make does not accept the sample, WalletFeed does not replace the URL.

To remove the destination, do these steps:

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Make destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. In the message **Delete Make?**, tap **Delete**.

The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay in Make.

To also remove the webhook, do these steps on your computer:

1. In the Make sidebar, click **Webhooks**.
2. Click **⋮** for the WalletFeed webhook.
3. Click **Delete**.
4. In **Please confirm**, click **Delete**.
5. In **Confirmation required**, click **OK**.

Make also removes the transactions in the queue of the webhook. The scenario stops.

## If there is a problem

### If you cannot tap Add

The text in the **Webhook Address** field is not a Make webhook URL. A Make webhook URL starts with `https://hook.`, for example `https://hook.us2.make.com/`.

1. On your computer, copy the URL again with the copy button in Make.
2. On your iPhone, paste the full URL in the **Webhook Address** field.

### If WalletFeed shows “The webhook refused the test (HTTP …)”

Make did not accept the sample, for example because the webhook has an API key, or because Make removed or deactivated the webhook.

1. In Make, add a new Custom webhook without an API key (refer to Step 1).
2. Copy the URL of the new webhook with the copy button.
3. In WalletFeed, paste the URL in the **Webhook Address** field.
4. Tap **Add**.

### If WalletFeed shows “Too many requests. Try again in a few minutes.”

Make accepts a maximum of 300 requests in 10 seconds.

1. After some minutes, tap **Add** again.

### If Make does not show the fields

Make did not show **Listening for data** when WalletFeed sent the sample.

1. On your computer, in the webhook panel, click **Detect new values**.
2. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
3. In **Destinations**, tap the Make destination.
4. Tap **Send Test**.
5. On your computer, make sure that Make shows the fields of the sample.
6. Click **Save** in the webhook panel.

### If WalletFeed shows “Rejected (HTTP 400)”

The queue of the webhook is full, and Make does not accept more requests. While the scenario is not active, Make keeps the requests in the queue. On the Free plan, the queue can contain a maximum of 50 requests. The **Webhooks** page in Make shows the number of requests in the queue, for example 50/50.

1. On your computer, open the scenario in Make.
2. To activate the scenario, click the **Inactive** switch.
3. If Make shows a message about the data in the queue, click the button that processes the data.
4. On your iPhone, open **Settings** › **Sync** in WalletFeed.
5. Tap **Sync Now**.
6. Tap **Done**.
7. In **Destinations**, tap the Make destination.
8. If the destination screen shows **Try Again** below **Sending History**, tap **Try Again**.

### If WalletFeed shows “Rejected (HTTP 410)”

Make removed or deactivated the webhook. If a webhook is not in a scenario for more than 5 days, Make deactivates it.

1. On your computer, add a new Custom webhook in Make (refer to Step 1).
2. Save the scenario (refer to Step 3).
3. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
4. In **Destinations**, tap the Make destination.
5. Tap **Replace URL**.
6. Paste the new URL in the **Webhook Address** field.
7. Tap **Replace**.

### If the scenario does not start for new transactions

The scenario is not active. Make keeps the transactions in the queue of the webhook.

1. On your computer, open the scenario in Make.
2. To activate the scenario, click the **Inactive** switch.
3. If Make shows a message about the data in the queue, click the button that processes the data.

### If Make receives transactions only while WalletFeed is open

**Background Sync** is off, or your iPhone started again and you did not type its passcode.

1. In WalletFeed, open **Settings** › **Sync**.
2. Set **Background Sync** to on.
3. After your iPhone starts again, type its passcode one time.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Notion

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a database in Notion. You make a connection in Notion and give it access to a page, and then WalletFeed makes the database on that page.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings in Wallet on that iPhone.
- WalletFeed, with [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/). WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.
- A Notion account. You must be a Workspace Owner in the workspace that receives your transactions, because only a Workspace Owner can make a connection.
- A computer with a web browser for step 1 and step 2.

## Your token stays on your iPhone

- WalletFeed keeps the token in the Keychain on your iPhone. iOS encrypts the Keychain.
- The token does not go to iCloud Keychain or to your other devices.
- WalletFeed has no account and no servers. No person at WalletFeed can see or get the token.
- Your iPhone sends the token only to Notion, in each request to Notion.
- When you delete the destination, WalletFeed deletes the token from your iPhone. You can also delete the connection in Notion.

## Step 1: Make a connection in Notion

On the **Configuration** tab of the connection, Notion shows the text "Keep it secret, since anyone with the token can act on behalf of the connection." For information about the token in WalletFeed, refer to [Your token stays on your iPhone](#your-token-stays-on-your-iphone).

- With the token, WalletFeed can open only the pages that the connection has access to. In step 2, you give the connection access to one page and its child pages.
- WalletFeed makes its database on the page from step 2. WalletFeed changes only the rows that it sends.
- You can delete the connection in Notion (refer to [Delete the connection in Notion](#delete-the-connection-in-notion)). After you delete the connection, Notion does not accept its token.

To make the connection, do these steps:

1. On your computer, open [Notion's Developer tools](https://app.notion.com/developers/connections).
2. If Notion shows **Log in to your Notion account**, get access to your Notion account.

   Result: Notion shows **Developer tools** on the **Connections** tab.

3. Click **+ New connection**.

   ![Notion's Developer tools page on the Connections tab, with the New connection button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/notion-developer-tools-connections.webp)

4. In **Connection name**, type a name for the connection, for example `WalletFeed`.
5. In **Authentication method**, select **API token**.

   If you select **OAuth**, Notion does not show an API token on the **Configuration** tab. WalletFeed uses the API token.

   ![The New connection dialog, with the name WalletFeed, the API token method and the Create connection button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/notion-new-connection.webp)

6. Click **Create connection**.

   Result: Notion opens the connection on the **Configuration** tab. In **Integration token**, the tab shows the **API token**. You will copy the token on your iPhone in step 3.

   ![The Configuration tab of the WalletFeed connection, with the API token field and the Copy button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/notion-configuration-api-token.webp)

7. Scroll to **Capabilities**.
8. Make sure that **Read content**, **Update content** and **Insert content** have a checkmark.

   Notion selects these three content capabilities for a new connection. WalletFeed uses the three capabilities.

9. In **User capabilities**, select **No user information**.

   Notion selects **Read user information including email addresses** for a new connection. WalletFeed does not use user information or comments. The tab has no **Save** button, because Notion saves each change when you make it.

   ![The Capabilities section of the connection, with the three content capabilities and No user information.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/notion-capabilities.webp)

## Step 2: Give the connection access to a page

A new connection cannot open pages in Notion. WalletFeed makes its database on a page that the connection can open.

> **Note:** If you give the connection access to a page, the connection also gets access to all of the child pages of that page. If the connection has access only to a new page for WalletFeed, the connection cannot open your other pages.

1. In Notion, click **New page** (the pencil icon at the top of the sidebar).
2. Click **Page**.

   ![The New page menu in the Notion sidebar, with Page as the first item.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/notion-new-page.webp)

3. Type a title for the page, for example `Budget`.
4. Move the pointer to the top of the page.

   While you type, Notion does not show the buttons at the top right of the page.

5. Click **•••** at the top right of the page.

   ![The Budget page in Notion, with the ••• button at the top right.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/notion-page-actions.webp)

6. Click **More** at the bottom of the menu.

   The menu does not show **Connections**. **Connections** is in **More**.

   ![The page menu, with More at the bottom.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/notion-page-menu-more.webp)

7. Click **Connections**.

   Result: Notion shows **Search for connections…** and a list of other apps.

   ![The More menu, with None next to Connections.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/notion-more-connections.webp)

8. In **Search for connections…**, type the name of your connection.

   Notion shows your connection only after you type its name. The apps below **Add a new connection**, for example Bardeen, are not your connection.

   ![The Connections menu, with the search field above a list of other apps.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/notion-connections-search.webp)

9. Click your connection.

   ![The Connections menu, with the WalletFeed connection as the search result.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/notion-connections-walletfeed.webp)

   Result: Notion shows a message with the name of your connection, for example **Add WalletFeed to this page**. The message shows the capabilities that the connection gets on this page and its child pages.

10. Click **Add to page**.

    Result: The connection gets access to the page. In the **More** menu, **Connections** shows 1.

    ![The message Add WalletFeed to this page, with the capabilities of the connection and the Add to page button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/notion-add-to-page.webp)

You can also give the connection access to the page in **Developer tools**:

1. On your computer, open [Notion's Developer tools](https://app.notion.com/developers/connections).
2. Click the name of your connection.

   ![The Connections tab of Developer tools, with the WalletFeed connection.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/notion-connections-list.webp)

3. Click the **Content access** tab.
4. Click **Edit access**.

   Result: Notion shows **Manage page access**.
