   ![The Content access tab of the WalletFeed connection, with No page access and the Edit access button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/notion-content-access.webp)

5. Click **Private**, or the teamspace that has the page.
6. Select the page that you made.

   ![The Manage page access dialog, with a checkmark for the Budget page.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/notion-manage-page-access.webp)

7. Click **Save**.

   Result: The **Content access** tab shows the page.

   ![The Content access tab, with the Budget page in the list.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/notion-content-access-budget.webp)

## Step 3: Paste the token in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations, and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In **Sheets & Databases**, tap **Notion**.

   ![The Add Destination list, with Notion in the Sheets & Databases section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows the **WalletFeed Pro** screen. After you get WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows the Notion screen.

5. Tap **Developer Portal**.

   Result: Your web browser opens **Developer tools** in Notion, on the **Connections** tab.

   ![The Notion screen in WalletFeed, with the Token field, four steps and the Developer Portal link.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/walletfeed-setup-notion.webp)

   > **Note:** The steps on the Notion screen in WalletFeed give the path **•••** › **Connections** › **Add connection**. In Notion, the path is **•••** › **More** › **Connections**. Step 2 on this page gives the path that Notion shows.

6. If Notion shows **Log in to your Notion account**, get access to your Notion account.
7. Tap the name of your connection.

   On an iPhone, the table of connections is wider than the screen. The name of the connection is at the left.

   ![Notion's Developer tools on an iPhone, with the WalletFeed connection on the Connections tab.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/notion-iphone-connections-list.webp)

   Result: Notion opens the connection on the **Configuration** tab.

8. In **API token**, tap **Copy**.

   **Copy** is the third icon to the right of the token.

   ![The Configuration tab on an iPhone, with the API token field and the Copy button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/notion-iphone-api-token.webp)

   > **Caution:** Do not tap **Refresh API token**, the icon to the left of **Copy**. If you tap it, Notion makes a new token and does not accept the token in WalletFeed.

9. Open WalletFeed again.
10. Paste the token in **Token**.

    Result: WalletFeed shows **Database** and **Page** below **Token**.

WalletFeed keeps the token in the Keychain on your iPhone.

## Step 4: Select the page and add Notion

1. Make sure that **Database** shows **New**.
2. In **Page**, select the page from step 2. WalletFeed shows "Adds a WalletFeed Transactions database to the page."
3. Tap **Add**. WalletFeed makes the **WalletFeed Transactions** database on the page.
4. On the message **Send Transactions to Notion?**, tap **Send**.

   The message tells you the data that Notion will receive, the Wallet accounts and the start date. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the destination and sends nothing. The empty database stays on the page.

WalletFeed starts to send your transactions to the **WalletFeed Transactions** database. In **Destinations**, the name of the new destination has "Notion ·" before the name of your Notion workspace.

> **Note:** **Database** also shows the databases that the connection can open and that have a text property with the name **WalletFeed ID**. If you select one of these databases, WalletFeed writes to the properties with a name from **WalletFeed Transactions** and a type that can contain the value. If you add Notion again and **Database** shows **New**, WalletFeed makes a second **WalletFeed Transactions** database.

## Properties in the database

WalletFeed makes the **WalletFeed Transactions** database with these properties. Each row is one transaction. The table gives the properties in the same sequence as the database in Notion.

![The WalletFeed Transactions database in Notion, with six sample transactions from WalletFeed.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/notion-walletfeed-result.webp)

| Property | Type | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Merchant** | Title | The merchant name. If Wallet has no merchant name, WalletFeed uses the description. |
| **Account** | Select | The name of the Wallet account, for example Apple Card. |
| **Amount** | Number, in dollars | Less than zero for money out (for example, a purchase). More than zero for money in (for example, a payment or a refund). |
| **Category** | Select | The WalletFeed category, for example Groceries or Travel. |
| **Currency** | Select | The currency code, for example USD. |
| **Date** | Date | The day of the transaction, in the time zone of your iPhone. |
| **Description** | Text | The description of the transaction in Wallet. |
| **Foreign Amount** | Number | The amount in the merchant's currency. It is less than zero when **Amount** is less than zero. It is empty for a purchase in dollars. |
| **Foreign Currency** | Select | The code of the merchant's currency. It is empty for a purchase in dollars. |
| **MCC** | Number | The merchant category code. This number identifies the type of merchant. |
| **Pending** | Checkbox | WalletFeed selects this checkbox while the charge is pending. |
| **Status** | Select | The status of the transaction in Wallet, for example pending or booked. |
| **Type** | Select | The transaction type in Wallet. |
| **WalletFeed ID** | Text | The ID that WalletFeed uses to find the row again. |

WalletFeed writes only to these properties. You can add other properties to the database, and WalletFeed does not change them. WalletFeed finds each property by its name and each row by its **WalletFeed ID**. Thus, the names of these properties and the **WalletFeed ID** values must stay the same.

Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to Notion. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. After Notion receives your transactions, the terms of Notion are applicable to them.

## New and changed transactions

While WalletFeed is open, Notion receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then sends the change.

WalletFeed sends a pending charge to Notion and selects **Pending**. When Wallet changes the status of the charge to booked, WalletFeed updates **Status** and **Pending** in the same row. A refund is a new row with an **Amount** of more than zero.

If Wallet changes the status of a pending charge to rejected, WalletFeed moves its row to the trash in Notion. WalletFeed also moves a row to the trash when Wallet removes the transaction. In Notion, you can move a row from the trash to the database again.

Notion has a limit on requests. Thus, WalletFeed sends not more than 3 requests each second. As a result, WalletFeed can be slow to send a long history.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. To change **Initial History**, do these steps before you add Notion:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In **Sync**, tap **Initial History**.
3. Select **Today**, **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

   ![The Settings screen, with Initial History set to All in the Sync section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/walletfeed-settings.webp)

To send more previous transactions to your Notion destination, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Notion destination.
2. Tap **Send History**.
3. Select **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

   ![The destination screen for Lunch Money, with Send History below Filter.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/walletfeed-destination-detail.webp)

If the database has a row for a transaction, WalletFeed does not add a second row. WalletFeed finds that row by its **WalletFeed ID** and updates it.

While WalletFeed sends the history, the destination screen shows **Sending History** and a progress bar. If you tap **Send History** › **Stop Sending**, WalletFeed stops before it sends all of the history. When WalletFeed completes the history, **History** shows **All sent**, or **Sent from** and the start date.

## Change or remove the destination

To change the destination, tap the Notion destination in **Destinations**. On the destination screen, you can do these tasks:

| Task | On the destination screen |
| --- | --- |
| Stop for a time | Set **Enabled** to off. To start again, set **Enabled** to on. |
| Send only some transactions | Set **Filter** to on. Then set **Include**, **Minimum**, **Include Pending**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**. |
| Use a new token | Tap **Replace Token**. Paste the new token. Tap **Replace**. WalletFeed makes sure that it can read the database with the new token. |
| Make sure that WalletFeed can write to the database | Tap **Send Test**. WalletFeed adds a test row with the merchant "WalletFeed" and the account "Sample Card". |
| Remove the destination | Tap **Delete**. Tap **Delete** again. The rows that WalletFeed sent stay in Notion. |

If Apple Intelligence is active on your iPhone, you can also type a filter rule in words:

1. Set **Filter** to on.
2. In the field below **Filter**, type a rule, for example "Travel over $50, not Uber".
3. Tap the Apple Intelligence icon at the end of the field.

If you remove the destination, the connection in Notion stays. The connection can open the page until you disconnect it from the page or delete it.

### Disconnect the connection from the page

1. On your computer, open the page in Notion.
2. Click **•••** at the top right of the page.
3. Click **More**.
4. Click **Connections**.
5. In **Active connections**, click the arrow to the right of your connection.

   ![The Connections menu of the page, with WalletFeed in Active connections.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/notion-active-connections.webp)

6. Click **Disconnect**.

After you disconnect the connection, it cannot open the page or the database. If WalletFeed has a Notion destination for this database, the destination shows "Rejected (HTTP 404)".

### Delete the connection in Notion

When you delete the connection, Notion also deletes its API token.

1. On your computer, open [Notion's Developer tools](https://app.notion.com/developers/connections).
2. Click the name of your connection.
3. On the **Configuration** tab, scroll to **Danger zone** at the bottom.
4. Click **Delete**.

   ![The bottom of the Configuration tab, with the Delete button in Danger zone.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/notion-danger-zone-delete.webp)

5. In **Delete connection?**, click **Delete this connection**.

   ![The message Delete connection?, with the Delete this connection button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/notion-delete-connection.webp)

After you delete the connection, Notion does not accept its token. If WalletFeed has a Notion destination with this token, the destination shows "Authentication failed".

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows "Token rejected. Copy it again from the Developer portal."

Notion did not accept the token. For example, you pasted only a part of the token.

1. On your iPhone, open [Notion's Developer tools](https://app.notion.com/developers/connections).
2. Tap the name of your connection.
3. In **API token**, tap **Copy**.
4. Open WalletFeed again.
5. Paste the token in **Token**.

### If WalletFeed tells you to give the connection access to a page

The connection has no access to the page or the database. WalletFeed shows "Share a page with your connection, then try again." or "Share the page or database with your connection, then try again."

1. Give the connection access to a page (refer to [step 2](#step-2-give-the-connection-access-to-a-page)).
2. In WalletFeed, tap **Try Again**.

### If WalletFeed shows "Give the connection read, update and insert content capabilities."

The connection does not have the three content capabilities that WalletFeed uses.

1. On your iPhone, open [Notion's Developer tools](https://app.notion.com/developers/connections).
2. Tap the name of your connection.
3. On the **Configuration** tab, scroll to **Capabilities**.
4. If **Read content**, **Update content** or **Insert content** has no checkmark, select it.
5. Open WalletFeed again.
6. Tap **Try Again**.

### If WalletFeed shows "Notion is limiting requests. Try again in a minute."

Notion has a limit on requests, and the connection got to this limit.

1. Wait for 1 minute.
2. In WalletFeed, tap **Try Again**.

### If the destination shows "Authentication failed"

Notion rejected the token. For example, a person deleted the connection, clicked **Refresh API token** or removed the checkmark from a content capability.

1. On your iPhone, open [Notion's Developer tools](https://app.notion.com/developers/connections).
2. Tap the name of your connection.

   If you cannot find the connection, make a new connection (refer to [step 1](#step-1-make-a-connection-in-notion)). Then give the new connection access to the page (refer to [step 2](#step-2-give-the-connection-access-to-a-page)).

3. In **API token**, tap **Copy**.
4. On the **Configuration** tab, scroll to **Capabilities**.
5. If **Read content**, **Update content** or **Insert content** has no checkmark, select it.
6. Open WalletFeed again.
7. Tap **Destinations**.

   ![The Destinations list, with a destination that shows Authentication failed.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/walletfeed-destinations-failure.webp)

8. Tap the Notion destination.
9. Tap **Replace Token**.
10. Paste the token in **Token**.
11. Tap **Replace**.

A Notion workspace on the Free plan with more than one member has a limit of 1,000 blocks. Each row in the database is a block. After the workspace gets to this limit, Notion does not accept new rows. Then WalletFeed shows "Authentication failed".

### If the destination shows "Rejected (HTTP 404)"

The connection cannot find the database. For example, a person disconnected the connection from the page.

1. Give the connection access to the page again (refer to [step 2](#step-2-give-the-connection-access-to-a-page)).
2. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap the Notion destination.
4. Tap **Send Test**.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-numbers/ -->
# Open Apple Card transactions in Numbers

WalletFeed saves your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a CSV file that you can open in Numbers. With WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed updates the file when your transactions change.

## Before you start

To do the steps on this page, you must have:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- WalletFeed, with access to your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account
- Numbers on your iPhone, or on a Mac that has access to your iCloud Drive
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), for a file that WalletFeed updates.

WalletFeed is available only in the US.

WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase. Without WalletFeed Pro, you can [make one CSV file](#make-one-csv-file-without-walletfeed-pro), but WalletFeed does not update that file.

## Step 1: Add a CSV file in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-numbers/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the search field, type `Numbers`.

   ![The Add Destination screen with the Destinations search field above the Budgeting list.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-numbers/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

5. Tap **CSV File**.

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, the **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens. After you get WalletFeed Pro, the **Files** screen opens.

6. Make sure that **Format** is **CSV**.
7. Make sure that **Save As** is **One File**.

   ![The Files screen with Format set to CSV, Save As set to One File and the name WalletFeed Transactions.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-numbers/walletfeed-setup-csv-file.webp)

   With **One File**, WalletFeed writes all your transactions to one file. The rows are in date sequence, and the row with the last date is at the top. You can also select **One File per Month**. Then each file has its month in the name, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.csv`.

8. Tap **Folder**.
9. Select a folder in iCloud Drive.

   **Folder** then shows the name of the folder.

10. To use a different file name, type it in **Name**.

    At the end of the name, WalletFeed adds `.csv`. For example, the file name is `WalletFeed Transactions.csv`.

11. Tap **Add** at the top of the screen.

    You can tap **Add** only after you select a folder.

12. When WalletFeed shows **Save Transactions to Files?**, tap **Save**.

    The message tells you the data that WalletFeed saves in the file. It also gives the accounts and the start date of the transactions. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the new destination.

WalletFeed then writes your transactions to the file.

## Step 2: Open the file in Numbers

1. On your iPhone, open Numbers.
2. Tap **Browse**.
3. Open the folder that you selected in Step 1.
4. Tap the file, for example `WalletFeed Transactions.csv`.

Numbers shows each transaction as a row in the spreadsheet. If WalletFeed changes the file after you open it, Numbers shows the changes only after you open the file again.

## Make one CSV file without WalletFeed Pro

[Export CSV](/docs/export-csv/) makes one CSV file with the transactions from a period that you select. You can use **Export CSV** without WalletFeed Pro. The file does not change after you save it.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Data** section, tap **Export CSV**.

   ![The Settings screen with Export CSV in the Data section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-numbers/walletfeed-settings-3.webp)

4. Tap **Range**.
5. Select **This Month**, **Last Month**, **Last 90 Days**, **This Year** or **All**.

   ![The Export CSV screen with Range set to This Month, 29 transactions and the Export button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-numbers/walletfeed-export-csv.webp)

   **Transactions** shows the number of transactions in the period.

6. Tap **Export**.

   The iOS menu opens with the name of the file, for example `Apple Card Last Month.csv`.

7. Tap **Save to Files**.
8. Select a folder in iCloud Drive.
9. Tap **Save**.
10. Open Numbers.
11. Tap **Browse**.
12. Open the folder that you selected in step 8.
13. Tap the file.

## Columns in the file

Each CSV file from WalletFeed has one row for each transaction. The file has these columns:

| Column | Data |
| --- | --- |
| **Date** | The date of the transaction, for example 2026-10-28. |
| **Posted Date** | The date that the charge posted. It is empty while the charge is pending. |
| **Merchant** | The merchant name. If Wallet has no merchant name, this column has the text from **Description**. |
| **Description** | The text of the transaction in Wallet. |
| **Original Description** | The text of the transaction on the card statement. |
| **Amount** | The value of the transaction, for example -23.40. It has a minus sign for purchases and fees, and no minus sign for payments and refunds. |
| **Currency** | The currency code, for example USD. |
| **Direction** | `debit` for purchases and fees, or `credit` for refunds, payments and deposits. |
| **Status** | The condition of the transaction in Wallet: `authorized`, `pending`, `booked` (posted) or `memo`. A file from **Export CSV** can also have `rejected` (a declined charge). |
| **Type** | The transaction type in Wallet, for example `pointOfSale` (a purchase), `refund`, `billPayment` (a payment) or `transfer`. |
| **Category** | The WalletFeed category, for example `Groceries`, `Dining` or `Cash & Transfers`. |
| **MCC** | The merchant category code from the card network. |
| **Account** | The Wallet account, for example Apple Card. |
| **Foreign Amount** | For a purchase in a different currency, the value in that currency. |
| **Foreign Currency** | The code of that different currency. |
| **WalletFeed ID** | The ID of the transaction. WalletFeed uses it to find and update each row. |

> **Caution:** Do not add columns or rows to `WalletFeed Transactions.csv`. When WalletFeed updates the file, it removes all other columns and all rows that have no **WalletFeed ID**.

## Changes to the file

While WalletFeed is open, `WalletFeed Transactions.csv` receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then updates the file. If WalletFeed cannot open the folder at that time, it updates the file when you open WalletFeed, or when your iPhone is on a charger.

A pending charge is in the file with `pending` or `authorized` in **Status**. When the charge posts, WalletFeed updates that row. WalletFeed removes the rows of declined and expired charges, and the rows of transactions that Wallet removes. A refund is a different transaction. Its **Amount** has no minus sign.

## Send previous transactions

A new CSV file also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. To add transactions from before that date, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap **WalletFeed Transactions**, or the name that you typed.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

Because WalletFeed finds each row by its **WalletFeed ID**, a transaction does not get a second row.

## Change or remove the destination

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap **WalletFeed Transactions**, or the name that you typed.

On the destination screen, you can do these tasks:

| Task | On the destination screen |
| --- | --- |
| Send only some transactions | Set **Filter** to on. Then set **Include**, **Minimum**, **Include Pending**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**. |
| Put the file in a different folder | Tap **Change Folder**. Then select the folder. |
| Stop the changes to the file | Set **Enabled** to off. |
| Remove the destination | Tap **Delete**. Then tap **Delete** again. |

After you select a different folder, WalletFeed writes your transactions from the start date to a file in that folder. If you delete the destination, the file and its transactions stay in the folder.

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows “Couldn't open this folder.”

WalletFeed cannot get access to the folder that you selected.

1. Tap **Folder** (or **Change Folder** on the destination screen).
2. Select a different folder in iCloud Drive.

### If WalletFeed shows “Can't open the folder. Choose it again.”

WalletFeed does not have access to the folder of the destination.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Change Folder**.
4. Select the folder again.

### If WalletFeed shows “The file has no WalletFeed ID column. Rename it to start a new one.”

Because the file in the folder has no **WalletFeed ID** column, WalletFeed cannot find the row for each transaction.

1. On your iPhone, open the Files app.
2. Open the folder of the destination.
3. Touch and hold `WalletFeed Transactions.csv`.
4. Tap **Rename**.
5. Type a different name, for example `WalletFeed Transactions 1`.
6. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
7. Tap the destination.
8. Tap **Send History**.
9. Tap **All**.

WalletFeed makes a new `WalletFeed Transactions.csv` with all your transactions.

### If the folder has no CSV file

WalletFeed writes the file only when there are transactions to put in the file.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Send Test**.

   Then WalletFeed writes `WalletFeed Test.csv` to the folder. This file has a sample transaction. If the folder has `WalletFeed Test.csv`, WalletFeed can write to the folder.

4. To write all your transactions to the file, tap **Send History**.
5. Tap **All**.

### If new transactions are not in Numbers

WalletFeed did not update the file, or Numbers does not show the changes that WalletFeed made after you opened the file.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Sync** section, tap **Sync Now**.
4. In Numbers, open `WalletFeed Transactions.csv` again.

### If text in a cell starts with an apostrophe

WalletFeed puts an apostrophe (`'`) before text that starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@`. Because the apostrophe is before the text, spreadsheet apps do not use the text as a formula.

### If you cannot tap **Export**

WalletFeed disables **Export** while it reads the transactions, or when the period has no transactions.

1. Look at **Transactions**.
2. If **Transactions** shows 0, select a different period in **Range**.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ofx/ -->
# Save Apple Card transactions as OFX files

WalletFeed saves your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone in one OFX file for each month. WalletFeed updates the files automatically in a folder that you select. Then you import the files into your app, for example Quicken for Mac or Actual.

## Before you start

You must have:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- WalletFeed, with [access to your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account](/docs/wallet-accounts/)
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/) (a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase)
- An app that can import OFX files, for example Quicken for Mac, Actual, GnuCash, Moneydance, Banktivity, Goodbudget or YNAB.

If your app is on a computer, you must have a folder that your iPhone and the computer can open, for example in iCloud Drive.

WalletFeed is available only in the US.

> **Note:** Quicken for Windows cannot import the OFX files from WalletFeed. WalletFeed does not write QFX files. Quicken for Windows can import a CSV file from WalletFeed. The [Quicken guide](/guides/apple-card-to-quicken/) has more information.

## Step 1: Add an OFX file in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ofx/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the **Destinations** search field, type `OFX`.

   ![The Add Destination screen with the Destinations search field above the Budgeting list.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ofx/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

5. Tap **OFX File**.

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, the **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens. After you get WalletFeed Pro, the **Files** screen opens.

6. Make sure that **Format** is **OFX**.

   ![The Files screen with OFX in Format, no folder in Folder and WalletFeed in Name.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ofx/walletfeed-setup-ofx-file.webp)

7. Tap **Folder**.
8. Select a folder in iCloud Drive.

   **Folder** then shows the name of the folder.

9. To use a different name for the files, type the name in **Name**.

   Each file name contains this name, the month and `.ofx`. For example, the file for October 2026 is `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`.

10. Tap **Add**.
11. When WalletFeed shows **Save Transactions to Files?**, tap **Save**.

    The message tells you the data that the folder receives from each posted transaction. This data includes the date, the merchant and the amount. The message also tells you the accounts and the period. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the new destination.

WalletFeed then writes one file for each month that has posted transactions.

## Step 2: Import a file into your app

1. On the computer or iPhone that has your app, open the folder that you selected in Step 1.
2. Find the file for the month, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`.
3. In your app, import the file into the account for your Apple Card.

   In Quicken for Mac, **Bank or Brokerage File (OFX, QFX)** is in **File** › **Import**. In Actual, **Import** is on the page of the account. Actual does not show **Import** on a phone.

4. Make sure that the transactions are in the correct account.

   ![The Apple Card account in Actual with five transactions from an OFX file.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ofx/actual-budget-walletfeed-result.webp)

> **Note:** If a file has Apple Card transactions, Actual imports only the Apple Card transactions from it. If you have one destination for each account, Actual can import the transactions of each account. The steps are in [If Apple Cash or Savings transactions are not in the correct account](#if-apple-cash-or-savings-transactions-are-not-in-the-correct-account).

The ID of each Wallet account is the same in each file. Thus, your app can put the transactions from each file into the same account.

You can import the file for a month again after WalletFeed updates it. Actual, GnuCash and Moneydance use the transaction ID to find each transaction that you imported. These apps do not import a transaction two times.

## Data in the file

Each file has one statement for each Wallet account that has posted transactions in the month of the file. A statement shows Apple Card as a credit card, Apple Cash as a checking account and Savings as a savings account. A statement also has the currency code, for example USD, and an ID for the Wallet account.

Each transaction in a statement has this data:

| Data in the file | From Wallet |
| --- | --- |
| Type | The type of the transaction, for example a purchase, a fee, a payment or a transfer. |
| Posted date | The date when the transaction posted. |
| Transaction date | The date of the transaction in Wallet. |
| Amount | The value of the transaction, for example -23.40. Purchases have a minus sign. Payments and refunds have no minus sign. |
| Transaction ID | The ID of the transaction in Wallet. Apps use it to find each transaction that they imported. |
| Name | The merchant name, or the description if Wallet has no merchant name. The file keeps the first 32 characters. |
| Memo | The description and the card statement text, if they are different from the name. A value in a different currency is also in the memo. |

Each date is the calendar day on your iPhone. The files do not include the account balance.

## Changes to the files

While WalletFeed is open, the files receive changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then updates the files.

If **Background Sync** is off, or if WalletFeed cannot open the folder at that time, the files change at these times:

- When you open WalletFeed
- When an [automation](/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/#send-transactions-with-an-automation) starts
- While your iPhone is on a charger.

The files contain only posted transactions. After a pending charge posts, WalletFeed writes it to the file. The posted charge has the same transaction ID as the pending charge. WalletFeed does not write declined charges to the files. A refund has no minus sign.

When a transaction in a month changes, WalletFeed writes all the transactions of that month to the file again. For a month without posted transactions, WalletFeed writes no file. If Wallet removes a transaction, WalletFeed removes it from the file. But if you imported the transaction, it stays in your app.

## Send previous transactions

A new OFX destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. With [Send History](/docs/send-history/), WalletFeed writes the files again for a period that you select.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap **WalletFeed**, or the name that you typed in **Name**.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

WalletFeed then writes the file for each month in that period. If your app uses the transaction ID, it does not import a transaction two times.

## Change or remove the destination

The destination has the name **WalletFeed**, or the name that you typed in **Name**. If you change **Name** on the screen of the destination, the names of the files do not change.

### Send only some transactions

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Set the **Filter** switch to on.
3. Set **Include**, **Minimum**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**.

### Put the files in a different folder

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Change Folder**.
3. Select the new folder.

   After you select the folder, WalletFeed writes all the files in the new folder.

### Stop the updates to the files

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Set the **Enabled** switch to off.

### Remove the destination

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. Tap **Delete** again.

   The files stay in the folder.

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows “Couldn't open this folder.”

WalletFeed cannot open the folder that you selected.

1. Tap **Folder**, or **Change Folder** on the screen of the destination.
2. Select a different folder in iCloud Drive.

### If WalletFeed shows “Can't open the folder. Choose it again.”

WalletFeed cannot open the folder that the destination uses.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Change Folder**.
4. Select the folder again.

### If the folder has no OFX file

WalletFeed writes a file only for a month that has posted transactions.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Send Test**.

   The folder then gets `WalletFeed Test.ofx` with a sample transaction. If this file is in the folder, WalletFeed can write files in the folder.

4. Do not import `WalletFeed Test.ofx` into your app.
5. To write all your transactions to the files, tap **Send History**.
6. Tap **All**.

### If a pending charge is not in the file

The files contain only posted transactions.

1. After the charge posts in Wallet, import the file for that month again.

### If Quicken for Windows does not import the file

Quicken for Windows cannot import the OFX files from WalletFeed. It can import a CSV file only in Quicken's CSV format.

1. In WalletFeed, add a **CSV File** destination.
2. Change a copy of the CSV file to Quicken's CSV format (refer to the [Quicken guide](/guides/apple-card-to-quicken/)).
3. Import the copy into Quicken for Windows.

### If a transaction has a different date in your app

Each transaction in the file has a posted date and a transaction date. Some apps, for example Actual, show the posted date. The posted date can be one or more days after the date in Wallet.

### If a transaction that Wallet removed stays in your app

WalletFeed removes the transaction from the file. But if you imported the transaction, your app keeps it.

1. In your app, find the transaction.
2. Delete the transaction.
3. If you import the file for that month again in Actual, clear **Reimport deleted transactions**.

   If you do not clear **Reimport deleted transactions**, Actual shows the deleted transaction again as a new transaction.

### If Apple Cash or Savings transactions are not in the correct account

One file contains the transactions of all the Wallet accounts that WalletFeed reads. Some apps, for example YNAB, put all the transactions from one file into one account. If a file has Apple Card transactions, Actual imports only the Apple Card transactions from it.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Set the **Filter** switch to on.
4. Tap **Accounts**.
5. Select one account.
6. Tap the back button at the top of the screen.
7. Tap **Send History**.
8. Tap **All**.
9. For each of your other accounts, do [Step 1](#step-1-add-an-ofx-file-in-walletfeed) again with a different name in **Name**.
10. For each new destination, do steps 1 thru 8 again with a different account in step 5.

    Each destination then writes the files for one account only.

11. In your app, import the files of each destination into a different account.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to PocketSmith

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to PocketSmith. You make a developer key in PocketSmith, then you paste the key in WalletFeed.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed on your iPhone, with access to your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account.
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/) (a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase). You must have WalletFeed Pro to send transactions to PocketSmith.
- A PocketSmith account and its password. You can use the Free plan of PocketSmith. The Free plan lets you have 2 accounts in PocketSmith.

## Your key stays on your iPhone

- WalletFeed keeps the developer key in the Keychain on your iPhone. iOS encrypts the Keychain.
- The developer key does not go to iCloud Keychain or to your other devices.
- WalletFeed has no account and no servers. No person at WalletFeed can see or get the developer key.
- Your iPhone sends the developer key only to PocketSmith, in each request to PocketSmith.
- When you delete the destination, WalletFeed deletes the developer key from your iPhone. You can also delete the key in PocketSmith.

## Step 1: Open the PocketSmith form in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations, and the + icon at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the search field, type `PocketSmith`.
5. Tap **PocketSmith**.

   ![The search field with the text PocketSmith, and the PocketSmith row below the field.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/walletfeed-add-destination-search.webp)

6. If WalletFeed shows **WalletFeed Pro**, get [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).

   Result: After you get WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows the PocketSmith form.

## Step 2: Make a developer key in PocketSmith

PocketSmith shows a warning on its developer keys page. The warning tells you that a developer key gives access to all of your PocketSmith data until you delete the key. PocketSmith also tells you not to paste a key into "a third-party website or hosted service". If you are not a software developer, PocketSmith does not recommend developer keys.

For information about the key in WalletFeed, refer to [Your key stays on your iPhone](#your-key-stays-on-your-iphone).

- With the key, WalletFeed gets the list of your PocketSmith accounts and can make an Apple Card account. WalletFeed also adds, changes and deletes the transactions that it sends.
- You can delete the key in PocketSmith (refer to [Delete the key in PocketSmith](#delete-the-key-in-pocketsmith)). After you delete the key, WalletFeed cannot connect to PocketSmith with it.

To make the key on your iPhone, do these steps:

1. In the PocketSmith form, tap **Manage Developer Keys**.

   ![The PocketSmith form in WalletFeed, with the Developer Key field and the Manage Developer Keys link.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/walletfeed-setup-pocketsmith.webp)

   Result: Your web browser opens PocketSmith.

2. If PocketSmith shows **Sign in to PocketSmith**, get access to your PocketSmith account with your e-mail address and your password.
3. In **Confirm your password**, type your PocketSmith password.

   Each time that you open **Manage developer keys**, PocketSmith shows this box.

   ![PocketSmith on an iPhone, with a message about the password above the Confirm your password box.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/pocketsmith-alt-iphone-confirm-password.webp)

4. Tap **CONFIRM PASSWORD**.

   Result: PocketSmith shows **Manage developer keys** and the warning. If the password is incorrect, PocketSmith shows "Sorry, your password was incorrect. Try again."

5. In **Create a new key**, type `WalletFeed` in **Name**.

   The name helps you find the WalletFeed key in the list of keys.

   ![The form for a new key in PocketSmith, with the name WalletFeed and the CREATE KEY button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/pocketsmith-create-key.webp)

6. Tap **CREATE KEY**.

   Result: PocketSmith shows the key in a box below a green message. PocketSmith shows the key only one time.

7. If the screen does not show the key, scroll to the green message above the **Create a new key** form.

   On an iPhone, the page can stay at the **Create a new key** form after you tap **CREATE KEY**.

   ![PocketSmith on an iPhone, with the new developer key in a box below the green message.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/pocketsmith-alt-iphone-key-created.webp)

8. Touch and hold the key.
9. Make sure that the highlighted text includes all of the key.

   The key has 128 letters and numbers. PocketSmith has no button to copy the key.

10. If the highlighted text does not include all of the key, drag the ends of the highlighted text.
11. Tap **Copy**.

> **Note:** You can also open **Manage developer keys** from the account menu in PocketSmith. The person icon at the top right opens this menu. The icon has no label. In the menu, the path is **Security & integrations** › **Manage developer keys**.

## Step 3: Paste the key in WalletFeed

1. Open WalletFeed again.
2. If WalletFeed does not show the PocketSmith form, do [Step 1](#step-1-open-the-pocketsmith-form-in-walletfeed) again.
3. Touch and hold **Developer Key**.
4. Tap **Paste**.

   Result: WalletFeed connects to PocketSmith with the key. Then WalletFeed shows **Account**.

5. In **Account**, select the account that receives your transactions.

   If PocketSmith has an account with the name Apple Card, WalletFeed selects that account. If PocketSmith has no account with that name, WalletFeed selects **New Apple Card Account**. With **New Apple Card Account**, WalletFeed makes a credit card account with the name Apple Card in PocketSmith.

   On the Free plan, PocketSmith does not let WalletFeed make a third account. If you have 2 accounts, select one of them.

6. Tap **Add**.

   Result: WalletFeed shows **Send Transactions to PocketSmith?** The message tells you the data that PocketSmith receives, the Wallet accounts and the start date. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed does not add the destination.

7. Tap **Send**.

   Result: WalletFeed starts to send your transactions to PocketSmith. In **Destinations**, the name of the new destination starts with "PocketSmith ·", for example "PocketSmith · Apple Card".

## Step 4: Find the transactions in PocketSmith

1. On a computer, open [PocketSmith](https://my.pocketsmith.com) in a web browser.
2. If PocketSmith shows "What's your main motivation for wanting to manage your money?", click **Skip**.
3. Click **Transactions** at the top of the page.
4. Click the panel icon to the left of the **Transactions** title.

   Result: PocketSmith shows **Accounts**.

5. In **Accounts**, click **Apple Card** or the account that you selected in WalletFeed.

   Result: The title changes to **Transactions** › **Apple Card**. Below each merchant, PocketSmith shows `wf:` and an ID.

   ![The Apple Card account in PocketSmith, with seven transactions from WalletFeed.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/pocketsmith-walletfeed-result.webp)

6. Click a transaction.
7. Click **Memo**.

   Result: PocketSmith shows the card statement text.

   ![The fields of a transaction in PocketSmith, with the wf: note and the card statement text in Memo.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/pocketsmith-result-transaction-note.webp)

## Data that PocketSmith receives

WalletFeed adds each transaction to the PocketSmith account that you selected. This account also receives the transactions from your other Wallet accounts, for example Apple Cash. To select the Wallet accounts, refer to [Send only some transactions](#send-only-some-transactions).

| From Wallet | In PocketSmith |
| --- | --- |
| The merchant name, or the description if there is no merchant name | **MERCHANT** |
| The amount, negative for a purchase and positive for a refund | **AMOUNT** |
| The date of the transaction, in the time zone of your iPhone | **DATE** |
| The card statement text, if it is different from the merchant name | **Memo** |
| `wf:` and the ID of the transaction in Wallet | The note below the merchant |

PocketSmith shows a purchase in parentheses, for example ($84.12). It shows a refund in green, for example $49.00.

PocketSmith receives no category and no balance. You can give each transaction a category in PocketSmith. After WalletFeed sends a transaction, WalletFeed changes only its amount and its date. Your changes to the merchant, the category and the labels stay.

The new Apple Card account starts with a balance of $0.00. PocketSmith calculates the **BALANCE** column from that balance. Thus, the **BALANCE** column can be different from the balance of your card.

> **Caution:** Do not change or delete the `wf:` note. WalletFeed uses the note to find the transaction again. If the note changes, WalletFeed adds the transaction again when the transaction changes in Wallet.

## New and changed transactions

While WalletFeed is open, PocketSmith receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then sends the change.

PocketSmith also receives pending charges. When a pending charge becomes posted, WalletFeed changes the amount and the date of the same transaction in PocketSmith. PocketSmith does not show a pending status for transactions from WalletFeed. To send only posted charges, you can set **Filter** to on and **Include Pending** to off (refer to [Send only some transactions](#send-only-some-transactions)).

WalletFeed deletes a declined charge from PocketSmith. WalletFeed also deletes a transaction that Wallet removes. PocketSmith receives a refund as a different transaction with a positive amount.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. If you change **Initial History** before you add PocketSmith, the new destination receives transactions from the new start date.

To send previous transactions after you add PocketSmith, do these steps:

1. In **Destinations**, tap the PocketSmith destination.
2. Tap **Send History**.
3. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

   Result: WalletFeed shows **Sending History** and the number of transactions that it sent.

4. To stop WalletFeed before it sends all of the transactions, tap **Send History** › **Stop Sending**.

WalletFeed sends a small number of previous transactions to PocketSmith, waits, and then sends more transactions. If you have many transactions, WalletFeed can be slow to send all of them.

**Send History** does not add a transaction two times. WalletFeed finds each transaction by its `wf:` note. If the amount or the date is different, WalletFeed changes the transaction that it finds. If you deleted a transaction in PocketSmith, **Send History** adds the transaction again.

For more information, refer to [Send previous transactions](/docs/send-history/).

## Change or remove the destination

You change the PocketSmith destination on its screen in **Destinations**. For more information about this screen, refer to [Destinations](/docs/destinations/).

### Send only some transactions

1. In **Destinations**, tap the PocketSmith destination.
2. Set **Filter** to on.
3. Change **Include**, **Minimum**, **Include Pending**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**.

   In **Accounts**, you select the Wallet accounts for PocketSmith. With Apple Intelligence, you can also type a rule in words, for example "Travel over $50, not Uber", and tap the Apple Intelligence icon.

For more information, refer to [Filter the transactions for a destination](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

### Stop the destination for a time

1. In **Destinations**, tap the PocketSmith destination.
2. Set **Enabled** to off.

   Until you set **Enabled** to on again, WalletFeed does not send transactions to PocketSmith.

### Replace the key

If you deleted the key in PocketSmith, or if PocketSmith does not accept the key, do these steps:

1. Make a new key in PocketSmith (refer to [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-developer-key-in-pocketsmith)).
2. Open WalletFeed again.
3. In **Destinations**, tap the PocketSmith destination.
4. Tap **Replace Key**.
5. Touch and hold **Developer Key**.
6. Tap **Paste**.
7. Tap **Replace**.

   Result: Before WalletFeed puts the new key in the Keychain, WalletFeed connects to PocketSmith with the key. Then **Replace Key** shows a green checkmark.

### Remove PocketSmith from WalletFeed

1. In **Destinations**, tap the PocketSmith destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. Tap **Delete** again.

   Result: WalletFeed removes the destination and deletes the key from your iPhone. The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay in PocketSmith. Until you delete the key in PocketSmith, PocketSmith accepts the key.

### Delete the key in PocketSmith

1. On a computer, open [Manage developer keys in PocketSmith](https://my.pocketsmith.com/security/manage_keys).
2. If PocketSmith shows **Sign in to PocketSmith**, get access to your PocketSmith account with your e-mail address and your password.
3. In **Confirm your password**, type your PocketSmith password.
4. Click **CONFIRM PASSWORD**.
5. In the row for WalletFeed, click **Revoke**.

   Result: PocketSmith does not show a message before it deletes the key. After PocketSmith deletes the key, it shows "Successfully deleted your WalletFeed key."

   ![The list of developer keys in PocketSmith, with the Revoke link for the WalletFeed key.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/pocketsmith-revoke-key.webp)

After you delete the key, the PocketSmith destination in WalletFeed shows "Authentication failed" when WalletFeed tries to send transactions. To send transactions again, you must make a new key and [replace the key](#replace-the-key) in WalletFeed.

## If there is a problem

To make sure that WalletFeed can send transactions to PocketSmith, do these steps:

1. In **Destinations**, tap the PocketSmith destination.
2. Tap **Send Test**.

   Result: If PocketSmith receives the test transaction, WalletFeed shows a green checkmark.

> **Note:** **Send Test** adds a test transaction of $4.20 to the PocketSmith account. The merchant of the test transaction is WalletFeed. If you tap **Send Test** again, WalletFeed does not add a second test transaction. You can delete the test transaction in PocketSmith.

### If WalletFeed shows "Key rejected (HTTP 401)"

PocketSmith does not accept the key, for example because you copied only a part of the key. WalletFeed then shows "Key rejected (HTTP 401). Create a new one in PocketSmith."

1. Make a new key in PocketSmith (refer to [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-developer-key-in-pocketsmith)).

   Before you tap **Copy**, make sure that the highlighted text includes all of the key.

2. Open WalletFeed again.
3. Touch and hold **Developer Key**.
4. Tap **Paste**.

### If WalletFeed shows "Key rejected (HTTP 403)" after you tap Add

On the Free plan, PocketSmith lets you have 2 accounts. If you have 2 accounts, WalletFeed cannot make the Apple Card account. WalletFeed then shows "Key rejected (HTTP 403). Create a new one in PocketSmith." The key is correct, and a new key does not help.

1. In **Account**, select one of your PocketSmith accounts.
2. Tap **Add**.

### If the destination shows "Authentication failed"

PocketSmith does not accept the key of the destination, for example because a person deleted the key in PocketSmith.

1. Make a new key in PocketSmith (refer to [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-developer-key-in-pocketsmith)).
2. Replace the key in WalletFeed (refer to [Replace the key](#replace-the-key)).

### If you did not copy the key

PocketSmith shows a key only one time.

1. In PocketSmith, open **Manage developer keys** again (refer to [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-developer-key-in-pocketsmith)).
2. In the row for WalletFeed, tap **Revoke**.
3. Make a new key (refer to [Step 2](#step-2-make-a-developer-key-in-pocketsmith)).

### If PocketSmith shows only the Welcome page

In a new PocketSmith account, PocketSmith shows the Welcome page until you complete a start path on that page.

1. On the Welcome page, click a start path, for example **Take guided mode**.
2. Complete all the steps of that path.

You can make the developer key before you complete a start path. Guided mode also makes an account with the name Main account. WalletFeed shows this account in **Account**.

### If PocketSmith shows a transaction two times

WalletFeed did not find the first transaction, because its `wf:` note changed.

1. In PocketSmith, find the transaction that has no `wf:` note.
2. Delete that transaction in PocketSmith.

### If PocketSmith receives transactions only while WalletFeed is open

When **Background Sync** is off, WalletFeed sends transactions only while it is open.

1. Tap the gear icon at the top of **Destinations**.
2. In **Settings** › **Sync**, set **Background Sync** to on.

For more information, refer to [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/).

### If the destination shows "Rejected (HTTP 404)"

A person deleted the PocketSmith account that the destination uses. If you tap **Replace Key**, WalletFeed shows "The account is gone from PocketSmith. Add this destination again."

1. Remove the destination (refer to [Remove PocketSmith from WalletFeed](#remove-pocketsmith-from-walletfeed)).
2. Add PocketSmith again (refer to [Step 1](#step-1-open-the-pocketsmith-form-in-walletfeed)).

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-qif/ -->
# Save Apple Card transactions as QIF files

WalletFeed writes your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to QIF files in a folder that you select. There is one file for each month. You import each file into an app, for example GnuCash or Banktivity.

## Before you start

You must have:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- WalletFeed, with [access to your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account](/docs/wallet-accounts/)
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/) (a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase)
- A folder in iCloud Drive, in **On My iPhone** or in a different app that the Files app shows, for example Dropbox
- An app that can import QIF files, for example GnuCash, Moneydance, Banktivity, Actual or YNAB.

WalletFeed is available only in the US.

If your app is on a computer, the computer must have access to the folder.

> **Note:** Quicken for Windows cannot import a QIF file into a credit card, checking or savings account. The [Quicken guide](/guides/apple-card-to-quicken/) tells you the files that Quicken can import.

## Step 1: Add a QIF file in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-qif/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the **Destinations** search field, type `QIF`.

   ![The Add Destination screen with the Destinations search field above the Budgeting list.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-qif/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

5. Tap **QIF File**.

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, the **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens. After you get WalletFeed Pro, the **Files** screen opens.

6. If **Format** does not show **QIF**, select **QIF** in **Format**.

   ![The Files screen with QIF in Format, no folder in Folder and WalletFeed in Name.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-qif/walletfeed-setup-qif-file.webp)

7. Tap **Folder**.
8. Select a folder, for example a folder in iCloud Drive.

   **Folder** then shows the name of the folder.

9. To use a different name for the files, type the name in **Name**.

   The name of each file contains this name, the month and `.qif`, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.qif`.

10. Tap **Add**.
11. When WalletFeed shows **Save Transactions to Files?**, tap **Save**.

    If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the new destination.

WalletFeed then writes a QIF file for each month that has posted transactions. WalletFeed keeps no copy of the files.

> **Note:** The **Save Transactions to Files?** message tells you the data that the folder receives, the accounts and the period. It also tells you that the folder receives only posted transactions.

## Step 2: Import a QIF file into your app

A QIF file has no ID for each transaction. Thus, some apps can import a transaction two times. Actual compares the amount and the date of each transaction in the file with the transactions in the account. As a result, Actual does not import a transaction two times. But Actual can make one transaction from two different charges with the same amount.

1. Wait until the end of the month.

   Each charge is in the file for the month of its date, but only after the charge posts. As a result, the file can change after the end of the month.

2. Open your app on the computer or iPhone that has access to the folder.
3. In your app, import the file for the month, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.qif`.
4. If your app lets you select a date format, select month, day, year (`MM/DD/YYYY`).
5. If your app lets you select an account, select the account for the transactions in the file.
6. Do not import the file for that month again.

   If you import the file for a month two times, your app can show each transaction two times.

> **Note:** Actual shows its **Import** button only on a computer. Actual can import a QIF file only if the file has one Wallet account. [Get one file for each account](#get-one-file-for-each-account) tells you how to make these files.

## Data in the QIF files

Each file contains the posted transactions of one month from the Wallet accounts for the destination. Each transaction has these fields:

| Field | Data |
| --- | --- |
| Date (`D`) | The date of the transaction in the sequence month, day, year (`MM/DD/YYYY`), for example `10/28/2026`. |
| Amount (`T`) | The amount of the transaction. Purchases have a minus sign, for example `-23.40`. Payments and refunds have no minus sign. |
| Cleared (`C`) | Each transaction has `*`, because the file contains only posted transactions. |
| Payee (`P`) | The merchant name. If Wallet has no merchant name, the payee is the description. |
| Memo (`M`) | The description and the card statement text, if they are different from the payee. |
| Category (`L`) | The WalletFeed category, for example **Groceries** or **Dining**. A transaction in **Other** has no category. |

For a transaction in a different currency, the memo also contains the amount in that currency and the currency code. The file has no fields for the currency, the posted date, the merchant category code or a transaction ID.

A file with one Wallet account has one section. A file with more than one Wallet account has one section for each account. Each section starts with the name of the account.

In the file, your Apple Card is a credit card account (`CCard`). Your Apple Cash and Savings accounts are bank accounts (`Bank`).

## Changes to the files

While WalletFeed is open, the files receive changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then updates the files.

If WalletFeed cannot open the folder at that time, the files change when one of these occurs:

- You open WalletFeed.
- An [automation](/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/#send-transactions-with-an-automation) starts.
- iOS starts WalletFeed while your iPhone is on a charger.

A pending charge is not in the file. When the charge posts, WalletFeed adds it to the file for the month of its date. WalletFeed does not put declined charges in the file. A refund is a different transaction. The amount of the refund has no minus sign.

When a transaction in a month changes, WalletFeed writes the file for that month again. Changes that you make to a file stay only until WalletFeed writes the file again. If Wallet removes a transaction from this month or from the month before this month, WalletFeed removes the transaction from the file. If your app has that transaction, the transaction stays in your app until you delete it.

## Send previous transactions

A new QIF destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

To write the files again for a period that you select, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap **WalletFeed**, or the name that you typed in **Name**.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

WalletFeed then writes the files of those months again. The start of the period also becomes the start date of the destination. Thus, the file for the first month of the period can contain only a part of that month.

> **Note:** If you import the file for a month again after **Send History**, your app can show each transaction of that month two times.

## Change or remove the destination

In WalletFeed, the destination has the name **WalletFeed**, or the name that you typed in **Name**. A change to **Name** on the screen of the destination does not change the names of the files.

### Send only some transactions

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Set **Filter** to on.
3. Set **Include**, **Minimum**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**.

WalletFeed uses the new [filter](/docs/choose-what-to-send/) for the files that it writes after the change. QIF files contain only posted transactions. **Include Pending** does not change this.

### Get one file for each account

A file contains the transactions of all the Wallet accounts for its destination. To get a different file for each account, use one destination for each account:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap **WalletFeed**, or the name that you typed in **Name**.
3. Set **Filter** to on.
4. Tap **Accounts**.
5. Tap the account for this destination.
6. On your iPhone, open the Files app.
7. In the folder, delete the QIF files of this destination, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.qif`.
8. In WalletFeed, on the screen of the destination, tap **Send History**.
9. Tap **All**.
10. For each account that you did not select in step 5, do [Step 1](#step-1-add-a-qif-file-in-walletfeed) again with a different name in **Name**.
11. For each new destination, do steps 1 to 9 of this list again.

### Put the files in a different folder

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Change Folder**.
3. Select the new folder.

   Then WalletFeed writes all the files again in the new folder.

### Stop the changes to the files

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Set **Enabled** to off.

### Remove the destination

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. Tap **Delete** again.

   The files stay in the folder.

## If there is a problem

### If your app shows each transaction two times

A QIF file has no transaction ID. Thus, your app cannot find the transactions that it imported the first time.

1. In your app, delete the transactions that you imported the second time.
2. Do not import the file for a month two times.

An OFX file has an ID for each transaction. GnuCash, Moneydance and Actual use this ID and do not import a transaction two times. If your app can import OFX files, you can use an [OFX file](/guides/apple-card-to-ofx/).

### If Actual shows "Failed parsing: doesn't look like a valid QIF file."

Actual cannot import a QIF file that has more than one Wallet account.

1. Do the steps in [Get one file for each account](#get-one-file-for-each-account).
2. In Actual, import each file into a different account.

### If your app puts the transactions of all accounts into one account

Some apps, for example YNAB, put all the transactions of a file into one account.

1. Do the steps in [Get one file for each account](#get-one-file-for-each-account).
2. In your app, import each file into a different account.

### If a charge is not in the file

A QIF file includes a charge only after the charge posts.

1. Wait until the charge posts in Wallet.
2. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. Tap **Sync Now**.
4. If the destination has a filter, make sure that the filter includes the charge (refer to [Send only some transactions](#send-only-some-transactions)).

### If the folder has no QIF file

WalletFeed writes a file only for a month that has posted transactions.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Send Test**.

   The folder then gets `WalletFeed Test.qif` with a test transaction. If this file is in the folder, WalletFeed can write to the folder.

4. Do not import `WalletFeed Test.qif` into your app.
5. To write all your transactions to the files, tap **Send History**.
6. Tap **All**.

### If the dates in your app are incorrect

The file uses US dates in the sequence month, day, year (`MM/DD/YYYY`).

1. In your app, delete the transactions with the incorrect dates.
2. Import the file again.
3. If your app lets you select a date format, select month, day, year.

### If WalletFeed shows "Couldn't open this folder."

WalletFeed cannot open the folder that you selected.

1. Tap **Folder**, or **Change Folder** on the screen of the destination.
2. Select a different folder.

### If the destination shows "Can't open the folder. Choose it again."

WalletFeed does not have access to the folder of the destination at this time.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Change Folder**.
4. Select the folder of the destination again.

### If you cannot tap Add

You can tap **Add** only after you select a folder.

1. Tap **Folder**.
2. Select a folder.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-quicken/ -->
# Import Apple Card transactions into Quicken

You can import your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions into Quicken for Mac from OFX files that WalletFeed saves in iCloud Drive. Quicken for Windows cannot import these OFX files, but it can import a copy of a WalletFeed CSV file that you change to Quicken's format.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- WalletFeed, with [access to your Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/)
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase
- Quicken for Mac, or Quicken for Windows with a spreadsheet app
- iCloud Drive on your iPhone and on your computer.

WalletFeed is available only in the US.

## Step 1: Add an OFX file in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-quicken/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the search field at the top, type `Quicken`.

   ![The Add Destination screen with the Destinations search field above the Budgeting list.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-quicken/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

5. Tap **OFX File**.

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, the **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens first. After you start the free trial or get a plan, the **Files** screen opens.

6. Make sure that **Format** shows **OFX**.

   ![The Files screen with OFX in Format, Choose… in Folder and WalletFeed in Name.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-quicken/walletfeed-setup-ofx-file.webp)

   If **Format** shows **OFX**, WalletFeed writes one file for each month.

7. Tap **Folder**.
8. Select a folder in iCloud Drive.

   The **Folder** row then shows the name of the folder.

9. To use a different name for the files, type the name in **Name**.

   If you do not change the name, the file for October 2026 is `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`.

10. Tap **Add**.
11. When WalletFeed shows **Save Transactions to Files?**, tap **Save**.

    The message gives the name of the folder, the data that the folder receives and the Wallet accounts. If there is a start date for the transactions, the message also gives that date. Because an OFX file has only posted transactions, the message uses the words “posted transactions”. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the new destination.

WalletFeed then writes a file for each month that has posted transactions. In **Destinations**, the new destination has the name **WalletFeed** or the name that you typed.

## Step 2: Import a file into Quicken for Mac

Quicken for Mac uses the same menu item for a WalletFeed OFX file and for a file from the website of a bank.

1. On your Mac, open Quicken.
2. Make a backup of your Quicken data file.
3. Click **File** › **Import** › **Bank or Brokerage File (OFX, QFX)**.
4. Click **Browse**.
5. In the iCloud Drive folder that you selected in WalletFeed, select the file for one month, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`.
6. Click **Open**.
7. On the **Choose Your Accounts** screen, select the Quicken account that receives the transactions, for example your Apple Card account.
8. Make sure that the new transactions are in that account.
9. To import the file for a different month, do steps 3 to 8 again.

For more information about these steps, refer to [Quicken's instructions to download and import transactions](https://info.quicken.com/mac/downloading-transactions).

## Use a CSV file with Quicken for Windows

Quicken for Windows cannot import the OFX files from WalletFeed. It imports QFX files (Web Connect files) that you download from the website of a bank. WalletFeed does not write QFX files.

Quicken for Windows can import a CSV file only in Quicken's CSV format. The columns of a WalletFeed CSV file are in a different sequence. The dates of the file are in a different format. Thus, before you import a file, you must change a copy of it to Quicken's format.

1. On your iPhone, do steps 1 to 5 in [Step 1](#step-1-add-an-ofx-file-in-walletfeed).
2. In **Format** on the **Files** screen, select **CSV**.
3. In **Save As**, select **One File per Month**.
4. Do steps 7 to 11 in Step 1.

   Then WalletFeed writes a CSV file for each month. If you do not change the name, the file for October 2026 is `WalletFeed 2026-10.csv`.

5. On your PC, open the iCloud Drive folder that has the files.
6. Make a copy of the file for one month.
7. Open the copy in a spreadsheet app.
8. In the copy, change the columns and the dates to Quicken's CSV format.

   For the columns and the date format, refer to [Quicken's instructions to import transactions from a CSV file](https://info.quicken.com/win/import-transactions-from-csv-file).

9. Save the copy as a CSV file.
10. In Quicken, click **File** › **File Import** › **Banking Transactions** › **From (.CSV) File**.
11. Click **Choose .CSV File to Import…**.
12. Select the copy of the file.
13. Click **OK**.
14. If Quicken shows **Account does not exist in Quicken**, select the Quicken account that receives the transactions.

> **Note:** Quicken adds all the transactions in a CSV file each time that you import the file. If you import the same transaction two times, Quicken shows the transaction two times.

A WalletFeed CSV file also has pending transactions. For a pending transaction, the **Status** column shows that the transaction is pending. For the columns of the file, refer to the [page about CSV files](/guides/apple-card-to-csv/).

WalletFeed can also write QIF files. But Quicken for Windows cannot import a QIF file into a credit card account, a checking account or a savings account.

## Data that Quicken receives

This table shows the data in the OFX file for each Wallet field.

| Wallet | In the OFX file |
| --- | --- |
| Merchant | The first 32 characters of the name of the payee. If Wallet has no merchant name, WalletFeed uses the description. |
| Amount | The amount of the transaction. Purchases are less than zero. Payments and refunds are more than zero. |
| Currency | The currency of the statement, for example USD. |
| Date | The date of the transaction. |
| Posted date | The date that the transaction posted. |
| Type | The type of transaction, for example a purchase, a payment, a fee or a transfer. |
| Description, card statement text and foreign amount | The memo. WalletFeed does not add text that is the same as the name of the payee. |
| Transaction ID | The ID of the transaction. It stays the same each time that WalletFeed writes the file. |
| Account | A different statement for each of your accounts. The account type is credit card for Apple Card, checking for Apple Cash and savings for Savings. |

The file does not include the WalletFeed category or the balance of the account.

## Changes to the files

While WalletFeed is open, the files receive changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then updates the files.

If WalletFeed cannot open the folder at that time, the files get the changes when one of these occurs:

- You open WalletFeed.
- A Shortcuts automation starts WalletFeed.
- iOS starts WalletFeed while your iPhone is on its charger.

An OFX file has only posted transactions. WalletFeed adds a pending charge to the file after the charge posts. A declined charge does not post, and thus it is not in the file. A refund is a different transaction. Its amount is more than zero.

WalletFeed puts each transaction in the file for the month of the transaction date. When a transaction in a month changes, WalletFeed writes the file for that month again. Thus, a file can change after the end of its month, for example when a charge from the last day of that month posts.

Each transaction keeps the same ID each time that WalletFeed writes the file. But Quicken's instructions tell you not to import transactions for the same dates two times, because Quicken can then show a transaction two times.

If Wallet removes a transaction, WalletFeed removes it from the file. WalletFeed cannot remove the transaction from Quicken.

WalletFeed keeps no copy of the files. The files are in your iCloud Drive. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers.

## Send previous transactions

A new OFX File destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. To change the start date, do these steps before you add the destination:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In **Sync**, tap **Initial History**.

   ![The Settings screen with Initial History set to All in the Sync section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-quicken/walletfeed-settings.webp)

3. Select **Today**, **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

After you add a destination, you can use [Send History](/docs/send-history/) to write previous transactions to its files:

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination, for example **WalletFeed**.
2. Tap **Send History**.
3. Select **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

   Then WalletFeed writes the files for those months again. While WalletFeed writes the files, the destination shows **Sending History** and a progress bar.

4. In Quicken, import the files for the months that you did not import.

To stop before WalletFeed writes all the files, tap **Send History** › **Stop Sending**.

## Change or remove the destination

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination, for example **WalletFeed**.
3. Make one of the changes in this table.

| Change | On the destination screen |
| --- | --- |
| Send only some transactions | Set **Filter** to on. Then set **Include**, **Minimum**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**. |
| Send only the transactions from one Wallet account, for example Apple Card | Set **Filter** to on. Tap **Accounts**. Then select the account. |
| Use a different folder | Tap **Change Folder**. Then select the folder. From the start date of the destination, WalletFeed writes the files again in the new folder. |
| Stop the changes to the files for a time | Set **Enabled** to off. |
| Change the name of the destination | Type a different name in **Name**. The names of the files stay the same. |
| Remove the destination | Tap **Delete**. Then tap **Delete** again. |

When you remove the destination, the files stay in the folder. Quicken keeps the transactions that you imported.

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows “Couldn't open this folder.”

WalletFeed cannot get access to the folder that you selected on the **Files** screen.

1. Tap **Folder**.
2. Select a different folder in iCloud Drive.

### If the destination shows “Can't open the folder. Choose it again.”

WalletFeed does not have access to the folder of the destination at this time.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Change Folder**.
3. Select the folder again.

### If the folder has no file for a month

WalletFeed writes a file for a month only when the month has posted transactions.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Send Test**.

   The folder then gets `WalletFeed Test.ofx`. This file has a test purchase of $4.20. If this file is in the folder, WalletFeed can write files to the folder.

3. Do not import `WalletFeed Test.ofx` into Quicken.

### If the file does not have new transactions

WalletFeed did not write the file after the last change in Wallet.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
