2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In **Sync**, tap **Sync Now**.

### If a pending charge is not in Quicken

An OFX file has only posted transactions. WalletFeed adds the charge to the file after the charge posts.

1. Wait until the charge posts in Wallet.
2. Import the file for that month again (refer to [Step 2](#step-2-import-a-file-into-quicken-for-mac)).
3. If Quicken then shows a transaction two times, delete one of the two transactions.

### If Quicken shows a transaction two times

Quicken imported the same transaction two times, for example when you imported the file for a month two times.

1. In Quicken, delete one of the two transactions.

### If Quicken has a transaction that Wallet removed

WalletFeed removes the transaction from the file, but it cannot remove the transaction from Quicken.

1. In Quicken, delete the transaction.

### If Quicken for Windows does not import the OFX file

Quicken for Windows cannot import the OFX files from WalletFeed.

1. Add a CSV file in WalletFeed (refer to [Use a CSV file with Quicken for Windows](#use-a-csv-file-with-quicken-for-windows)).

### If Quicken for Windows does not import the CSV file

The file is not in Quicken's CSV format. Quicken then shows a message that gives the necessary changes.

1. In the copy of the file, make the changes that the message gives.
2. Import the copy again (refer to [Use a CSV file with Quicken for Windows](#use-a-csv-file-with-quicken-for-windows)).

### If Destinations shows “Sync Requires Pro”

You do not have WalletFeed Pro at this time. WalletFeed keeps the destination but does not write the files.

1. In **Destinations**, tap **Upgrade**.
2. Get a plan, or tap **Restore Purchases**.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Supabase

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a Postgres database in your Supabase project. You copy the project URL and the publishable key to WalletFeed. Then you paste the SQL from WalletFeed in the Supabase **SQL Editor**.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed, with access to your [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/).
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/) (a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase). You must have WalletFeed Pro to send transactions to Supabase.
- A Supabase account, or an e-mail address for a new account. You can use the Free plan of Supabase.
- A web browser on a computer. In this guide, you use the Supabase **SQL Editor** on the computer.

> **Note:** The Supabase [pricing page](https://supabase.com/pricing) tells you that Free plan projects "are paused after 1 week of inactivity". [If Supabase stopped your project](#if-supabase-stopped-your-project) tells you how to start the project again.

## Your key stays on your iPhone

- WalletFeed keeps the publishable key in the Keychain on your iPhone. iOS encrypts the Keychain.
- The publishable key does not go to iCloud Keychain or to your other devices.
- WalletFeed has no account and no servers. No person at WalletFeed can see or get the publishable key.
- Your iPhone sends the publishable key only to your Supabase project, in each request to your Supabase project.
- When you delete the destination, WalletFeed deletes the publishable key from your iPhone. You can also delete the key in Supabase.

## Step 1: Make a Supabase project

A Supabase project has its own Postgres database. If you have a project for your transactions, go to [Step 2](#step-2-open-the-supabase-form-in-walletfeed).

1. On your computer, open the [Supabase sign-up page](https://supabase.com/dashboard/sign-up) in a web browser.
2. Type your e-mail address in **Email**.
3. Type a password in **Password**.
4. Click **Sign up**.

   ![The Supabase sign-up page, with the highlighted Sign up button below the Email and Password fields.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/supabase-sign-up.webp)

5. If Supabase shows an hCaptcha image check, obey the instructions in the check.
6. If Supabase sends you an e-mail, open the hyperlink in the e-mail.
7. If Supabase shows "Sign in to your account", get access to your Supabase account with your e-mail address and your password.

   ![The Supabase sign-in page, with the highlighted Sign in button below the Email and Password fields.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/supabase-sign-in.webp)

8. On the "Your organizations" page, click **New organization**.

   A new Supabase account has no organization. An organization contains your projects.

   ![The Supabase organizations page with no organizations, and the highlighted New organization button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/supabase-organizations.webp)

9. In **Name**, replace the text with a name for the organization, for example `WalletFeed`.
10. In **Type**, select a type, for example **Personal**.
11. In **Plan**, select a plan, for example **Free - $0/month**.
12. Click **Create organization**.

    ![The "Create a new organization" form, with the name WalletFeed Docs, the Personal type, the Free plan and the highlighted Create organization button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/supabase-new-organization.webp)

    Result: Supabase shows "Create a new project".

13. In **Project name**, replace the text with a name for the project, for example `WalletFeed`.
14. Click **Generate a password**.

    Supabase puts a password in **Database password**. WalletFeed does not use the database password.

15. In **Region**, select a region, for example **West US (Oregon)**.
16. In **Security**, make sure that **Enable Data API** has a checkmark.

    WalletFeed sends your transactions to the Data API of the project.

17. Click **Create new project**.

    ![The "Create a new project" form, with a checkmark for Enable Data API and the highlighted Create new project button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/supabase-new-project.webp)

18. Wait until the project page shows **Healthy** below **STATUS**.

> **Note:** On the sign-up page, you can also make the account with **Continue with GitHub**, **Continue with ChatGPT** or **Continue with SSO**.

## Step 2: Open the Supabase form in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations, and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the search field, type `Supabase`.

   ![The Add Destination screen, with the Destinations search field above the list of destinations.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

5. Tap **Supabase**.
6. If WalletFeed shows **WalletFeed Pro**, get [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).

   Result: After you get WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows the Supabase form.

   ![The Supabase form in WalletFeed, with the Publishable Key field, the URL field, Share SQL and the Supabase Dashboard link.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/walletfeed-setup-supabase.webp)

7. Keep the Supabase form open until you tap **Add** in [Step 5](#step-5-add-the-destination-in-walletfeed).

   You can use a different app while the form is open. Each time that you open the Supabase form, WalletFeed makes new SQL with a new token for the table. If you close the form, do Step 2, Step 3 and Step 4 again.

## Step 3: Copy the publishable key and the project URL

Do these steps on your iPhone. To copy the key and the URL on a Mac, refer to [Copy the key and the URL on a Mac](#copy-the-key-and-the-url-on-a-mac).

1. In the Supabase form, tap **Supabase Dashboard**.

   Result: Your web browser opens Supabase.

2. If Supabase shows "Sign in to your account", get access to your Supabase account with your e-mail address and your password.
3. If Supabase does not show "Select a project to continue", tap **Supabase Dashboard** in WalletFeed again.
4. In "Select a project to continue", tap your project.

   ![Supabase on an iPhone, with the page "Select a project to continue" and the highlighted WalletFeed Docs project.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/supabase-iphone-select-project.webp)

5. In "Connect to your project", tap **Server**.

   ![The "Connect to your project" panel on an iPhone, with the highlighted Server button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/supabase-iphone-connect.webp)

6. Scroll to `.env`.
7. Tap the copy button in the `SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=` row.

   The publishable key starts with `sb_publishable_`. Do not copy the `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY=` row. WalletFeed does not accept a secret key.

   ![The .env rows in the Connect panel on an iPhone, with the highlighted copy button for the publishable key.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/supabase-iphone-connect-key.webp)

8. Open WalletFeed again.
9. Touch and hold **Publishable Key**.
10. Tap **Paste**.
11. Open the Supabase page in your web browser again.
12. Tap the copy button in the `SUPABASE_URL=` row.
13. Open WalletFeed again.
14. Touch and hold the field that shows `https://abcd.supabase.co`.
15. Tap **Paste**.

### Copy the key and the URL on a Mac

If your Mac uses the same Apple Account as your iPhone, you can copy on the Mac and paste on the iPhone with [Universal Clipboard](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102430).

1. On your Mac, open your project in the [Supabase dashboard](https://supabase.com/dashboard).
2. Click **Copy**, to the right of the project URL.
3. Click **Publishable key**.

   ![The Copy menu on the project page, with the highlighted Project URL and Publishable key items.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/supabase-copy-menu.webp)

4. On your iPhone, touch and hold **Publishable Key** in the Supabase form.
5. Tap **Paste**.
6. On your Mac, click **Copy** again.
7. Click **Project URL**.
8. On your iPhone, touch and hold the field that shows `https://abcd.supabase.co`.
9. Tap **Paste**.

> **Note:** **Connect** at the top of the project page opens the same panel as on the iPhone. On **Framework**, the key and the URL are in one block of text. On **Server**, each row has a copy button.

## Step 4: Make the table in Supabase

The SQL from WalletFeed makes the `walletfeed_transactions` table in your project. On the **API Keys** page, Supabase shows "Publishable keys can be safely shared publicly". Thus, the SQL also adds a policy to the table. The policy lets WalletFeed read and change the table only with the token of this destination. A person with only the project URL and the publishable key cannot read your transactions.

1. On your iPhone, in the Supabase form, tap **Share SQL**.

   Result: iOS opens a menu with **Copy**.

2. Send the SQL to your computer, for example with AirDrop.

   If your computer is a Mac with Universal Clipboard, you can tap **Copy**.

3. On your computer, open your project in the [Supabase dashboard](https://supabase.com/dashboard).
4. In the bar on the left, click the **SQL Editor** icon.

   The icons in this bar have no names on the page. When you put the pointer on an icon, Supabase shows its name.

   ![The empty SQL Editor, with the highlighted SQL Editor icon in the bar on the left.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/supabase-sql-editor.webp)

5. If Supabase shows "Snippets no longer save automatically", click **Understood**.

   ![The Supabase message "Snippets no longer save automatically", with the Understood button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/supabase-sql-editor-notice.webp)

6. Paste the SQL in the editor.

   The editor shows 28 lines of SQL. Do not change the SQL.

7. Click **Run**.

   ![The SQL Editor with the WalletFeed SQL, and the highlighted Run button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/supabase-sql-run.webp)

   Result: Supabase shows "Potential issue detected". Supabase shows this message because the SQL removes all access to the table first. Then the SQL gives access only to this destination. The SQL does not delete the table or its rows.

8. Click **Run query**.

   ![The Supabase message "Potential issue detected", with the highlighted Run query button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/supabase-destructive-warning.webp)

9. Make sure that the result is "Success. No rows returned".

   ![The SQL Editor with the result "Success. No rows returned", and the highlighted Table Editor icon in the bar on the left.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/supabase-sql-success.webp)

> **Note:** It is not necessary to save the SQL in Supabase. In the destination, **Share SQL** gives you the same SQL again.

## Step 5: Add the destination in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed again.
2. In the Supabase form, tap **Add**.

   Result: WalletFeed tries to read the table with the project URL and the publishable key.

3. If WalletFeed shows a message in red below **Share SQL**, refer to [If there is a problem](#if-there-is-a-problem).
4. In **Send Transactions to Supabase?**, tap **Send**.

   The message tells you the data that Supabase receives and the Wallet accounts. If **Initial History** is not **All**, the message also gives the start date. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed does not add the destination. The Supabase form stays open.

   Result: WalletFeed starts to send your transactions to Supabase. In **Destinations**, the name of the new destination has two parts, for example "Supabase · abcd". The second part is from the project URL.

## Step 6: Find the transactions in Supabase

1. On your computer, open your project in the [Supabase dashboard](https://supabase.com/dashboard).
2. In the bar on the left, click the **Table Editor** icon.
3. Click `walletfeed_transactions`.

   ![The Table Editor, with the highlighted walletfeed_transactions table in the list.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/supabase-table-list.webp)

   Result: The Table Editor shows one row for each transaction. For the columns, refer to [Columns in the Supabase table](#columns-in-the-supabase-table).

## Columns in the Supabase table

Each transaction is one row in the `public.walletfeed_transactions` table.

![The walletfeed_transactions table in the Supabase Table Editor, with six rows from WalletFeed.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/supabase-walletfeed-result.webp)

WalletFeed puts these values in the columns:

| Column | Postgres type | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `text` | The WalletFeed ID of the transaction. This column is the primary key. |
| `date` | `date` | The day of the transaction, in the time zone of your iPhone. |
| `merchant` | `text` | The merchant name, or the description if Wallet has no merchant name. |
| `amount` | `numeric` | The amount of the transaction. A purchase or a fee is less than 0. A payment or a refund is more than 0. |
| `currency` | `text` | The currency code, for example `USD`. |
| `category` | `text` | The WalletFeed category, for example Groceries or Travel. |
| `status` | `text` | The status in Wallet, for example `pending`, `authorized` or `booked`. |
| `pending` | `boolean` | `true` when the status is `pending` or `authorized`, and `false` for a different status. |
| `account` | `text` | The name of the Wallet account, for example Apple Card. |
| `description` | `text` | The description of the transaction in Wallet. |
| `type` | `text` | The transaction type in Wallet, for example `pointOfSale` or `refund`. |
| `mcc` | `integer` | The merchant category code. |
| `foreign_amount` | `numeric` | For a purchase in a different currency, the amount in that currency, with the same sign as `amount`. |
| `foreign_currency` | `text` | The code of that different currency. |

For a purchase in US dollars, `foreign_amount` and `foreign_currency` have no value (`null`). When a transaction changes, WalletFeed updates the row that has the same `id`. If you change a value in a WalletFeed column, WalletFeed replaces your change when the transaction changes again.

> **Caution:** Do not change the `id` of a row. WalletFeed uses the `id` to find the row. If the `id` changes, WalletFeed adds a new row when the transaction changes in Wallet.

Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to your Supabase project. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. After Supabase receives your transactions, the terms of Supabase are applicable to them.

## New and changed transactions

While WalletFeed is open, Supabase receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then sends the change. **Background Sync** is on until you set it to off.

A pending charge has the value `true` in `pending`. When its status changes to `booked`, WalletFeed updates the same row. WalletFeed deletes the row of a declined or expired charge. WalletFeed also deletes the row of a transaction that Wallet removes.

A refund is a new row. Its `amount` is more than 0.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

To send previous transactions after you add Supabase, do these steps:

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Supabase destination.
2. Tap **Send History**.
3. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.
4. To stop WalletFeed before it sends all of the transactions, tap **Send History** › **Stop Sending**.

**Send History** does not make copies of rows. WalletFeed updates the row that has the same `id`. If you deleted a row in Supabase, **Send History** adds the row again.

For more information, refer to [Send previous transactions](/docs/send-history/).

## Change or remove the destination

You change the Supabase destination on its screen in **Destinations**.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the Supabase destination.

   ![The screen of a Lunch Money destination, with Name, Enabled, Last Sync, Replace Token, Filter, Send History, Send Test and Delete.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/walletfeed-destination-detail.webp)

The screen of a Supabase destination has the same items. In place of **Replace Token**, it has **Project**, **Share SQL** and **Replace Key**.

### Send only some transactions

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Supabase destination.
2. Set **Filter** to on.
3. Change **Include**, **Minimum**, **Include Pending**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**.

For more information, refer to [Filter the transactions for a destination](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

### Stop the destination for a time

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Supabase destination.
2. Set **Enabled** to off.

   Until you set **Enabled** to on again, WalletFeed does not send transactions to Supabase.

### Replace the key

If you deleted the publishable key in Supabase, or if Supabase does not accept the key, do these steps:

1. If the project has no publishable key, make a key (refer to [If the project has no publishable key](#if-the-project-has-no-publishable-key)).
2. On your iPhone, open the [Supabase dashboard](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/_?showConnect=true).
3. Copy the publishable key with steps 2 thru 7 of [Step 3](#step-3-copy-the-publishable-key-and-the-project-url).
4. Open WalletFeed again.
5. In **Destinations**, tap the Supabase destination.
6. Tap **Replace Key**.
7. Touch and hold **Publishable Key**.
8. Tap **Paste**.
9. Tap **Replace**.

   Result: Before WalletFeed puts the new key in the Keychain, WalletFeed reads the table with the key. Then **Replace Key** shows a green checkmark.

### Use the SQL of the destination again

In the destination, **Share SQL** gives the SQL with the token of this destination. This SQL keeps the rows in the table. If the table does not have the `foreign_amount` and `foreign_currency` columns, the SQL adds them.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Supabase destination.
2. Tap **Share SQL**.
3. Send the SQL to your computer, for example with AirDrop.
4. On your computer, open the **SQL Editor** of your project.
5. Paste the SQL in the editor.
6. Click **Run**.
7. Click **Run query**.
8. In WalletFeed, tap **Send Test**.

### Remove Supabase from WalletFeed

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Supabase destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. Tap **Delete** again.

   Result: WalletFeed removes the destination and deletes the key from your iPhone. The rows that WalletFeed sent stay in your Supabase table. You can delete these rows or the table in Supabase.

### Delete the key in Supabase

After you delete the key, Supabase does not accept the key from WalletFeed. Supabase also does not accept the key from a different app that uses it.

1. On your computer, open your project in the [Supabase dashboard](https://supabase.com/dashboard).
2. In the bar on the left, click the **Project Settings** icon.
3. Click **API Keys**.
4. In the row of the publishable key, click **⋮**.
5. Click **Delete API key**.

   ![The menu of the default publishable key, with the highlighted Delete API key item.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/supabase-delete-publishable-key.webp)

6. In the dialog, type the name of the key, for example `default`.
7. Click **Yes, irreversibly delete this API key**.

   Result: Supabase shows "Successfully deleted publishable key". The WalletFeed destination then shows "Authentication failed".

## If there is a problem

To make sure that WalletFeed can send transactions to Supabase, do these steps:

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Supabase destination.
2. Tap **Send Test**.

   Result: If Supabase receives the test row, WalletFeed shows a green checkmark.

> **Note:** **Send Test** adds a test row with the description `WalletFeed test transaction` to the table. If you tap **Send Test** again, WalletFeed does not add a second test row. You can delete the test row in the **Table Editor**.

### If you cannot tap Add

WalletFeed lets you tap **Add** only when the form has a key and a project URL. If the key is a secret key, you cannot tap **Add**, and WalletFeed shows "Use the publishable key. Secret keys skip the table's policy."

1. Copy the publishable key again (refer to [Step 3](#step-3-copy-the-publishable-key-and-the-project-url)). The key starts with `sb_publishable_`.
2. In WalletFeed, clear the **Publishable Key** field.
3. Paste the key in the **Publishable Key** field.
4. Make sure that the field below the key contains the project URL.

### If WalletFeed shows "Key rejected. Copy the publishable key again."

Supabase did not accept the key. For example, you copied only a part of the key, or a person deleted the key in Supabase.

1. Copy the publishable key again (refer to [Step 3](#step-3-copy-the-publishable-key-and-the-project-url)).
2. In WalletFeed, clear the **Publishable Key** field.
3. Paste the key in the **Publishable Key** field.
4. Tap **Add**.

If the project has no publishable key, refer to [If the project has no publishable key](#if-the-project-has-no-publishable-key).

### If WalletFeed shows "Table not found. Run the SQL, then try again."

The project has no `walletfeed_transactions` table. For example, you did not click **Run query**, or you pasted the SQL in a different project.

1. On your computer, open the project that has the URL from Step 3.
2. Open the **SQL Editor**.
3. In WalletFeed, tap **Share SQL**.
4. Send the SQL to your computer, for example with AirDrop.
5. On your computer, paste the SQL in the **SQL Editor**.
6. Click **Run**.
7. Click **Run query**.
8. In WalletFeed, tap **Add**.

### If WalletFeed shows "Couldn't connect"

WalletFeed cannot connect to the project URL in the form.

1. Make sure that your iPhone has an internet connection.
2. Copy the project URL again (refer to [Step 3](#step-3-copy-the-publishable-key-and-the-project-url)).
3. In WalletFeed, clear the field below the key.
4. Paste the URL in this field.
5. Tap **Add**.

### If the project has no publishable key

A new project has a publishable key with the name `default`. If a person deleted this key, Supabase shows "No publishable keys created yet" on the **API Keys** page.

1. On your computer, open your project in the [Supabase dashboard](https://supabase.com/dashboard).
2. In the bar on the left, click the **Project Settings** icon.
3. Click **API Keys**.

   ![The Project Settings page in Supabase, with the highlighted settings icon and API Keys item.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/supabase-project-settings.webp)

4. Click **New publishable key**.
5. Obey the instructions in Supabase.
6. Copy the new key, as in [Step 3](#step-3-copy-the-publishable-key-and-the-project-url).

   On a Mac, you can also click the copy button in the row of the key. The **API Keys** page does not show the project URL.

   ![The API Keys page, with the highlighted copy button of the default publishable key above the secret keys.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/supabase-api-keys.webp)

### If the destination shows "Authentication failed"

Supabase did not accept the key or the token of the destination. For example, a person deleted the key in Supabase, or SQL from a different Supabase form or destination replaced the token in the policy.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.

   ![The Destinations list, with an n8n destination that shows Authentication failed.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/walletfeed-destinations-failure.webp)

2. Use the SQL of the Supabase destination again (refer to [Use the SQL of the destination again](#use-the-sql-of-the-destination-again)).
3. If **Send Test** shows an error, replace the key (refer to [Replace the key](#replace-the-key)).

> **Note:** When you tap **Add**, WalletFeed does not make sure that the token in the policy is correct. If the token is not correct, the destination shows "Authentication failed" after WalletFeed tries to send the first transactions.

### If the destination shows "Rejected (HTTP 404)"

The project has no `walletfeed_transactions` table. For example, a person deleted the table in Supabase.

1. Use the SQL of the Supabase destination again (refer to [Use the SQL of the destination again](#use-the-sql-of-the-destination-again)).

### If Supabase stopped your project

The Supabase [pricing page](https://supabase.com/pricing) tells you that Free plan projects "are paused after 1 week of inactivity".

1. On your computer, open your project in the [Supabase dashboard](https://supabase.com/dashboard).
2. If Supabase stopped the project, obey the instructions on the project page to start the project again.
3. On your iPhone, tap the Supabase destination in **Destinations**.
4. Tap **Send Test**.

### If no new rows show in the table

WalletFeed sends changes when it is open, or when iOS starts it in the background.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap the gear icon at the top of **Destinations**.
3. In **Settings** › **Sync**, make sure that **Background Sync** is on.
4. In **Destinations**, tap the Supabase destination.
5. Make sure that the destination shows no error below **Last Sync**.
6. Make sure that **Filter** is off, or that the filter includes the transactions.
7. Tap **Send Test**.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Sure

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to Sure. Sure is a self-hosted budget app that is a fork of Maybe Finance. You add a card account and make an API key in Sure. Then you paste the key in WalletFeed.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings in Wallet on that iPhone.
- WalletFeed with [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.
- A Sure server and an account on that server. Sure is open source, and you can get it without a purchase.
- An `https://` address for the Sure server. [Step 1](#step-1-get-an-https-address-for-your-sure-server) gives the conditions for this address.
- A computer with a web browser. You use it to add the card account and to make the key in Sure.

## Your key stays on your iPhone

- WalletFeed keeps the API key in the Keychain on your iPhone. iOS encrypts the Keychain.
- The API key does not go to iCloud Keychain or to your other devices.
- WalletFeed has no account and no servers. No person at WalletFeed can see or get the API key.
- Your iPhone sends the API key only to your Sure server, in each request to your Sure server.
- When you delete the destination, WalletFeed deletes the API key from your iPhone. You can also revoke the key in Sure.

## Step 1: Get an HTTPS address for your Sure server

WalletFeed connects only to an address that starts with `https://`. With [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/), WalletFeed also sends transactions when your iPhone is not on your home network. Thus, your iPhone must connect to the address from all locations.

If you install Sure with Docker and do not change its configuration, Sure uses an `http://` address on port 3000. WalletFeed cannot use this address. A tunnel service, for example Tailscale or Cloudflare Tunnel, can give Sure an `https://` address.

1. If the address of your Sure server starts with `http://`, make an `https://` address with a tunnel service.
2. If a tunnel service gives Sure its `https://` address, set `RAILS_ASSUME_SSL: "true"` in the Sure configuration.

   The HTTPS section of [the Docker instructions for Sure](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/blob/main/docs/hosting/docker.md) gives more information.

3. Disconnect your iPhone from your home Wi-Fi.
4. On your iPhone, open the `https://` address of your Sure server in Safari.
5. Make sure that Sure opens.

## Step 2: Add a card account in Sure

WalletFeed writes the transactions to one account in Sure. The Sure API cannot make accounts. Thus, you must add the account in Sure first.

1. On your computer, open your Sure server in a web browser.
2. If a **What's new** dialog opens, click **Got it**.
3. On **Home** › **Dashboard**, click **Add account** or **New**.

   ![The Sure dashboard with no accounts and the Add account button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-home-add-account.webp)

4. Click **Credit Card**.

   ![The Sure dialog that shows the account types, with Credit Card highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-choose-credit-card.webp)

5. Click **Enter account balance**.

   ![The Sure dialog that shows the procedures to add the card, with Enter account balance highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-enter-account-balance.webp)

6. In **Account name**, type `Apple Card`.
7. In **Balance on date:**, type `0`, or type the card balance on the **Opening balance date**.
8. Click **Create Account**.

   ![The credit card form in Sure with the name Apple Card, and with the Create Account button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-credit-card-details.webp)

> **Note:** Sure shows a credit card on the **Debts** tab of the account list. The **Assets** tab does not show it.

> **Note:** Sure calculates the card balance from the balance in **Balance on date:** and from the transactions that Sure receives. The balance in Sure is the same as the balance in Wallet only if the balance in **Balance on date:** is correct. Sure sets the **Opening balance date** to 2 years before the day that you add the account.

## Step 3: Make a Read/Write API key in Sure

WalletFeed uses the key to read your Sure accounts and to write transactions. With [Universal Clipboard](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102430), you can copy the key on a Mac and paste it on your iPhone.

> **Caution:** Do not send the key to yourself in a message or an e-mail. With the key, a different person can read your Sure accounts and write transactions.

1. On your computer, open your Sure server in a web browser.
2. At the bottom of the left bar, click the button that shows the first letters of your name.

   ![The Sure account page with the button at the bottom of the left bar highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-open-account-menu.webp)

3. Click **Settings**.

   ![The Sure account menu, with Settings highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-account-menu-settings.webp)

4. In the **Settings** list, scroll to the **ADVANCED** group.
5. Click **API Keys**.

   ![The Sure Settings list with API Keys highlighted in the ADVANCED group.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-settings-api-keys.webp)

6. Click **New API Key**.

   ![The API Keys page in Sure, with no keys and the New API Key button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-api-keys-empty.webp)

7. In **API Key Name**, type `WalletFeed`.
8. In **Permissions**, click **Read/Write**.

   ![The page for a new key in Sure with the name WalletFeed, and with the Read/Write permission highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-create-key-read-write.webp)

9. Click **Save API Key**.

   ![The page for a new key in Sure, with the Save API Key button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-save-api-key.webp)

10. Click **Copy API Key**.

    ![The API Key Created Successfully page in Sure, with the Copy API Key button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-key-created-copy.webp)

> **Note:** Sure shows the key on this page only. The `curl` example on the same page also contains the key, but WalletFeed cannot use the `curl` example.

> **Note:** Sure does not select a permission for you. With a **Read Only** key, Sure does not accept the transactions from WalletFeed.

To make the key on your iPhone, do these steps:

1. In WalletFeed, do steps 1 to 5 of [Step 4](#step-4-add-sure-in-walletfeed).
2. Tap **Open API Keys**. Your web browser opens the **API Keys** page of your Sure server.
3. If Sure shows its sign-in page, get access to your Sure account.
4. If Sure then shows its dashboard, tap **Open API Keys** in WalletFeed again.
5. On the **API Keys** page, do steps 6 to 10 of the first procedure in Step 3.
6. Open WalletFeed again.
7. Do steps 6 to 10 of Step 4.

## Step 4: Add Sure in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The empty Destinations screen with the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In **Budgeting**, tap **Sure**. If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed first shows the WalletFeed Pro screen.

   ![The Add Destination list, with Sure and the text Self-hosted in the Budgeting group.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

5. In the field that shows `https://sure.example.com`, type the `https://` address of your Sure server.

   ![The WalletFeed screen for Sure with the server field, the API Key field and three steps.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/walletfeed-setup-sure.webp)

6. In **API Key**, paste the key. WalletFeed connects to Sure and shows **Account**.
7. In **Account**, select your card account.

   If an account has Apple Card in its name, WalletFeed selects that account for you. If no account has Apple Card in its name, WalletFeed selects a credit card account.

8. Tap **Add**.
9. In the **Send Transactions to Sure?** message, tap **Send**.

   The message tells you the data that Sure will receive, the Wallet accounts and the start date.

10. On your computer, click **Transactions** in Sure. Sure shows the transactions from WalletFeed in the list.

    ![The Sure Transactions page with seven sample transactions from WalletFeed in the Apple Card account.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-walletfeed-result.webp)

## Data that Sure receives

WalletFeed sends these fields for each transaction to the Sure account that you selected:

| From Wallet | In Sure |
| --- | --- |
| The date of the transaction, in your time zone | Date |
| The merchant name, or the description if there is no merchant name | Name |
| The amount | Amount. A purchase is an expense, and a refund or other credit is income. |
| The currency | Currency |
| The ID of the transaction in Wallet | An ID that WalletFeed uses to change the transaction |

WalletFeed does not send categories. Sure shows new transactions as **Uncategorized** until you give them a category.

Sure shows a purchase with a minus sign, for example -$6.75, and a refund in green without a minus sign. The **Debt balance** of the card increases with each purchase.

WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. Thus, your iPhone sends the transactions directly to your Sure server. The server address and the key stay in the Keychain on your iPhone.

## New and changed transactions

While WalletFeed is open, Sure receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then sends the change.

WalletFeed sends a pending charge to Sure. Sure does not show that the charge is pending. When Wallet shows the charge as posted, the date or the amount can change. Then WalletFeed makes the same change in Sure. WalletFeed does not change the name, category, merchant, tags and notes that you set in Sure.

If Wallet removes a pending charge, for example a declined charge, WalletFeed deletes the transaction from Sure. WalletFeed deletes only transactions from the last 90 days.

If WalletFeed sends a transaction again, Sure does not make a second copy. Sure keeps one transaction for each Wallet transaction.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

You can also send previous transactions with [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the Sure destination, for example **Sure · Apple Card**.
3. Tap **Send History**.
4. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**. WalletFeed shows **Sending History** with the number of transactions that it sent.

To stop Send History before WalletFeed sends all of the transactions, tap **Send History** › **Stop Sending**.

## Change or remove the destination

To open the Sure destination, do these steps:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the Sure destination.

For more information, refer to [Destinations](/docs/destinations/).

### Send only some transactions

1. Set **Filter** to on.
2. Select the transactions with **Include**, **Minimum**, **Include Pending**, **Accounts**, **Categories** and **Exclude**.

To send only Apple Card transactions to this destination, select Apple Card in **Accounts**.

For more information, refer to [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

### Replace the key

1. Make a new Read/Write key in Sure, as in [Step 3](#step-3-make-a-read-write-api-key-in-sure). While the previous key is active, the new key must have a different name, for example `WalletFeed 2`.
2. In the Sure destination, tap **Replace Key**.
3. In **API Key**, paste the new key.
4. Tap **Replace**.

WalletFeed keeps the new key only if the key can read the card account and write transactions.

### Stop or remove the destination

To stop the destination but not remove it, set **Enabled** to off.

To remove the destination, do these steps:

1. In the Sure destination, tap **Delete**.
2. In the **Delete Sure · Apple Card?** message, tap **Delete**.
3. On your computer, open **Settings** › **API Keys** in Sure.
4. Click **Revoke** for the WalletFeed key.

   ![The API Keys list in Sure, with the Revoke button for the WalletFeed key highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-revoke-key.webp)

5. Click **Confirm**.

   ![The Sure dialog about the WalletFeed key, with Confirm highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-revoke-confirm.webp)

If you remove the destination, the transactions that WalletFeed sent stay in Sure.

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed does not show Account or Open API Keys

The address starts with `http://`. WalletFeed connects only to `https://` addresses, and it shows no message for an `http://` address.

1. Get an `https://` address for your Sure server, as in [Step 1](#step-1-get-an-https-address-for-your-sure-server).
2. In WalletFeed, type the `https://` address.

### If WalletFeed shows "Create an account in Sure"

When Sure has no accounts, WalletFeed shows "Create an account in Sure for your card, then try again."

1. Add a card account in Sure, as in [Step 2](#step-2-add-a-card-account-in-sure).
2. In WalletFeed, delete the key in **API Key**.
3. Paste the key in **API Key** again.
4. Make sure that WalletFeed shows **Account**.

### If WalletFeed shows "Key rejected (HTTP 401)"

When Sure does not accept the key, WalletFeed shows "Key rejected (HTTP 401). Use a Read/Write key." The key is incorrect or expired, or you clicked **Revoke** for the key in Sure.

1. Make sure that you copied the key with **Copy API Key**, and not the `curl` example.
2. If you copied the `curl` example, do the steps in [If you closed the key page before you copied the key](#if-you-closed-the-key-page-before-you-copied-the-key).
3. If you copied the key with **Copy API Key**, make a new Read/Write key in Sure, as in [Step 3](#step-3-make-a-read-write-api-key-in-sure). While the previous key is active, the new key must have a different name, for example `WalletFeed 2`.
4. In WalletFeed, paste the new key in **API Key**.

### If Destinations shows "Authentication failed" for Sure

Sure does not accept the key when WalletFeed sends transactions. For example, this occurs if the key is **Read Only**, or if you clicked **Revoke** for the key in Sure.

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.

   ![The Destinations screen, where one destination shows Authentication failed.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/walletfeed-destinations-failure.webp)

2. Tap the Sure destination.
3. Replace the key, as in [Replace the key](#replace-the-key).

### If WalletFeed shows "Can't connect" or "Couldn't connect"

WalletFeed cannot connect to your Sure server. The server does not operate, or your iPhone can connect to it only on your home network.

1. Make sure that your Sure server operates.
2. Disconnect your iPhone from your home Wi-Fi.
3. On your iPhone, open the `https://` address of your Sure server in Safari.
4. If Sure does not open, get an `https://` address for all locations, as in [Step 1](#step-1-get-an-https-address-for-your-sure-server).
5. If you added Sure in WalletFeed, tap **Send Test** in the Sure destination.

The test writes a transaction of $4.20 with the name WalletFeed to the card account in Sure. You can delete the test transaction in Sure.

### If WalletFeed shows "No Sure API at this address"

When the address is not correct, WalletFeed shows "No Sure API at this address, or the account is gone." If you deleted the card account, WalletFeed also shows this message when you replace the key.

1. Make sure that the address is the same address that you use to open Sure in a web browser.
2. If you deleted the card account in Sure, add a new card account, as in [Step 2](#step-2-add-a-card-account-in-sure).
3. If you added a new card account, add Sure again in WalletFeed, as in [Step 4](#step-4-add-sure-in-walletfeed).

### If you closed the key page before you copied the key

Sure shows a key one time only. Sure also does not accept two active keys with the same name.

1. On your computer, open **Settings** › **API Keys** in Sure.
2. Click **Revoke** for the WalletFeed key.
3. Click **Confirm**.
4. Make a new Read/Write key in Sure, as in [Step 3](#step-3-make-a-read-write-api-key-in-sure).
5. In WalletFeed, paste the new key in **API Key**.

### If the card balance in Sure is not correct

Sure calculates the balance from the balance in **Balance on date:** and from the transactions. If Sure receives many transactions in a short time, Sure can show a balance without the last transaction.

1. In Sure, open the card account.
2. On the right side of the account name, click the icon with two arrows in a circle. Sure calculates the card balance again.

   ![The Apple Card account in Sure, with the icon of two arrows in a circle highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/sure-refresh-account-balance.webp)

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Toshl Finance

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to Toshl Finance. You make a personal token in Toshl, then paste it into WalletFeed.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed, with access to the [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/) that have the transactions for Toshl.
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/), because destinations are part of it. WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.
- A Toshl Finance login with an e-mail address and a password. You can make personal tokens on the Toshl Free plan.
- A computer with a web browser, to add an account in Toshl in Step 1.

## Your token stays on your iPhone

- WalletFeed keeps the personal token in the Keychain on your iPhone. iOS encrypts the Keychain.
- The personal token does not go to iCloud Keychain or to your other devices.
- WalletFeed has no account and no servers. No person at WalletFeed can see or get the personal token.
- Your iPhone sends the personal token only to Toshl, in each request to Toshl.
- When you delete the destination, WalletFeed deletes the personal token from your iPhone. You can also delete the token in Toshl.

## Step 1: Add an Apple Card account in Toshl

WalletFeed adds each transaction as an entry in one Toshl account. If the name of an account contains "Apple", WalletFeed selects that account for you. If you have a Toshl account for your card, this step is not necessary.

1. On your computer, open the [Toshl web app](https://toshl.com/app/).
2. If Toshl shows the **Log In** page, get access with your e-mail address and password.
3. Click **All accounts**.

   ![The Toshl web app with a red frame around the All accounts button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/toshl-home-all-accounts.webp)

4. In the **Accounts** panel, click **ADD ACCOUNT**.

   ![The Toshl Accounts panel with a red frame around the ADD ACCOUNT button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/toshl-add-account.webp)

   On the Toshl Free plan, you can have only 2 accounts. If Toshl shows **Upgrade to Toshl Pro or Medici**, click **X**. Then go to [Step 2](#step-2-open-the-toshl-finance-form-in-walletfeed).

5. Click **General financial account**.

   ![The Toshl Add account dialog with a red frame around General financial account.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/toshl-general-account.webp)

   Do not click **Connected financial account**. This account connects to a bank, and only the Medici plan has it.

6. In **Title**, type `Apple Card`.

   You can keep 0.00 in **New account balance** and **Account limit**.

   ![The Toshl Add account form with the title Apple Card and a red frame around the SAVE button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/toshl-account-title.webp)

7. Click **SAVE**.

   The **Accounts** panel shows the new Apple Card account.

   ![The Toshl Accounts panel with the new Apple Card account below Cash.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/toshl-account-added.webp)

## Step 2: Open the Toshl Finance form in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. In **Destinations**, tap **+**.

   ![The Destinations screen in WalletFeed with the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

3. In **Budgeting**, tap **Toshl Finance**.

   ![The Add Destination list in WalletFeed with Toshl Finance in the Budgeting group.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/walletfeed-add-destination.webp)

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows **WalletFeed Pro** first. After you get WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows the Toshl Finance form.

## Step 3: Make a personal token in Toshl

1. In the Toshl Finance form, tap **Open Apps**.

   ![The Toshl Finance form in WalletFeed with the Personal Token field and the Open Apps link.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/walletfeed-setup-toshl-finance.webp)

   Your web browser opens the Toshl **Apps** page.

If the page shows "Please login to proceed.", do these steps:

1. Tap **login**.

   ![The Toshl Apps page with the message Please login to proceed and a red frame around login.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/toshl-apps-login.webp)

2. Type your Toshl e-mail address and password.
3. Tap **Log in**.

   Toshl opens its web app. Toshl does not open the **Apps** page.

4. In WalletFeed, tap **Open Apps** again.

To make the token on the **Apps** page, do these steps:

1. In **Description**, type `WalletFeed`.

   ![The Toshl Apps page with a red frame around the Description field.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/toshl-apps-page.webp)

2. In **Password**, type your Toshl password.
3. Tap **Create**.

   ![The new personal token form with the description WalletFeed and a red frame around the Create button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/toshl-create-token.webp)

   Toshl shows the new token in a gray box below **Tokens list**. Toshl shows all of the token only one time.

4. Touch and hold the token in the gray box.

   ![The Toshl Tokens list with a red frame around the new token and the description WalletFeed in the same row.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/toshl-token-created.webp)

5. Make sure that the highlighted text includes all of the token.

   The token has 72 characters, and Toshl can show it on more than one line. The text WalletFeed in the same row is the description, and it is not part of the token. Toshl has no button to copy the token.

6. Tap **Copy**.

> **Note:** With the token, an app can read and change all of your Toshl data. In Toshl, you cannot give a token access to only some of the data.

## Step 4: Add Toshl Finance in WalletFeed

1. Open WalletFeed again.
2. If WalletFeed does not show the Toshl Finance form, do [Step 2](#step-2-open-the-toshl-finance-form-in-walletfeed) again.
3. Touch and hold **Personal Token**.
4. Tap **Paste**.

   After WalletFeed makes sure that the token is correct, WalletFeed shows **Account** with your Toshl accounts. The token stays in the Keychain on your iPhone.

5. In **Account**, select the Toshl account for your card (for example, Apple Card).
6. Tap **Add**.

   Then WalletFeed shows the **Send Transactions to Toshl Finance?** message. The message tells you that Toshl Finance receives the date, merchant, amount, currency and category of each transaction. The message also gives the Wallet accounts and the start date. If **Initial History** is **All**, the message shows "including earlier ones", not a date. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed does not add the destination.

7. Tap **Send**.

   **Destinations** shows the new destination (for example, **Toshl · Apple Card**). Then WalletFeed starts to send your transactions.

   ![The Toshl Expenses page with sample purchases from WalletFeed by date, each with its category and merchant.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/toshl-walletfeed-result.webp)

## Data that Toshl Finance receives

WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to Toshl. After Toshl receives your transactions, the terms of Toshl are applicable to them.

Each transaction becomes one entry in the Toshl account that you selected. The transactions from different Wallet accounts go to this one Toshl account. Toshl does not receive the name of the Wallet account.

| In Wallet | In Toshl Finance |
|---|---|
| A purchase | An expense |
| A refund or other credit | An income |
| Amount | Amount. WalletFeed does not send a transaction with an amount of 0, because Toshl does not accept it. |
| Currency | Currency |
| Purchase date | Date, as the day in your time zone |
| Merchant, or the description if there is no merchant | Description, with a maximum length of 255 characters |
| Category | Category, from the category table |
| Transaction ID | The same ID, in a field that Toshl keeps but does not show |

For each new entry, WalletFeed compares your Toshl categories with the names in the second column, in sequence. WalletFeed uses the first name that agrees with a Toshl category. Capital letters do not change the result. If no name agrees, WalletFeed uses **Other**.

| WalletFeed category | Toshl category names, in sequence | Result for a new Toshl login with English categories |
|---|---|---|
| Groceries | Groceries, Food & Drinks, Food | Food & Drinks |
| Dining | Restaurants, Dining, Food & Drinks, Food | Food & Drinks |
| Transport | Transport, Transportation | Transport |
| Fuel | Fuel, Car, Transport | Transport |
| Entertainment | Entertainment, Leisure | Leisure |
| Travel | Travel, Holidays | Other |
| Shopping | Shopping, Clothing, Clothing & Footwear | Clothing & Footwear |
| Subscriptions | Subscriptions, Bills & Fees, Bills | Other |
| Utilities | Utilities, Home & Utilities, Bills & Fees, Bills, Home | Home & Utilities |
| Health | Health, Healthcare, Health & Personal Care, Health & Beauty | Health & Personal Care |
| Services | Services | Other |
| Cash & Transfers | Cash, Transfers | Other |
| Other | Other | Other |
| A refund or other credit | Refunds, Other (income categories) | Other |

WalletFeed sets the category only when it adds an entry. If you change the category, tags, location or reminders of an entry in Toshl, WalletFeed keeps your changes. If you change the amount, date or description in Toshl, WalletFeed replaces your change when it sends the transaction again.

## New and changed transactions

While WalletFeed is open, Toshl receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then sends the change.

Toshl has no pending status. Thus, Toshl shows a pending purchase as an expense. When the purchase becomes posted, WalletFeed changes the amount, date and description of the same entry.

If a pending purchase does not become posted (for example, after a decline), WalletFeed removes its entry from Toshl. WalletFeed does this only for entries from the last 90 days.

A refund is an income in Toshl, in the category **Refunds** or **Other**.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

To send a different period, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Toshl Finance destination.
2. Tap **Send History**.

   ![A destination screen in WalletFeed (for Lunch Money) with Send History below Filter.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/walletfeed-destination-detail.webp)

3. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

   The destination screen shows **Sending History** while WalletFeed sends the history. To stop, tap **Send History** › **Stop Sending**.

WalletFeed sends the history in small parts, at a speed that Toshl accepts.

If you send a period again, WalletFeed finds the entries that it sent before. WalletFeed changes an entry only if a change is necessary. It does not add a second entry for a transaction.

## Change or remove the destination

You change the Toshl Finance destination on its screen in **Destinations**.

### Send only some transactions

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Toshl Finance destination.
2. Set **Filter** to on.

   For more about the filter, refer to [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

### Stop the destination for a time

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Toshl Finance destination.
2. Set **Enabled** to off.

### Replace the token

1. Make a new personal token, as in [Step 3](#step-3-make-a-personal-token-in-toshl).
2. In **Destinations**, tap the Toshl Finance destination.
3. Tap **Replace Token**.
4. Paste the new token in **Personal Token**.
5. Tap **Replace**.

   If the new token does not have access to the same Toshl account, WalletFeed does not accept the token. The entries that WalletFeed sent before stay in Toshl. WalletFeed does not add these entries again.

### Remove Toshl Finance from WalletFeed

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Toshl Finance destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. Tap **Delete** again.

   The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay in Toshl. The token also stays in Toshl until you delete it in Toshl.

### Delete the token in Toshl

1. On your computer, open the [Toshl Apps page](https://developer.toshl.com/apps/).
2. In **Tokens list**, click **Delete** in the row of the WalletFeed token.

   ![The Toshl Tokens list with a red frame around the Delete button for the WalletFeed token.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/toshl-delete-token.webp)

   Toshl does not show a message before it deletes the token.

## If there is a problem

### If WalletFeed shows "Token rejected" or "Authentication failed"

Toshl does not accept the token, because you copied only part of it or you deleted it in Toshl.

1. Make a new personal token, as in [Step 3](#step-3-make-a-personal-token-in-toshl).
2. If you added the destination before, do steps 2 thru 5 in [Replace the token](#replace-the-token).
3. If WalletFeed shows the Toshl Finance form, paste the token in **Personal Token**.

### If the token in Toshl ends with "..."

Toshl shows all of the token only one time. After that, Toshl shows only the first part of the token, and WalletFeed cannot use this part.

1. Make a new personal token, as in [Step 3](#step-3-make-a-personal-token-in-toshl).
2. In **Tokens list**, tap **Delete** in the row of the token that ends with "...".
3. If you added the destination before, do steps 2 thru 5 in [Replace the token](#replace-the-token).
4. If WalletFeed shows the Toshl Finance form, paste the new token in **Personal Token**.

### If WalletFeed shows "Create an account in Toshl first."

Toshl has no active account for your login.

1. Add an account in Toshl, as in [Step 1](#step-1-add-an-apple-card-account-in-toshl).
2. In WalletFeed, remove the token from **Personal Token**.
3. Paste the token again.

### If WalletFeed shows "This token can't see" and the account name

The new token is from a different Toshl login, or the account is not in Toshl at this time. WalletFeed cannot send transactions to an account that is not in Toshl.

1. Get access to Toshl with the login that has the account.
2. Make a new personal token, as in [Step 3](#step-3-make-a-personal-token-in-toshl).
3. In WalletFeed, tap **Replace Token**.
4. Paste the new token in **Personal Token**.
5. Tap **Replace**.
6. If WalletFeed shows the message again, do the steps in [Remove Toshl Finance from WalletFeed](#remove-toshl-finance-from-walletfeed).
7. After you remove the destination, add Toshl Finance again from [Step 1](#step-1-add-an-apple-card-account-in-toshl).

### If Toshl shows "Upgrade to Toshl Pro or Medici"

On the Toshl Free plan, you can have only 2 accounts. The account Cash is one of them.

1. Click **X**.
2. In WalletFeed, in **Account**, select an account that you have in Toshl.

### If you do not know your Toshl password

To make a token, you must type your Toshl password. If you use Apple, Google or Facebook to get access to Toshl, it is possible that you have no Toshl password.

1. Open the [Toshl Log In page](https://toshl.com/login/).
2. Tap **Forgot password?**.
3. Set a Toshl password.

### If many entries are in Other

A new Toshl login has no category names for some WalletFeed categories (for example, Travel, Subscriptions and Services).

1. On your computer, in the Toshl web app, click **Expenses**.
2. Click **Edit categories**.
3. Add an expense category with a name from the [category table](#data-that-toshl-finance-receives) (for example, `Travel`).

   The new category is for new entries only.

4. For an entry that WalletFeed sent before, change the category in Toshl.

### If Toshl shows a negative balance

The new account starts at 0.00, and each purchase is an expense. Thus, the balance is less than zero after the first purchase. This balance is usual for a card account. It does not show a problem with the destination.

### If Toshl shows no transactions

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. In **Destinations**, tap the Toshl Finance destination.
3. Read **Last Sync**.
4. If the screen shows a message below **Last Sync**, find that message on this page.
5. Tap **Send Test**.

   Toshl receives a test expense of $4.20 with the description WalletFeed.

6. On your computer, in the Toshl web app, click **Expenses**.
7. To show a different month in Toshl, click the arrows adjacent to the month name.
8. After the test, remove the test expense in Toshl.

### If Toshl shows an entry two times

If two iPhones send the transactions of one card to Toshl at the same time, each iPhone can add an entry.

1. On one of the two iPhones, do the steps in [Remove Toshl Finance from WalletFeed](#remove-toshl-finance-from-walletfeed).
2. In Toshl, remove one of the two entries.

### If WalletFeed shows "Toshl is limiting requests. Try again later."

In a short time, Toshl received more requests than it accepts.

If WalletFeed shows this message in the Toshl Finance form, do these steps:

1. Wait some minutes.
2. Remove the token from **Personal Token**.
3. Paste the token in **Personal Token** again.

If WalletFeed shows this message below **Replace Token**, do these steps:

1. Wait some minutes.
2. Do steps 3 thru 5 in [Replace the token](#replace-the-token) again.

### If WalletFeed shows "Rejected (HTTP 429)" or "Too many requests."

Toshl received more requests than it accepts while WalletFeed sent transactions. WalletFeed stops, and it continues when it sends transactions to Toshl again. No step is necessary.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-webhook/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to a webhook

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a webhook. A webhook is an `https://` URL in n8n or on your server. WalletFeed sends each new or changed transaction to that URL in JSON format.

## Before you start

For this procedure, you must have:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings in Wallet on that iPhone.
- WalletFeed with [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/). WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase.
- An n8n workflow, or a server that can receive HTTPS requests. The URL must start with `https://`.
- A computer for the steps in n8n or on your server.

WalletFeed also sends transactions when your iPhone is not on your home network. Thus, the URL must operate from the internet.

## Your URL and secret stay on your iPhone

- WalletFeed keeps the URL, the authorization value and the signing secret in the Keychain on your iPhone. iOS encrypts the Keychain.
- These items do not go to iCloud Keychain or to your other devices.
- WalletFeed has no account and no servers. No person at WalletFeed can see or get these items.
- Your iPhone sends the URL and the authorization value only to your server. WalletFeed uses the signing secret to sign each request, but WalletFeed does not send the signing secret.
- When you delete the destination, WalletFeed deletes these items from your iPhone.

## Step 1: Get a webhook URL

Do the steps for n8n, or the steps for your server.

### Get the URL in n8n

The Webhook node in n8n gives you the URL. With **Header Auth**, the node also makes sure that each request has the correct `Authorization` value.

1. On your computer, open n8n.
2. Make a new workflow.
3. Click **Add first step…**.
4. Select **On webhook call**.

   Result: n8n adds a Webhook node to the workflow.
5. In **HTTP Method**, select **POST**.
6. In **Authentication**, select **Header Auth**.
7. In **Credential for Header Auth**, select **Create new credential**.
8. In **Name**, type `Authorization`.
9. In **Value**, type `Bearer`, a space and a long password that you make.
10. Keep a copy of the header value (the text in **Value**) for Step 2.
11. Save the credential.
12. In **Respond**, select **Immediately**.
13. Select **Production URL**.
14. Copy the URL that n8n shows.
15. Click **Publish**.

    Result: n8n shows a window with a name for the version.
16. In that window, click **Publish**.

    Result: n8n starts to receive requests at the **Production URL**.
17. Send the URL and the header value to your iPhone, for example with AirDrop.

You must use the **Production URL** in WalletFeed. The **Test URL** operates only for 120 seconds after you click **Listen for test event**.

If **Respond** is **Immediately**, n8n sends the status code when the workflow starts. WalletFeed waits a maximum of 30 seconds for the status code. If an error stops the workflow after n8n sends the status code, WalletFeed does not send the data again.

n8n uses only the version of the workflow that you published. If you change the workflow, you must publish it again.

If requests go to your n8n server through a reverse proxy, n8n gets the **Production URL** from the environment variable `N8N_WEBHOOK_URL`. The value of this variable must be your `https://` address. Before n8n 2.35.0, the name of this variable was `WEBHOOK_URL`. From version 2.35.0, if you use `WEBHOOK_URL`, n8n writes a warning in its log.

### Use your server

Your server must do these tasks:

- Accept `POST` requests with a JSON body at an `https://` URL.
- Send a status code from 200 to 299 after the server saves the data.
- Use the `id` of each transaction to find the same transaction in the saved data.
- Remove the transactions that have their IDs in `data.deletedIDs`.

WalletFeed sends a transaction again when the transaction changes. If the server does not send a status code from 200 to 299, WalletFeed keeps the changes. WalletFeed sends them again each time that it sends data, until the server accepts them.

[Webhook format](/docs/webhooks/) gives the JSON format and the steps to examine the signature. You get the secret for the signature in Step 2.

## Step 2: Add the webhook in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The empty Destinations screen with the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-webhook/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. Tap **Webhook**, below **Developers** at the bottom of the list.

   Result: WalletFeed shows the **Webhook** screen. If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed shows **WalletFeed Pro** first.

   > **Note:** The search field also finds **Webhook** if you type `webhook` or `n8n`.

5. If WalletFeed shows **WalletFeed Pro**, get [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).
6. To give the destination a different name, for example n8n, type the name in **Name**.

   ![The Webhook screen in WalletFeed with Name, the URL field, Authorization (Optional), Share Signing Secret, Send Test and the Webhook Format link.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-webhook/walletfeed-setup-webhook.webp)

7. Paste the URL in the field that shows `https://example.com/hook`.

   If the URL does not start with `https://`, you cannot tap **Send Test** or **Add**.
8. If you use n8n, paste the header value in **Authorization (Optional)**.
9. If you use your server, and it examines the `Authorization` header, type the value for that header in **Authorization (Optional)**.
10. If the server does not examine the signature (for example, n8n with **Header Auth**), go to step 14.
11. Tap **Share Signing Secret**.

    Result: iOS shows a menu with **Copy**. The secret starts with `whsec_`.
12. Tap **Copy**.
13. Add the secret to your server.
14. Tap **Send Test**.

    Result: WalletFeed sends one test transaction of $4.20 from the merchant WalletFeed. If the server accepts it, WalletFeed shows a green checkmark.

    If the server does not accept it, WalletFeed shows the error below **Send Test**. In n8n, the **Executions** tab of the workflow shows the test.
15. Tap **Add**.

    Result: WalletFeed shows **Send Transactions to Your Server?** with a message. The message tells you the data that your server will receive. The message also gives the Wallet accounts and the start date, or "including earlier ones" if **Initial History** is **All**.

    If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the new destination and does not send data.
16. Tap **Send**.

    Result: WalletFeed starts to send transactions to the URL.

    ![The Destinations screen with the n8n webhook destination and three other destinations.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-webhook/walletfeed-destinations.webp)

## Data that the webhook receives

WalletFeed sends each change to the URL in an HTTP `POST` request with a JSON body. One request contains a maximum of 100 transactions. The body has these items:

- `type` is `transactions.changed`. For **Send Test**, the value is `walletfeed.test`.
- `timestamp` is the date and time when WalletFeed sent the request.
- `data.upserted` is a list of the new and changed transactions.
- `data.deletedIDs` is a list of the IDs of the transactions to remove.

WalletFeed sends the IDs to remove in one request, and the new and changed transactions in a different request. Thus, in each request, one of the two lists is empty.

This table shows the fields of each transaction in `data.upserted`.

| WalletFeed sends | JSON field |
| --- | --- |
| Transaction ID, which stays the same when the transaction changes | `id` |
| ID and name of the Wallet account, for example Apple Card | `accountID`, `accountName` |
| `liability` for Apple Card, or `asset` for Apple Cash and Savings | `accountType` |
| Date and time of the transaction | `date` |
| Date and time when the charge posted, if Wallet gives it | `postedDate` |
| Amount (a positive number) | `amount` |
| `debit` for purchases and fees, or `credit` for refunds, payments and deposits | `direction` |
| Currency code, for example `USD` | `currencyCode` |
| Amount and currency of a purchase in a different currency | `foreignAmount`, `foreignCurrencyCode` |
| Description from Wallet | `description` |
| Description from the card network | `originalDescription` |
| Merchant name, if Wallet has it | `merchantName` |
| Merchant category code (MCC), if Wallet has it | `merchantCategoryCode` |
| WalletFeed category, for example `dining` or `groceries` | `category` |
| Wallet status: `authorized`, `pending`, `booked` or `memo` | `status` |
| Transaction type from Wallet, for example `pointOfSale`, `refund`, `billPayment` or `transfer` | `type` |

If Wallet has no value for a field, the transaction does not include that field. The dates use the ISO 8601 format and UTC, for example `2026-10-30T06:29:40Z`.

Each request also has the Standard Webhooks headers `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` and `webhook-signature`. The `User-Agent` header is `WalletFeed-Webhooks/1`. If you typed a value in **Authorization**, the request has that value in the `Authorization` header.

WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. Thus, your iPhone sends the data to the URL. The Keychain on your iPhone keeps the URL, the **Authorization** value and the secret. The server or service that receives the data keeps it. The terms of that service are applicable to the data.

### Get one item for each transaction in n8n

The Webhook node puts the JSON in `body`. To get one n8n item for each transaction, do these steps:

1. After the Webhook node, add a **Split Out** node.
2. In **Fields To Split Out**, type `body.data.upserted`.
3. Click **Publish**.
4. In the window, click **Publish**.

The IDs of the transactions to remove are in `body.data.deletedIDs`.

The request from **Send Test** also starts the workflow. In that request, `body.type` is `walletfeed.test`.

## New and changed transactions

While WalletFeed is open, the webhook receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then sends the change.

In Wallet, a new charge is pending until the charge posts. WalletFeed sends the charge with `pending` or `authorized` in `status`. When the charge posts, WalletFeed sends the same `id` again with `booked` in `status` and the posted amount. To keep one item for each transaction, you must change the item that has the same `id`. If Wallet gives the posted charge a new ID, WalletFeed sends the previous ID in `deletedIDs` and the new transaction in `upserted`.

If **Include Pending** is off in the filter, WalletFeed sends charges only after they post. [Send only some transactions](#send-only-some-transactions) tells you how to set the filter.

A refund is a different transaction. Its `direction` is `credit`.

If Wallet shows a declined or expired charge, or removes a transaction, WalletFeed sends the ID of that transaction in `deletedIDs`.

If the server does not send a status code from 200 to 299, WalletFeed keeps the changes. WalletFeed sends them again each time that it sends data, until the server accepts them. Thus, the server can receive the same data two times or more. Two requests with the same data have the same `webhook-id`. The `webhook-timestamp` header, the `timestamp` value and the signature are different in each request.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. To start from a different date, you must set **Initial History** before you add the webhook.

To send more previous transactions after you add the webhook, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In **Destinations**, tap the webhook destination.
2. Tap **Send History**.
3. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

   Result: WalletFeed shows **Sending History** and a progress bar.

WalletFeed uses `transactions.changed` requests for previous transactions, and it sends the newest transactions first. It sends them in groups of approximately 500 and waits 1 second between groups. Each request contains a maximum of 100 transactions. n8n starts the workflow one time for each request.

To stop **Send History**, do these steps:

1. In the destination, tap **Send History**.
2. Tap **Stop Sending**.

## Change or remove the destination

### Send only some transactions

1. In **Destinations**, tap the webhook destination.
2. Set **Filter** to on.
3. Set the filter controls (refer to the table).

| Control | WalletFeed sends |
| --- | --- |
| **Include** | All transactions, only purchases or only credits |
| **Minimum** | Only transactions of this amount or more |
| **Include Pending** | If it is off, charges only after they post |
| **Accounts** | Only transactions from the Wallet accounts that you select |
| **Categories** | Only transactions in the categories that you select |
| **Exclude** | No transactions from the merchants that you type (with a comma between two merchants) |

If Apple Intelligence is active, you can also type a rule, for example "Travel over $50, not Uber". When you tap the Apple Intelligence icon at the end of the field, WalletFeed makes the filter from the rule. For more information about the filter, refer to [Choose what to send](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

WalletFeed uses the filter only for the transactions that it sends after you set the filter.

### Change the URL

1. In **Destinations**, tap the webhook destination.
2. Tap **URL**.

   Result: WalletFeed shows **Webhook URL** with the URL that the destination uses.
3. Delete the URL in the field.
4. Paste the new URL.

   If the URL does not start with `https://`, you cannot tap **Save**.
5. Tap **Save**.

   Result: WalletFeed starts to send changes to the new URL.

The **URL** row shows only the server name from the URL. WalletFeed does not send the previous transactions to the new URL. You can send them with **Send History**.

### Change the Authorization value

1. In **Destinations**, tap the webhook destination.
2. Tap **Authorization**.
3. Delete the value in the field.
4. Type or paste the new value.
5. Tap **Save**.

If the field is empty when you tap **Save**, the destination has no value, and **Authorization** shows **None**.

You can get the secret again with **Share Signing Secret** in the destination. The destination always uses the same secret.

### Stop or delete the destination

To stop the destination for a time, set **Enabled** to off in the destination.

To delete the destination, do these steps:

1. In **Destinations**, tap the webhook destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. Tap **Delete** again.

The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay on your server or in n8n.

To stop the n8n workflow, do these steps in n8n:

1. Open the menu adjacent to **Publish**.
2. Select **Unpublish**.

## If there is a problem

### If you cannot tap Send Test or Add

**Send Test** and **Add** operate only if the URL starts with `https://` and has a server name. For **Add**, a name is also necessary.

1. Make sure that the URL starts with `https://` and has a server name after it.
2. Make sure that **Name** is not empty.

### If WalletFeed shows "Rejected (HTTP 404)"

The server has no webhook at the URL. For example, the URL is the n8n **Test URL**, you did not publish the workflow, or **HTTP Method** is not **POST**. For this problem, **Send Test** on the Webhook screen shows "The server returned an error (HTTP 404)."

1. In the n8n Webhook node, make sure that **HTTP Method** is **POST**.
2. Make sure that you published the workflow after your last change.
3. In the Webhook node, select **Production URL**.
4. Copy the URL again.
5. In WalletFeed, do the steps in [Change the URL](#change-the-url).
6. In the destination, tap **Send Test**.
7. If WalletFeed shows "Rejected (HTTP 404). Check the destination, then try again." below **Sending History**, tap **Try Again**.

If the HTTP code is not 404, the server did not accept the request because of a different problem. To find the problem, examine the log of your server, or the **Executions** tab in n8n.
