### If the destination shows "Authentication failed"

The server did not accept the **Authorization** value (HTTP 401 or 403). In n8n, this problem occurs if the value is different from **Value** in the **Header Auth** credential.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.

   ![The n8n destination in WalletFeed, which shows Authentication failed below Last Sync and None for Authorization.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-webhook/walletfeed-destination-failure.webp)

2. Tap **Authorization**.
3. Delete the value in the field.
4. Type the header value from **Value** in n8n.
5. Tap **Save**.
6. If WalletFeed shows "Authentication failed. Check the connection." below **Sending History**, tap **Try Again**.

### If the destination shows "Can't connect"

Your iPhone cannot connect to the URL, or the server did not send a status code in 30 seconds. For example, the server is off, or the URL operates only on your home network.

1. Make sure that your server or n8n is on.
2. On your iPhone, set Wi-Fi to off.
3. In the destination, tap **Send Test**.

   If WalletFeed shows an error, the URL operates only on your home network. You must use a URL that operates from the internet.
4. Set Wi-Fi to on again.
5. In n8n, make sure that **Respond** is **Immediately**.

WalletFeed sends the changes again each time that it sends data, until the server accepts them.

### If the destination shows "Server error"

The server sent a status code of 500 or more. The destination shows the code, for example "Server error (500)". WalletFeed sends the same changes again each time that it sends data, until the server accepts them.

1. Examine the log of your server, or the **Executions** tab of the workflow in n8n.
2. Correct the error.
3. In the destination, tap **Send Test**.

### If the server receives a transaction two times

WalletFeed sends a transaction again when the transaction changes, for example when a pending charge posts. WalletFeed also sends a request again if it did not get a status code from 200 to 299.

1. Find the item that has the `id` of the transaction.
2. Change that item. Do not add a new item.
3. To find a request that the server received two times, compare the `webhook-id` headers.

### If the webhook does not receive new transactions

Something stops the transactions to the URL. For example, the destination is off, or **Background Sync** is off. After your iPhone starts again, WalletFeed cannot send data to destinations until you type your passcode one time.

1. Open WalletFeed. While WalletFeed is open, it sends changes in seconds.
2. If **Destinations** shows **Sync Requires Pro**, tap **Upgrade**.
3. If the destination shows **Off**, set **Enabled** to on in the destination.
4. If **Filter** is on, make sure that the filter includes the transaction.
5. In n8n, make sure that you published the workflow.
6. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of **Destinations**.
7. Make sure that **Background Sync** is on.
8. Tap **Sync Now**.

To make sure that WalletFeed can send data to the URL, tap **Send Test** in the destination. If the server accepts the test transaction, WalletFeed shows a green checkmark.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ynab/ -->
# Put Apple Card transactions in YNAB

The YNAB app for iPhone can connect to Wallet and put your Apple Card transactions in YNAB. WalletFeed can also write your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions to OFX or CSV files that YNAB can import on a computer.

## Connect YNAB to Wallet

The YNAB Help Center gives these steps for the newest YNAB app on iOS 17.4 or a newer version:

1. On your iPhone, open YNAB.
2. In the **Accounts** tab, tap **Add Account**.
3. In **Popular Options**, tap the Apple icon.
4. To connect YNAB to Wallet, do the steps that YNAB shows.
5. Select the Wallet accounts to connect to YNAB.
6. Tap **Next**.
7. To change the name or the type of an account, tap **Edit**.
8. Tap **Next**.

The YNAB Help Center tells you that YNAB gets the Wallet transactions only through the iPhone that you used to add the connection. On that iPhone, **Background App Refresh** must stay active in **Settings** › **Apps** › **YNAB**. The [YNAB Help Center page for Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings](https://support.ynab.com/en_us/apple-connections-rkShEfrUh) gives all the steps and the error messages.

## Before you start

To import WalletFeed files into YNAB, you must have:

- WalletFeed on an iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/) for files that WalletFeed updates (a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase)
- YNAB in a web browser on a computer, or YNAB in Safari on an iPad (YNAB does not import files on an iPhone)
- iCloud Drive on your iPhone and on your computer, or a different app that Files shows, for example Dropbox.

WalletFeed is available only in the US.

WalletFeed Pro is not necessary for **Export CSV**.

## Step 1: Add an OFX File destination in WalletFeed

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen has no destinations and shows the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ynab/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the **Destinations** search field, type `OFX`.
5. Tap **OFX File**.

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, the **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens. After you get WalletFeed Pro, the **Files** screen opens.

6. Make sure that **Format** is **OFX**.

   ![The Files screen shows OFX in Format and WalletFeed in Name.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ynab/walletfeed-setup-ofx-file.webp)

7. Tap **Folder**.
8. Select a folder in iCloud Drive.

   After you select a folder, you can tap **Add**.

9. To use a different name for the files, type the name in **Name**.

   Each month has one file. If the name is `WalletFeed`, the file for October 2026 is `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`.

10. Tap **Add**.

    Result: WalletFeed shows **Save Transactions to Files?** with a message. The message tells you that the folder receives the date, the merchant, the amount and other data of posted transactions. The message also gives the accounts and the period.

11. Tap **Save**.

    Result: WalletFeed writes your posted transactions to the files.

> **Note:** WalletFeed keeps no copy of the files. The files are in your iCloud Drive. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers.

## Step 2: Keep only Apple Card transactions in the files

YNAB puts all the transactions in a file into one account. If WalletFeed reads only your Apple Card account, this step is not necessary.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination, for example **WalletFeed**.
2. Set **Filter** to on.
3. Tap **Accounts**.
4. Select your Apple Card account.
5. Tap the back button at the top of the screen.
6. Tap **Send History**.
7. Tap **All**.

   Result: WalletFeed writes the file again for each month that has Apple Card transactions. These files then have only your Apple Card transactions.

To put your Apple Cash transactions in a different YNAB account:

1. Add a second OFX File destination with a different name in **Name**, for example `Apple Cash` (refer to Step 1).
2. In **Destinations**, tap the new destination.
3. Set **Filter** to on.
4. Tap **Accounts**.
5. Select your Apple Cash account.
6. Tap the back button at the top of the screen.
7. Tap **Send History**.
8. Tap **All**.

## Step 3: Import a file in YNAB

1. On your computer, open YNAB in a web browser.
2. Open the iCloud Drive folder that has the files from WalletFeed.
3. Drag the file for a month, for example `WalletFeed 2026-10.ofx`, into YNAB.

   Result: YNAB shows **Import Transactions**. You can drag more than one OFX file at the same time.

4. At the top of **Import Transactions**, make sure that YNAB shows your Apple Card account.
5. To put the memos in YNAB, select **Import Memos**.

   The memo has the description and the card statement text, if they are different from the merchant name. If a transaction has a foreign amount, the memo also has it.

6. Import the file.

If you import a file again, YNAB does not add the transactions that have the same date and amount as transactions that it added before.

> **Note:** On an iPad, you can drag the file from Files into YNAB in Safari. The [YNAB Help Center page for file import](https://support.ynab.com/en_us/file-based-import-a-guide-Bkj4Sszyo) gives the steps.

YNAB does not keep the file, but it keeps the transactions from the file. The terms of YNAB are applicable to these transactions.

## Use a CSV file

YNAB also imports CSV files. The OFX file has only posted transactions. A CSV file from WalletFeed has posted and pending transactions. For a pending transaction, the Status column contains `pending` or `authorized`.

WalletFeed Pro is not necessary for **Export CSV**. To make a CSV file one time:

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. At the top of the screen, tap **Settings** (the gear button).
3. In the **Data** section, tap **Export CSV**.

   ![The Settings screen shows Export CSV in the Data section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ynab/walletfeed-settings-3.webp)

4. Tap **Range**.

   ![The Export CSV screen shows the range This Month and 29 transactions.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ynab/walletfeed-export-csv.webp)

5. Select a range, for example **Last Month**.
6. Tap **Export**.
7. Tap **Save to Files**.
8. Save the file in iCloud Drive.

The file has the transactions of all the Wallet accounts that WalletFeed reads. YNAB puts all these transactions in the account that you select.

With WalletFeed Pro, a CSV File destination updates a file when your transactions change. The destination can have a filter for one account. The [guide for a CSV file](/guides/apple-card-to-csv/) gives the steps.

In YNAB, use these columns of the CSV file:

| YNAB field | Column in the CSV file |
| --- | --- |
| **Date** | Date |
| **Payee** | Merchant |
| **Memo** | Description |
| **Outflow** | Amount |
| **Inflow** | Amount |

To import the CSV file in YNAB:

1. On your computer, open YNAB in a web browser.
2. Drag the CSV file into YNAB.
3. At the top of **Import Transactions**, make sure that YNAB shows your Apple Card account.
4. Make sure that each YNAB field uses the CSV column that the table shows.

   The CSV file has one Amount column. A purchase is a negative amount. The YNAB Help Center tells you to select **Amount** for **Outflow** and for **Inflow**.

5. Import the file.

## Data that YNAB receives

The OFX file has this information for each posted transaction:

| Wallet data | In the OFX file | In YNAB |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Merchant | The merchant name, or the description if Wallet has no merchant name. The file keeps the first 32 characters. | **Payee** |
| Amount | A purchase is negative. A payment or a refund is more than zero. | **Outflow** or **Inflow** |
| Date and posted date | The date of the transaction and the date that it posted | **Date** |
| Description, card statement text and foreign amount | The memo of the transaction | **Memo**, if you select **Import Memos** |
| Account | One statement for each Wallet account | The YNAB account that you select |

The OFX file has no category. The YNAB Help Center tells you that YNAB changes the payee names from a file. YNAB also gives each transaction the category that its payee usually has. You can change the payee and the category of each transaction in YNAB.

## Changes to the files

While WalletFeed is open, its files in iCloud Drive receive changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then updates the files.

If **Background Sync** is off, or if WalletFeed cannot open the folder at that time, the files get the changes when one of these occurs:

- You open WalletFeed.
- A Shortcuts automation starts WalletFeed.
- iOS starts WalletFeed when your iPhone gets power from a charger.

WalletFeed writes the file for a month again each time that a transaction in that month changes. YNAB gets the changes only when you import the file again.

A pending transaction is not in the file. When the transaction posts, WalletFeed adds it to the file for its month. A refund is a new transaction with an amount that is more than zero.

If Wallet removes a transaction, WalletFeed removes it from the file. If the transaction is in YNAB, you must delete it in YNAB.

## Send previous transactions

A new OFX File destination also receives previous posted transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it.

The YNAB Help Center recommends that a file has only transactions from the last 12 months. If a file has transactions from before the start date of your YNAB account, YNAB lets you include them. But it is not necessary to include them.

To write the previous transactions to the files again:

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap the destination, for example **WalletFeed**.
4. Tap **Send History**.
5. Tap **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

   Result: WalletFeed writes the file for each month in that period again. The file for the first month then has only the transactions from the start of the period.

The [Send History](/docs/send-history/) page gives more information.

## Change or remove the destination

To change the destination, tap it in [**Destinations**](/docs/destinations/). You can make these changes:

- To send only some transactions, set **Filter** to on. Then select the accounts, the categories or a minimum amount. Refer to [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).
- To use a different folder, tap **Change Folder**. WalletFeed then writes all your transactions to new files in that folder.
- To stop the changes to the files for a time, set **Enabled** to off.
- To change the name of the destination, type a different name in **Name**. The names of the files stay the same.

To remove the destination:

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. In the message, tap **Delete** again.

The files stay in iCloud Drive. The transactions from the files stay in YNAB.

## If there is a problem

### If YNAB puts Apple Cash transactions in your Apple Card account

The file has the transactions of more than one Wallet account.

1. In WalletFeed, set a filter for your Apple Card account (refer to Step 2).
2. In YNAB, delete the transactions that are not from your Apple Card account.

### If some transactions from a file are not in YNAB

YNAB does not add a transaction from a file if it added the same transaction before. If you deleted the transaction in YNAB, YNAB does not add it again.

1. In **Import Transactions**, look at the transactions above **Options**.

   For each transaction that YNAB did not add, YNAB shows the cause.

2. If you deleted the transactions in YNAB, type them in YNAB.

### If a pending transaction is not in the file

The OFX file has a transaction only after the transaction posts.

1. After the transaction posts, import the file for its month again.

### If the destination shows "Can't open the folder. Choose it again."

WalletFeed cannot open the folder that you selected.

1. In **Destinations**, tap the destination.
2. Tap **Change Folder**.
3. Select the folder again.

   Result: WalletFeed writes your transactions to the files again.

### If the files on your computer do not show new transactions

WalletFeed did not update the files after the last change in Wallet.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. At the top of the screen, tap **Settings** (the gear button).
3. In the **Sync** section, tap **Sync Now**.

   Result: **Sync Now** shows the time of the last update.

### If Destinations shows "Sync Requires Pro"

You do not have WalletFeed Pro at this time. WalletFeed keeps the destination, but it does not update the files.

1. In **Destinations**, tap **Upgrade**.
2. Select a plan.
3. Tap **Start Free Trial**, **Subscribe** or **Buy Lifetime**.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/ -->
# Send Apple Card transactions to Zapier

WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to Zapier. You make a Zap with a **Catch Hook** trigger in Zapier, then you paste the webhook URL of the trigger in WalletFeed.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed on your iPhone. WalletFeed must have access to your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account.
- [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/) (a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase). WalletFeed Pro is necessary for all destinations.
- A Zapier account on a Professional, Team or Enterprise plan. These plans include **Webhooks by Zapier**. The Free plan of Zapier does not include it.
- A computer for the steps on the Zapier website.

> **Note:** A new Zapier account starts with a 14-day Professional trial. A payment card is not necessary for the trial. During the trial, you can use **Webhooks by Zapier**. After the trial, the account changes to the Free plan. Then your Zap cannot use **Webhooks by Zapier**.

## Your URL stays on your iPhone

- WalletFeed keeps the webhook URL in the Keychain on your iPhone. iOS encrypts the Keychain.
- The webhook URL does not go to iCloud Keychain or to your other devices.
- WalletFeed has no account and no servers. No person at WalletFeed can see or get the webhook URL.
- Your iPhone sends the webhook URL only to Zapier, in each request to Zapier.
- When you delete the destination, WalletFeed deletes the webhook URL from your iPhone.

## Step 1: Make a Zap with a Catch Hook trigger

The Catch Hook trigger has a webhook URL. When WalletFeed sends data to this URL, the Zap starts.

1. On your computer, open [Zapier](https://zapier.com/app/home).
2. If you have a Zapier account, get access to it.
3. If you do not have a Zapier account, make an account on [Zapier's sign-up page](https://zapier.com/sign-up).
4. Click **+** at the top of the left sidebar.

   ![The Zapier home page, with the + button at the top of the left sidebar highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/zapier-home-create.webp)

5. Click **Zaps**.
6. Click the **Trigger** box.
7. In the search box, type `Webhooks`.
8. Click **Webhooks**. Zapier then shows the app as **Webhooks by Zapier**.

   ![The app list in Zapier, with Webhooks in the search box and the Webhooks result highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/zapier-search-webhooks.webp)

9. Under **Trigger event**, click **Choose an event**.
10. Click **Catch Hook**. Do not click **Catch Raw Hook**.

    ![The list of Webhooks by Zapier trigger events, with Catch Hook highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/zapier-catch-hook.webp)

11. Click **Continue**.

    Zapier can show a box about **API by Zapier**. WalletFeed does not use **API by Zapier**. You can close the box with **×**.

12. On the **Configure** tab, make sure that the **Pick off a Child Key** field has no text. If this field has text, Zapier keeps only a part of each transaction.
13. Click **Continue**.

    ![The Configure tab with no text in the Pick off a Child Key field, and the Continue button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/zapier-configure-continue.webp)

14. On the **Test** tab, under **Your webhook URL**, click **Copy**.

    ![The Test tab with the webhook URL, and the Copy button highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/zapier-copy-webhook-url.webp)

    The field shows only the first part of the URL. But **Copy** copies all of the URL.

15. Keep this page open. You will use it again in Step 3.

> **Note:** The URL stays on the **Test** tab of the trigger. You can open the Zap again at a different time and copy the URL.

> **Note:** If you use a Mac with the same Apple Account as your iPhone, you can paste the URL on your iPhone with [Universal Clipboard](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102430).

## Step 2: Add Zapier in WalletFeed

Before you add Zapier, you can set **Initial History** to **Today**. Then Zapier receives no previous transactions. With a different value, Zapier receives a maximum of 30 days of previous transactions. To set **Initial History**, do these steps:

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Sync** section, set **Initial History** to **Today**.

   **Settings** shows the **Sync** section only with WalletFeed Pro.

4. Tap **Done**.

To add Zapier, do these steps:

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen in WalletFeed with the + button and no destinations.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. Under **Automations**, tap **Zapier**. You can also type `Zapier` in the search field.
5. If WalletFeed shows the **WalletFeed Pro** screen, get WalletFeed Pro on that screen. WalletFeed then opens the **Zapier** screen.
6. Paste the URL in **Catch Hook URL**.

   ![The Zapier screen in WalletFeed with the Catch Hook URL field, three steps and the Zapier Help link.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/walletfeed-setup-zapier.webp)

   Because a person with the URL can start your Zap, WalletFeed keeps the URL in the Keychain on your iPhone.

7. Tap **Add**. WalletFeed sends a sample transaction to Zapier.
8. Read the message **Send Transactions to Zapier?**

   The message tells you the data that Zapier receives. It also tells you the accounts and the start date of the data.

9. Tap **Send**.

   If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed does not add the destination.

**Destinations** then shows the new Zapier destination.

## Step 3: Find the sample in Zapier

1. On your computer, in the Zap editor, click **Test trigger**.
2. Click **request A**.

   ![The Test tab with the record request A highlighted.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/zapier-request-found.webp)

   Zapier shows the fields of the sample. **Merchant** is WalletFeed, and **Amount** is -4.2.

3. Click **Continue with selected record**. Zapier then shows the apps for the **Action** step.

## Step 4: Add the Action step in Zapier

The **Action** step uses the data in an app. For example, the step can add a row to a Google Sheets spreadsheet.

1. Select the app that receives the data, for example **Google Sheets**.
2. Do the steps that Zapier shows for this app.
3. If the action must have a value from the transaction, use the fields from Step 3, for example **Merchant** and **Amount**.
4. Click **Publish** at the top right of the editor.
5. In **Automations** › **Zaps**, make sure that the **Status** of your Zap is on.

Each time that the Zap does an action step, it uses one task in Zapier. The trigger uses no task. The Zap starts one time for each new transaction and for each change to a transaction.

**Zap history** in Zapier shows each time that the Zap started, and the tasks that it used.

![The Zap runs tab of Zap history in Zapier, with four runs of the WalletFeed test Zap that each show Successful and 1 task.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/zapier-walletfeed-result.webp)

## Data that Zapier receives

Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to Zapier. WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. After Zapier receives your transactions, the terms of Zapier are applicable to them.

In the Zap, the data of each change has these fields:

| Field in Zapier | Value from Wallet |
| --- | --- |
| **Event** | `created` for a new transaction and for each transaction from **Send History**, `updated` for each subsequent change, and `deleted` when Wallet removes the transaction |
| **ID** | The transaction ID from Wallet. It stays the same when the transaction changes. |
| **Date** | The date of the purchase in your time zone, for example 2026-10-29 |
| **Merchant** | The merchant name, or the description if Wallet has no merchant name |
| **Amount** | Negative for a purchase, for example -84.12, and positive for a refund or a payment, for example 49 |
| **Currency** | The currency code, for example USD |
| **Category** | The WalletFeed category, for example Groceries |
| **Status** | The Wallet status: `pending`, `authorized` or `booked` |
| **Pending** | `true` while the purchase is pending or authorized, and `false` after the status changes to `booked` |
| **Account** | The Wallet account, for example Apple Card |
| **Description** | The description from Wallet |
| **Type** | The type of transaction, for example `pointOfSale` or `refund` |
| **Mcc** | The merchant category code, for example 5411 |
| **Foreign Amount** and **Foreign Currency** | The amount and the currency code of a purchase in a different currency |
| **querystring** | A field that Zapier adds. It always has no value. |

![A Whole Foods Market transaction from WalletFeed in the Zapier test results, with one field on each line.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/zapier-result-transaction-fields.webp)

For a deleted transaction, the data has only **Event** and **ID**. If Wallet does not give a value for a field, the field has no value in Zapier. An example is **Foreign Amount** for a purchase in dollars. In Zapier, an amount has no zeros at the end, for example 49 for $49.00.

## New and changed transactions

While WalletFeed is open, Zapier receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then sends the change.

**Background Sync** is on until you set it to off.

One transaction can start the Zap more than one time:

- Zapier receives a new purchase with **Event** `created` and **Status** `pending`.
- When the **Status** changes to `booked`, Zapier receives the same **ID** again with **Event** `updated`.
- If the bank does not accept a pending charge, or Wallet removes a transaction, Zapier receives **Event** `deleted` and the **ID**.

A refund is a different transaction. It has a positive **Amount** and the **Type** `refund`.

If WalletFeed stops while it sends changes, it sends the same changes again at a subsequent time. Zapier starts the Zap again for each change that it received before. Thus, a Zap that adds a row for each change can add a transaction two times. A Zap that first finds the row by **ID**, and then updates it, keeps one row for each transaction. This Zap uses two tasks for each change.

Zapier can start the Zap for some changes at the same time. Thus, the Zap does not always get the changes in the sequence that WalletFeed sends them.

## Send previous transactions

A new Zapier destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. But Zapier receives a maximum of 30 days of previous transactions.

To send more transactions, use [Send History](/docs/send-history/):

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Zapier destination.
2. Tap **Send History**.
3. Select a period (**30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**).
4. In the message **Send History to Zapier?**, tap **Send**.

   The message shows "Each transaction runs your Zap."

WalletFeed sends the newest transactions first. Each transaction starts the Zap one time. Each action step uses one task in Zapier.

**Send History** sends each transaction with **Event** `created`. Thus, Zapier can receive the same transaction two times as `created`.

To stop **Send History**, do these steps:

1. Tap **Send History**.
2. Tap **Stop Sending**.

## Change or remove the destination

### Send only some transactions

1. In **Destinations**, tap the Zapier destination.
2. Set **Filter** to on.
3. Change **Include**, **Minimum**, **Include Pending**, **Accounts**, **Categories** or **Exclude**.

For more information, refer to [Choose what a destination receives](/docs/choose-what-to-send/).

To stop the destination for a time, set **Enabled** to off.

### Replace the URL

If you make a new Zap, give its URL to WalletFeed:

1. In Zapier, copy the webhook URL of the new Zap (refer to Step 1).
2. In WalletFeed, open the Zapier destination.
3. Tap **Replace URL**.
4. Paste the new URL in **Catch Hook URL**.
5. Tap **Replace**. WalletFeed sends a sample to the new URL before it keeps the URL.

The destination screen shows **Webhook** with `hooks.zapier.com`. It does not show all of the URL.

### Delete the destination

1. In WalletFeed, open the Zapier destination.
2. Tap **Delete**.
3. In the message, tap **Delete** again.

The transactions that WalletFeed sent stay in Zapier. They also stay in the apps that received them from your Zap.

When the Zap is off or deleted, it does not start for your transactions. But Zapier can accept requests at the URL for some hours, and WalletFeed shows no error.

To delete the Zap, do these steps:

1. Open the Zap in Zapier.
2. Click the Zap name at the top of the editor.
3. Click **Delete**.
4. If Zapier shows a message, click the button that deletes the Zap.

## If there is a problem

### If you cannot tap Add

The text in **Catch Hook URL** is not a Zapier webhook URL. The URL must start with `https://hooks.zapier.com/hooks/`.

1. In Zapier, open the **Test** tab of the Catch Hook trigger.
2. Click **Copy**.
3. In WalletFeed, delete the text in **Catch Hook URL**.
4. Paste the URL again.

### If WalletFeed shows "The webhook refused the test"

Zapier did not accept the sample, because the URL is not correct or Zapier stopped the URL.

1. In Zapier, open **Automations** › **Zaps**.
2. If your Zap is not in the list, make a new Zap (refer to Step 1). Then do step 6.
3. Click your Zap in the list.
4. Click the **Catch Hook** trigger.
5. On the **Test** tab, click **Copy**.
6. In WalletFeed, delete the text in **Catch Hook URL**.
7. Paste the URL in **Catch Hook URL**.
8. Tap **Add**.

### If the destination shows "Rejected (HTTP 404)"

Zapier did not accept the transactions, because the Zap is off or deleted. After the Zap is off, Zapier can wait some hours before it stops the URL.

1. In Zapier, open **Automations** › **Zaps**.
2. If your Zap is in the list, set its **Status** to on.
3. If your Zap is not in the list, make a new Zap (refer to Step 1).
4. If you made a new Zap, give its URL to WalletFeed (refer to [Replace the URL](#replace-the-url)).

### If Zapier finds no request

You clicked **Test trigger** before WalletFeed sent the sample.

1. In WalletFeed, open the Zapier destination.
2. Tap **Send Test**. WalletFeed sends the sample again.
3. In Zapier, click **Find new records**.

Zapier loads a maximum of 3 records at a time, and it does not always load the newest records. This limit is only for the test. When the Zap is on, it starts for each change.

### If the Zap does not do its action

The Zap is a draft, or it is off. Zapier accepts the requests for the Zap, but the Zap does not do its action. WalletFeed shows no error.

1. In Zapier, open the Zap.
2. Click **Publish**.
3. In **Automations** › **Zaps**, set the **Status** of the Zap to on.

   ![The list of Zaps in Zapier, with the WalletFeed Zap and its Status switch in the off position.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/zapier-zap-list-off.webp)

### If the Zap stops after the Zapier trial

After the 14-day trial, the Zapier account is on the Free plan. The Free plan does not include **Webhooks by Zapier**.

1. In Zapier, click **Upgrade** at the top of the page.
2. Select a plan that includes **Webhooks by Zapier**, for example Professional.

### If one transaction makes two rows

The Zap starts for each change to a transaction. WalletFeed can also send the same change two times.

1. In the Zap, before the step that adds a row, add a step that finds the row by **ID**.
2. If the step finds a row, update that row.

### If Zapier receives transactions only while WalletFeed is open

**Background Sync** is off.

1. In WalletFeed, open **Settings** › **Sync**.
2. Set **Background Sync** to on.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/export-apple-card-transactions/ -->
# Make an export file of your Apple Card transactions

You can make an export file of your Apple Card transactions in Wallet on your iPhone, at card.apple.com or in WalletFeed. With WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed also updates a file or a service when your transactions change.

## Before you start

You must have:

- Your Apple Card in Wallet on your iPhone
- For card.apple.com, a computer with a web browser
- For WalletFeed, an iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version
- For a file or a service that WalletFeed updates, [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).

WalletFeed is available only in the US. WalletFeed must have [access to your Apple Card](/docs/wallet-accounts/).

WalletFeed Pro is a subscription with a 1-week free trial, or a one-time Lifetime purchase. WalletFeed Pro is not necessary for **Export CSV**.

## Make a file from a statement in Wallet

Wallet has a statement for each previous month. **Export Transactions** makes a CSV, OFX, QFX or QBO file with the transactions of a statement.

1. On your iPhone, open Wallet.
2. Tap your Apple Card.
3. Tap **Card Balance**.
4. Scroll to **Statements**.
5. Tap a statement.
6. Tap **Export Transactions**.
7. Select a file format (for example, CSV for a spreadsheet in Numbers or Excel).
8. To save the file in the Files app, tap **Save to Files**.

   You can also send the file with Mail or AirDrop.

9. Select a folder.
10. Tap **Save**.

To download a PDF file of a statement:

1. In Wallet, open a statement (refer to steps 1 to 5 in this section).
2. Tap **Download PDF Statement**.
3. When the PDF file opens, tap the **Share** button.

   You can then save, print or send the file.

## Make a file of transactions between two dates in Wallet

1. On your iPhone, open Wallet.
2. Tap your Apple Card.
3. Tap **Card Balance**.
4. Below **Statements**, tap **Export Transactions**.
5. Select a start date.
6. Select an end date.
7. Select a file format.
8. Tap the done button.

## Make a file at card.apple.com

1. On your computer, open [card.apple.com](https://card.apple.com).
2. Get access to your Apple Card with your Apple Account.
3. Click **Statements**.
4. Click **Export Transactions**.
5. Select a start date.
6. Select an end date.
7. Select a file format.
8. Click **Export**.

To download a PDF file of a statement:

1. In the sidebar, click **Statements**.
2. Click the download button for a statement.

Apple gives the steps for Wallet and card.apple.com in [Download your Apple Card statements or export your transactions](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102284).

## Make a CSV file with Export CSV

[Export CSV](/docs/export-csv/) in WalletFeed makes one CSV file with your transactions from a period that you select. You can use it without WalletFeed Pro. The file includes pending transactions. The file does not change after WalletFeed makes it.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Data** section, tap **Export CSV**.

   ![The Settings screen with Export CSV in the Data section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/export-apple-card-transactions/walletfeed-settings-3.webp)

4. Tap **Range**.
5. Select a period: **This Month**, **Last Month**, **Last 90 Days**, **This Year** or **All**.

   ![The Export CSV screen with Range set to This Month, 29 transactions and the Export button.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/export-apple-card-transactions/walletfeed-export-csv.webp)

   **Transactions** shows the number of transactions in the period.

6. Tap **Export**.
7. Tap **Save to Files**.
8. Select a folder.
9. Tap **Save**.

The name of the file includes the period, for example `Apple Card Last Month.csv`. The file has the transactions from each Wallet account that WalletFeed can read. The **Account** column shows the account of each transaction. WalletFeed makes the file on your iPhone and does not keep it.

## Columns in the CSV file

Each CSV file from WalletFeed has one row for each transaction and these columns:

| Column | Data |
| --- | --- |
| **Date** | The date of the transaction, for example 2026-10-28. |
| **Posted Date** | The date that the charge posted. It is empty while the charge is pending. |
| **Merchant** | The merchant name, or the description if Wallet has no merchant name. |
| **Description** | The description of the transaction in Wallet. |
| **Original Description** | The description of the transaction with no changes. |
| **Amount** | The value of the transaction, for example -23.40. Purchases and fees have a minus sign. Payments and refunds have no minus sign. |
| **Currency** | The currency code, for example USD. |
| **Direction** | `debit` for purchases and fees, or `credit` for refunds, payments and deposits. |
| **Status** | The status in Wallet, for example `pending` or `authorized` before the charge posts, `booked` after it posts, or `rejected` for a declined charge. |
| **Type** | The type of transaction in Wallet, for example `pointOfSale` for a purchase, `refund`, `transfer` or `fee`. |
| **Category** | The WalletFeed category, for example `Groceries`, `Dining` or `Cash & Transfers`. |
| **MCC** | The merchant category code (ISO 18245), for example 5411 for a grocery store. It is empty if Wallet has no code. |
| **Account** | The Wallet account, for example Apple Card. |
| **Foreign Amount** | For a purchase in a different currency, the value in that currency. |
| **Foreign Currency** | For a purchase in a different currency, the code of that currency. |
| **WalletFeed ID** | The ID of the transaction. You can use it to find the same transaction in a different file. |

## Update a file or a service with WalletFeed Pro

With WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed sends your transactions from your iPhone to a [destination](/docs/destinations/). When your transactions change, WalletFeed updates the destination. Thus, it is not necessary to make a new file.

WalletFeed has no account and no WalletFeed servers. Your transactions go from your iPhone directly to the folder or the service that you select.

Some of the destinations are:

- A [CSV file](/guides/apple-card-to-csv/) in a folder, for example in iCloud Drive
- An [OFX file](/guides/apple-card-to-ofx/) or a [QIF file](/guides/apple-card-to-qif/) for each month
- A spreadsheet in [Google Sheets](/guides/apple-card-to-google-sheets/)
- A budget app, for example [Lunch Money](/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/) or [PocketSmith](/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/).

For a CSV file, WalletFeed writes one file, or one file for each month. You can open a CSV file in [Excel](/guides/apple-card-to-excel/) or [Numbers](/guides/apple-card-to-numbers/).

An OFX or QIF file from WalletFeed includes a charge only after the charge posts.

> **Note:** WalletFeed writes CSV, OFX and QIF files. It does not write QFX or QBO files. Quicken for Windows cannot use the OFX files from WalletFeed, but it can use the CSV files.

To add a CSV file that WalletFeed updates:

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Destinations**.
3. Tap **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![The Destinations screen with no destinations and the + button at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/export-apple-card-transactions/walletfeed-destinations-empty-pro.webp)

4. In the search field, type `CSV`.
5. Tap **CSV File**.

   If you do not have WalletFeed Pro, the **WalletFeed Pro** screen opens. After you get WalletFeed Pro on that screen, the **Files** screen opens.

   ![The Files screen with Format set to CSV, Save As set to One File and the name WalletFeed Transactions.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/export-apple-card-transactions/walletfeed-setup-csv-file.webp)

6. Tap **Folder**.
7. Select a folder, for example in iCloud Drive.

   **Folder** then shows the name of the folder.

8. Tap **Add**.
9. When WalletFeed shows **Save Transactions to Files?**, tap **Save**.

   The message tells you the data that the folder will receive. It also gives the accounts and the period of the transactions. If you tap **Cancel**, WalletFeed removes the new destination.

WalletFeed then writes your transactions to `WalletFeed Transactions.csv` in the folder.

## Changes to the file

While WalletFeed is open, the file receives changes in seconds. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet. If [Background Sync](/docs/background-sync/) is on in **Settings** › **Sync**, WalletFeed then updates the file. If WalletFeed cannot open the folder at that time, the file changes when you open WalletFeed, when an automation starts, or while your iPhone charges.

## Send previous transactions

A new destination also receives previous transactions from the start date in **Settings** › **Sync** › **Initial History**. **Initial History** is **All** until you change it. After you add the destination, you can send the transactions of a different period with [Send History](/docs/send-history/) on the destination screen. You can select **30 Days**, **90 Days**, **1 Year** or **All**.

## Delete a destination

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Destinations**.
2. Tap the destination.
3. Tap **Delete**.
4. Tap **Delete** again.

After you delete the destination, the file and the transactions in it stay in the folder. A service keeps the transactions that it received. The terms of that service are applicable to these transactions.

## If there is a problem

### If this month has no statement in Wallet

Wallet makes a statement only after the end of the month. **Export CSV** in WalletFeed can make a file with the transactions of this month.

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. In the **Data** section, tap **Export CSV**.
4. Tap **Range**.
5. Select **This Month**.
6. Tap **Export**.
7. Tap **Save to Files**.
8. Select a folder.
9. Tap **Save**.

### If you cannot tap **Export** in WalletFeed

You cannot tap **Export** while WalletFeed reads your transactions, or when the period has no transactions.

1. Make sure that **Transactions** shows a number.
2. If the number is 0, select a different period in **Range**.

### If there is an apostrophe before a name or a description

In the **Merchant**, **Description**, **Original Description** and **Account** columns, WalletFeed puts an apostrophe (`'`) before text that starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@`. Thus, a spreadsheet does not use the text as a formula. WalletFeed does not put an apostrophe before an amount.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/find-apple-card-subscriptions/ -->
# Find subscriptions on your Apple Card

WalletFeed finds the subscriptions and other [recurring charges](/docs/recurring-charges/) on your Apple Card and shows them on its [Spending](/docs/spending/) screen. It can also send you a notification when a charge becomes a recurring charge or when its price changes.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed on your iPhone, with [access to your Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/). These accounts are Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings.
- Two or more charges from one merchant in Wallet. For a charge that occurs each week, three charges are necessary.
- For short names and for [Ask Spending](/docs/ask-spending/), an iPhone that can use Apple Intelligence, with Apple Intelligence on.

[WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/) is not necessary for Recurring Charges or for Recurring Charge Alerts.

## Step 1: Open Recurring Charges

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Spending**.
3. Scroll to **Recurring Charges**.

   ![The Recurring Charges section on the Spending screen, with PG&E, Netflix and Spotify.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/find-apple-card-subscriptions/walletfeed-recurring.webp)

Each row shows a name, the price of the last charge, and **Monthly** or **Weekly**. With Apple Intelligence, the row can also show the type of service, for example **Streaming · Monthly**.

The list starts with the charge that has the highest price for one month. If WalletFeed finds no recurring charges, the **Spending** screen does not show the **Recurring Charges** section. For more information, refer to [Recurring Charges](/docs/recurring-charges/).

## Step 2: Get the total price for one month

Ask Spending calculates the total price of your recurring charges for one month. For this step, Apple Intelligence must be on. Without Apple Intelligence, the **Spending** screen does not show **Ask about your spending**. To set Apple Intelligence to on, refer to [Ask Spending](/docs/ask-spending/#if-spending-does-not-show-ask-about-your-spending).

1. On the **Spending** screen, tap **Ask about your spending**.

   ![The Spending screen with the Ask about your spending field at the top.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/find-apple-card-subscriptions/walletfeed-spending.webp)

2. Type `Subscriptions I pay for`.
3. Tap **Go** on the keyboard.

   Ask Spending shows the number of recurring charges and their total price for one month. Below the chart, **Recurring Charges** shows the price of each charge for one month.

4. To show the usual **Spending** screen again, tap **Clear** (the x button) in the field.

For a charge that occurs each week, WalletFeed multiplies the price by approximately 4.3 to get the price for one month. The total price includes charges that are not subscriptions, for example a charge for electricity each month.

If you also type a period of time, for example `last month`, Ask Spending shows the total price of your recurring charges in that period.

## Step 3: Get a notification when a charge starts or changes

1. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Notifications** section, set **Recurring Charge Alerts** to on.

   ![The Settings screen with the Recurring Charge Alerts switch in the Notifications section.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/find-apple-card-subscriptions/walletfeed-settings.webp)

3. If iOS shows a message about notifications, tap **Allow**.
4. Tap **Done**.

When a charge becomes a recurring charge, the notification shows, for example, “Netflix repeats monthly” and “$15.49 each month”.

If the price of a recurring charge changes by more than 2%, the notification shows, for example, “Netflix costs more” and “$17.99, up from $15.49”.

WalletFeed sends notifications only for charges from the last 7 days. For each charge, it sends only one notification. It does not send notifications for the charges that were in Wallet before you set **Recurring Charge Alerts** to on.

When you open WalletFeed, it examines your transactions and sends the new notifications. When WalletFeed is not open, iOS starts WalletFeed approximately 1 hour or less after a change in Wallet.

> **Note:** For these notifications, WalletFeed keeps only transaction IDs. It keeps no prices and no merchant names.

## Conditions for a recurring charge

WalletFeed examines your transactions from this month and from the two months before it. It shows the charges from a merchant in **Recurring Charges** when the charges agree with these conditions:

- All the charges have the same merchant name. For example, “Netflix.com” and “NETFLIX.COM” are the same merchant name.
- The difference between the price of each charge and the price of the last charge is 15% or less.
- For **Monthly**, there are two or more charges, and each charge is 26 to 35 days after the charge before it.
- For **Weekly**, there are three or more charges, and each charge is 6 to 8 days after the charge before it.

**Recurring Charges** does not show these transactions:

- Apple Card Monthly Installments (the **Monthly Installments** section on the **Spending** screen shows them)
- Refunds, transfers, bill payments and rejected transactions
- Charges that occur each year.

## Names from Apple Intelligence

With Apple Intelligence, WalletFeed shows a short name and a type of service. For example, for the merchant name “NETFLIX.COM 866-579” from Wallet, WalletFeed shows Netflix and **Streaming**. If the first word of the name from Apple Intelligence is not in the merchant name, WalletFeed does not use that name. WalletFeed gets names only for the first 12 charges in the list. Below the list, **Recurring Charges** shows **Apple Intelligence suggested these names.**

Apple Intelligence gets only the merchant names. It operates on your iPhone. WalletFeed does not send data to a server for these names.

Without Apple Intelligence, each row shows the merchant name from Wallet, and **Monthly** or **Weekly**.

## Stop the notifications

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Notifications** section, set **Recurring Charge Alerts** to off.
3. Tap **Done**.

A notification shows the name of the charge and the prices. When notification previews are off, iOS does not show the text of the notification on the Lock Screen.

## If there is a problem

### If Spending shows “No Cards”

WalletFeed does not have access to your Wallet accounts.

1. Tap **Choose Accounts**.
2. Set **Apple Card** to on.

   ![The Share Wallet Data screen with the Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings switches on.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/find-apple-card-subscriptions/walletfeed-wallet-access.webp)

3. Tap **Share**.

If WalletFeed shows **Wallet Access Off**, refer to [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/).

### If Spending shows “Couldn't Read Wallet”

WalletFeed did not get your transactions from Wallet.

1. To try again, swipe down on the **Spending** screen.

### If a new subscription is not in Recurring Charges

WalletFeed shows a charge that occurs each month only after the second charge from the merchant. It shows a charge that occurs each week only after the third charge.

1. When Wallet shows a new charge from the merchant, open **Spending** again.

### If a subscription with a new price is not in Recurring Charges

If the price changes by more than 15%, WalletFeed does not show the charge. WalletFeed shows the charge again when all the charges from the merchant in this month and the two months before it have the new price.

Recurring Charge Alerts can send a notification when the price changes by more than 15%. To get these notifications:

1. In WalletFeed, tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
2. In the **Notifications** section, set **Recurring Charge Alerts** to on.

### If a subscription with a charge each year is not in Recurring Charges

WalletFeed finds only charges that occur each month or each week.

To find the charges from the merchant:

1. Tap **Search** at the bottom of the screen.
2. Type the name of the merchant.

### If a charge shows the merchant name from Wallet

The cause is one of these:

- Apple Intelligence is not active.
- Apple Intelligence gave no name that agrees with the merchant name.
- The charge is not in the first 12 charges of the list.

If Apple Intelligence is not active, do these steps:

1. Make sure that your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence.

   Apple gives the list of iPhone models in [Get started with the next generation of Apple Intelligence](https://support.apple.com/en-us/121115).

2. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
3. Tap **Apple Intelligence & Siri**.
4. Set **Apple Intelligence** to on.
5. In WalletFeed, open **Spending** again.

### If Recurring Charge Alerts does not stay on

iOS does not let WalletFeed send notifications.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Notifications** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Set **Allow Notifications** to on.
4. Open WalletFeed.
5. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
6. In the **Notifications** section, set **Recurring Charge Alerts** to on.

### If you do not get a notification

WalletFeed sends a notification only when a charge becomes a recurring charge, or when its price changes by more than 2%. It sends notifications only for charges from the last 7 days.

1. Open WalletFeed.
2. Tap **Settings** (the gear button) at the top of the screen.
3. Make sure that **Recurring Charge Alerts** is on.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/ -->
# Guides

Each guide shows how to send Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to one app or file type with WalletFeed.

- [Send Apple Card transactions to Zapier](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-zapier/index.md): Send your Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to Zapier with WalletFeed. A Catch Hook trigger starts your Zap for each transaction and each change.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Make](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-make/index.md): Send your Apple Card transactions to Make (the previous name of Make is Integromat). A Custom webhook receives each new or changed transaction.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to a webhook](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-webhook/index.md): WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a webhook in n8n or on your server.
- [Run a shortcut after each Apple Card purchase](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-shortcuts/index.md): Make a Shortcuts automation that sends each Apple Card purchase to your WalletFeed destinations seconds after you tap your iPhone.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Lunch Money](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-lunch-money/index.md): WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to Lunch Money. You paste a Lunch Money access token in WalletFeed.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to PocketSmith](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-pocketsmith/index.md): WalletFeed sends your Apple Card transactions to PocketSmith with no import file. You make a developer key in PocketSmith and paste it in WalletFeed.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Firefly III](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-firefly-iii/index.md): Send Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to Firefly III. Make a personal access token in Firefly III. Then paste the token in WalletFeed.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Sure](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-sure/index.md): Send Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to Sure, a self-hosted fork of Maybe Finance. Make an API key in Sure. Then paste the key in WalletFeed.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Toshl Finance](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-toshl/index.md): Send your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to Toshl Finance. Make a personal token in Toshl, then paste it into WalletFeed.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to BankSync](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-banksync/index.md): WalletFeed sends your Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to a BankSync table. Your AI agents can read them with BankSync's MCP tools or REST API.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to AWS](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-aws/index.md): Send your Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to Amazon S3, SQS, Kinesis Data Streams, DynamoDB or EventBridge in your AWS account with WalletFeed.
- [Make an export file of your Apple Card transactions](https://walletfeed.app/guides/export-apple-card-transactions/index.md): You can get an export file of your Apple Card transactions from Wallet, card.apple.com or WalletFeed. With WalletFeed Pro, WalletFeed also updates a file.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to your app or server](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-api/index.md): There is no web API for your Apple Card transactions. iPhone apps read them with FinanceKit. WalletFeed sends them to a webhook, AWS, Supabase or BankSync.
- [Save Apple Card transactions to a CSV file automatically](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-csv/index.md): WalletFeed writes your Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to a CSV file in a folder that you select, and updates the file automatically.
- [Save Apple Card transactions as OFX files](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ofx/index.md): WalletFeed saves your Apple Card transactions in one OFX file for each month and updates the files automatically. You import the files into your app.
- [Save Apple Card transactions as QIF files](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-qif/index.md): WalletFeed saves your Apple Card transactions from your iPhone as QIF files. It writes one QIF file for each month to a folder that you select.
- [Import Apple Card transactions into Quicken](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-quicken/index.md): You can import your Apple Card transactions into Quicken for Mac from OFX files that WalletFeed saves in iCloud Drive. Quicken for Windows uses a CSV file.
- [Import Apple Card transactions into Actual Budget](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-actual-budget/index.md): You can import Apple Card transactions into Actual Budget. WalletFeed writes them to an OFX file each month, and you import the file on a computer.
- [Import Apple Card transactions into GnuCash](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-gnucash/index.md): You can import your Apple Card transactions into GnuCash. On your iPhone, WalletFeed writes an OFX file for each month. Then, you import the files.
- [Put Apple Card transactions in YNAB](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-ynab/index.md): You can put your Apple Card transactions in YNAB with the YNAB app for iPhone. WalletFeed can also save them in OFX or CSV files that YNAB imports.
- [See Apple Card spending by category](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-by-category/index.md): See your Apple Card spending by category on your iPhone, with the total for the month and the merchants. You can use Spending without WalletFeed Pro.
- [Find subscriptions on your Apple Card](https://walletfeed.app/guides/find-apple-card-subscriptions/index.md): Find the subscriptions and other recurring charges on your Apple Card in WalletFeed. Get a notification for a new recurring charge or a new price.
- [Search Apple Card transactions](https://walletfeed.app/guides/search-apple-card-transactions/index.md): Search in WalletFeed finds a purchase in your Apple Card transactions. You can type a merchant, an amount or a category, or use Apple Intelligence.
- [Add an Apple Card spending widget](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-spending-widget/index.md): Add an Apple Card spending widget to your iPhone Home Screen or Lock Screen. It shows this month and the month before this month, to the same day and time.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Google Sheets](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-google-sheets/index.md): WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a Google Sheets spreadsheet in your Google Drive.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Airtable](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-airtable/index.md): WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to an Airtable base. Each transaction is a record.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Notion](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-notion/index.md): WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a Notion database. You can use the database for a budget.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Coda](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-coda/index.md): WalletFeed sends your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions from your iPhone to a table in Coda (Superhuman Docs) with an API token.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Supabase](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-supabase/index.md): WalletFeed sends your Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to a Postgres database in Supabase. Each transaction is one row in a table.
- [Send Apple Card transactions to Linear](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-linear/index.md): WalletFeed sends your Apple Card transactions from your iPhone to Linear. Each transaction becomes an issue in a Linear team.
- [Open Apple Card transactions in Excel](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-excel/index.md): WalletFeed writes your Apple Card transactions to a CSV file on your iPhone. Excel opens the file on a Mac or a PC.
- [Open Apple Card transactions in Numbers](https://walletfeed.app/guides/apple-card-to-numbers/index.md): Open your Apple Card transactions in a Numbers spreadsheet. WalletFeed saves them from your iPhone to a CSV file in iCloud Drive and updates the file.

<!-- https://walletfeed.app/guides/search-apple-card-transactions/ -->
# Search Apple Card transactions

On your iPhone, [Search](/docs/search/) in WalletFeed finds a purchase in your Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings transactions. You type the merchant, the amount or the category of the purchase. With Apple Intelligence, one search can have more than one filter, for example `dining over $50 last month`.

## Before you start

You must have these items:

- An iPhone with iOS 26 or a newer version. WalletFeed is available only in the US.
- WalletFeed on your iPhone, with access to your Apple Card, Apple Cash or Savings account. You can use Search without [WalletFeed Pro](/docs/walletfeed-pro/).
- An iPhone that can use Apple Intelligence, with Apple Intelligence active (necessary only for Search with Apple Intelligence).

## Step 1: Open Search

1. On your iPhone, open WalletFeed.
2. Tap the search button in the bottom right corner of the screen.

   ![The Transactions screen with the tab bar and the search button at the bottom of the screen.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/search-apple-card-transactions/walletfeed-transactions.webp)

   Then WalletFeed opens the search field and the keyboard. When the search field is empty, WalletFeed shows the categories of your transactions below **Categories**.

## Step 2: Find a purchase

1. Type a merchant name (`Uber`), an amount (`23.40`) or a category (`Dining`).

   When you type, WalletFeed shows the transactions that have your text in their merchant, description, category or amount.

   The results have one section for each month. In each section, the newest transaction is at the top. The rows are the same as in [Transactions](/docs/transactions/).

2. To start a different search, tap the clear button (x) in the search field.

When the search field is empty, you can also tap a category below **Categories**. Then WalletFeed puts the name of the category in the search field. The results show all the transactions in that category. The results can also include transactions that have the name of the category in their merchant or description.

## Step 3: Use Apple Intelligence in Search

If your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence and Apple Intelligence is active, the empty search field shows the example "Dining over $50 last month". If the empty search field shows "Transactions", Apple Intelligence is not available (refer to [If Apple Intelligence does not read the search](#if-apple-intelligence-does-not-read-the-search)).

1. In the search field, type your search, for example `dining over $50 last month`.
2. Tap **Search** on the keyboard.

   When Apple Intelligence reads the search, WalletFeed shows the Apple Intelligence icon and a progress indicator.

   At the top of the results, WalletFeed shows the filters that Apple Intelligence found, for example "Groceries · Over $50.00 · Last 30 days". Below the filters, a row shows the number of transactions and their total.

   ![The search results with the filters Groceries, Over $50.00 and Last 30 days, and a row that shows 4 transactions and a total of $277.57.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/search-apple-card-transactions/walletfeed-search.webp)

3. If you change the search, tap **Search** on the keyboard again.

   Until you tap **Search**, WalletFeed shows only the transactions that have your text.

> **Note:** On your iPhone, Apple Intelligence reads only your search. WalletFeed finds the transactions and calculates the total.

## Searches that Apple Intelligence can read

Apple Intelligence finds filters in your search. Then WalletFeed uses these filters to find your transactions. A search can have:

- One or more categories, for example **Dining** or **Groceries**
- A merchant, for example "Uber"
- An amount, with "over" or "under", for example "over $50"
- One period (**Last 7 days**, **Last 30 days**, **This month** or **Last month**)
- Only purchases (**Purchases**) or only money that you received (**Money in**).

Apple Intelligence can also find a category from a word that is not the name of the category. For example, it finds **Dining** for "restaurants" and **Fuel** for "gas".

For a merchant in the search, capital letters, accents, punctuation and an "s" at the end do not change the results. For example, "Ubers" finds Uber, and "trader joes" finds Trader Joe's.

WalletFeed calculates the number of transactions and the total. If the top of the results shows **Money in**, the total is the money that you received. If the top of the results does not show **Money in**, WalletFeed adds the amounts of your purchases. A refund decreases this total. Transfers and card payments do not change this total.

If WalletFeed finds no transactions for the filters, the row shows "0 transactions" and $0.00.

## Start a search with Siri

1. Tell [Siri](/docs/siri-and-shortcuts/) "Search WalletFeed" or "Find a transaction in WalletFeed".
2. When you hear "What are you looking for?", tell Siri your search, for example "dining over $50 last month".

   Then WalletFeed opens Search and shows your search in the search field. If your iPhone can use Apple Intelligence and Apple Intelligence is active, Apple Intelligence reads the search.

Siri does not get the results of the search or the total.

## If there is a problem

### If Search shows "No Cards"

You did not tap **Share** or **Don't Share** on the Wallet access screen.

1. Tap **Choose Accounts**.

   Then iOS shows the Wallet access screen (**Share Wallet Data**).

2. Select the accounts that WalletFeed can read.

   ![The Share Wallet Data screen, with the switches for Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings set to on.](https://walletfeed.app/guides/search-apple-card-transactions/walletfeed-wallet-access.webp)

3. Tap **Share**.

### If Search shows "Wallet Access Off"

You tapped **Don't Share**, or you stopped Wallet access for WalletFeed in the Settings app. iOS shows the Wallet access screen only one time. After this, you can change the access only in the Settings app.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Select the accounts that WalletFeed can read.
4. Open WalletFeed.

### If Search finds no transactions

No transaction has the text that you typed. Search shows "No Results for" and your search.

1. Make sure that the name of the merchant is correct.
2. Type a shorter search, for example only the first part of the name.
3. If WalletFeed shows "Tap Search to use Apple Intelligence.", tap **Search** on the keyboard.

### If Apple Intelligence does not read the search

Apple Intelligence reads a search only when Apple Intelligence is active and the search has 2 to 200 characters. If the empty search field shows "Transactions", Apple Intelligence is not available.

1. Make sure that your iPhone model is on the list in [Get started with the next generation of Apple Intelligence](https://support.apple.com/en-us/121115).
2. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
3. Tap **Apple Intelligence & Siri**.
4. Set **Apple Intelligence** to on, or tap **Turn on Apple Intelligence**.
5. Open WalletFeed.
6. Make sure that the search has 2 to 200 characters.
7. Tap **Search** on the keyboard.

### If Search shows "Couldn't read this search. Showing text matches."

In your search, Apple Intelligence did not find filters that WalletFeed can use. Then WalletFeed shows the transactions that have your text.

1. Type a short search with a category, a merchant, an amount or a period, for example `groceries this month`.
2. Tap **Search** on the keyboard.

### If a purchase is not in the results

Search finds only the transactions of the [Wallet accounts](/docs/wallet-accounts/) that you selected for WalletFeed. For each account, iOS gives WalletFeed the transactions from the start date that you selected.

1. On your iPhone, open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Privacy & Security** › **Wallet** › **WalletFeed**.
3. Change the accounts or the start date of each account.
4. Open WalletFeed.
5. Do the search again.
